## 2026-09-13 afternoon · ★Probe 0 step-size sweep: the x linear additive amplifier's first-order effect ≈ 0, the whole family is out★

The user ordered "start" (on the plan rewritten in plan.md). The first thing is plan.md §4's probe 0 —— it is cheap (using the 40-layer
amplifier already on disk, solving nothing new), and it judges the **entire form family**, not one set of hyperparameters.

### How it was judged (in plain words)

Multiply each layer's correction in the incumbent 40-layer amplifier by an overall coefficient β, then look at the end-to-end five metrics. The expansion of the exit loss in the step size is
`L(β) ≈ L0 − aβ + bβ²`: a is "does this correction direction actually help the exit" (first order), b is "how harmful is what was injected
in itself" (second order). **a > 0 ⇒ there exists a small β that makes end-to-end better**, the disease is only that the step is too big; **a ≈ 0 ⇒ this direction
has no leverage on the exit at all**, so no matter how you tune λ/K/whitening/target it is wasted tuning. Tuning hyperparameters cannot settle this, only sweeping β can.

The engine gains `--zchain-scale β` (at load time multiply A by β; multiply A and not B because A is the second GEMM's weight, do not touch
the numeric range of the first launch T=x·B), and judge's engine tier gains a fourth field. Four points run in a row with one command, each point ≈4.5 minutes.

### Measured (financial verdict shard vqfin41/vqhalf_j 8192, engine --score-ids same route as deployment, teacher PPL 6.9781)

| β | Σmin | median | p5 | Mean KLD | Same top | PPL ratio | ΔKLD vs bare |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **0 (bare line)** | **0.6762** | 0.7182 | 0.1883 | **0.70469** | **68.95%** | 1.457 | — |
| 0.1 | 0.6766 | 0.7238 | 0.1848 | 0.71399 | 68.97% | 1.477 | +0.0093 |
| 0.25 | 0.6744 | 0.7206 | 0.1749 | 0.74077 | 68.71% | 1.527 | +0.0361 |
| 0.5 | 0.6636 | 0.7113 | 0.1512 | 0.82324 | 66.85% | 1.662 | +0.1186 |
| 1.0 | 0.6005 | 0.6061 | 0.0740 | 1.19551 | 60.77% | 2.356 | +0.4908 |

(β=1 agrees with 09-12's 0.5999/1.203/60.51 ⇒ same state reproduced, the readings are trustworthy.)

### Verdict: a ≈ 0 ⇒ ★the entire x linear additive family is out★

ΔKLD is **strictly quadratic** in β: the four points' ΔKLD/β² = 0.93 / 0.58 / 0.47 / 0.49, settling around 0.48 for β≥0.25.
Solving `ΔKLD = aβ + bβ²` from the β=0.5 and β=1.0 points gives **a = −0.016, b = 0.507** ⇒ optimal step
β* = −a/(2b) = **0.016**, the gain at that point = a²/(4b) = **0.0001 KLD**. The grader's resolution over 8192 rows is
on the order of 0.01 —— in other words **the gain at the optimal step is two orders of magnitude smaller than the grader's resolution**, i.e. zero.
Σmin/Same top on the same caliber: at β=0.1 +0.0004 / +0.02pp, pure noise.

This is exactly the shape plan.md §2.1 predicted, and it is a conviction on the **curve shape**, not yet another "inexplicably negative" point:
- If the disease were "step too big" (a>0), a small β would show a **negative** ΔKLD, and none of the four points does.
- If the disease were "overfitting/regularization/rank", those knobs change the content of M, while the quadratic law says the damage depends only on the injected magnitude ‖βΔ‖,
  independent of M's content ⇒ those knobs cannot raise a off 0.

**⇒ that M which wins +9~19% in each layer has zero first-order leverage on the exit.** Combined with the 09-13 morning L39 distillation target's
held-out +0.09% (the exit-sensitive direction is only 0.09% inside x's linear space), two independent pieces of evidence point at the same thing:
**the direction the exit cares about is not a linear function of x, so the y += x·(B·A) form has no usable first-order gain.**

### What this invalidates (do not spend more time)

- Tuning λ / K / whitening / how many layers to mount / changing the target (the distillation target was already judged dead in the morning) —— all of these change M's content, none can move a.
- "exit step picking" (the fallback in plan.md's original §4 for when probe 0 came out positive): β* = 0.016 gain 0.0001, this path does not exist.
- The incumbent 40-layer amplifier directory is kept on file as diagnostic material, **not deployed**.

### Still standing

Sequential solving closes the positive-feedback coupling; both ends of the target share the same x; layout-layered held-out; the C chain and the torch path reproduce to four significant digits;
the in-layer held-out +9~19% is real (the downstream just does not care).

### Code (workspace, Mac make ds4 + linecount pass, spark make cuda-spark passes)

`--zchain-scale β`: `ds4_v41_api.h` (setter declaration) / `core_v41_api.c` (global + setter, β≤0 treated as 1.0) /
`core_v41.h` (extern) / `core_v41_amp.c` (multiply A by β after reading it out, log β) / `cli_opts.c` (goes through the global setter,
does not go into ds4_engine_opts —— ds4.h is already at the 500-line ceiling) / `cli_print.c` (help) / `v41_judge.sh` (engine tier
fourth field β).

### Probe 1 (same day 14:25, pure CPU two minutes): the damage is uniformly coherent, no out-of-distribution behaviour

The grader already has `--row-out` (per-position dump of KL/Σmin/whether same top), no code change needed. The student logits of the bare
state and the β=1 state are both on disk, just run anchor_metrics twice and subtract row by row. Cross-tab script `v41_rowkl_diff.sh` (new, checked in).

```
全段 ΔKL 均值 +0.4908   变差行占比 75.6%   (n=8192)
窗首 8 行 +0.6551       窗尾 8 行 +0.4869
域: announce +0.4553 | exam +0.5351 | flash +0.4954 | article +0.4797 | news +0.4871
按基线 KL 分位: <0.1 +0.1517 | 0.1-0.4 +0.4201 | 0.4-1.2 +0.6239 | >1.2 +0.9264
```

- **three quarters of the tokens get worse**, the five subdomains' damage is level within ±8% ⇒ it is not one domain refusing.
- The window head (context cold start) is 35% heavier than the window tail, but the same order of magnitude —— not "it only collapses at cold start".
- By baseline KL quantile it is **monotonic**: positions the model was already unsure about suffer more (+0.93), positions it was very sure about suffer less (+0.15)
  —— the damage is proportional to "how sure this position originally was", the natural shape of a deterministic bias superimposed on the distribution, not an exogenous collapse.

**⇒ plan.md §2.2's "coherent bias" is confirmed**: what each layer injects is a deterministic function of x, and the 40 layers superpose coherently along
the same residual stream, every token eats a bit. There is no "a few positions collapsing" to find —— the 09-12 per-row/per-channel diagnostics found
nothing in-layer because it simply is not in-layer.

### The conclusion of the two probes together

| Question | Evidence | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| Is the step too big? | ΔKLD purely quadratic in β, fit a=−0.016 b=0.507, β*=0.016 gain 0.0001 | No. First-order leverage ≈ 0 |
| Is it a few positions collapsing? | 75.6% of rows worse, five domains level, quantiles monotonic | No. Uniformly coherent bias |
| Are the hyperparameters mistuned? | the quadratic law says the damage depends only on the injected magnitude, independent of M's content | No. λ/K/whitening/target cannot move a |

**Next step per plan.md §3: move the correction inside the routing (per-expert weight side, per-token nonlinear), move the landing criterion to the exit grader.**

## 2026-09-13 afternoon · ★Form change: the correction moves inside the routing (weight-side per-expert gain)★ —— segment 0, three layers, first positive end-to-end

After probe 0/probe 1 judged the "add a linear function of x at the exit" family dead, change form per plan.md §3. **No longer add anything to the exit, change the weights themselves.**

### In plain words: what is changed

In the quantized file each expert's each matrix stores `W[r][c] = codebook[idx][d] × g[r]` (vq_fmt.h), g is a per-row scalar.
The down matrix's "row" is exactly the **output channel** ⇒ re-solving g = giving each expert's each output channel a new gain. The plugin stores only a **scale factor**
s (anchor 1 = unchanged), and at engine decode time `g_eff = the g in the payload × s[e][row]` —— **not one byte of the on-disk weights moves, and not mounting means the bare base**.

Why it can get around the wall probe 0 judged dead: the injected correction Δ = Σ_e rw_e·(s_e−1)·y_e varies per token with "which experts were selected,
what each expert's hidden layer is", and is **not a linear function of x** —— while what probe 0 proved is exactly that "a linear function of x
has no first-order leverage on the exit".

### Math (independent per output channel, closed form)

What the engine emits at this layer is `y[i][d] = round_bf16( Σ_k rw[i][k]·ye[i][k][d] + ysh[i][d] )` (ye = per-expert down output,
not multiplied by the routing weight; ysh = shared expert output). Scale expert e's gain by s_e[d], the target is the FP whole-block output:
```
min_s  Σ_i ( ysh + Σ_k s·rw·ye − y_fp )²  +  λ · den_bar[d] · Σ_e (s_e − 1)²
```
The gain is diagonal ⇒ **the 5120 output channels are completely independent**, each channel is a 384-dimensional least squares. Solution = per-expert
Gauss-Seidel rotated 3 rounds (each expert touches only its own ~128 rows, the residual is updated immediately after solving), no assembling 5120 384×384 systems.

### The three pieces landed + two traps actually hit

| Item | Approach |
|---|---|
| Capture | the engine hook additionally hands over `ye[n][n_used][D]` (the prefill GEMM path's ys before reduce, expanded by inv) and `ysh[n][D]`. ★No recomputing★ —— it uses exactly the numbers the engine's weighted sum uses |
| Solving | `gguf-tools/amp/v41_gr_solve.cu` (new) + driver orchestration `v41_gr_run.inc.c` (new, included by v41_amp_run.c as a single TU, split into files only to keep the 500-line rule) |
| Deployment | artifact `gr_Lnn.bin` (header `<i32 n_expert><i32 D><i32 1>` + s[384][5120] f32, 7.9 MB/layer). The engine's `--zchain <dir>` loads it through the same entry point; the prefill GEMM path and the decode gemv path consume this table **in the same form** (verdict and deployment do not fork) |

★**Trap one: the scale of the ridge**★ the first version used each expert's own energy den_e as the ridge scale, i.e. `s = (num/den_e + λ)/(1+λ)` ——
this expression puts **no constraint whatsoever** on s's absolute deviation: a cold expert is selected only a few times in the fitting segment, den_e is small, the ridge shrinks with it,
and the solution is pushed to extremes by a few rows. Measured L00 **train +32.7% while val −2685%**, and raising λ from 0.01 to 1 only pulls val to −1002
(the ridge "grows" but its relative strength does not change). After switching to **the average energy of all experts in this channel** as the unified scale, the same layer's val jumped straight to **+27.0%**.
Uneven routing is the core risk of this path: the experts selected the fewest times have no data supporting changing them, and the ridge must cover for them.

★**Trap two: fake sequencing**★ the multi-pass sequential relies on the `ok_layers` count to decide whether the next pass mounts this directory, and that count is accumulated only on the low-rank path,
the weight-side path missed that entry ⇒ **every pass solved on the bare base, the inter-layer coupling was never closed at all, and it reports no error**. After the fix the log prints per pass
"[反修·权重侧] N 层挂上", which is real sequencing.

★Capture self-check (mechanism audit, run on every layer)★: `round_bf16(Σ_k rw·ye + ysh)` against the engine's y is **bit-identical 99.996%,
relative difference 1.7e-5** (the 0.004% that differ are f32 accumulation order flipping a bit at a bf16 boundary). A mispairing reports no error, only a false account, so this probe is a hard gate.

| Grader | | PPL (ratio) | Σmin (median/p5) | Mean KLD | Same top |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **financial j 8192 (main grader)** | bare | 10.1659 (1.457) | 0.6762 (0.718/0.188) | 0.70469 | 68.95% |
| | **+37 layers** | **9.3432 (1.339)** | **0.7180** (0.782/0.240) | **0.58006** | **72.08%** |
| | change | −8.1% | **+0.0418** | **−17.7%** | **+3.13pp** |
| eight domains j 8192 (gatekeeper) | bare | 15.4641 (1.485) | 0.6422 (0.643/0.204) | 0.73544 | 65.20% |
| | **+37 layers** | **14.2341 (1.367)** | **0.6748** (0.679/0.249) | **0.63188** | **67.54%** |
| | change | −8.0% | +0.0326 | −14.1% | +2.34pp |
| wt2 512 (gatekeeper) | bare | 3.3099 (1.998) | 0.7405 (0.925/0.043) | 0.790 | 75.98% |
| | **+37 layers** | **3.0582 (1.846)** | **0.7590** (0.932/0.059) | **0.70799** | **77.54%** |
| | change | −7.6% | +0.0185 | −10.4% | +1.56pp |

★**The general grader not only did not regress, it rose**★. This is the opposite of the V4 era's experience of "financial z on wt2 KLD +11.6%", and the mechanism is clear:
what is corrected is the **quantization error of the weights themselves** (by how much each expert's own down gain is off), not domain-specific behaviour. The financial corpus
is only the sample used to **estimate** this error, the error itself is domain-independent —— so the correction fitted on financial works just as well on the eight domains and English Wikipedia.
The three graders' relative gains are also consistent (KLD −17.7 / −14.1 / −10.4%), financial is fattest because the fitting material is financial, but the gap is 1.7×, not an order of magnitude.

**p5 rose on all three graders** (0.188→0.240 / 0.204→0.249 / 0.043→0.059): the worst batch of positions is also improving, it is not padding the mean with easy positions.

### The true account of size and bandwidth (whole-byte caliber, nothing cherry-picked)

- On disk: 37 layers × 7.86 MB (f32) = **291 MB**; after switching to f16 **146 MB** (the scale factors are always near 1, f16's resolution at 1
  is 2^-10 ≈ 0.1%, three orders of magnitude smaller than the quantization error it has to fix). Base 110.6 GB ⇒ +0.13%, equivalent to **+0.0021 bpw**.
- Decode bandwidth: **not zero**. Per token per layer an extra read of the 6 experts × 5120 channels coverage table = f32 123 KB/layer, f16 61 KB/layer,
  37 layers total 4.5 / 2.3 MB/token, which against 10.05 GB/token is **0.045% / 0.023%**. Negligible, but do not call it zero.

### How far from the north star (no vagueness)

The bit-width curve (wt2 512): every 0.5 bpw ≈ 10pp Same top. The financial main grader 68.95 → 72.08 = **+3.13pp ≈ the work of +0.16 bpw**,
bought with 146 MB (+0.0021 bpw) —— a leverage of about **75×**. To the 80% target there are still 7.9pp missing.
**The next rung (codebook re-solve) is the second rung of §3.2's rank ladder**: the unknowns go from 5120 gains per expert to 32768 codebook entries, the same set of
capture/sequencing/picking/exit criterion, with one Gauss-Newton step added to the solver.

### ★Segment 1 verdict (20:37) + plan revised to a second version (back.md rewritten)★

Segment 1 actually finished: training set 8 items (fitting 7088 rows / val 479 / 147 decision points), the gradient target ‖α·g‖/‖y_q‖=0.0020 amplified to 0.05, y-space solving
gives **train +0.20% / val +0.04%** (λ=0.1, the scale factors already ran to [0.29, 2.00]), did not pass the 0.5% gate, produced no file ⇒ no levering to speak of.
Conviction: **the target was placed in the wrong space**. The loss gradient is a 5120-dimensional dense direction determined by the target token's word vector, with no structural relation to "which 6 experts were selected", and the gain form
can only express a per-channel reweighting of the expert output ⇒ the two are nearly orthogonal; while "whether a decision point flips" is decided by the single scalar ℓ[correct]−ℓ[wrong], and from the last layer's MoE output to it is
exactly linear. Second version: one linear equation per decision point (target = τ − m⁰), non-decision rows get a "the original top1−top2 difference is unchanged" constraint, the ridge is the same as 反修, solved in one CG;
the criterion becomes two levels: grader A = the flip rate of the training day's own decision points (≥90%, linear prediction should be ~100%, falling short = the pipe leaks), grader B = the verdict set's flip rate vs 50.75%.
No more η; the y-space val gate is void for ③; candidates that fail the gate are not rm'd (moved to rejected/). Full text in back.md. No code changed, awaiting approval.

### Segment 1′ smoke test first probe (21:39): the mechanism works, one caliber error corrected on the spot

3 samples, 80 decision points (31/32 + 15/16 + 34/34 usable), all 3268 constraint rows usable, ye buffer 0.41 GB, one candidate 1.5 seconds.
All 12 candidates: fitting flip 91.7~100%, constraint rows with |Δm|>0.5 **0.00%**, |s−1| mean 0.014~0.028. The form has enough capacity, the pipe is open.

★But the val flip rate is 90.00% identically for all 12 candidates★ —— opening predict.txt on the spot showed it was false:
```
val 决策点 20 个: 基线 m0>0 18 个 (90.0%), 解后 18 个 (90.0%)   ← 解算零贡献
fit 决策点 60 个: 基线 47 (78.3%), 解后 60 (100.0%)             ← 只是记住了训练点
val 逐行 m⁰: +12.415 / +13.585 / +14.283 ...
```
**Conviction: the opponent was chosen wrong.** With the "wrong-version token" as the opponent, 81.25% of the 80 decision points already had m⁰>0 (mean +5.86), that is,
the model at those positions was already extremely biased toward the correct version, not a wrong judgement at all; while the same batch under the argmax caliber is only 50.75%.
What beat the correct version on the missing 30pp is a **third-party token**, not the wrong version —— pressing the correct version past the wrong version, argmax still does not choose it.
**The fix (landed)**: the decision row's opponent becomes "the token with the highest current probability other than the correct version", so m>0 is strictly equivalent to argmax=correct version,
and the optimization objective and the deployment behaviour become the same quantity. The wrong-version sequence is still read, but only to decide "do the two versions really differ on this row".
The on-disk top-K and rms tables need not be re-burned (what changed is the row caliber), `sftsolve` solves again directly.

### Segment 1′ second probe (21:50, after the opponent became the "strongest opponent"): the caliber lines up, the training points all flip, generalization = 0

The same batch of material (top-K/rms not re-burned), `sftsolve` re-solves, each of the 12 candidates 1.5 seconds:
```
[后训练·基线] 决策点 80 个: m⁰>0 的 44 个 = 55.00%, 平均 m⁰ -0.4026   ← 与 argmax 口径 50.75% 对上了
dec_fit 60 个: 基线 33 (55.0%) → 解后 60 (100.0%), 平均 dm +3.0049
dec_val 20 个: 基线 11 (55.0%) → 解后 11 (55.0%), 平均 dm +0.3986   ← 9 个错的一个没翻
```
val row by row: the direction is right (−12.706 was pushed by +5.242, −8.361 was pushed by +1.298), but the magnitude is an order of magnitude too small.
**Mechanism**: 60 decision equations against 1.97M unknowns, the minimum-norm solution covers almost only the subspace spanned by the points it has seen ——
the correction is highly "point-specific". This is the typical behaviour of an underdetermined solution, not a bug.
Across the board the constraint rows have |Δm|>0.5 at 0.00% (only 0.03% even at ρ=10 λ=10), which says "do not move elsewhere" holds.
**This is not a verdict**: only 3 samples and 60 fitting decision points. What segment 2 (8 items) is to look at is whether val rises with sample count.
The next step is first to pass grader A with a real forward (the design says explicitly: <90% is a misalignment bug, stop and check, do not tune parameters).

### ★Segment 1′ third probe (22:13, real forward grader A): caught the third, and the real mechanism problem★

```
★尺A 训练日决策点翻转: 54/73 = 73.97%★ (门 ≥90%)
  守门1 约束行 argmax 仍是原 top1: 2049/3268 = 62.70% (门 ≥99.5%)
  自检2 预测 vs 真前向: 相关 1.0000, 翻/不翻一致 99.91% (门 相关≥0.95 且一致≥95%)
```
(on the first run grader A/gatekeeper 1 reported 0/0 —— the grader's `--rows` does not accept "@file" and the error was swallowed by `|| true`.
Both are fixed: `--rows` and the solver share one syntax (there should only have been one copy all along), and a grader failure always stops.)

**The three numbers do not contradict each other, together they are the mechanism**: self-check 2 proves the prediction of "the logit difference of that one token pair we pinned" matches the real forward bit for bit
(correlation 1.0000) —— the math chain/capture/fp4 round trip are all correct. But gatekeeper 1 collapses to 62.70% while the solver predicts "the constraint rows moved 0.00%":
the constraint row pins the [original top1 vs original top2] difference, and that difference really did not change; what changed is ★a third token rising above the original top1★.
grader A 73.97% rather than the predicted 100% for the same reason: the decision row pins "the correct version vs the strongest opponent at solve time", and after solving the strongest opponent is a different token.

★Root cause: the correction acts on the whole 5120-dimensional channel and will lift the logits of a whole bunch of tokens together; pinning a single pair per row is not enough.★

**The correct fix (within the existing framework, no change of form or solution)**: expand "one pair" to "the entire top-64 ranking" ——
the decision row requires ℓ_correct > ℓ_v for all v on the ranking; the constraint row requires ℓ_top1 > ℓ_v for all v on the ranking.
This is the correct use of that active set in back.md §4.2: after solving, use ★linear prediction★ (already proven accurate to correlation 1.0, no real forward needed)
to compute Δℓ for every token on the ranking, add the risers as new equations and re-solve. Still linear equations, still conjugate gradient.

### Active-set version landed (22:2x~) + a trap I ran into myself

Per the mechanism above the equations change from "one per row" to "one group per row": after solving, use ★linear prediction★ to sweep the whole top-64 ranking
(`v41_klt_margin_scan`, millisecond scale, no real forward), whoever rises in front of "the one that should win" is added as a new equation, re-solve, at most 6 rounds.
the decision row = the correct version must beat everyone on the ranking; the constraint row = the top spot must not change hands. The solver's self-reported metrics also switch to the ★argmax caliber★,
measuring the same thing as the real forward's grader A / gatekeeper 1 —— the earlier "predicted 100% but real forward 74%" looked like a contradiction, the root is that the two rulers differ.
The code was split into `v41_sft_run.inc.c` (capture/list/row table) + `v41_margin_solve.inc.c` (solve/active set), keeping the 500 lines;
`anchor_metrics.c` likewise had `anchor_metrics_rows.inc.c` split out.

★A real hit (22:29)★: the ranking-sweep kernel `an illegal memory access`. The real cause was my own oversight —— the row-compaction stretch
copied the fields one by one twice, and later four arrays of "the whole ranking" (tid/tlp/want/wlp) were added to the accumulator, added only at the fill site, ★both copy sites were missed★,
so the val segment and the constraint segment read a misaligned ranking. The locating clue was that the baseline val reported 45.00% while the same batch was 55.00% the round before.
Neither fix is "add those four lines": ①the field list is factored into a single `mg_acc_move` (two lists would leak again sooner or later);
②the ranking-sweep kernel gains a vocabulary bounds check —— a mis-assembled ranking is treated as 0 and left for the self-check to find, better than scrapping the entire CUDA context.

there), so it is not "how much was broken" at all. The correct measurement is to compare [the two top-K tables] (baseline state vs candidate state) on the same batch of rows:

### ★The user challenges "this little data and it takes an hour, that cannot be right" —— right, half of it was burned for nothing★

The account (8 samples × 6000 token):
| Item | Time | Necessary? |
|---|---|---|
| the scoring pass launches ./ds4 independently 8 times, loading the model 107s each time | ≈14 min | ★unnecessary★ |
| the scoring pass's 8 forwards to get top-K/NLL/rms | ≈28 min | necessary |
| the capture pass, one load + 8 forwards to get per-expert output | ≈22 min | ★completely duplicates the previous item★ |
| solving 12 candidates | 1.5 min | necessary |

★The root: the same batch of tokens was forwarded twice.★ The ranking is computed at the exit step, the per-expert output is taken at the hook step —— they are by nature in one
forward (back.md §6's own words are "the hook returns 0 and the forward continues to the exit, the target and the gradient come from the same forward"), the implementation drifted:
the hook returns 1 and stops early, on the grounds that "running to the exit writes full-vocabulary logits" (517 KB/position = draining GPU memory). But 09-13 already
landed --score-no-logits + --score-topk/--score-nll/--score-rms, three small exits, so the exit section writes only tens of MB,
and the reason for stopping early has long ceased to exist.

**Three things changed** (effective from the next round; this round's scoring is already paid for, stopping and restarting would not be faster, so let it finish):
1. The hook by default runs to the exit, the ranking/NLL/rms and the per-expert output land ★in the same pass★; only `--reuse-tables` stops early (used for re-solving after a row-caliber change).
   Side benefit: the two come from the same forward pass, so even the assumption "are the two passes bit-identical" is no longer needed.
2. `--verify-tabs <prefix>`: with a candidate mounted, one load runs all samples and emits the tables, replacing gatea's 8 ./ds4 launches (saving another 14 min).
3. The script's `③②` section changed to only stopping the service, the tables are emitted by the solver itself.

After the change, per night: capture + tables ≈30 min (one load) + solving 1.5 min + verifying one candidate ≈30 min.
**Also noted**: a single 6000-token forward is 3.5 min ≈ 29 t/s prefill, that number is low in itself, it is the engine's existing performance, listed separately and not in this round.

### ★09-14 third version (generalization side) landed + smoke test: grader L's self-check passes, "val zero" gets a quantitative cause★

The second version's mechanism was fully open but not one decision point flipped (09-13 23:07 real forward val 55.00%, 09-14 00:30 eight samples 12 candidates
val 55.26%, not a decimal place off). **The root cause is neither a bug nor too few samples**: 60~117 decision equations against 1.97M unknowns,
the minimum-norm solution always lies in span{A_i}, an out-of-fold point Δm_j = Σ β_i<A_j,A_i> —— if A_j is nearly orthogonal to the training set it is always 0.
So the third version changes neither the form nor the solution, it only does three things (the plan lands in back.md's third version):

1. **Grader L (leave-one-out generalization grader)**: leave-one-out by ★sample item★ (random folds by point = adjacent points in the same report leak), each fold solves one CG +
   fp4 round trip (not written to disk), looking only at whether out-of-fold decision points flip. `v41_margin_gen.inc.c` added.
   **The candidate sort key changes from "training fit rate" to this** —— sorting by fit rate is specifically picking the one best at memorizing (measured 09-14: the two candidates with fitting
   76.92% and 57.26% flipped the verdict points identically).
2. **Two generalization priors**: ①expert-frequency ridge `ridge = λ·den_bar[d]·w_e`, `w_e=(f_max+κ)/(f_e+κ)` normalized to mean 1
   (without normalizing, the effects of κ and λ mix together); ②word-pair repetition `ν`: how many times the same (should-win, opponent) token pair appears across items,
   the decision equation's weight ×(1+ν·(rep−1)) —— the direction table C is entirely determined by this word pair, across days the same word pair has exactly the same C, the strongest reuse lever.
3. **Diagnostic Gram** (`v41_gr_margin_gram` GPU kernel + host Cholesky): the out-of-fold decision equations' projection share onto the in-fold subspace.

**Smoke-test readings (09-14 08:0x, 3 samples, τ=1 ρ=1 λ=3, material re-captured)**:

**Two conclusions**:
- **Grader L's regression self-check passes**: the Δ +0.00pp reported in 21 seconds matches exactly last night's half-hour real forward's "not one val flipped"
  (back.md §7 segment 2b's gate). From now on picking candidates need not gamble a whole night.
- **"val zero" now has a quantitative cause**: only 6.8% (median 0.6%) of the out-of-fold decision equations' energy falls inside the in-fold subspace.
  ★An unexpected one★: **expert overlap is as high as 86.9%** —— the routing is highly repetitive, so the orthogonality is not caused by routing,
  it is the product direction `ye_ik[d]·c_i[d]` itself that is orthogonal. ⇒ merely "taking the same experts" is not enough, the prior must push on the c (word pair) side.

Also fixed a bug that would produce a false account: with `--share` the candidate directory is called `candS_*` while candidates.txt writes `cand_*`,
so the gate section following the table finds nothing. At the same time "quantization round trip" was factored out of `gr_write_bin` into `gr_fp4_roundtrip` —— leave-one-out needs "round trip but not
written to disk" in every fold, and the two places must be the same implementation, otherwise grader L measures the solved state while gate measures the landed state, and the two numbers are not comparable.

★Two traps stepped in (both my own operational errors, recorded to prevent repeating)★:
1. After changing `z_nightly_spark.sh`'s κ/ν parameters, launched ★without re-syncing to spark★, the old script ran ⇒ the first round's
   24 candidates shrank to 4 (κ/ν both at the binary defaults). **Before launching you must confirm the script on the other side is new**, not just the binary.
2. The wait condition was hung on "grader L line count ≥ 25", while that round would only emit 4 lines ⇒ 40 minutes wasted. **For long jobs always hang the wait on
   "process exit"** (`until ! pgrep -f v41_amp_run`), never on your own estimated output line count.

not rising ⇒ the last layer's constant gain has no "conditional slot", the form must change (segment 4's x keying), rather than tuning parameters further.

Coverage curve: 3 items → 8 items, projection share 6.8% → 9.3%, ΔL 0 → −0.85pp. By the third version's own §4.8 criterion: **slope ≈ 0, adding days is useless, priors/dimensionality reduction ineffective, the third version is dead.**

**User: "the latest fine-tune is still not quite satisfying, analyse the problem, design a better plan and land it in back.md, do not write code".** Pulling up the 12 samples' raw text
(`gguf/v41/night/samples_all.json`), the disease common to the first three versions was caught, none of it in the solver (those linear predictions with correlation 0.9995 were all correct):
1. **The target holds only numbers, no lessons**: the 12 samples cover only 2 trading days, 48 edits; each report has only 1 real root decision (the target price revised down for ADX overheating / high-level high turnover / range-bound market
   making the golden ratio untrustworthy), the rest are all arithmetic derivations of return/risk-reward/JSON; the human-written `why` (= four or five rules recurring across stocks, the only generalizable thing in this data)
   **never once entered an equation**. The solver can only memorize "002104 position 2870 writes 13 not 14", which is meaningless for 600410 (the correct value is 9.30) —— adding samples brings new numbers, not the same rule.
2. The form has no conditional slot (expert overlap 94.6% ⇒ routing is not a discriminative key, the constant gain is the same for every token of the whole report).
3. The ruler measures the wrong half: most of the verdict set's decision points are derived arithmetic positions / a number's first token, and an argmax hit is neither sufficient nor necessary for "learned the rule".
4. The verdict set and the training set share a day (all 4 verdict items are 09-07, and the training set also has 5 items from 09-07).
5. It drifted from the teacher settled by the user on 09-08 ("the self that has read the retrospective"), and from 09-13 quietly switched to "the tokens the human changed".

**Fourth version (back.md rewritten)**: teacher = ①+② itself + a retrospective memory segment (`why` raw text concatenated deterministically, zero LLM rewriting, zero new corpus); target = the teacher state vs the student state on
**every token** of the report, the top-64 distribution difference (8 items ≈840k equations, no longer 60 against 1.97M; "do not move elsewhere" is intrinsically included); **first measure grader C (the context ceiling)**:
if the rules laid out in front of it on the verdict day change no judgement ⇒ stop and report to the user, not one line of solver is written; if it passes the gate ⇒ level 1 (the same constant gain as ②, the incumbent solver only swaps the right-hand side, grader L in seconds),
and if it cannot reach half the ceiling go to level 2 (an exit conditional head ĥ' = ĥ + U·tanh(Vᵀĥ), R≤32, 655 KB, training needs no engine back-propagation, it has a per-token "conditional slot").
The verdict set changes to hold out by day (09-07's nine verdict items, resolution 1.5pp→0.7pp); decision points are bucketed (root/derived, text/number), numeric root decisions change to measuring the probability mass centre's direction;
③each night solves from scratch rather than multiplying night by night. It does not conflict with probe 0's verdict (that was the first-order leverage for fixing quantization noise, this is a first-order visible behaviour shift). No code changed, awaiting approval.

### ★09-14 night · the 反修 plugin lands FP4: direct grid solve (not solve-then-compress), 291.0 → 38.6 MB while the main grader advances instead of regressing★

User order: **"the current 反修 is a positive gain, but the output file is not fp4 precision"** → then **"what I want is for the 反修 output to be fp4 directly,
not converted data"**. The full plan and criteria are in `fp4.md`, this section records only the landing and the readings.

**Starting facts**: the incumbent ② `gguf/v41/gr-fin-40/` header is `384 5120 1` = **f32**, 37 layers × 7.86 MB = **291.0 MB**.
The one that scored 72.08% on 09-13 is exactly this. The "write fp4" comment in the code was the intention at the time, and on disk it was never changed.

**Why the "solve then compress" path must be rejected** (let the numbers speak first, then touch the code): re-encoding the incumbent f32 artifact as is,
the RMS distortion relative to [the correction amount itself] —— storing s−1 **11.18%**, storing s directly **60.52%** (the latter a dead end: the gains are all crammed near 1,
the block scale is pinned by the maximum, the grid spacing 0.11 is the same order as the correction amount). The 11% is not the encoder being badly tuned: the block scale already searches 6 levels per block,
E2M1 has only 8 magnitude grid points ⇒ 4 bit's relative precision is on the order of 10%, it is the physical precision of the bit width.
**Solve then compress = throwing away 11% of the correction amount, and no one takes over that error.**

**Landing: direct grid solve** (`v41_gr_solve.cu`). Gauss-Seidel's original two steps "solve → update residual" are split into three:
①solve the one-dimensional ridge least squares (writing only s, keeping s_old) → ②`gr_fp4_quant_kernel` projects s−1 onto the fp4 grid and ★directly produces
the 17 B/block codeword★ → ③updates the residual by [grid value − s_old]. So this expert's quantization error enters the residual on the spot, and the experts queued behind
compensate within the same round, with rounds 2 and 3 compensating further. Isomorphic to GPTQ/OBQ's error compensation, the unknowns being per-expert per-channel one-dimensional gains.
What lands on disk is exactly ②'s codeword, **zero conversion in between**; before writing it is read back with `src/common`'s single decoder for a **bit-level self-proof**, and if they differ it stops.
Also fixed a caliber error along the way: previously λ was chosen by the **solved-state** val and then the winner was compressed to fp4, now every λ's val is on the grid,
so picking and deployment share a caliber. `gr_recode` (the conversion path) and its Makefile target are deleted —— the solver is allowed only one implementation.

**Single-layer probe** (L00, same fitting material, same λ grid): landed val **+26.72%** vs 09-13's f32 free solve's **solved state** +26.99%
⇒ **the cost of the grid constraint is only 0.27pp (1.0% relative)**, not 11%. The error compensation works.

**40-layer sequential** (09-14 21:24 → 09-15 00:00, fitting material vqfin41/vqhalf_a 8192): **37 layers mounted / 3 gated**,
**the same batch of layers** as the 09-13 f32 round (L29/L30/L32 blocked by the 0.5% gate); fitting material PPL 13.3940 → **11.9617**
(the f32 round was 12.0121, this round is lower). Per-layer val comparison (fp4 landed state vs f32 solved state): L00 26.72/26.99 ·
L01 17.79/17.96 · L02 14.04/14.16 · L13 8.96/9.1 · L19 14.40/14.5 · L38 8.50/8.9 · L39 15.28/16.7
—— shallow layers almost lossless, deep layers differ by 1~1.4pp.

**★Financial main grader verdict (09-15 00:03, vqfin41/vqhalf_j 8192, engine --score-ids same route as deployment)★**:

| | PPL (ratio) | Σmin (median/p5) | Mean KLD | Same top | on-disk size |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| bare (①) | 10.1659 (1.457) | 0.6762 (0.718/0.188) | 0.70469 | 68.95% | — |
| ② f32 (09-13) | 9.3432 (1.339) | 0.7180 (0.782/0.240) | 0.58006 | 72.08% | 291.0 MB |
| **② fp4 direct grid solve** | **9.2545 (1.326)** | **0.7181 (0.7813/0.2448)** | **0.57474** | **72.18%** | **38.6 MB** |

★**7.5× smaller in size, not one of the five metrics regressed**★ (Same top +0.10pp / KLD −0.9% / p5 +0.0048 / PPL ratio 1.339→1.326).
The gate line was originally "regress ≤0.5pp", in fact it rose. Against the 110.6 GB base: +0.26% → **+0.035%** (0.00035 bpw);
decode bandwidth per token 4.5 MB → 0.6 MB (0.045% → 0.006% against 10.05 GB/token).

**Why fp4 is a bit better than f32 instead**: not that fp4 is more accurate, it is that the direct grid solve's solution is **different** —— it is re-solved under the constraint "only these
values may be taken", and ridge + error compensation put it at a point that generalizes more stably (the verdict material is unseen corpus). The 0.10pp gap is at the edge of the noise band,
**the conclusion goes only as far as "did not regress", no bragging about "better"**.

**The gate question (raised by the user on the spot)**: the gated-out L29/L30/L32 val is +0.41 / +0.27 / +0.46% ——
★L32 is only 0.04pp from the 0.5% gate★. This gate's origin is "the same gate as the low-rank path for easy cross-comparison", **it was never verified on the end-to-end grader**.
After fp4 even size is no longer a reason (1.04 MB/layer, three layers +3.1 MB = 0.003% of the base). The user ordered "anything greater than 0 is not gated",
`GR_GATE` 0.5 → 0 (the criterion `val <= 0` is what does not mount: ≤0 is "broken on the held-out", those must still be blocked).
**The control run launched 09-15 00:05**, artifact `gr-fin-40-fp4-gate0`, judged with the same main grader.
Note the gate is not "nothing happened": under sequencing nothing is written to disk ⇒ that layer's error stays in the residual for later layers to compensate, so the two runs are **not in a "three more layers" relation,
the next 10 layers' solutions will also differ**, and only a full rerun of the whole pass is comparable.

The user asked "are these gated-out ones really worthless", and ordered "change it to keep greater-than and run again". `GR_GATE` 0.5 → 0, whole run redone
(`gr-fin-40-fp4-gate0`, verdict 05:24). **This is the first time this gate has been verified end to end** —— its origin was only "same gate
as the low-rank path for easy cross-comparison", the 09-13 round used it directly and never ran a control.

| Finance main ruler j 8192 | 37 layers (gate 0.5) | 40 layers (gate=0) | diff |
|---|---:|---:|---:|

| Mean KLD | **0.57474** | 0.57718 | +0.4% |

|s−1| mean 0.011 (the attached fat layers are 0.2~0.3), writing them in is near-identity, they neither helped nor hurt, they just took 3.1 MB more.

### 09-15 · Gate curve swept to the end (0 / 0.5 / 1.0): ★0.5 and 1.0 are indistinguishable, only 0 is clearly worse —— knob at the end, stop★

The user asked "0.5 is magical, why does pinning this improve things, while turning it to 0 instead decreases, and what happens if it becomes 1", and ordered another run.

| Gate | Layers | Size | Same top | Mean KLD | PPL(ratio) | Σmin(p5) | Fit-corpus PPL |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0(keep all) | 40 | 41.8 MB | 72.08% | 0.57718 | 9.2930(1.332) | 0.7178(.2423) | 11.9799 |
| **0.5(in service)** | 37 | 38.6 MB | **72.18%** | 0.57474 | 9.2545(1.326) | 0.7181(**.2448**) | **11.9617** |
| 1.0 | 35 | 36.6 MB | 72.08% | **0.57429** | **9.2512**(1.326) | 0.7181(.2430) | 【not recorded】 |

**The readings contradict each other**: Same top and p5 say 0.5 wins, KLD and PPL say 1.0 wins (and it is 2 MB smaller); the gaps 0.10pp / 0.08% /
0.0033 —— all within the noise band. ★0.5 and 1.0 are indistinguishable on the main ruler★. **The only certain thing is that 0 (keep all) is worst** (all four items negative).
So the curve is not "a peak at 0.5", it is **flat from 0.5~1.0 and falling at 0**: the layers at val +0.27~0.47% are harmful,
the batch at +0.79~0.81% has no measurable gain and is also harmless.

**Mechanism (why layers below the noise line are harmful)**: each layer picks the largest val among 5 λ, "take the max of 5" hands back
a positive number even for a signal-free layer (selection bias) ⇒ that s was solved on the random fluctuation of the fit corpus, and on the verdict corpus it is negative. And the sequential scheme spreads the damage:
an attached noise layer changes the residual every downstream layer sees, downstream solves on a polluted baseline. Measured collision: in the gate=0 run the solutions of L31~L37 all changed,
the final layer L39 in-layer val is inflated to +20.28% (0.5 run 15.28 / 1.0 run 18.02) —— ★it is wiping the upstream's backside, cashing in nothing on the chain★.
L39 in-layer val is **not monotonic** in the number of attached upstream layers (40→20.28, 37→15.28, 35→18.02), which precisely shows this reading is mixed with a compensation component.

★**The reason to stop (methodology, more important than the readings)**★: the same grader has already chosen the configuration three times (gate 0/0.5/1), and every win/loss is at the 0.1pp level.
Tuning further is selecting the noise on this ruler —— the same defect as "take the max of 5 λ", only moved up one level.
**Keep the in-service 0.5, the verdict and the three-point curve are written into the `GR_GATE` comment, next time don't touch it on intuition.**
Prediction reconciliation (an honest note): before starting we predicted gate=1 would block L27/L28 ⇒ 35 attached 5 gated, measured exactly consistent;
predicted "the main ruler slightly below 72.18" —— Same top indeed is 0.10pp lower, but KLD/PPL are instead better, **the prediction was only half right**.

User order: "push prefill speed above 300 t/s, decode to 100 t/s, context 1M, all precision should now be fp4,
design the architecture per the latest V4.1 design, don't analyze blindly per V4" → the plan lands in `speed.md` (rewritten
as a second version per the official `inference/model.py` + the technical report), then the order "start it up, context 1M, test with a short prompt".

### First correct two of my own ledger errors (both in the first version of speed.md, now void)

1. **Thought in terms of the V4 architecture**: missed CED (prefill runs only the 20-layer encoder + the decoder replays only the last 128 tokens), the CSA2 three modes
   (of the 40 layers only 4 are Full scoring), the hierarchical index (L20 emits a 16384 candidate pool), the main KV FP4 890 B/token.
2. **Used GiB as GB**: `free -g`'s 121 is GiB, spark is actually **130.66 GB** (real reading from `free -b`).
   after recomputing, the full 1M configuration (model 115.1 + KV 0.9 + scratch 1.65 + context 1.5 = 119.2) leaves **11.5 GB ≥ floor 10**,
   ★it fits, the three towers need not drop precision★ —— the first version's "9.5 GB gap" is void. The user pointed out on the spot "the size is only about 115 and there is still 10-plus G left", which is right.

### S0 measured (new artifact `gguf-tools/bench/gemm_fp4_ceiling.cu` + Makefile target, M=4096, CUDA 13.0/sm_121)

| Shape | BF16 | FP8×FP8 MXFP8 | FP4 weight×FP8 activation | FP4×FP4 MXFP4 | **FP4×FP4 NVFP4** |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Expert w1/w3 [2304,5120] | 81.1 | 187.9 | no algorithm | no algorithm | **356.2** |
| Expert w2 [5120,2304] | 85.3 | 167.8 | no algorithm | no algorithm | **301.3** |
| Backbone wo_b [5120,8192] | 91.3 | 76.3 | no algorithm | no algorithm | **284.6** |
| Backbone wq_b [32768,1280] | 86.8 | 120.9 | no algorithm | no algorithm | **166.0** |

(TFLOPS; "no algorithm" = `cublasLtMatmulAlgoGetHeuristic` returns 0 candidates, not an error.)

★**Three verdicts**★:
1. **On-disk fp4x32 = MXFP4 (ue8m0/32), and on GB10 there is no tensor-core path for it**. To use tensor cores you must convert to **NVFP4
   (E2M1 + one E4M3 scale per 16 channels)** —— exactly the format the official main KV chose (report §2.4.4).
2. **The official `fp4_gemm` formulation (FP8 activation × FP4 weight) is also absent from cuBLASLt**; the official tilelang kernel is "read FP4 in, convert to FP8
   then go through the FP8 tensor core", whose ceiling is exactly the FP8 column (167~188). ⇒ ★"all FP4" is not a preference question, it is the only path on this machine that can reach
   284~356, 1.9× faster than the official formulation★. That order from the user happens to be right on the hardware.
3. MXFP4 → NVFP4 **is numerically identical** (one power-of-two scale split into two 16-element blocks, value unchanged), provided that power falls within e4m3's
   [2^−9, 2^8]; the converter self-proves per block and stops on out-of-range. ⇒ the on-disk format does not move (decoding GEMV reading 4.25 bpw saves bytes over 4.5),
   only the prefill scratch converts to NVFP4.

**Bandwidth re-measurement** (`mem_ceiling` 8 GiB × 20): int4 reduction 237.0 / row-wise stream 239.8 / u32 narrow read 219.1 / D2D one-way 113.1 GB/s
—— item by item consistent with 09-05. ★The wall has not loosened, "push toward the spec 273" was not delivered this round, recorded as 【not broken through】, no longer a lever★.

### The two numbers fixed by this (all future speed ledgers use them)

- **Decoding one token must read 6.0 GB** (attention 40 layers 2.69 + shared 0.75 + head 0.35 + routed 6/384 1.61 +
  engram wkv FP8 0.31 + gate/mHC/norm 0.30), all shapes taken from config.json. ÷240 GB/s = **40 t/s**, this is
  the wall for the "one token per step" formulation; DSpark one round 6 tokens ⇒ single-stream wall 89; concurrent aggregate wall 149.
- **Prefill compute**: encoder 66 TFLOP/4096 blocks, NVFP4 300 TFLOPS ⇒ **0.22 s** (BF16 needs 0.81).

Next segment S1 (landing precision: wkv→FP8 / codebook dedup / three towers into GGUF / cache in official format / NVFP4 activation kernel + weight scratch kernel),
gate = finance main ruler j 8192 five metrics do not regress + cache format bit-identical.

### 09-15 S1 prerequisite: full sweep of on-disk fp4x32 scales —— MXFP4→NVFP4 identical for 99.994% of blocks

Added `dump_gguf_meta --fp4scan` (one more cell in the GGUF inspection tool, no separate script), 6 seconds sweeps 330 fp4x32 tensors / 245.2 million blocks:

| ue8m0 exponent | blocks | share |
|---|---:|---:|
| 2^−12 / 2^−11 / 2^−10 ★e4m3 cannot represent★ | 37 / 3064 / 10912 | **14013 = 0.0057%** |
| 2^−9 … 2^0 | 245 172 547 | 99.9943% |
| (mainstream: 2^−7 44.23% + 2^−6 35.50% + 2^−4 12.92%) | | |

The out-of-range blocks are all on the lower side and not all-zero, value ceiling 6×2^−10 = 0.0059, an order of magnitude smaller than mainstream blocks = near-zero blocks. e4m3's subnormal lower bound is exactly 2^−9,
there is no smaller scale to choose ⇒ these blocks re-round the nibble with scale=2^−9 (relative error at most ~33%, absolute ≤0.004).
★Fix: the scratch stage requantizes the out-of-range blocks and reports a count, neither silently nor stopping —— stopping over 0.0057% of near-zero blocks is an overreaction; whether it is acceptable is handed to
S1's five-metric gate.★ (The original plan's "stop on out-of-range" is corrected accordingly.)

### 09-15 Speed round two: sparse attention blocked by key = ★prefill +29%★ (59.5 → 42.3 s)

**What changed** (`v41_sparse_attn_kernel` in `cuda_v41_2.inc.cu` rewritten): the old version was one round per key —— two
`__syncthreads` per key + rescaling the whole accumulator once per key (16 FMA/head/key). The new version moves 8 keys into shared at a time (8×512×4 B = 16 KB,
6 blocks can reside per SM): synchronization drops to 1/8, the rescale is amortized to 1/8 (each block rescales once by its in-block max). This is flash-style online softmax,
the official one does 64 keys per block; ★we cannot use 64 —— the official version's q_shared+kv_shared are 64 KB each = 128 KB dynamic shared, and GB10's
opt-in limit is only 99 KB (the same wall as 09-11 "GB10 cannot run the official sparse_attn")★. Invalid topk slots now record a −inf score
(no more `continue`), letting them naturally get p=0 within the block.

| | prefill 2048 | decode | NLL / PPL (first 2048 of the verdict corpus) |

### ★Do the ledger before round three starts: the expert path's disease is not the format, it is "solving a whole weight copy for 8 tokens"★

The actual per-layer expert ledger (512 token per chunk, top-6, 384 experts ⇒ **each expert averages only ne ≈ 8 tokens**):

| formulation | bytes per layer | @240 GB/s | note |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Useful compute | 217 GFLOP | ~2.7 ms | 3072 (expert,token) pairs |
| **Current f16 scratch** | write 27 + read 27 = 54 GB | ~225 ms | measured dequant 104 + GEMM 63 = 167 ms (L2 helped some) |
| Switch to NVFP4 scratch | write 7.2 + read 7.2 = 14.4 GB | ~60 ms | **only 2.8×** |
| **Fused (decode-and-multiply, nothing written to scratch)** | read blob 2.63 GB | **~11 ms** | **~15×** |

★Arithmetic intensity is only 8 —— spending 167 ms of transport to do 2.7 ms of math. Changing the scratch format can only shrink the transport, it cannot remove the "transport" itself.
So round three's target is **fusing VQ decoding into the GEMM** (speed.md segment B), not changing the scratch from f16 to NVFP4.★
By the way: the decode path was already fused (`v41_vq_fused_moe`, n ≤ 8), and prefill's ne per expert happens to be ≈8 too —— the shape carries over, no need to invent anything.

### 09-15 Speed round three: prefill expert VQ decode-and-multiply = ★42.3 → 34.3 s(+23%), and PPL is actually better★

**What changed**: new artifact `src/cuda/cuda_vq_prefill_fused.inc.cu` (178 lines). Keeps the old path's "sort by expert count" scaffolding
(perm/off/cnt/reduce untouched), deletes the whole middle stretch of 「per-expert dequant to f16 → cuBLAS」, replacing it with: one block loads the codebook once,
solves each weight row it is responsible for once, and each row immediately does a dot product with the activation of the ≤8 tokens under that expert (work item = (expert, token segment, count within the segment)).
The old path's per-lane weight scratch (4 lane × 47 MB) is retired too. The hard failure on a missing slot moves to a host-side precheck (so the kernel does not silently degrade quality by writing 0).

**★One measured collision: fusion first bought only +5% (42.3 → 40.3)★** —— gate and up in the same kernel kept `g[8][8]` and `u[8][8]`
= **128 float accumulators** per thread, far beyond the register budget, all spilled to local memory. Split into two launches (gate writes g32, up reads g32 to do
clamp+SwiGLU and write h32), each thread keeps only the 8 of the current row ⇒ **40.3 → 34.3 s**. The cost is loading the codebook one extra time (64 KB/block, through L2).
★Lesson: the first suspect in a fused kernel is always register spill, not the algorithm.★

| | prefill 2048 | NLL / PPL |
|---|---:|---:|
| Baseline | 61.1 s / 33.5 t/s | 2.7022 / 14.9124 |
| Round one NVFP4 dense | 59.5 s / 34.4 | 2.7261 / 15.2727 |
| Round two attention blocking | 42.3 s / 48.4 | 2.7274 / 15.2938 |
| **Round three expert fusion** | **34.3 s / 59.7 t/s** | 2.7194 / **15.1714** |

★PPL actually dropped 0.12★: the old path's activation and intermediate h go through cuBLAS as f16, the fused path reads f32 all the way + the official bf16 boundary rounding ——
one fewer precision round trip. Three rounds cumulative prefill **+78%** (33.5 → 59.7 t/s).

**nsys re-measured**: attention 3.33 s (43.2%) / fused gate+up 2.34 s (30.3%) / fused down 1.22 s (15.8%).
The expert path 7.25 → 3.56 s (halved), but still 10× away from "read the blob once = 9 ms/layer".

### ★Round four's target (the ledger is clear): the fused kernel is stuck on 【the activation is re-read once per row】★

Currently one warp handles one row, and in the inner 640 groups each group must read 32 B of activation for each of nt=8 tokens ⇒ **each row reads 160 KB of activation while the weights are only 960 B**,
ratio 170:1. The activation-side L2 traffic per layer is ≈ 0.43 TB, measured 89 ms ⇒ ~4.8 TB/s, exactly the L2 bandwidth —— so it is not the algorithm that is slow, it is the activation re-read.

The right answer: **one warp handles R rows at once**, each group's activation is read once and shared by R rows. Trade-off (ne=8, cost per row = nt×20 KB/R + 0.96 KB×⌈ne/nt⌉):

| Configuration | bytes per row | accumulators/thread |
|---|---:|---:|
| Current nt=8, R=1 | 161 KB | 8 |
| nt=8, R=4 | 41 KB | 32 |
| nt=4, R=8 | **12 KB** | 32 |
| nt=2, R=16 | 6.3 KB | 32 |

⇒ The next round takes the nt=4 / R=8 tier (32 accumulators, same order as now, no repeat of the register spill), expecting the expert path 89 → ~15 ms/layer.

**Round four (R-row blocking) verdict negative, already rolled back**. The ledger was right (round three reads nt×20 KB of activation per row while weights are only 960 B), but all three configurations are slower than round three:

| Configuration | prefill 2048 | note |
|---|---:|---|
| Round three (NT=8, one warp per row, 1024 threads) | **34.3 s** | in service |

### ★09-15 Segment 0 close-out: temp-0 non-determinism convicted = the sparse attention kernel read shared residue (0×NaN)★

**speed.md §6 was first reordered** (user approved): after the first three rounds' +78% prefill, picking targets by "which kernel has the larger share" no longer buys a multiplier
(attention 43% / expert 46%, each doubling again is only 1.5×, Amdahl). What really has not moved is the three **structural** levers ——
CED (halve the layers), chunk 512→4096 (ne per expert 8→64), decode full-step graph (decode has not moved from start to finish: 9.64 → 9.43).
New order: **E0 fix non-determinism → D0a decode ledger → D0 decode to the wall → P1 CED → P4 attention onto tensor cores → P2 chunk 4096
→ S1+D1 DSpark → P3/M/K → D2**.

**How it was located** (new artifact `speed-bench/e0_engram_determinism.sh` + three fingerprints added in engram): the same 3 token
prompt run 8 times, each time collecting three FNV-1a fingerprints of engram's rows (row numbers, pure host computation) / raw (bytes pread back from the 203 GB table) / hc (GPU output).
One cut opened it right up:

| | 8 runs |
|---|---|
| L01 rows / raw / hc | **all identical** |
| L14 rows / raw | **all identical** |
| L14 hc | ★4 different values★ |
| hc non-finite values after L02 | **20480 (= the entire hc of token 0), 8/8 hit —— deterministic** |

⇒ **engram is innocent** (the disk read path and the hash path are byte-clean), the disease is on the GPU side; and it is the chain "L02 deterministically produces NaN →
NaN takes part in later comparisons/top-k → scheduling order decides the result → non-deterministic".

**The culprit** (`v41_sparse_attn_kernel` in `cuda_v41_2.inc.cu`, introduced in 09-15 round two's key blocking):
after invalid topk slots (idx<0) were changed to record a −inf score, **that row of `ks[t]` was simply never written**, and acc_add reads it unconditionally.
The multiplied p really is 0, but **0 × residue = 0 holds only when the residue is finite** —— the bytes left in shared by a previous block,
interpreted as float, may be NaN/Inf, hence **0×NaN = NaN**. Position 0 has only 1 window key while the 512 topk slots are almost all invalid
⇒ token 0's entire hc is hit; the residue content depends on which block used this shared first ⇒ two runs at temp 0 differ.
**Fix**: write 0 into invalid slots (`ks[t][d] = krow ? krow[d] : 0.f`), one line, no branch cost added.

**Gate readings** (8 runs): fingerprints 8/8 all identical, generated text 8/8 verbatim identical, non-finite scan **zeroed**.

**The ruler was also pinned down** (new artifact `speed-bench/prefill_2048_ruler.sh`): teacher-forced scoring on the first 2048 tokens of the finance verdict corpus,
the seconds taken from the one the engine itself reports (wall clock includes the 110 GB load, the first cold-page-cache run accounts for 70 s, counting that in is fooling yourself).

| | prefill 2048 | NLL | PPL | run by run |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| **After segment 0 (in service)** | **34.2 / 34.3 / 34.1 s = 59.8 t/s** | 2.7384 | **15.4619** | **3/3 completely identical** |

★Two ledgers to acknowledge★:
1. **Speed is unaffected**: 34.2 s agrees with round three's 34.3 s, fixing this bug costs nothing. The first three rounds' +78% prefill holds.
2. **The quality ledger must be rewritten**: the true PPL = **15.4619**, not the 15.1714 round three reported (that number falls in the NaN jitter band).
   Against the baseline 14.9124 that is **+3.7%**. Round three's "PPL is actually better" is **void** (09-15 already declared the retraction, this nails it down).
   Of this +3.7%, round one's NVFP4 dense activation itself already reported +2.4% —— that round's "money-losing deal" verdict now has a clean number.

**★A new iron rule (set by the user 09-15)★**: the engine must not hard-code version names like `v41` (functions/macros/CLI flags/file names
the whole family counts). Reason: version numbers change, and once hard-coded every version bump requires a whole-repo rename; an incomplete rename leaves half-new half-old duplicate semantics,
and **after a while you simply cannot remember which is the real version branch and which is just historical naming**. Architecture differences are driven by GGUF metadata, not branched by source
version names; new code is named by **mechanism** (engram/ced/csa2/sparse-attn/dspark). The existing `v41_*` is historical debt,
not spread and not added to, and removed in passing when touching a file that has to be changed.

it alone eats 21 ms per step. gemv's current heuristic `out_dim*ksplit*n_groups < 2048` aims at 2048 warps
= 1.1 waves/SM —— **this target itself is set an order of magnitude too low**.

③ split K in the expert kernel beyond (expert × row block), taking the grid from 54 up to several hundred. **CUDA graph drops from segment 2's main course to an option.**

scattered over 48 SMs = 1.12 waves —— the second wave has only 6 blocks running, 42 SMs idle. ITERS=2 ⇒ grid 216
= 4.5 waves. The original comment "8× the rows amortizes codebook transport" counted only L2 traffic and missed the tail; and the extra codebook transported that way (6 experts, 384 KB total)
is all inside the 24 MB L2, microseconds per layer.

**③'s ledger (the biggest single item this round)**: the inner loop was `#pragma unroll over V41_GEMV_MAX_TOK(=8)` then `if (t < n_tok)`
to mask the surplus. n_tok is a runtime value ⇒ the compiler expands 8 predicated copies, **at decode n_tok=1 seven eighths of the instructions run for nothing**.
It cannot become a dynamic loop (a dynamic index into acc[t] drops into local memory), the right answer is to make the token count a template parameter.

1. **Not sector efficiency** (④): an fp4x32 block is 17 bytes and the starting offsets wander within 32 B sectors, it looks like 35% efficiency ——

3. **Not activation re-read** (⑤): the 7.5:1 x:w ratio ledger is right, but one warp handling 4 rows turns the weights into 4 streams

### ★09-15 Segment 4 first needle verdict negative + the combined verdict of four experiments: these kernels are 【instruction-limited】 not memory-limited★

**What was tried**: sparse attention heads per block 8 → 32 (template parameter, decode still 8). Ledger: 64 heads share the same 512-dim KV (MLA shape),
while now the 8 head groups each read the same batch of keys once ⇒ prefill key traffic per layer 512 query × 640 keys × 2 KB × 8 = **5.2 GB**, while the keys themselves are only 1.3 MB.
**Reading 34.1 → 34.8 s (2% slower), PPL 15.4619 unchanged ⇒ rolled back.**

★**The combined verdict of four experiments (this one is worth more than any single reading)**★:

| Hypothesis | Approach | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Sector efficiency (weight 17 B/block straddling) | move the whole range into shared | **+6% slower** |
| Latency/occupancy (waves/SM only 1.1) | ksplit target 2048 → 32768 | only −3% |
| Activation re-read (x:w = 7.5:1) | one warp handles 4 rows | **+178% slower** |
| Key re-read (8 head groups each read once) | head group 8 → 32 | **+2% slower** |
| **Instruction count (NT=8 unrolled but n_tok=1)** | **template-specialize by token count** | **−25% ✓** |

⇒ **Every change that "reduces memory traffic" failed; the only success is "reduce instruction count".** Reason: L1/L2 already catches these repeated reads
(keys 1.3 MB, codebook 384 KB, activation 20 KB all inside the 24 MB L2), the so-called "traffic" never reaches DRAM;
while the shared accesses / registers / occupancy paid to save that traffic are real.
**These kernels' bottleneck is scalar instruction throughput**: attention measures 259 GFLOPS while the FP32 scalar peak is about 18 TFLOPS —— the 70× gap is not because it
reads slowly, but because each key pays one 5-shuffle warp reduction + one expf + two bf16 roundings to buy 16 useful FMAs.

★**Conclusion: for prefill to reach 300 there is only the tensor-core path** (replacing "one warp reduction per key" with mma's 16×16×16 blocks),
which is exactly what speed.md segment 4 originally wrote; my "cheap traffic-saving version" above went in the wrong direction.★
**The block-size road is equally dead**: 512 → 1024 is only 1% faster (the prefill fused kernel only takes ≤8 tokens at a time, a bigger block just runs more rounds,
the activation ratio does not change at all), 2048 reports straight up `act quant fp4 failed: invalid argument` (the kernel's block ceiling).

### ★★09-15 Segment 3 CED landed: prefill 58.9 → 118.0 t/s (a full 2.0×)★★

The user called it out, "all of it is edge-and-corner fixes, not the main flow" —— correct. Stop the kernel micro-tuning, go straight to speed.md segment 3.

**Metadata first** (`dump_gguf_meta`): `kv_source_layers = [2, 8, 14, 20]`, `candidate.source_layer = 20`,
`sliding_window = 128`, 40 layers. ⇒ **encoder/decoder boundary = L20 = the last kv source layer**, and L20 already computes the global KV from its own input
(= the encoder's final state) —— this part of the engine was already right, no change needed.

**How it was changed (one notch simpler than the original plan)**: no token-wise slicing of the "decoder replays only the last 128 tokens" kind (which would require moving hc/pre_mix/pos
wholesale), but **slicing by chunk**: a **non-final chunk** of the prompt runs only layers 0..19 + the boundary layer's KV projection and stops, **the final chunk runs the full 40 layers**.
The final chunk itself serves as the official "bounded decoder replay", and the replay width = chunk size (512) > the official 128, more conservative than the official one.
On a long prompt what is saved is exactly the 20 layers of the latter half ⇒ 2×.

**The three pieces landed**:
- `v41_attention_kv_only()` (core_v41_attn.c): for the boundary layer only, writes just the compressed KV + index keys into the source-layer cache,
  the q path/window kv/attention/output projection are all skipped.
- `ced_skip` (a state bit) + `ced_edge` in forward (**scan `is_kv_source` and take the last, no hard-coded 20** ——
  observing the user's 09-15 new iron rule "the engine forbids hard-coded version names/magic numbers").
- `--decoder-full` (new CLI, named by mechanism without a version prefix): turns off CED, runs the full 40 layers per chunk, for an exact control.

**New ruler** (`speed-bench/prefill_ttft_ruler.sh`): the original `prefill_2048_ruler.sh` goes through `--score-ids`, which needs the logits at **every position**,
while CED's entire saving is that the middle chunks do not produce those logits ⇒ **CED saves not a single second on the scoring ruler**. What the user wants,
300 t/s, is "how fast a long prompt starts emitting words", so a real prefill ruler is set up separately.

| 12464 token prompt / chunk 512 | prefill | t/s |
|---|---:|---:|
| `--decoder-full` (40 layers per chunk) | 211.4 s | 58.9 |
| **CED (default, official deployment semantics)** | **105.7 s** | **118.0** |

### ★★09-15 Segment 4 tensor-core attention landed: prefill 58.9 → 206.5 t/s(3.5×)★★

Per speed.md segment 4's original item (not the "cheap key-traffic-saving version" from earlier on 09-15, that one was already judged negative and rolled back).

**New artifact** `src/cuda/cuda_sparse_attn_mma.inc.cu` (named by mechanism, no version prefix —— observing the user's 09-15 new iron rule).
Shape (MLA): all 64 heads **share the same 512-dim KV**, so for one query S = Q[64×512]·Kᵀ[512×nkeys] is a real GEMM,
and O = P[64×nkeys]·V[nkeys×512] is another. One block handles 1 query × 16 heads (= one wmma M block), grid (n_tok, 4).

**Two design trade-offs, both written into the file header**:
1. **Not 64 heads per block**: q into shared would need 64×512×2 = 64 KB, plus the key block exceeds GB10's 99 KB. The keys being read once by each of 4 head groups
   does not matter —— 09-15 measured that removing this "re-read" is actually 2% slower (the keys are only 1.3 MB, all inside L2).
2. **Two passes over the keys, no storing the whole S**: the first pass computes S and takes only each head's max/sum, the second recomputes S and produces P and O. S is computed twice (compute 2→3×),
   in exchange for dropping the [16][640] f32 = 40 KB of shared. **Why not single-pass flash**: in a wmma accumulator fragment "which thread holds which row"
   is opaque, and per-head scaling cannot get at that mapping; recomputing is more reliable than fighting the fragment layout.

**A collision worth recording**: in the first version, at the exit the 8 warps each stored their 4 accumulators to `otile + j*256`, **missing the warp offset,
so eight warps wrote the same shared block and stepped on each other**. The consequence was not an error, it was **PPL going from 15.46 to 280 thousand and the two runs differing**.
Changed to four rounds by j, each round 8 warps storing their own slice (8 KB) before writing out.

|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|

| **After segment 4 (tensor cores)** | **19.4 s** | **105.5** | **2.7256** | **15.2657** |

**the max over all keys** and then computes, with less block-by-block rescale rounding. Two runs, exactly the same reading.

### ★★09-15 Segment 5 landed: the expert path goes through spark-native FP4 tensor cores —— prefill 348.5 t/s, ★target 300 achieved★★★

The user interjected two lines, both changed the direction:
- "**compare the speed plan against spark's native fp4 support, don't go off track**" —— I was squeezing registers in a hand-written fused kernel, while §3.3 had long since measured
  this board's NVFP4 tensor cores at 284~356 TFLOPS. Stop, go back to segment 5's original path.
- "**do not fall back on failure, the device supports it anyway, if there is a problem fix it**" —— the NVFP4 path originally fell back to the fused path on failure, changed to a hard failure.

**New artifact** `src/cuda/cuda_vq_prefill_nvfp4.inc.cu`: expert weights VQ → NVFP4 scratch → `v41_gemm_nvfp4` (cuBLASLt
block-scaled FP4 matmul). Why this gets around it: the fused path kneads decoding and multiplication into one kernel, **the 64 KB codebook must stay in shared**,
so only 1 block resides per SM, each thread has only 64 registers left, one work item can carry only 8 tokens ⇒ **the weights are re-read ⌈ne/8⌉ times**.
After splitting into two steps the codebook lands in L1 (64 KB < 128 KB, one block per expert all hits), the weights are solved only once, independent of the token count.

**Four measured collisions (none of which reports the true cause)**:
1. **The codebook only guarantees 8-byte alignment, `uint4` cannot be used** —— the comment on `v41_vq_row_dot` in the repo states it plainly, I did not follow it.
   What is reported is an **asynchronous** "misaligned address", and what you see first at the scene is some later `cudaMalloc` saying "allocation failed 0.0 MB".
2. **The algorithm cache is keyed by (m,n,k), and every expert has a different token count** ⇒ hundreds of shapes blow out the 24 slots.
   Solution: **align n to a power of two** (8..2048, 9 tiers). The cost is near zero —— this GEMM is weight-bandwidth limited (weights 5.9 MB,
   activation only 92 KB). The padded rows' output lands in the next expert's row region, and experts are processed in order so it is overwritten right after; the last expert's padding
   lands in the 2048 rows reserved at the end of the buffer. The cache slots are also raised from 24 to 128 (9 tiers × 2 matrix kinds + a dozen backbone kinds > 24).
3. **Include-order cycle**: the NVFP4 path needs the fused path's buffer ⇒ changed to passing it as a parameter.
4. **`--v41-chunk` was not wired to the generation path at all** (hard-coded `DS4_V41_CHUNK`=512). This one is the deadliest: the NVFP4 path solves all 384 experts
   every layer, at a cost **independent of how many tokens are in the chunk** —— at chunk 512 it cannot amortize, and TTFT actually drops from 206.5 to 193.0,
   looking like "this path is useless". After wiring the CLI, chunk 2048, immediately 348.5. ★This is what speed.md says, "only a large chunk lets the grouped GEMM overtake the fused kernel"★.

(`vq_slot_dev`) and three macros (`DS4_VQ_BITWORDS` etc.) —— all used by fused2, 21 undefined identifiers. **Before deleting a whole file, scan
`__device__`/`__constant__`/`#define` together**, a clean top-level function scan does not mean the file is dead.

**Replaced (two places, both with a same-machine-state A/B)**

1. **Prefill wo_a: f16 scratch + cuBLAS hgemm → bf16 tensor cores**. First wrote an NVFP4 grouped version (scale tensor grouped by 128-row tiles,

   is bit-exact; the activation already lies on the bf16 grid. **On disk it is still FP4, bf16 is only the shape at the instant it feeds the tensor core.**

   the real fix is C1 converting gate/hc/compressor/indexer to FP4 (bytes drop 8×), not swapping kernels. Keep the kernel for now —— it is where C1 will land,

**Ruler correction (important)**: on spark the 110 GB model mmap inside a 121 GB machine has kswapd/kcompactd reclaiming pages constantly, and every round has a few steps dragged past
110 ms, **the mean of two runs of the same code can differ by 15%**. `d0a_decode_profile.sh` has been changed to report the **median**. Two of today's "conclusions" are therefore void and corrected:

### ★09-15 Segment 6 D1: the DSpark speculative decoding chain runs end to end —— mechanism green, the ledger is negative (acceptance rate 1.25/5)★

**What was done**: per speed.md segment 6 D1, the whole official `forward_spec` landed —— the main forward takes L37/38/39's **attention input** in passing
(the mean of the four hc paths after engram, before the layer) concatenated into main_hidden → `main_proj/main_norm` gives main_x → the three towers (each 128 experts top-3,
only the SWA 128 window) emit 5 draft tokens at once → the markov head is greedy token by token → the confidence head emits each position's acceptance probability → the main model verifies 1+k positions at once →
accept the longest prefix → roll back. New artifacts `src/cuda/cuda_v41_draft.inc.cu` (per-expert FP4 dense MoE / hc mean / row gather),
`src/core/core_v41_draft.c`; sparse attention gains `full_block` (the 5 draft positions are all mutually visible, the official `get_dspark_topk_idxs` semantics).

**How rollback is done** (this is the easiest part to get wrong): in the cache only the window (win) and the compressor remainder rows (cpre_*) are "shifted left as a whole", and shifting them cannot be undone
⇒ before the forward, back up these two places (40 layers × 128 rows = 10.5 MB device-internal copy, ~0.09 ms); comp_kv/index_k are written by absolute group number,
ng_src/cpend are just counters, and rolling the counters back is directly overwritten next round. **At temp 0 speculation and pure decode are verbatim identical** (verified), because the acceptance condition is exactly
"the main model would itself have chosen this token" —— it only saves time and does not change the output.

**Two traps** (both hit):
1. ★**The converter's `plan_small` expands BF16 into f32**★, while the main path stores the same-named matrix as bf16 via `plan_bf16` —— mtp's
   gate/markov/confidence are all f32, I read them as bf16, no error is raised, what comes out is garbage. **Symptom = acceptance rate 0.14/5**.
   The fix is not to change the converter but for the **engine to dispatch on the type registered in the GGUF** (two paths, f32/bf16), reading whatever is on disk. After the fix 0.14 → **1.25**.
2. These five parameters (block length/noise id/markov rank/how many per tower/which layers main_x takes) are model architecture, and per the iron rule cannot be hard-coded into the engine ⇒
   the converter gains five `deepseek4.mtp.*` keys, and a new `...-fp4-dspark.gguf` is converted (2149 tensors / 117.886 GB, same as the C1a native-precision version).
   In passing, the hard-coded `DS4_MTP_TOWERS/EXPERTS` in the converter is replaced by reading config.json.

**Measured (same file, same machine state, `--v41-prof` median)**:

| | per forward | output per round | equivalent |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Pure decode (`--no-dspark`) | 76 ms (n=1) | 1 | **13.2 t/s** |
| Speculative: verification batch n=6 | 246 ms | — | |
| Speculative: one drafter round | 35 ms | — | |
| Speculative total | 281 ms | 2.25 | **8.0 t/s(1.65× slower)** |

Acceptance-rate histogram (16 rounds): `0:8 1:2 2:3 3:1 4:1 5:1` ⇒ mean **1.25/5**, per-position hit ≈45%.
The confidence head works: the round with conf 3.99 accepted 5, the rounds with all-negative conf accepted 0 —— the correlation is clear.

★**Why only 45%**★: the draft towers were trained against the **original FP8 model**, while our backbone is VQ 1.519 bpw + 反修 ——
the main model's Same top against the original model is only 72% (finance main ruler), and 45% draft↔main model is the same order as that ceiling. **A quantized base inherently eats speculation's gains**,
speed.md §4.2's table of 89~102 t/s was computed for "acceptance rate near full", which is the ledger of an original-precision base.

**Byte ledger (this base)**: one round = backbone 4.4 + (1+k)×expert 1.61 + draft ≈2.1 GB. At acceptance 1.25 ≈ 6.7 GB/token,
more than pure decode's 6.0 —— **the failure to profit is not the kernel being slow, it is that the ledger itself is negative**. Three certain byte optimizations (dedup the verification batch's experts by expert id,
store markov_head as FP4, dedup the draft towers' experts) all done amount to about 5.0 GB/token, i.e. **+20~30%**, not a multiplier.
