**★★Same prompt online `--dspark` vs pure decode (11:37): a real bug caught —— resting rounds' steps do not advance the window, the drafter loses the most recent context★★**

| | pure decode | `--dspark` (scheduler) |
|---|---:|---|
| decode 1399 token | 54.0 s = **25.90 t/s** | 59.2 s = **23.65 t/s**; 131 rounds, **the scheduler judged it a loss and rested 79 times** (×16 steps = 1264 steps resting); histogram 0:76 1:32 2:18 3:3 4:2 ⇒ **p1 = 55/131 = 0.42**; one round 78.3 ms producing 1.65 token |

Teacher-forced on the same text ① = 0.747, online only 0.42. The difference is in the code: in the online loop `v41_draft_step(…, confirmed)` only at **the step that emits a draft** advances
`mainh`'s last confirmed row into the three-tower window, while mainh only keeps the rows of the last forward —— during the scheduler's resting rounds (16 steps without emitting a draft) those positions' main_x
**can never enter the window**, and when draft emission resumes the window is missing the most recent 15 tokens of context (the window maps rows by position, the gap shifts the whole window) ⇒ the draft gets worse ⇒ the scheduler judges a loss again
⇒ rests again —— a vicious cycle, 79 times. Also: once `--dspark` is on, even resting steps go direct-dispatch (`!spec && graph_ready`), paying 5 ms of launch gap for nothing each step ⇒ slower than pure decode.

**Fix (already changed, compiled on Mac, spark waiting for the queue to drain before a synced rebuild)**: ① `mainh` becomes a ring pinned by absolute position (position p goes in slot p % 128; the `hc_mean` kernel takes
dst_pos0/cap/posd, the graph path slots by device position), the main state records `mainh_end` (latest row position) and `mainh_n` (number of consecutive valid rows ending at it; the forward settles by contiguity,
the CED-skipped blocks and speculation rollbacks each invalidate theirs); ② the drafter records `win_end`, and before every draft round it takes (win_end, pos_main] out of the ring by position (new kernel `ring_rows`)
and pushes them through main_proj to advance the window —— make up exactly what is missing, rebuild the whole window beyond 128, so resting rounds and graph steps never break the chain; the `confirmed` parameter and `mainh_rows` are deleted;
③ resting steps of speculation go through the decode graph (`draft_now` replaces `!spec`). Gate: pure decode 2K/12k byte-identical to baseline (hc_mean only changes slotting, the graph carries posd),
speculation same track, self-consistent; then rerun `--dspark` on the same finance prompt to see p1 and the number of resting rounds.

**Extraction-method verification (12:07, announcement 1533 pairs, the four candidate main_hidden computed by feeding the official three towers the teacher; new piece `v41_dspark_variants.sh` + teacher `--dump-mainh-variants`)**:

|---|---:|---:|
| layer input hc mean (official model.py's method) | **0.648** | **0.726** |
| layer input folded by pre_mix (hc_pre) | 0.629 | 0.712 |
| layer output mean | 0.589 | 0.685 |
| layer output folded | 0.588 | 0.668 |

⇒ The reference implementation's extraction method is the best of the four, the "wrong extraction method" suspicion is ruled out; the easiest tier being only 0.7 on the announcement is a property of the content (the drafter skips over when a human-written text deviates from the base's expectation),
not the implementation. The engine (quantized hidden state) 0.705 differs from the official FP 0.726 by only 2 points, confirming once again that quantization is worthless.

**The first-version fix's gate (compiled 12:13, gate all green 12:40: pure decode 2K/12k byte-identical to pre-fix + self-consistent, speculation self-consistent + same track) —— but on the same prompt online `--dspark`
ran not a single speculation round** (no DSpark summary line, output byte-identical to pure decode, 24.4 t/s). Diagnosis: material fetching (1 row per step) first-position agreement 0.63 is normal; pinning k=3 with prof
also zero rounds ⇒ `v41_draft_step` silently false online. Real cause: **the scratch area behind the three-tower window kept only block+1 = 6 rows**, and the first draft round after prefill has to push the
79 positions at the end of the prompt's main_kv into the window at once → `ds4_gpu_tensor_copy` goes out of bounds and fails silently. This is a **latent bug that predates the fix**: under the old register the first round always failed
(the window never had the prompt's context!), only later rounds advancing 1 row each could run; the new register makes up the whole span by position difference each round, so the entire path silently dies.
Fix: the scratch area keeps max(cap, SWA) rows; the three-steps-make-up-window failure becomes audible. ★Gate lesson★: "speculation == pure decode" is **vacuously true** when not a single round speculated, the gate must
also look at the DSpark summary line (rounds > 0), otherwise the entire speculation path is dead and the gate is still green (the guard has been added to `d1_kv_ring_gate.sh`).
The second-version gate (13:20) was caught by the guard immediately: 2K/12k speculation still zero rounds, audible error reported 64 times "main_proj/main_norm 128 rows failed" ⇒ a second layer of latent bugs:
`v41_fp8blk_gemv_g` returns 0 directly and silently for n_tok > 8 (the GEMV template's ceiling), the 128-row whole-window rebuild cannot get through (the 79-row finance prompt hits the scratch area first,
the 2K/12k prompts hit this one). Fix: above the ceiling loop in 8-row segments (read the weights a few more times, only on that one whole-window rebuild). The third version, after a synced rebuild, gate + online comparison rerun.
**Third version (13:30)**: speculation finally really ran —— 12k gate: 11 rounds/63 steps, self-consistent ✓ same track ✓, 29 graph steps fine; but **2K speculation and the online finance prompt both hit
"CUDA illegal memory access"** (2K: crashed after 14 graph steps, produced only 38 token; online: crashed after 30 rounds, before the crash **p1 = 26/30 = 0.87, mean acceptance 1.77/5,
158 token 28.73 t/s versus pure decode 26.2**). Both crashed cases had positions < 2048, 12k did not crash; the common factor is "speculation's direct-dispatch batch + rollback" running mixed with "resting rounds going through the graph". Suspicion:
the graph path's compressed source layers advance on a device-side counter (posg, the "append + pool when full" kernel), the direct-dispatch batch path on a host counter (cpend/ng_src) + memcpy, and rollback only changes the host counter ⇒
once the two sides misalign, the graph's append write goes out of bounds. **Not localized, filed separately**: the fourth version first changes speculation back to all direct-dispatch (`!spec` guards the graph, resting rounds pay ~5 ms more per step), F1 (ring + window make-up) unchanged;
localizing needs compute-sanitizer or a step-by-step bisect.

### ★★09-19 User order "the hit rate is that high yet the speed did not improve, there must be a bug, solve it": the first bug convicted + fixed —— speculation 26.85 → 27.93 t/s (pure decode 26.19)★★

**bug ① (convicted, fixed): the decode whole-step graph's baked-in scratch pointer, invalidated by the speculation verification batch growing the scratch ⇒ the third version's "resting rounds go through the graph" illegal memory access.**
Mechanism (determined by reading the code, not guessed): `v41_grow` (cuda_v41_1.inc.cu) does `cudaDeviceSynchronize + cudaFree + cudaMalloc` when scratch is insufficient; the kernel nodes in the graph have baked in
the pointer at the moment of capture —— attn local pieces (length by nseg×n_tok), hc mix segment sums (by n_tok), VQ's h/partial/x (by n_tok×K) all scale with batch length. The speculation verification batch goes direct-dispatch,
n at most 6 rows, as soon as a batch larger than at capture time arrives the pointer changes, and resting rounds issuing the graph again read a freed page. 12k not crashing was luck (that run was k=5 on the very first round, the scratch had already grown to the top before capture).
Fix (mechanism-level, not a fallback): backend scratch generation `ds4_gpu_v41_scratch_generation()` (+1 on every reallocation), core_decode_graph.c checks the generation before issuing the graph and recaptures
if it changed (tens of ms, scratch only grows never shrinks ⇒ at most a few times per session); `!spec` guarding the graph reverts to `!draft_now` (resting rounds go through the graph).
**Demonstration** (same finance prompt 1400 token, new piece `d1_kv_ring_gate.sh … online`): the log shows three times "scratch changed pointer (generation 51→54→63→72), graph invalidated, recaptured",
809 graph steps + 221 speculation rounds ran mixed all the way to the end, no crash; same track ✓ (first 6730 bytes same).
| | fix4 (resting rounds direct-dispatch) | v5 (resting rounds through graph) |
|---|---:|---:|
| speculation 1400 token | 52.1 s = 26.85 t/s | **50.1 s = 27.93 t/s** |
| pure decode graph | 26.25 (steady state 37.97 ms/step) | 26.19 (steady state 38.07) |
Scheduler decisions byte-identical (221 rounds / rest 54 / acceptance 1.67, temp 0 deterministic), all that was saved is 810 resting steps × 3 ms each. Speculation versus pure decode +2.3% → **+6.6%**.

**bug ② (measured, awaiting the jury's verdict): the scheduler settles by conf, yet conf is systematically low in the middle tier, and the conditional acceptance of positions 2/3 is as high as the first's.**
New diagnostic line `[dspark] pos k val acc conf×5` (one line per draft emitted under --emit-trace) aggregated (221 rounds, k≥1):

acceptance is 0.44~0.73 —— at current costs (direct-dispatch verifying 1 row 1.12 steps + 0.34 steps per row + draft 0.355 steps) k=1 needs s1 > 0.815 just to break even, but k=3 earns 10% already at s1 = 0.7.

   (ReviewCrew thinking register attribution → HindsightCrew non-thinking register editing ≤4 spots, **no human**; the "human-written why" recorded on 09-08 is a misremembering). 11/12 are
   overestimated_target; the 12 `why` fields name 12 different indicators (ADX>50 / ADX<25 / ADX≈40 / MACD death cross / MA50 / RSI / high turnover / volume-price divergence),
   the only cross-sample consistencies are "lower the target price" and "widen the stop to 1.5 ATR" (8/12). All that can transfer is the "more conservative" bias.
2. **The review's ruler and the target-price definition are inconsistent, the answer key is not reproducible**: CFO 4.2 defines the target price = T+1 **high**, yet the review computes the deviation by **close**. By the high:
   the original target price 12/12 above the next day's high (a real disease, none of them reachable); after correction 8/12 fall below the high, but those positions were picked by HindsightCrew **looking at the next day's high/low**
   (only copying the number is forbidden, looking is not) —— 002104's original 14.36 was only +1.3% away from the high 14.18, the corrected 13.51 is instead −4.7% off. A number that cannot be computed that day cannot be learned.

   which by the report's own "trade only at ≥3:1" should be re-judged as no trade, the answer key still says "trade". The high target price is demanded by the chain: the stock-picking crew's goal "capture the next day's limit-up", CFO 4.2
   "the benchmark must be the strategy data's predicted high", cap close×1.21, the persona "consider the limit-up restriction", 4.3's stop = entry×0.98 hard-coded. ③ (last-layer constant gain)

   deliberately passes it empty, `_fetch_lesson_pool` retrieving by symbol never catches anything —— the 09-03 report text itself says "no historical lesson data seen".

## 2026-09-19 night · The 100 GB recipe (Q4_K skeleton + 11-bit VQ experts): size accounting + evaluation ladder (plan, awaiting approval, no code touched)

User order: "quantize the V4.1 model skeleton in spark with q4, design it for a total size of around 100 GB, give the overall evaluation plan, no code".
Starting point = current `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-vq8x4096-fp4-mtpnative.gguf` **118.020 GB** (decimal, as actually read on spark), after startup
MemAvailable is down to only 6.4~6.7 GB (09-19 smoke test), the landing register the user set on 09-10 is 100 GB / leave 10 G for cache and context.

### Conclusion (first)

1. **The 100 GB money can only come from the routed experts**: in 118.02 the expert VQ takes 105.2 (89%), the skeleton only 4.17, and switching the skeleton to Q4_K is instead +0.25.
   dim8 VQ's index bitwidth has only three grid points 12/11/10 bit (= 1.5/1.375/1.25 bpw; dim must divide gcd(5120,2304)=256,
   only 8 and 16 are selectable, 16's codebook does not fit in shared), **12-bit and 100 GB are incompatible** (even dropping the three towers + dedup takes 108.8).
2. **Recipe A (recommended)**: routed dim8×nc2048 (11-bit, 1.387 bpw) + skeleton Q4_K (4.5 bpw) + the same VQ for the three-tower experts + codebook dedup (optional)
   = **102.4 GB** (103.4 without dedup). Hard ≤100 has only two routes: drop the three towers **99.8** (speculation's +8% gone) / experts 10-bit **93.4** (quality down one more tier).
3. **Skeleton Q4_K is ≈0 for quality**: measured 09-12 "skeleton FP4-ization" is worth only Σmin −0.007@wt2 512 (noise band), Q4_K's reconstruction error is half of E2M1's,
   but end-to-end it is inside the noise. What it really buys is: ① the prefill skeleton no longer goes through the NVFP4 activation-FP4 path (convicted 09-15, PPL +2.4%), ② decode bytes +0.22 GB/token
   (3.79 → 4.01), the skeleton kernel must be as efficient as the current fp4x32 GEMV (199 GB/s) to not lose speed.
4. ★**User order (appended 09-19 night): "quantize directly by the weights, not the corpus kind"**★ ⇒ zero corpus throughout quantization: the expert VQ's codebook is solved with Lloyd on the **weight vectors themselves**
   (`--vq-stride` is the sampling stride over weight rows, not a corpus), row gains come from the weights; the skeleton follows `quants.c`'s q4_K **reference path** (not p2's imatrix-weighted path);
   no `--act-from`, no activation column weights captured, no calibration of any kind. The corpus appears only on the **ruler** (teacher-forced scoring needs text), it enters no product.
   Hence ② 反修 (the gain table solved from the finance fit set) is a corpus-fitted sidecar, **not in this plan**: verdicts are naked ① against naked ①; whether to re-solve ② after the new ① is settled is a separate step.

### Size accounting (decimal GB, all-bytes register)

| component | parameters | current mtpnative | recipe A |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| routed experts | 543.582 B | VQ 8×4096 12-bit 1.519 bpw, codebook three copies **105.24** | VQ 8×2048 11-bit: index 93.43 + codebook 0.50 (dedup)/1.51 + row gain 0.30 = **94.23 / 95.24** |
| skeleton (attn five projections/shared/indexer wq_b/embed/head) | 7.842 B | fp4x32 4.25 bpw **4.17** | Q4_K 4.5 bpw (144 B/256) **4.41** |
| MTP three-tower experts (3×128) | 13.589 B | fp4x32 pass-through **7.22** | VQ 8×2048 **2.36** |
| three-tower dense (FP8/BF16, original precision since 09-17) | | 0.20 | 0.20 |
| norm/gate/hc/sink f32 + engram wkv f16 + constants + tokenizer | | 1.20 | 1.20 |
| **total** | | **118.02** | **102.4 (dedup) / 103.4** |
| variants | | | drop three towers **99.8**; experts 10-bit (85.49+4.41+2.34+1.20)= **93.4** |

Reconciliation: 12-bit index 543.582e9×12/64 = 101.92 + codebook 64 KB×15360 = 1.007 + row gain 19456 B×15360 = 0.299 = 103.23
(= the 09-12 quantizer's ledger 103.227 ✓); GGUF vqblob 98.01 GiB = 105.24 ⇒ the extra 2.01 = the codebook's two other copies ✓.
engram 203 GB is still a disk sidecar (O_DIRECT/io_uring row fetch), does not enter the file, does not take memory.

**Memory accounting**: current startup used 123.5 GB (free -b register, including the skeleton device-resident copy + scratch ≈ 5.5) ⇒ recipe A ≈ 107.9 used,
**MemAvailable 6.4 → ~22 GB**; under the user's 09-10 register 102.4 + 5.5 + 10 = 117.9 < the 120 safety line. Disk: quantization directory ~100 + GGUF ~103,
spark currently has 615 GB left, not a single old file deleted.

### Expected readings (every number carries its basis; these are the targets the evaluation ladder must check, not promises)

- **Quality**: the 09-11 bitwidth ladder (wt2 512, naked) three points 1.004/0.4450, 1.518/0.7462, 2.004/0.8480, the two segment slopes 0.586 and 0.209 Σmin/bpw
  (the curve is convex, below 1.5 is steeper than above). 11-bit Δbpw −0.131 ⇒ **Σmin −0.027 ~ −0.077, Same top −2.7 ~ −4.6 pp**;
  10-bit Δ −0.254 ⇒ −0.053 ~ −0.149 / −5.3 ~ −8.9 pp. Moved to the finance main ruler (current naked 0.6762/68.95%):
  **11-bit naked expected Σmin 0.60~0.65, Same top 64.3~66.2%**; 10-bit naked 0.53~0.62 / 60~63.6%. The ladder itself is also naked-line uncalibrated numbers, same register.
  Zero-size levers (never tuned, recorded 09-11): `--vq-iters 8→32`, `--vq-stride 8→4` (sampling 1/8→1/4), only cost quantization time, measured together in A1.
- **Decode**: bytes per token 6.00 → **6.08 GB** (skeleton 3.79→4.01, routed 1.61→1.47); current per-kernel gemv 19.1 / gateup 7.1 / down 3.8 / attn 2.0 ms
  ⇒ at equal skeleton-kernel efficiency +1.1 ms, expert kernels −0.14 GB about −0.9 ms ⇒ **12k 25.4 → ~25.3 t/s (flat)**. Codebook 64→32 KB (2 blocks can reside per SM,
  the R-row blocking and dedup kernels sentenced negative on 09-15/16 were both pinned by the 64 KB codebook)= unmeasured headroom, not counted into the expectation.
- **Prefill**: the dense skeleton GEMM takes 0.4% of prefill (09-15 nsys), Q4_K going dequant→bf16→cuBLAS does not affect speed; the skeleton no longer passes NVFP4 activation quantization
  ⇒ **prefill_2048 PPL expected ≤ 15.46** (current 15.4619), this is a clean recheck of the 09-15 +2.4% conviction.
- **Speculation**: the three-tower experts pressed from 4.25 bpw to 1.387, the drafter's agreement rates (current draft↔base 0.557 / base↔FP 0.720 / draft↔FP 0.514, finj 8190) will drop,
  by how much there is no precedent (09-17 tower FP4↔FP8 was worth only 1 point, but that was 4.25↔8 bpw); use `dspark_sim` to replay the online gain from the measured agreement rates, rather than trying it on the machine.

### Risks and items for the user to decide

1. **Register**: whether 102.4/103.4 counts as "around 100"; a hard ≤100 forces choosing drop-three-towers 99.8 or 10-bit 93.4.
2. Whether **codebook dedup** enters this round (format v3, −1.0 GB, the decode kernel's codebook fetch changed to once per expert).
3. **Skeleton kernel choice**: write a new f32-activation Q4_K GEMV (clean parity check, must be tuned to 199 GB/s) vs reuse V4's q8_K activation kernel (fast out of the box, but adds one activation quantization, violating [[engine_must_not_alter_model_output]]); the former is recommended.
4. **Speculation**: after the three towers' VQ the agreement rate has no precedent, stage E computes it with sim first before shipping; if speculation cannot beat pure decode it is 2.6 GB of dead weight.
5. **A1's ×4 extrapolation is a pessimistic upper bound** (shallow layers are the most sensitive), the true number is in stage D; but A1 is already enough to judge "whether to dispatch the full run".
6. **The bitwidth ladder is the wt2 512 naked-line numbers**, the finance main ruler's slope may differ, the expected band is deliberately written wide.

#### ① Extending the λ grid downward (the thing the user named): the basis is the current product's own ledger

The user's exact words: "the 反修 has an r-parameter problem, previously the parameters were picked upward from 1, 10, add 0.01, 0.1 and such downward to the range". Verified —— **the user is right, and it is more serious than expected**.
`gr-fin-40-fp4/manifest.txt`'s λ distribution over the 37 mounted layers:

| λ | 0.1 (old lower bound) | 1 | 10 | 100 | 1000 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| layers | **9** | 26 | 2 | **0** | **0** |

The 9 layers hitting the lower bound = L00~L05 + L13 + L19 + L39, **precisely the fattest batch** (L00's in-layer val +26.7%).
★Landing on the boundary = the grid is wrong on that side★: these layers' optimal λ is very likely below 0.1, the ridge pressed the correction down too small, and the old grid cannot measure this ——
it can only report "0.1 is best", it cannot report "we want it even smaller". The upper half is dead at the same time.
**The change (`v41_gr_run.inc.c`)**: `GR_LAMS` from `{0.1, 1, 10, 100, 1000}` to **`{0.001, 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 100}`** ——
extended two cells downward (same 10× ladder), cutting the never-selected 1000 (the fallback is carried by GR_GATE).
★Cost accounting★: the selection bias of "pick the max out of N" grows slightly as N goes from 5 to 6, and GR_GATE (0.5%)'s significance drops slightly with it; **the gate is not moved for this**
(that number was swept with the end-to-end ruler on 09-15). ★Next round's checkpoint★: after the run, look at the manifest, if another batch of layers hits the new lower bound 0.001, the grid must be extended further down.

### 2026-09-19 late night · The real cause and fix of the q4_K skeleton wiring's negative verdict: wo_b missed the dispatcher (conviction + fix + three verifications)

**Real cause (one line of code)**: `src/core/core_v41_attn.c`'s attention output projection second stage `attn_output_b` (wo_b) was still calling
`ds4_gpu_v41_matmul_fp4x32_tensor` directly, not going through the type-dispatched `v41_tproj` —— **the one spot missed** among the skeleton matrices
(q_a/q_b/kv/wo_a/shared's three/indexer q_b/embed/head were all changed). With a q4_K skeleton it reads q4_K's bytes with the fp4x32 decoder:
fp4x32's 17th byte per 32 elements is a ue8m0 exponent (2^(b−127)), and q4_K's f16 scale/6-bit packed bytes landing randomly at that spot are on the
2^100 order ⇒ attn_out overflows to inf/NaN ⇒ the whole hc after L00 is non-finite ⇒ routing logits NaN, argmax collapses to one expert ⇒ all BOS.
Last night's three `--v41-prof` symptoms (143360 non-finite / unique experts 1 / all BOS) match one by one.
**Why last night's static review missed it**: the suspicion was locked on "the three newly written q4_K kernels or the 11-bit VQ instance", and the review covered all the kernel internals (lane mapping/packing/
alignment/reduction), the culprit was at a call site outside the kernels —— an old line never touched. Lesson: **when changing format, first grep every call site that directly calls a format-specific kernel, then look at the kernels**.

**The fix (working tree, uncommitted)**:
- `core_v41_attn.c`: wo_b switched to `v41_tproj` (with a conviction comment).
- `core_v41_draft.c`: the draft tower's `main_proj` FP8/fp4x32 either-or changed to `v41_tproj` (the same class of hazard: with q4_K it likewise reads wrong silently).
- `core_v41_dcap.c` + new `ds4_gpu_v41_head_colnorm_q4k_tensor` (`cuda_v41_q4k.inc.cu` +36 lines, header/Metal stub synced):
  the dcap exit metric (the head's column sum of squares) dispatched by exit-head type —— the original kernel was fp4x32-specific, on a q4_K head it silently produces a whole column of fake metrics.
- `v41_engine_parity_spark.sh`: added `--gguf` to change the file under test. ★Fixed the watchdog along the way★: the old pkill pattern `ds4 -m gguf/v41[/]`
  never matches the absolute path `ds4 -m /home/…/gguf/v41/…` —— this watchdog never actually blocked anything, changed to `ds4 -m .*gguf/v41[/]`.
- Grepped the whole repo: there is no skeleton consumption point left in the engine that directly calls the three fp4x32 pieces (only those three lines inside `v41_tproj`/`v41_embed`/`v41_tproj_grouped` remain).

**Three verifications**:

## 2026-09-19 late night · Conviction and fix of the prefill's two FP4 re-quantizations (user order "fix the bug")

Seeing 69.89% the user asks "the size got smaller, why did quality drop so much, not even 70%". Broken apart: the big drop **is not the q4k recipe, it is the engine prefill**.

### The lesion: prefill presses activations to 4 bit, while the decode path never does that

| spot | before the change | what it did | who measured it on 09-15 |
|---|---|---|---|
| dense skeleton prefill `ds4_gpu_v41_matmul_fp4x32_tensor` | NVFP4 tensor core | weights identical, **activations f32 → E2M1 (1-bit mantissa)** | only the wo_a branch was measured (3.9% PPL regression, sentenced negative back to bf16), **the other branches were not measured** |
| expert prefill `vqp_fused_run` | unconditionally forwarding to `vqn_prefill_run` | one layer **three re-quantizations**: VQ weights f16→E2M1 / activations→E2M1 / swiglu exit h→E2M1 | the file header itself admits "the criterion is the five metrics", **that criterion was never run** |

Both are "compute state precision lowered for speed", when landed on 09-15 they did not pass the quality gate, and no one re-measured the current model with the same ruler —— the 09-13 three-ruler table's "current" scores were the old prefill path's, the service has been paying this ever since.

### The fix and the cut-by-cut readings (wt2 512, engine ↔ the Python student of **the same fp4 file** —— it measures "how far the engine is from its own quantization file")

| | Σmin | KLD | Same top | PPL | 512 token forward |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| before the change (skeleton + experts both NVFP4) | 0.8747 | 0.1430 | 87.11% | 3.8494 | 5.7s |
| only the skeleton back to bf16 GEMM | 0.9158 | 0.0789 | 91.80% | 3.5303 | 6.3s |
| **both fixed (current state)** | **0.9632** | **0.0184** | **96.88%** | **3.4369** | **5.5s** |
| 09-12 engine (never had these two to begin with) | 0.9626 | 0.0342 | 96.09% | 3.3137 | — |

★The two cuts together pull the engine back to its own file state, KLD even lower than 09-12★ (that 09-12 build had other implementation gaps). **And it did not get slower**:
5.7 → 5.5s. The 09-15 archived "fused path 398 ms/layer vs NVFP4 64 ms/layer" is the account under 4096 chunking (one expert spreads over 64 tokens ⇒ weights re-decoded 8 times),
whereas `--score-ids` goes **512 chunking** (one expert spreads over ~8 = NT exactly one pass) ⇒ that account does not hold on this ruler. ★The server-side 4096-chunking cost is unmeasured, see the outstanding item below★

### A pit I stepped into myself: the bf16 scratch raised the memory peak by 1 GB

After fixing the skeleton, the 118 GB model's verdict run **was killed by the watchdog at the 5th chunk** (available 7 GB < 8 GB), while the same command before the change passed.
Real cause: one bf16 element is 2 B, **3.8×** NVFP4's (nibble + scale ≈ 0.53 B); the exit head 129280×5120 flattened whole = **1.32 GB** (NVFP4 needs only 0.35 GB).
With the 118 GB model loaded MemAvailable's trough was already only 9~10 GB (the 12 GB floor during loading is the "before copying" judgment), this extra 1 GB presses the line.
★The symptom is deceptive★: it reports "watchdog stopped the machine", not any line of memory error; sampling once every 20 seconds ⇒ the same command sometimes passes sometimes not.
**The fix**: the weight scratch is chunked by output dimension, capped at `V41_BF16_STAGE_ELEMS` = 200 M elements (400 MB, the same order as the NVFP4 scratch it replaced),
the exit head is sent to cuBLAS in 4 segments (output column-major m=out_dim, one segment's rows = D pointer +r0, m becomes the segment length, the activations one copy untouched).
**Gate: the chunked and non-chunked outputs are byte-identical** (`cmp` passed), the peak is back to the avail 9 GB tier.
Also fixed `v41_judge.sh`'s `run_eng`: `--ctx` is given per NTOK (the default 32768 context buffer 2416 MiB → 865 MiB at 8192); the verdict feeds only NTOK tokens, a ctx larger than that is useless.

   Attribution first (D1 below), do not touch sampling first. It and the p5 tail (finance j's p5 is only 0.19) are two faces of the same thing: position breakdown ⇒ derailment during generation.

### Codebook re-solve: the math and the solution

- In the file, `Ŵ_m[r][c] = g_m[r] · C_m[idx_m[r][c/8]][c%8]`, m ∈ {w1, w3, w2}. **The indices and row gains stay fixed, only C_m is re-solved** ⇒ Ŵ_m is linear in C_m.
- The deployment-state x for the tokens under expert e is given by the incumbent hooks (the same capture as for gr).
  **w1/w3**: `min ‖(W_m^fp − Ŵ_m(C)) X_e‖²`, target = the factory FP weights multiplied by the same x (`v41_fp_moe.cu` already reads the factory file, it only needs to emit per-expert z1/z3 as well);
  after solving, recompute h with the new codebook; **w2**: input the new h, target = the factory expert's down output ye_fp (sequential inside the expert: the downstream is solved on the state the upstream has already been repaired to, the same reasoning as across layers).
- Ridge: `λ · (mean Gram diagonal) · ‖C − C0‖²`, **a single shared scale** (09-13 pitfall one: rarely-routed experts have little data, so the ridge must pull them back to the original codebook); λ grid {0.01, 0.1, 1, 10};
  fitting/val stratified by `<ids>.layout` window; experts with < 8 tokens under their name are not solved (they keep the original codebook). ★Thin data is the main risk★: 128 tokens per expert on average, X_e has rank ≤ 128,
  and the codebook has 3× more degrees of freedom than the gains, so cross-corpus degradation must be judged by the eight-domain/wt2 gatekeeper rulers, not on finance alone.
- Do not form the 16384² normal equations (1 GB/matrix × 15360 experts is infeasible): **conjugate gradient**, one iteration = GPU-decode Ŵ → cuBLAS `Ŵ X` → residual → `X Rᵀ` →
  scatter-add back into the codebook slots by index. All GPU, zero CPU reference path. After solving, round to f16 (lattice point 2^-10, three orders of magnitude smaller than fp4's 11%, no direct lattice solve needed).
- Then on the new codebook state **solve the stage-1 gains again** (the incumbent gr solver as-is, recapturing the material), one table reporting three numbers: gr / cb / cb+gr.
- Artifact `cb_Lnn.bin` = [n_expert][3][nc][dim] f16 (37.7 MB/layer; 40 layers is **1.5 GB on disk**, do not call it zero). Zero bytes at runtime: on load it is written into the device-side weight cache's
  codebook slots (the same mechanism as `ds4_gpu_v41_set_gr_override`, both the prefill fused kernel and the decode kernel read the codebook from the payload ⇒ judging and deployment are the same form).
  The deployment form is a choice of two, pending the user's decision: burn it into the GGUF (zero growth on disk, ① becomes "quantization + codebook 反修") / a differential fp4 sidecar (≈0.4 GB, deleting it is the rollback).
  ③'s `base.fnv` fingerprint must be computed together with the cb file (if ② changes version ③ must be re-solved; the incumbent hard gate is unchanged).

### The ladder (each stage carries its own gate; a broken threshold = stop and dig for the bug, do not sit and wait)

| **D1 looping attribution** | q4k's looping output `--dump-tokens` → ids → teacher anchor → teacher argmax at the looping positions | teacher anchor + `anchor_metrics --row-out` | if the teacher also picks "约/？" at the looping position ⇒ model nature (a deployment-side sampling matter); otherwise ⇒ quantization, stage 2 goes straight at it | zero new code |
| **D2 tail profiling** | finance j 8192 `--row-out`, bucketed by token class (digits / Chinese / punctuation / English) for Σmin and same-top | same as above | see which class the 30% disagreement concentrates in (a digits collapse = lost fact recall, same root as the looping) | zero new code |
| **Stage 0** | L0~L2 codebook re-solve (sequential) + the stage-1 gains on top | finance j 8192 | **cb+gr (3 layers) vs gr (3 layers): Same top ≥ +0.5 pp and Σmin ≥ +0.004** (09-13 stage 0's three-layer gains were +1.23 pp / +0.0095, ruler noise 0.1~0.3 pp) | solving one layer > 15 min, stop; val all negative = solver bug, check the capture self-check first |

**How to read the mechanism (not a bug: all three self-checks pass, and the fitting-corpus PPL and the judging-corpus reading point the same way)**:
1. ★The two routes inside a layer eat the same piece of meat★: L00's gr-only gets block-exit val +26.8% in one go; solve the codebook first (expert exit +23.2%) and then the gains, and only +3.4% is left for the gains to repair —
   the codebook repairs nothing more than the 5120 row gains do, it just eats the same error first. All three layers are like this (L01 19.4 vs 15.6+2.2, L02 14.7 vs 15.0+1.1).
2. ★Why 16384 unknowns did not eat more than the 5120 gains★: each expert has 128 tokens on average under its name, and the input x spans only ≤128 of the 5120 dimensions — of the weight error
   only the projection onto this subspace is identifiable, and that part is exactly the "amplitude" component the row gains (one scalar per row, 128 equations pinning one unknown) can already express;
   the codebook's extra degrees of freedom have no support in the data, and the ridge pulls them back to the original codebook (the λ chosen by val: 63% of experts pick 1 = ridge as strong as the data, 34% pick 0.1, only 2% pick 0.01;
   any looser λ makes val worse = overfitting). Another 17~33% of the experts do not even have 8 rows of fitting corpus (66/91/126 skipped), so the codebook never touched them.
3. So at this data volume of 8192 fitting token, everything the two 反修 stages can repair is the low-dimensional error of the "one amplitude scale per expert" kind; what remains is the index-level (which
   codeword each weight lands on) high-dimensional error, which can only be fixed by reassigning indices — that route has already been ruled out by the user's "never touch the quantized base".

**Only one variable is left to overturn this verdict: the number of fitting rows per expert** (the codebook's degrees of freedom need data to hold them up). The account must be reported clearly first:
- The fitting set `vqhalf_a.ids` is exactly 8192 rows (the whole file), the judging set and the quantization set are 8192 each. To get 4× the rows you would have to cut a longer fitting set out of the finance corpus (the corpus itself has 1.44M token, enough),
  which is a matter of touching the corpus slicing, and needs the user's nod.
- Memory: this run's watchdog low-water mark was **avail = 8 GB** (08:02, right on the line and not killed; the codebook route takes an extra dZs 0.9 GB + 2.4 GB of page cache per layer's blob + device scratch).
  The capture buffers grow linearly with token count (rye/hye/dye at 1 GB each @8192), so 16k needs ~4 GB more ⇒ first change the capture to bf16 / drop the hye copy, only then do you qualify to run 16k.
- Without taking that step, this is where it ends: the stage-2 code stays in the tree (the engine-side cb override mechanism and the verdict mode are both clean, use them directly when there is enough data in the future), not submitted for deployment.

## 2026-09-20 · The router-bias sidecar (router 反修) moves to V4.1 + ablation moves into the 反修 tool (proposal, pending approval, no code touched)

User: "the two schemes that worked before are router 反修 and engine ablation, but I do not want to change the engine; put the ablation inside 反修, analyze the problem, design the scheme."

### 1. What these two things are in the record (reconcile first, do not go on impressions)

1. **Router 反修 = V4's router-bias sidecar** (`ds4quant_run_p4.inc.c` 2026-07-28, one of the champion recipe's operations "α·Δb FIT", α=2.5):
   - Origin: an oracle probe (the 反修 forward forcing the anchor routing) proved that **all of 反修's byte loss lives in routing drift** (agree 77.6 → 82.9 = the anchor-routing ceiling).
   - FIT: while replaying the student's routing, accumulate per layer and per expert the **selection-score margin shortfall** between "the FP anchor's chosen set vs the student's chosen set" (missed += thr−v, extra −= v−thr,
     thr = the student's 6th selection score), mean + count (arm only at ≥8) → Δb[L][E].
   - APPLY: α·Δb is added only to the **selection score** (the bias side), the mixing weights are untouched — semantically isomorphic to the engine's exp_probs_b.
   - Effect: **teacher-forced metrics do not move, what it repairs is free-generation stability** (the real cause of R36's degenerate loop = the router FIT never having run in fixed-mode, memory
     `feedback_recipe_diff_before_engine_blame`: "when static metrics tie, check the dynamic-stability operations even more; router 反修 is exactly the cure for this").
2. **Engine ablation = oracle/permutation-type probes**: the V4 反修 tool carries its own 43-layer forward, and anchor routing / forcing FP layers / the T1-T2 decomposition were all done inside the tool; V4.1 反修 runs on the engine's own forward
   (v41_amp_run + hooks), so these probes turned into engine flags (09-13's `--zchain-scale β` probe 0 is one example). User order: **do not add ablation flags to the engine, ablation goes back into the 反修 tool**.

### 2. Why routing is now the one to do (it lines up with the "looping")

- The incumbent 反修 (stage-1 gains) repairs T1 = y_q(x_q, r_q) − y_fp(x_q, r_q): the weight quantization error under the same input and **the same routing**. It is powerless against "picked the wrong expert":
  the student picks number 200 while FP picked number 37, and the gain on number 200 cannot conjure number 37's output — the error from one flip is the magnitude of **an entire expert's contribution**, the largest single error quantum on a token.
- Flips are discrete and propagate forward along the residual stream: one flip in free generation changes the input of every token after it. This is exactly the class of disease the teacher-forced ruler cannot see and that shows up as "looping" in free generation
  (09-20 early morning: both tiers loop from the 40% mark on the finance prompt, unrelated to bit width). Corroborating evidence V4.1 already has: in the per-layer engine vs Python drift, "y is about 2~3× x at every layer (MoE routing flips amplify)" (09-12);
  on 09-08 a slight change of context swapped 1.3~1.7 experts per layer.
- A single global Δb[E] can only repair **systematic** misses/extras (an expert's selection score being pushed down or up across the board by upstream error); it cannot repair per-token random flips — so we first need to measure:
  how much of the total error the routing drift accounts for, and how much of that is the systematic part. That is the ablation's job, and it can all be done inside the 反修 tool, without moving one line of the engine.

### 3. Moving ablation into the 反修 tool: what it is done with (zero engine changes)

The 反修 tool already has: hook captures (x_q / y_q / sel_q / rw_q / per-expert ye_q, per layer), the FP block evaluator `v41_fp_moe_layer` (**the input x and the routing hsel/hrw are all parameters**,
so any combination can be fed in), and a GGUF reader (reads `blk.L.ffn_gate_inp.weight` bf16 and `exp_probs_b.bias`, recomputes the router scores inside the tool, the same form as the engine).
Only one thing is missing: **the FP chain state x_fp for each layer** (the input the teacher itself propagated to layer L). It is written to disk by the Python teacher `v41_teacher.py --dump-moe` (the flag already exists,
x_L%02d.bin / y_L%02d.bin, f32 [n][D], 168 MB per layer at 8192 token, 13.4 GB for 40 layers), and only runs once per corpus — Python serves only as a golden-fixture generator, all the numerics are in C/CUDA.
With x_fp, the tool can compute r_fp = router(x_fp) (the gate weights are native bf16, the same copy as the FP model ⇒ it is FP's true routing).

**The per-layer decomposition (one row per token, all in the MoE exit space)**:

| Term | Algorithm | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| E | y_q(x_q, r_q) − y_fp(x_fp, r_fp) | the deployment-state total error (y_fp(x_fp,r_fp) is exactly the y the teacher dumped) |
| T1 | y_q(x_q, r_q) − y_fp(x_q, r_q) | the weight quantization error, the piece stage 1/stage 2 repairs (the incumbent target) |
| **T_route** | y_fp(x_q, r_q) − y_fp(x_q, r_fp\|x_q) | the cost of **swapping only the chosen set** (weights recomputed on x_q by the engine's formula) = the **ceiling** of any router 反修 |
| T2 | y_fp(x_q, r_fp\|x_q) − y_fp(x_fp, r_fp) | the response to upstream input drift, this layer cannot repair it |
| routing agreement rate | r_q vs r_fp: top-6 intersection histogram (6/6…0/6), top-1 same, per-expert count difference N_q(e) − N_fp(e) and the mean margin shortfall | systematic vs random: if the count differences concentrate on a few experts and share a sign ⇒ the global Δb has a target |
| Δb's repairable share | solve Δb on the fitting rows with the V4 estimator, apply it to the student's selection score on the val rows, measure the agreement-rate increase and the T_route energy decrease | how much of T_route the global bias can eat |

This whole set = `v41_amp_run --ablate <teacher dump directory>`: one capture pass per layer (the same route as the incumbent capture) + two FP evaluations (r_q / r_fp) + recomputing the router scores inside the tool (self-check: agreement with the hook's sel
top-6 ≥ 99.9%, otherwise halt). Zero engine changes. The 10-minute version first runs L0~L4 + L19 + L30 + L39, judges "is there a target" and only then decides on all 40 layers.

### Part four: routing-bias sidecar (V4.1 version)

- **Artifact** `rb_Lnn.bin` = [n_expert] f32 Δb (1.5 KB/layer, 61 KB over 40 layers), in the same directory as gr_Lnn.bin; the quantized file does not move by a single byte.
- **Solution**: reuse the V4 estimator (mean margin shortfall, armed at count ≥ 8), pick the best α ∈ {0.5, 1, 2.5} by the **agreement rate on val rows** (the V4 champion 2.5 was a guess, this time let val choose);
  layer gate = do not attach when the top-6 agreement rate on val rows does not rise. Sequential: the Δb at layer k changes this layer's routing ⇒ the downstream input changes ⇒ the same multi-pass sampling as the gain.
- **The one point on the deployment side that has to move** (this is product loading, not an ablation; the same family as gr, a dozen lines): the engine loads rb_Lnn.bin from the `--zchain` directory, and the bias used by the routing kernel = on-disk exp_probs_b + Δb
  (either of two approaches: a device-side table of the same kind as the gain override, or applied onto the device copy of exp_probs_b). Without this point Δb cannot be deployed — the only zero-code alternative is to rewrite
  exp_probs_b inside the GGUF, which violates "the base is never touched", so it is not done. ★Pending the user's nod.★
- **Grader**: run the five metrics as usual, but the V4 experience is that teacher-forced does not move; the primary verdict must add a **free-generation grader**: the same finance 1400 token prompt + 12k readme prompt, temperature 0,
  count the repeated n-gram rate and the number of "约？"-style placeholder loops in the generated segment (the in-service `d1_kv_ring_gate.sh … online` already prints the text, add an awk count, do not build a new script), paired before and after attaching rb.
  Also do D1: feed the looping output to the teacher anchor and see whether the teacher also picks the same token at the looping position (to decide "model nature vs quantization").

### Part five: gate (each stage carries its own stop line)

| Stage | What to do | Pass gate | Stop line |

| F fixture | teacher `--dump-moe` fit split 8192 | all 40 layers' x/y files present, y_L from the same pass as the teacher anchor | 13.4 GB disk; self-consistent with y_fp(x_fp) (the evaluator recomputes on x_fp = the dumped y, relative difference < 1e-3) |
| Stage 0 ablation | `--ablate` 8 layers | get the two columns T_route/E and "fraction repairable by Δb" | ‖T_route‖²/‖E‖² < 5% on every layer ⇒ routing 反修 has no target, stop; if there is a target but Δb cannot take 10% of T_route on val ⇒ the flip is per-token random, a global bias cannot repair it, stop |

| Stage 2 verdict | five metrics + free-generation grader, attached/not attached as a pair | loop count drops and the five metrics do not regress past the noise (0.3 pp) | five metrics regress > 0.5 pp = Δb broke the teacher-forced routing, go back to α |

### ★09-20 09:55 the user asserts again "it must be a bug: at a fixed position it breaks on a number, other text does not break": bucketing by token class — numbers are the disaster zone of quantization, the engine is not sick★

Three sets of logits on the same verdict set (finance j 8192): FP teacher anchor / file-state Python student (reads the same q4k file, ★without going through the engine★, produced 09-19) / engine bare q4k (re-dumped today's binary on the prefill path, PPL 12.011).
`anchor_metrics --row-out` writes KL/Σmin/same per position, bucketed by "target token contains a digit (594 rows) / does not (7598) / input token contains a digit (594)" (decided by the tokenizer, a one-off Python classification):

| Student → reference | Whole span Σmin / KLD / same | Target has a digit | Target has none | Input has a digit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| engine bare → Python student (the same file) | 0.9667 / 0.0069 / 96.3% | 0.961 / 0.0096 / **95.6%** | 0.967 / 0.0067 / **96.3%** | 0.979 / 0.0032 / 98.3% |
| Python student → FP teacher (pure quantization loss, no engine) | 0.6247 / 0.914 / 64.4% | 0.566 / 1.007 / **51.5%** | 0.629 / 0.906 / **65.4%** | 0.753 / 0.488 / 80.3% |
| engine bare → FP teacher | 0.6279 / 0.907 / 64.6% | 0.569 / 0.999 / 52.5% | 0.633 / 0.899 / 65.6% | 0.755 / 0.482 / 80.0% |

- **At digit positions the engine is as close as the Python student that does not go through the engine** (95.6% vs 96.3%, KLD 0.0096 vs 0.0067): the engine has no "breaks on a number" disease.
- **Numbers are the disaster zone of quantization itself**: at positions where "a number should come out" the Python student that bypasses the engine has only 51.5% top-1, against 65.4% elsewhere; the engine's numbers are exactly the same (52.5 / 65.6).
  This is the true form of "what drops the ball where concrete data has to be given" — factual recall (which number) is the first capability quantization loses; experts at 1.39 bpw cannot remember numbers.
- **Long non-numeric text does not loop**: readme 2K prompt + gr, temperature 0, 1400 tokens generated, repeated-word 4-grams only 9.5%, coherent English throughout (verbatim: "...Inference engine + HTTP API, GGUF
  specially crafted, testing/validation with coding agents — this is a coherent end-to-end vision..."), decode 23.7 t/s.
  "Fixed position" is not a position, it is semantics: once the model reaches the sentence "I need to give specific data", it must emit a number it cannot remember, and temperature-0 greedy decoding locks onto the placeholder.
⇒ The engine is innocent (three independent pieces of evidence: the decode path == the prefill path noise floor; the engine == the Python student, digit positions included; long non-numeric generation does not loop). What needs curing is quantization's loss on numbers, or deployment-side sampling.

## 2026-09-20 midday · routing 反修 + gain 反修 [merged sequential] run from scratch (user order "merge routing 反修 and normal 反修 and start over, see how much can be pulled back on q4k")

### Why merge, and what the merge looks like (the approach first)

The morning's rb was **added after the fact**: first came 37 layers of gr (solved on bare routing), then one pass with it attached produced the statistics for 29 layers of Δb. The two were solved independently and neither had ever seen the other:
when gr was solved this layer's routing was still the old one; after Δb is attached some tokens at every layer switch experts, and those tokens' gains were "solved for other experts"; and the deployment state that Δb's statistics were taken on
had gr only as the previous generation's artifact, and no upstream layer's Δb had ever entered its input. Merged sequential strings the two into one chain; pass k:

1. Attach the rb + gr already written to disk for L0..L(k−1) (the same directory), and stop sampling at L(k) — the hook does two things in one pass: routing statistics (recompute 384 scores from the student x, FP routing recomputed from
   the teacher fixture x_fp) + gain sampling (x/y/sel/rw/per-expert ye). The same material, the same deployment state.
2. Solve this layer's Δb: the mean margin shortfall on fit rows (armed at count ≥ 8), with α∈{0.5,1,1.5,2.5} chosen by the val-row same-set rate, and **only a strict rise is written to disk** as rb_Lk.bin.
3. If it was written to disk ⇒ this layer's routing changed ⇒ **attach Δb and re-sample this layer** (the ye in the old material are experts chosen by the old routing, and solving the gain from them solves for a routing that will not be deployed), then solve the gain;
   if it was not written to disk ⇒ the first pass's material is the deployment state, so solve the gain directly. The gain's target does not change: y_fp(x_q, r_q) − y_q(x_q, r_q), only r_q now contains Δb.
4. The gr gate / λ grid / direct grid solve are all left alone (GR_LAMS {0.01..1000}, gate 0.5%).

## 2026-09-20 afternoon · 反修 plus a [bias term] (quantization bias correction; user order "quantization itself has an offset, there are papers supporting that debiasing algorithms work, try changing it and look at the five metrics")

### Approach (what was changed, first)

The mean of the quantization error ΔW·h is not zero: E[ΔW·h | expert e] = ΔW·E[h|e] is a **constant** per expert and per output channel, and the in-service gain (multiplicative) cannot repair a constant offset.
In the literature this is called bias correction (Nagel 2019 DFQ §4 / Finkelstein 2019 "Fighting Quantization Bias with Bias" / Banner 2019 ACIQ):
measure the mean difference of the output before and after quantization on calibration data, and add the bias back. The landing form (solved jointly with the gain inside a single solve, zero Python):

- **Solver** `v41_gr_solve.cu`: each (expert e, channel d) goes from a one-dimensional ridge least squares to a 2×2 joint solve (s−1, c), with the model
  `ŷ = ysh + c_sh + Σ_k ( s_e·rw·ye + rw·c_e )`; c_sh is a whole-layer common term (estimated jointly over all fit rows, weight 1), and c_e goes in and out with the routing weight.
  Ridge λ_c·wbar·c_e² (wbar = the fit pairs' rw² averaged over each expert, the same dimensionless convention as the gain's den_bar; the common term's data term 6144 is negligible against this ridge).
  Gauss-Seidel solves the common term first and then the experts in each round, and **c is likewise solved directly by grid to fp4x32** (anchor 0) and enters the residual on the spot. λ_c ≤ 0 = do not solve the bias, formula-for-formula identical to the old solver.
- **Grid**: λ (6) × λ_c∈{0, 0.1, 0.3, 1, 3, 10} = 36 cells, val decides; "0" must be in the grid (a layer where the bias hurts on held-out data must be able to fall back to pure gain).
- **Artifact** `eb_Lnn.bin` = `<i32 n_expert+1><i32 D><i32 43>` + c's fp4x32 codewords (last row the common term), 1.05 MB/layer, same directory as gr; before writing to disk
  the same decoder self-verifies it. The fingerprint (ds4_gr_fnv.h) is computed together with eb.
- **One engine load point**: `ds4_gpu_v41_set_eb_override` + `ds4_gpu_v41_eb_apply_tensor` (cuda_vq_prefill.inc.cu): after the shared expert output
  and before the MoE tail, `so += c_sh + Σ_k rw·c[sel_k]` — the decode path's single shot of the tail kernel and the prefill path's three shots both do the f32 addition after so and then round to bf16, and the one-shot small kernel is the same formula on both paths.
  `core_v41_amp.c` reads the eb file (unloading everything first each time), and everything is unloaded before a bare state is opened; the draft tower is not attached.
- **Verdict script** `v41_judge.sh engamp:…:<mode>` new modes `greb` (gain + bias) / `grrbeb` (routing + gain + bias merged sequential) / `grebs` `grebe` (split probes,
  see below) / `ebaudit:` (mechanism audit: `--verify-eb` comparison + single-layer per-row diagnostics). Tool flags `--eb [--eb-mode full|shared|expert]`, `--verify-eb <dir>`.

### Three-layer probe (the 10-minute method): wins 4 pp in-layer, regresses end to end

The same grader (finance verdict set j 8192, the same binary, teacher anchor PPL 6.9781), q4k base, solving only the first 3 layers:

| Deployment state | In-layer val L00/L01/L02 | Fit-set PPL | PPL (ratio) | Σmin (median/p5) | Mean KLD | Same top |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| gr-only 3 layers (the 09-20 codebook probe run) | +26.76 / +19.36 / +14.65 | 15.1528 | 11.3794 (1.631) | 0.6411 (0.6616/0.1444) | 0.85261 | **65.59%** |
| **gr + bias 3 layers** (λ_c picked 0.3 on all three layers) | **+31.04 / +23.30 / +18.81** | **15.3118** | 11.4823 (1.645) | 0.6405 (0.6597/0.1403) | 0.86201 | **65.26%** |
| Difference | +4.3 / +3.9 / +4.2 pp | **+1.0%** | +0.9% | −0.0006 (p5 −0.004) | +1.1% | **−0.33 pp** |

In-layer val rises 4 pp on every layer (the pure-gain column λ_c=0 reads bit-identically to the gr-only run, so the grid is not broken), four of the five metrics regress the same way, and **the fit set's own PPL also regresses 1%**
— the bias is solved on exactly these 8192 rows, and on the same rows the in-layer residual energy drops 11% while the exit PPL rises. It is not that the verdict set changed domain; it is that the in-layer L2 and the exit do not point the same way.
(At first I inferred from the λ_c grid that "3/4 of the in-layer gain comes from the common term" — wrong, the split probe below overturns it: λ_c=10 did not push down the popular experts' c_e, because the ridge scale is "averaged over each expert", and for a popular expert Σrw² ≫ wbar.)

### Mechanism audit (iron rule: when in-layer is good and end-to-end is bad, look for a bug first, do not just gate it)

1. **Engine application vs solver model, bit-for-bit comparison** (`ebaudit` ①: put only L00's eb file in the directory, two passes to L00, bare vs attached, and compare the shared output difference against c_sh+Σrw·c):
   relative RMS difference **2.289e-7**, largest absolute difference 2.5e-7 (predicted rms 0.0128), and y is still rebuilt bit-for-bit from ye/ysh 99.9968% ⇒ **the engine's kernel is correct**.
   (The first pass was wasted once: the soft link used a relative path, and the engine's fopen failure is treated only as "no such file", refusing to open the state — switched to an absolute path and wrote it into the script comment.)
2. **Per-row energy concentration** (`ebaudit` ②, L00 val 2048 rows): the top 1% of target energy (20 rows) accounts for only **6.2%**; over all of val, gain +26.76 / +bias +31.04,
   after removing the top 1% it is +26.08 / +30.38, and taking only the lower-energy half +15.49 / +19.23 ⇒ the in-layer gain is **broad-spectrum**, not a fake account driven by a few huge-value tokens.

### Split probe (common term only / per-expert term only, 3 layers each, the same grader)

| Deployment state, 3 layers | In-layer val L00/L01/L02 | Fit-set PPL | PPL | Σmin (median/p5) | Mean KLD | Same top |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| gr-only | +26.76 / +19.36 / +14.65 | 15.1528 | 11.3794 | 0.6411 (0.6616/0.1444) | 0.85261 | 65.59% |
| + common term + per-expert term (greb) | +31.04 / +23.30 / +18.81 | 15.3118 | 11.4823 | 0.6405 (0.6597/0.1403) | 0.86201 | 65.26% |
| + common term only (grebs, c_sh mean 0.004) | +27.39 / +20.09 / +15.22 | 15.3631 | 11.4827 | 0.6416 (0.6629/0.1431) | 0.86113 | 65.71% |
| + per-expert term only (grebe) | +31.01 / +23.26 / +18.74 | 15.2924 | 11.5599 | 0.6365 (0.6541/0.1363) | 0.86906 | 65.32% |

- **The in-layer gain is all in the per-expert term** (per-expert only +31.01 ≈ both terms +31.04; common term only just +0.6 pp), and the common term (one constant vector estimated from 6144 rows) has almost no in-layer value.
- **Both halves lose at the exit**: common term only PPL +0.9% / KLD +1.0% (Same top +0.12 is noise); per-expert term only PPL +1.6% / KLD +1.9% / Σmin −0.0046 / Same top −0.27 pp.

**Per-position paired difference (anchor_metrics --row-out, 8192 positions paired one to one, to rule out any "noise band" doubt)**:

| vs gr-only | ΔKLD mean ± standard error | t | ΔSame top | ΔKLD by gr-only Σmin quartile (hard → easy) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| greb (both terms) | +0.00940 ± 0.00112 | **8.4** | −0.33 pp | +0.0213 / +0.0116 / +0.0037 / +0.0010 |
| grebs (common term only) | +0.00853 ± 0.00112 | **7.6** | +0.12 pp | +0.0214 / +0.0100 / +0.0019 / +0.0009 |
| grebe (per-expert term only) | +0.01646 ± 0.00122 | **13.5** | −0.27 pp | +0.0343 / +0.0208 / +0.0091 / +0.0016 |

For all three variants the KLD degradation is significant at a dozen-plus standard errors, and **the loss is concentrated in the quarter of positions where the teacher is least certain** (bucket 0: the hard positions where gr-only has a mean KLD of 2.28,
ΔKLD +0.02~+0.03), while the easy positions (bucket 3, KLD 0.04) barely move; what Same top loses is the medium-difficulty positions (bucket 1 −1.0 pp).

### ★Verdict: the bias term (quantization bias correction) is ruled a loss on V4.1 反修 — a real in-layer win, a real exit loss, and the mechanism is located★

1. The paper's premise holds: the quantization error has a systematic per-expert per-channel offset, repairing it lowers the in-layer held-out residual magnitude by 4 pp (broad-spectrum, not huge-value rows), and the engine's application is bit-for-bit right.
2. The exit does not honor it, and it is not noise (t 7.6~13.5), not domain drift (the fit set's own PPL also regresses), not an engine bug (comparison 2e-7).
3. Where it loses is visible at a glance: **a mean-based additive correction is right for "typical tokens" and wrong for "hard tokens"** — the bias is the (expert-conditional) mean of the residual over fit rows, the easy positions
   (where the teacher's top-1 probability is saturated) change nothing at the exit however accurately they are solved, while the hard positions (where the hidden state is far from that expert's typical activation) are pushed in the wrong direction, and the exit grader (KLD/PPL) is dominated precisely by the hard positions.
   The gain does not have this disease: what it fixes is a proportion, and the quantization error on typical and atypical tokens stretches by the same proportion. This has the same mechanism as the 09-13 pin 0 verdict that killed "adding a linear function of x at the exit"
   (the in-layer L2 weights by energy and so eats the mean direction, while the exit has no first-order response to it), and the bias is the zeroth-order term of that family.
4. After the three-layer probe failed I did not launch the 40 layers, and the user ordered "the last round pushed it to 70%, how come you went backwards" — what was wanted was to add the bias on top of that 70.52% state (grrb 40 layers), run it fully and then judge, so it departed (next section).
5. The only lever not yet tried (no code touched, pending approval): weight the solve rows by exit sensitivity (teacher entropy / gr-only per-position KL as row weights, so that the hard positions dominate the solve of the bias and the gain); that is a change of the objective function,
   it affects the in-service gain solver's convention, and must be filed as its own item.

### ★All 40 layers run (grrbeb = routing + gain + bias merged-sequential, user order; departed 13:22, wrapped up 14:35, fit 70 min verdict 3 min)★

manifest `# 完成 挂40 闸0 路由30 偏置40`: all 40 layers were picked by val with bias (λ_c: 0.1×1 / 0.3×14 / 1×18 / 3×5 / 10×2), routed 30 layers (grrb 28).
**In-layer val is 1.5~3 times grrb on every layer** (L00 +31.04 vs +26.75, L12 +14.73 vs +5.77, L19 +19.06 vs +15.36, L38 +16.74 vs +7.92, L39 +34.55 vs +18.33; average +10.73%),
not one layer was gated — by the in-layer ruler this is the fattest run in history.

| Deployment state (q4k 103.4 GB, finance j 8192, same binary) | fit-data PPL | PPL (ratio) | Σmin (median/p5) | Mean KLD | Same top |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| grrb (in-service best, rb 28 + gr 39) | 12.8897 | 10.1600 (1.456) | 0.7039 (0.7590/0.2078) | 0.67317 | **70.52%** |
| **grrbeb (rb 30 + gr 40 + eb 40)** | **16.7744** | **14.4427 (2.070)** | 0.6465 (0.6924/**0.0985**) | **1.04177** | **63.89%** |

**All four metrics collapse, back to the bare base's level**: Same top −6.6 pp (only 0.7 above bare), PPL +42%, KLD +55%, p5 0.208 → 0.099; the fit data's own PPL climbs from 12.89 to 16.77
(worse than the 13.60 of gr-only 40 layers) — the bias was solved on exactly these 8192 rows, and while the held-out residual shrinks on every one of the 40 layers, the exit on the same rows collapses all the way down.
The three-layer probe's −0.33 pp amplifies to −6.6 pp at 40 layers: the per-layer additive correction **accumulates** along the chain, and each layer's share of "gets typical tokens right, hard tokens wrong" stacks 40 times down the residual stream.

**Final verdict**: the bias term (quantization-deviation correction) is **judged dead** on V4.1 q4k 反修, not deployed. The in-service best is still grrb (70.52%). The in-layer L2 ruler is completely blind to the "add a constant / add the mean" family of corrections

## 2026-09-20 afternoon · 110 GB recipe (q4_K skeleton + experts mixed 12/11 bit): size ledger + checklist (plan, pending approval, no code touched)

User order: "requantize the q4-version skeleton model by weight, design the total size as 110 GB, and now give the checklist for the plan".
Reading (same caliber as 09-19's "quantize directly by weight, not the corpus kind"): **zero corpus throughout**, the codebook Lloyd solution lives in the weights themselves, q4_K takes the `imatrix=NULL` reference path;
the corpus shows up only on the rulers. The skeleton is pinned to q4_K (the user named it); size caliber = GGUF on-disk decimal GB, 110 = a 110,000,000,000 byte upper bound.

### Conclusions (first)

1. **The extra money has only one place it can be spent: expert bit width**. dim8 VQ has just the two grid points 11/12 bit (1.375/1.5 bpw); 40 layers all 12-bit + q4_K + three-tower VQ = 113.4 GB does not fit,
   all 11-bit = 103.4 (ready-made on 09-19). **110 GB = 25 layers 12-bit + 15 layers 11-bit + three-tower 12-bit VQ = 109.92 GB**. One layer 11→12 bit is exactly +0.250 GB in GGUF
   (index 0.212 + three codebook copies 0.038), and the three towers' 384 experts have the same shape as one layer, so also +0.250.
2. **Which 15 layers drop to 11-bit is measured with the ruler, not guessed**: both products are on disk — the in-service directory (40 layers 12-bit) and the 100 GB directory (40 layers 11-bit); symlink together 5 directories (all-12-bit baseline + four 10-layer blocks each dropped to 11-bit)
   with zero quantization, run only the verdict, and get per-block sensitivity; the drop goes to the least sensitive block. The artifact tensors are still pure weight quantization; the corpus only serves as a ruler. Known prior: 09-13's "correction magnitude decreases with depth" (shallow layers most sensitive); if the ruler comes out flat, go shallow-first (L00~24 stay 12-bit).
3. **Three towers**: on 09-10 the user set "MTP must stay but must also be quantized", and 09-19 already VQ'd it; but the drafter kernel only accepts per-expert fp4x32 ⇒ the 100 GB tier's speculation goes unarmed (09-20 ruler: deployment caliber −17%).
   There is only one wiring point: the `st->draft` branch of `v41_moe` in `core_v41_forward.c` switches to `ds4_gpu_v41_routed_moe_tensor` (tower blob, NE=128, KU=mtp_used), and the main-trunk expert kernel is reused as is.
   **First get this path working on the ready-made 103.4 GB GGUF and measure the acceptance rate with the fixtures + dspark_sim**, then decide the three-tower tier: speculation > pure decode ⇒ three-tower VQ 12-bit (recipe A);
   otherwise the three towers stay FP4 (+4.83 GB, recipe B: only 6 layers can still go 12-bit, 109.76 GB).
4. The single-variable effect of the q4_K skeleton gets isolated along the way (baseline directory = 12-bit experts + q4_K common; its difference against the 09-19 in-service 0.6768 is exactly that), and the A2 leg that 09-19 did not run is booked here too.

| Version | Skeleton | Experts | Rest | Total GB | Byte wall ÷242 | Engineering ceiling (09-18 per-kernel bookkeeping, each kernel hugging its own wall) | 12k through the graph, measured |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|

★pgrep self-match trap★: `pgrep -af "<filename>"` will hit the very `zsh -c` that launched the query (its command line contains the same filename), so filter by process name first (ds4/v41_amp_run/v41_teacher.py) and only then grep the filename.
(The same trap, second time: if the shell command line that owns the watch loop `while pgrep -f "x[.]sh"` also writes the real name `x.sh` somewhere else, the loop never exits.)

### ★Roadblock: the 反修 fit does not fit in 121 GiB -- it is not that the model cannot fit, it is that "model + fitting workspace" cannot fit★

The engine log's own account: `CUDA registered 105.87 GiB model mapping` → `startup model cache prepared 105.87 GiB` → `[缓存对账] 装进设备 105.87 GiB / 走主机映射 0.00`
-- spark's cache limit = total memory − 8 GiB = 113 GiB (`cuda_model_cache_limit_bytes`), if 105.87 fits it is copied wholesale into the device; `--mem-budget-mb 40000` only governs the L1 gate/watchdog/
offload decision, it cannot reach this cache (which is why the VQ blob's "forced offload" on spark is an empty phrase). During the comparison run the avail valley was 10 GiB = 121 − 105.87 − runtime 5.
09-20 midday grrb on a 96.3 GiB model hit a valley of 8 GiB ⇒ the fitting workspace ≈ 16.7 GiB (FP teacher layer + 8192-token per-expert ye capture) ⇒ 105.87 + 16.7 = 122.6 > 121, the watchdog 8 GiB line will certainly halt.
The user asked "113 into 128 should fit anyway, what code are you changing": what fits is the weights (15 GiB spare in serving state), what does not fit is the fit. The corpus/layer count are the recipe and cannot be cut, there is nothing else on the machine to free ⇒ only the cache can give way.

**Fix (code change, no approval needed; not passing it = the deployment path unchanged word for word)**: new CLI `--weight-cache-mb N` (`ds4_gpu_set_model_cache_limit_mb`, contract goes into ds4_gpu_core.h, Metal empty stub;
the former env `DS4_CUDA_WEIGHT_CACHE_LIMIT_GB` was deleted during the 08-22 env cleanup, this is it coming back in CLI form). Once set, three things on the CUDA side:
①`cuda_model_cache_limit_bytes` takes min(platform default, N) ②`ds4_gpu_set_model_map` no longer cudaHostRegister's the whole mapping (otherwise the segments that do not fit silently go UVA -- the 09-12 last-page dirty read /
09-15 kswapd long tail were both on that path; and the per-layer streaming path registering a sub-segment on an already-registered whole mapping reports AlreadyRegistered) ③`ds4_gpu_v41_routed_moe_tensor` is changed to "cache hit (new `cuda_model_range_cached_ptr`)
first → only if the whole mapping is registered go the old way → if neither, go the per-layer streaming path written on 09-12 but unreachable until now"; the streaming path's registration is changed to only unregister/register when switching layers (8192 chunked by 512, one layer gets called 16 times, each registering 2.6 GB
the page tables alone are seconds), no longer madvise(DONTNEED) (after unregistering it is just ordinary page cache, the kernel reclaims under pressure). v41_amp_run gains a parameter of the same name; v41_judge.sh's three engine invocations uniformly use `--weight-cache-mb 88000`
(85.9 GiB: skeleton 4.4 + 33 layers; account = 121 − 16.7 workspace − 8 watchdog − 2.5 pinning one layer − margin).
**Verification**: Mac `make ds4` + linecount + **`make test` all green**; spark rebuild; same GGUF same 512 token rerun with the cap: `装进设备 85.83 / 走主机映射 20.04` (in reality per-layer streaming),
avail valley 10 → **30 GiB**, PPL 3.4652 same, **logits file sha256 byte-identical** (b0217550…) -- the bytes computed by the streaming path and the cache path differ not at all; 512 token 5.3 → 8.6 s.
★core's `[缓存对账]` label "走主机映射" is a misnomer under the cap mode (those 20 GiB are per-layer streaming), the wording is pending a change.★

## 2026-09-20 night · user ruling: the q4k skeleton deployment pair = pure-gain 反修 (gr-only), no routing 反修; and answering "why do the routing 反修 five metrics improve but the free generation get worse"

The user's exact words: "Then the q4 skeleton version of the current model, no routing 反修, only gain 反修, think about why the result got worse when the routing 反修 metrics clearly got better".

### Answer (conclusion first): the metrics and the result are not contradictory, the two graders do not measure the same thing, and routing bias happens to be exactly the kind of correction that "helps the first thing and harms the second"

1. **The grader's level -- the five metrics are inherently blind to repetition.** The five metrics are teacher-forced: each step is fed the FP correct prefix, only one step is tested, averaged over 8192 positions. The vast majority of positions are "writing along",
   the real branch points (what to write after "让我仔细思考。") number only a few dozen, weightless in the average. Repetition is a closed loop: the model is fed its own written prefix, one branch point flips wrong, and the input of every subsequent step changes;
   under temperature 0, as soon as it enters the same local context twice it can never get out. So "+0.9 pp same-top" and "infinite loop from 1500 characters" can both be true at once. When the case was opened on 09-20 morning this presupposition was written down
   ("a disease that the teacher-forced grader cannot see and that turns into looping in free generation"), only the presupposition then was "fixing the routing can cure the looping", and the measurement came out the opposite.
2. **rb's level -- why it pushes precisely toward the bad side.**
   - Δb is one constant vector per layer, not a per-token correction. The 09-20 morning account: deep-layer same-set rate 2~20%, the misalignment random per token, "picks that the per-expert count difference can explain" account for only 3~22%,
     Δb raises the same-set rate by only 0~3 pp ⇒ only a small part of Δb fixes systematic misalignment, the bulk is the domain prior of "which experts FP prefers on the financial corpus". On a same-domain teacher-forced grader it nets a gain,
     outside that distribution (repeated text looks like no report; wt2 is English) it is pure perturbation. **Evidence: the 09-20 night wt2 gate, q4k-12+grrb loses to fp4+gr on three items (PPL +3.5% / KLD +6.9% / same-top −0.39 pp),
     while the q4k-12 bare base is no worse than fp4 bare on wt2 (Σmin 0.7465 vs 0.7391, same-top level) -- the base did not regress, attaching grrb regresses = the domain-tax signature.**
   - In this architecture bias's semantics is a load-balancing knob (slowly tuned at training with step 0.001, experts and downstream layers co-adapt under that usage statistic), not a quality parameter. Adding Δb after the fact = changing the expert usage statistic while the downstream stays put;
     under teacher-forced each step is pulled back on track by the FP prefix so it does not show, under free generation no one pulls.
   - Repetition is an attractor, escaping relies on some step's argmax flipping. The three tiers order grrb infinite loop > bare (wobbles then escapes) > gr-only (no wobble): the gains calibrate each expert's output amplitude back, the content signal is stronger, helping the escape;
     rb compresses the choice toward a fixed subset, more concentrated and more certain, fewer chances to flip. Two generations same direction (q4k-11: gr 92 → gr+rb 130; q4k-12: gr-only 0 → grrb infinite loop).
3. **The explanation that cannot be ruled out and should be checked first: the FP teacher itself also repeats on this prefix.** The five metrics reward "looks like the teacher", not "does not repeat"; if the teacher also copies earlier text after "让我仔细思考。", rb makes the student more like the teacher
   = likes repeating more, "good metrics" and "bad result" are the same thing. ⇒ D1: feed grrb's 1478 tokens (79 prompt + 1399 generated) to the teacher anchor, split by repetition period, and look at the teacher's argmax hit rate in pass 2/3.

**The grader's lesson**: 反修's gate has only ever been the teacher-forced grader, the free-generation grader was never in the gate ⇒ gr-only this time passes three gates (five metrics / wt2 gate / looping grader).

   - **The grader's geometry**: Same top gap ∝ √KLD (bare KLD 0.685 gap 30.25, grrb 0.545 gap 27.03: gap ratio 0.894 vs √KLD ratio 0.893, they match). 80 = gap 20 ⇒ requires **KLD ≈ 0.30**,
     i.e. cut another 46% from gr-only's 0.554, 56% from bare's 0.685. The bit-width ladder prices this quantity: 12→11 bit KLD +33% (0.688 → 0.914, −0.132 bpw); the wt2 ladder 1.517 → 2.004 bpw KLD 0.828 → 0.358 (−57%).
     ⇒ **80 is exactly the level of "expert 2.0 bpw bare tier"**; the equal-size levers must do the work of ~0.4 bpw of bit width, and the only precedent (column weights) is worth just −2.8% KLD.

     | Lever | Estimate | Basis |

### Calibration statistics (one engine pass, `v41_amp_run --dump-calib DIR`)

- The hook already exists: `ds4_engine_v41_set_moe_hook` callbacks per layer (x[n][D], sel[n][6], rw[n][6]); `set_moe_hook_layer(-1)` = 40 layers in one pass, a callback returning 0 does not halt. The current amp_run hook recognizes only one layer and stops once collected, the new mode = all layers, does not halt, writes to disk.
- Written to disk per layer: x rows bf16 [8192][5120] = 84 MB + sel/rw; 40 layers 3.4 GB. Derived from it: layer E[x²] (rw-weighted, 5120 numbers); per-expert E[h_e²] (the quantizer computes h = silu(W1 x)⊙(W3 x) on the spot with the factory fp4 w1/w3, 2304 numbers, experts with < 8 rows under their name fall back to the layer mean);
  per-expert Gram X_eᵀ diag(rw) X_e (for level 2). Self-check: 40 layers' top12 channel energy share (the 08-24 huge-value channel prior: deep layers ~10%) + the per-layer distribution of row counts under a name (cold expert count).
- The fit portion a is untouched (left for gr), the judgment portion j does not enter any product. Calibration corpus = the q portion 8192, not extended (the algorithm-wins iron rule); level 2 wanting more rows (q+a = 16384, ~256 per expert) needs the user's nod.

### Quantizer changes (`v41_quantize.c` / `v41_vq.cu`, one copy of the code)

- Level 1: `v41_vq_expert_encode_gpu` gains a colw two-way entry (x column weights 5120 for w1/w3, h column weights 2304 for w2 -- the current "w2 eats h with equal weighting" is a debt recorded in a code comment); training also eats column weights:
  `gather_stride_kernel` carries the original vector index when sampling to compute the column phase (the only reason "training uses equal weighting" today is that this one line lost the phase). Weighted Lloyd = weighted assign + weighted centroid.
- Level 2: after the codebook and row gains are fixed by level 1, per-expert GPTVQ-style error feedback: H = X_eᵀdiag(rw)X_e/Σrw + β·H_layer + δ·mean(diag)·I (β ∈ {0.1, 1} chosen between two by the val window, δ = 0.01);
  Cholesky(H⁻¹) upper triangular, 8 columns per block left to right: within a block, pick the codeword weighted by the H block, the error is updated per GPTQ and passed to the columns on the right (128-column lazy-update GEMM). w1/w3 share H (same x), w2 uses h's Gram. All GPU (cusolver + cuBLAS), no CPU path.
- Skeleton: shared experts q4_K go through `ds4q_quantize_chunk(..., imatrix=E[x²])` (x already available, free); the attention-projection side imatrix needs a new hook, not done yet (≤ 0.2 pp, a separate item).
- The recipe string/recipe KV records the calibration source and level (`cal=vqfin41_q8192 lv=1|2`); the directory recipe.txt records the calibration file sha.

### Verdict

1. **"90%" is not the same grader.** The token-level top-1 agreement rate in the public data: 1.78 bpw 61.6%, 2.2 bpw 76.9%, **only 4.83 bpw reaches 94.2%** ⇒ Same top 90% = Q3~Q4 tier (3~5 bpw), no 1.5 bpw post-quantization has ever reached it.
   Others' "90%" is either a task-score retention rate (MMLU/Aider), or 2.0 bpw + end-to-end fine-tuning (the QTIP/PV-tuning family, which the iron rule of zero training closes off), or our own grader's "benchmark ≥0.90" target line.
   On the financial grader even the same model with a different chunking is only 94.3% agreement ⇒ this grader's ceiling ≈ 94, and 73 must be read against 94.
2. **Same grader same tier, we are in the same tier as the community's best 1.6~1.75 bpw**: wt2 mean KLD 0.73 falls between Unsloth IQ1_M 0.80 and IQ2_XXS 0.52; Same top 78.9% is above Mistral-7B IQ1_S's 61.6% (the model is 80 times bigger, not comparable, it only indicates the order of magnitude).
   **The real gap**: against ubergarm R1 IQ1_S_R4's NLL difference 0.61 vs 0.42 nats, we trail it by ~30%.
3. The gap is in four things, three are in the plan, one has not been tried:
   - Calibration: theirs imatrix 400k~1.5M token, ours incumbent 0 (plan 8192); imatrix needs only diagonal statistics, layer-level E[x²] 8192 is enough, per-expert is not -- it is in plan level 1.
   - down (w2) protection: their down is one tier above gate/up (1.75 vs 1.5), our w2 is the worst treated in the whole chain (h equal weighting) -- it is in plan level 1.
   - Shallow layers/attention/shared 4-bit: attention and shared are already q4_K for us; "first 3 layers 4-bit" for R1 is dense layers costing almost nothing, V4.1's 40 layers are all MoE, raising 3 layers of experts to fp4 costs +13.9 GB -- not transferable.
   - **Block scale granularity**: IQ1_S = 11-bit index/8 weights + one scale per 16~32 weights (1.5625); we have 12-bit index + **one gain per row** (5120 wide), the in-row dynamic range all pushed onto the codebook. An equal-rate recipe like "11-bit + fine scale" has never been tried, it is not in this plan (it needs kernel changes), a separate item.
4. What we got right: the median KLD 0.047 shows most positions are already good, the gap is in the tail (p95 4.2, financial p5 Σmin 0.25); the tail is exactly what imatrix-style outlier protection + w2 column weights cure (the V4-era official imatrix q2's KLD −10% against equal weighting is this mechanism).

The user followed up "the current plan vs ternary quantization": ternary (the TQ1_0 family, weights −1/0/+1 + one f16 scale per 256 weights) saves at most 1.6875 bpw, a single routed expert 543.6 B already 114.7 GB, breaking the 113 cap first;
at the same byte count the quality also loses (the optimal 3-level relative error for Gaussian-shaped weights ≈0.19σ², our 8-dimensional Lloyd codebook measured cos 0.9106 = 0.171σ² and with fewer bits); the codebook is fixed dead, the financial calibration has no anchor point.
Ternary's only advantages are speed and simplicity (multiplication becomes addition/subtraction, does not occupy the 64 KB codebook shared), and it needs BitNet-style weights trained ternary from scratch to have quality -- DeepSeek has none, iron rule zero training. **Not doing it**.
