## 2026-09-21 · dynamically allocating layer/expert size by weight (equal size 113.68 GB): plan and account (plan, awaiting approval, no code touched)

User order: "the current best result = q4 skeleton + 反修, fidelity 73%; but the output still shows '？', the main problem is that the bare-state 70% base fidelity is low;
can you dynamically design each layer's size and the different experts' sizes by weight, total size still 113 GB; give the plan first, do not write code".
History revisited: on 08-08 the north star rejected "dynamic layers/hot-cold experts allocating resources by calibration-domain data" (domain bias); in the V4 era the cold tier using TQ1_0 was only a size-saving measure;
the 09-20 mixed-bit-width probe measured only the b0 block (shallow 10 layers dropped to 11-bit); the 09-21 early-morning financial column weights (level 1) hit the domain-tax wall. Allocating "by weight" does not violate the 08-08 item, but the account is below.

### Conclusion (first)

1. **It can be done, the format already half-supports it**: the GGUF's DQVL blob has each matrix payload carrying dim/nc (the kernel infers the bit width from nc), and the directory format's codebook is one per expert anyway.
   The quantizer only lacks a "per-expert nc table"; the engine only lacks "block-level dispatch of mixed bit widths within a layer" and "13-bit codebooks (nc 8192 = 128 KB, over GB10's 99 KB shared limit) going the global route" (the kernel's `cb_shared=0` branch already exists).
2. ★**But the premise that "the 70% bare state is caused by uneven allocation" does not hold, and the ceiling of pure equal-size reallocation ≈ +1 pp**★, all three pieces of evidence are measured:
   - **The bit-width curve is concave**: 12→11 bit all-drop = Same top −5.3 pp (09-20 file-state 69.86 → 64.40, saving 10.25 GB) ⇒ **−0.52 pp/GB**;
     upward, converted by the wt2 ladder 1.518 → 2.004 bpw (+10.15 pp / +0.486 bpw), 12→13 bit all-rise ≈ +2.6~3.7 pp / +10 GB ⇒ **+0.30 pp/GB**.
     dropping bits loses 1.7 times more than raising bits gains ⇒ "A drops bits to give B a raise" only breaks even when B is worth **≥ 1.7 times** more per GB than A.
   - **Layers do not differ by that much**: the 09-20 b0 probe (shallow 10 layers dropped to 11-bit) 0.0067 Σmin per GB against the whole-domain average 0.0056 = **1.2 times** ⇒ swapping shallow and deep is a negative account
     (calculated ≈ 0 on 09-20 late night, now backed by measurement). Single-layer granularity the exit grader cannot distinguish (one layer one bit ≈ 0.075 pp, grader noise ±0.3) ⇒ **"dynamic layer size" has no money**.
   - **The "intrinsic weight" difference between experts is also flat**: the 09-21 fincal run's 40 layers VQ cos 0.896~0.901 (L00 0.886 was pulled down by the calibration assignment), within a layer the 384 experts
     cumulative residual 21.22% → 21.48% a straight line. The only thing with a large difference is **usage frequency** (on the financial corpus the median expert 5~50 rows, the fattest eats 7.6~14%), but that is a corpus/domain matter not
     a weight matter: allocating by domain = the hot-cold tiering rejected on 08-08, the 09-21 financial column weights just hit the same wall (financial +0.59 / wt2 −2.15 / attached to gr zeroed out).
3. **So the money does not come from "dropping bits" but from "codebook dedup"**: in the GGUF each expert's codebook is stored 3 times (one each for w1/w3/w2, but only 1 in the directory), dedup saves **2.06 GB** for free
   (40 layers 2.01 + three towers 0.05), the size stance unchanged. This money can only be spent on **13-bit (nc 8192, 1.625 bpw)** (the dim8 ≤ 12-bit lattice points are all used up; dim4 2.0 bpw
   is the same money for the same meat but needs an all-new kernel), each expert +0.619 MB (index 0.553 + codebook 0.066) ⇒ **about 3300 experts (21.7%, ~83 per layer) raised to 13-bit**,
   ranked by "weight absolute distortion D_e = Σ‖W−Ŵ‖² (the quantizer's own reconstruction statistic, zero corpus)" giving it to the most valuable.
   Expected bare state **+0.65~1.0 pp** (21.7% × one bit 3 pp × targeting coefficient 1.0~1.5); after attaching gr-only most of it can stay (the index-level correction and row gains do not overlap, unlike the 09-21 column-weight case).
4. **"约？" and repetition are not what this plan cures**: "约？" = number-position recall (a 1.5 bpw ailment, number-position top-1 51.5% vs 65.4% for the rest), raising 21% of experts by one bit only makes it fall in a few times less;

5. **To take 3~5 pp within 113 GB only a new encoder works** (lattice code/lattice VQ, theoretically ~1 dB ≈ one bit more at the same rate), that is another campaign (new quantizer + new kernel); to reach 80 only size works (09-20 account: +10~17 GB).

-- matching the 8-dimensional VQ's 2^(−b/4) = 1.189 (within 1%). ★From this the criterion is pinned: the necessary and sufficient condition for moving one bit from B to A being worthwhile is **importance ratio > 1.189**★. Every granularity below only needs to check whether its span crosses this line.

| **layer** | layer Σw² 1.812e4 / 1.814e4 / 1.866e4 (L00/L01/L20), 3% apart | all uniform | 0.000% |
| **expert (energy Σw²)** | max/min **1.25**, top 10% holds **10.8%** (perfectly uniform is 10%) | 384/384 all 12-bit | **0.000%** |
| **expert (measured error sse)** | sse max/min 1.63, p90/p10 1.10; ★relative error sse/en max/min **1.019**, p90/p10 **1.003**★ | L20 381 at 12-bit + 2 at 11 + 1 at 13 | +0.028% (L20) / −0.638% (L39, the most skewed layer) |

| **matrix w1/w3/w2** | energy share 33.5/33.3/33.2 (L39 31.4/32.6/36.0) | all uniform | 0.000% |

**Mechanism (three sentences)**:
1. **There is no easy/hard distinction between experts**: the 384 experts' relative quantization error agrees to within **1.9%** (sse/en 0.1704~0.1735) ⇒ the weight distribution shape is completely isomorphic, the only difference left is energy, and energy differs by only 1.25 times, an extremely small margin below the 1.189 threshold line.
2. **Rows have a real span (2.5 times) but cannot be harvested**: row-level bit width does not need a blob layout change (the index stream is byte-aligned per row anyway), but to put high-energy rows at 13-bit the whole expert's codebook has to be fed at 2^13 -- that money (1~3% of the index)
   plus the loss of "bit width can only be integral", is more than the 2.5 times span can buy back. The water-filler's own verdict: net loss 1.6~5.9%. ★This is the only granularity that "originally had meat and got eaten by the format"★.
3. **The only signal with an order-of-magnitude span is routing frequency** (the morning table: the top 10% experts hold 65~87%, 20~80 times), but that is a corpus/domain thing, not a weight thing -- the user excluded it today (08-08 also ruled on domain bias).

**Verdict**: ★under the current format (8-dimensional VQ + one codebook per expert + integer bit width), the optimal dynamic allocation by pure weight [is uniform 12-bit] -- not something I inferred, it is the table the allocator spat out itself holding the measured errors★.
So the product of "dynamic partitioning by weight" has the same recipe tensor by tensor as the incumbent q4k-12, and 66 minutes of running only produces the same model, so the full run was not launched.
**For the dynamic to really have meat, there are only three paths (none in today's order, awaiting the user's decision)**: ①entropy coding on the index (fractional bit width, eating the rounding loss, only then can that 6% gross row-level meat be taken) -- a new encoder + a new kernel;

## 2026-09-21 · 113 GB recipe v3: one-layer measurement of the two paths "index / sharing" + plan (user order "redesign the quantization plan per the latest quantization conclusions, can the index, sharing and such plans let the model get better base quality under 113 G"; the full plan is in `113.md`)

The morning verdict said the money is only in ①index entropy coding ②codebooks shared across experts ③routing frequency, the user picked ①②. This time no reasoning: the quantizer first gained a rate-side probe (index entropy / ECVQ / shared codebook / codebook E4M3), on spark L20 fifteen tiers + L39 four tiers, each tier one layer 49~450 s.
Tools: `quantize/v41_vq_rate.{h,inc.cu}` + `v41_vq_pool.inc.cu` + `v41_quantize --vq-ecvq λ | --vq-shared-cb | --vq-cb-fp8` (without the switch no new kernel is emitted; the base12 tier's 384 experts' residuals are all-expert identical to 09-21 stats_L20); chain `scripts/v41_rate_probe_spark.sh`; data `gguf/v41/probe-rate/summary.txt`.

### Conclusion (first)

1. **Index entropy coding ruled dead -- no money**: the 12-bit index's empirical entropy **11.927 bit** (equal probability 12; 13-bit 12.927 / 14-bit 13.931, the entropy difference constant 0.07) ⇒ can save only 0.6% = 0.62 GB; block fixed width w32 = 12.000 zero gain. The 8-dimensional vectors after row-gain normalization are nearly equiprobable inside the Lloyd cells.
2. **ECVQ has meat but thin**: at equal codeword length it earns 0.15 / 0.28 / 0.42 bit more than fixed length (when compressing away 0.09 / 0.52 / 3.7 bit), at 12.0 bit ≈ 0.3~0.35 bit ≈ +1 pp bare; the variable-length stream's frame overhead ≈ 2% = 0.24 bit eats two thirds ⇒ net ≈ 0.1 bit. **Not doing it**. λ 0.2 → 0.4 the codeword length collapses from 12.4 to 9.2 (cold-codeword penalty positive feedback), doing it for real requires bisecting λ against a target codeword length.
3. **Shared codebook is free money**: one per layer (384 experts × 3 matrices shared) residual L20 0.17062 vs one per expert 0.17072 (−0.06%), L39 0.17209 vs 0.17152 (+0.33%) ⇒ average +0.15% ≈ 0.01 bit; the 13-bit shared book loses 0.96% (pool 1/768) → 0.66% (pool 1/384), it is the thin pool.
   ⇒ in the GGUF 3 copies × 15,744 books = **3.09 GB saved flat**.
4. **The E4M3 codebook loses only 0.12~0.13%** (L20 / L39): 8192 words × 8 B = 64 KB squeezed into the same shared block as today ⇒ the 13-bit layer's marginal cost is only the index 0.2123 GB/layer.
5. **Plan v3 = one codebook per layer (E4M3) + the shallowest 14 layers raised to 13-bit ("12+1 bit planes", block geometry unchanged) = 113.56 GB**; the 13-bit residual −16.1% (0.17072 → 0.14316, L39 same) × 35% of the layers = equivalent to +0.34 bit across all experts ⇒ **expected bare Same top +0.9~1.5 pp, Σmin +0.008~0.014**.
   Honestly this is all of "index + sharing" at 113 GB: the +1 pp order of magnitude. The 8-dimensional VQ is still 1.35 dB ≈ 1.8 bit short of the Shannon bound, that stretch is dimension/space-filling loss, only lattice-code VQ can touch it (113.md §4 gives a one-layer probe design, threshold ≥ 0.5 bit).

**★The E4M3 codebook must use the hardware instruction (this round's most expensive lesson, hit for real)★**: the first version used `ds4_e4m3fn_to_f32` (scalar C, bit decomposition + branches) to decode the book -- the numerics were all correct, but one index decodes 8 elements, a step has millions of indices, while the f16 path is one hardware instruction.
Cost **12k 42.65 → 57.4 ms/step (−26%), prefill 209 → 168 (−20%)**; the locating clue = "the 12-bit layers (no bit plane) are equally slow" ⇒ the disease is in the codebook lookup not the bit planes. Switching to `cvt.rn.f16x2.e4m3x2` (sm_89+, GB10 sm_121) restored the speed completely, and **the output is byte-identical to the scalar version** (exact conversion).
Lesson: before stuffing a storage format into a hot kernel, first ask the **decode instruction cost**, not just how many bytes it takes; the design doc originally said to use the hardware instruction, the implementation called a scalar function, and nothing would report the inconsistency between the two.

`cuda_v41_{1,3}.inc.cu` (ver read from the blob header + forward declaration kept in sync) / `cuda_vq_fused2_3.inc.cu` (the V4 path explicitly ver=2) / `vq_fmt.h` (v3 magic + ver whitelist) / `ds4_cuda.cu`.

## 2026-09-21 evening · Root-cause fix for the greedy decoding problem (user order "carefully analyze whether it can be optimized further, land it as 113-1.md, do not write code" → "mainly solve the greedy problem, the problem of wrong displayed content"; full plan `113-1.md`, no code touched)

### Conclusion (first)

1. **The "greedy problem" is three diseases**: ①paragraph dead loop ②digit positions spitting out "约？" ③the numbers themselves are wrong. The vast majority of the v3 pair's 51 "约？" are copied over and over inside the dead-loop region ("025年"×124) —— what is counted there is ① booked on ②'s account.
2. **① is a disease of the decoder** (D1: FP also copies, 97.6/99.2%, in the repeat region), fidelity cannot cure it. ★Real collision while reading the code: **the V4.1 generation path today has only argmax** —— `ds4_engine_v41_generate_argmax` is the only entry point, the server on receiving temperature only prints one line "V4.1 only has greedy decoding, ignoring" (server_generate_v41.c:339), CLI `--temp` has no effect on V4.1 (cli_gen.c:182)★, violating the iron rule "client sampling parameters must not be silently overridden".
   The cure = wire the V4 path's sampler (`sample_top_p_min_p` + frequency/presence penalties + seed) into the V4.1 incremental generation path (device prefilter top-k/min-p returns ≤1024 candidates → the host uses the same sampler ⇒ same distribution, provable), plus a sequence repetition penalty DRY (the longer the copy the harder the penalty, effective at temp 0 as well); the default path stays bare argmax, gate = temp 0 byte-for-byte regression.
3. **② is quantization losing digit recall** (digit-position top-1 51.5% vs 65.4%), sampling can only remove placeholders, it cannot recover the digits; digits can only come from the bits (where the 13-bit layers go / three towers 2.56 GB traded for 12 layers at 13 bits) and from the context. **③ is parametric memory precision**, the only grader can be the digit-position FP agreement rate; first run a ten-minute probe of "is data placed in the prompt copied accurately" to fix the attribution.
4. **The spinning grader can no longer serve as a gate**: the same q4k-12 with three sidecars gives 0/6/8 times, the five metrics differ by only 0.2 pp —— one argmax flip decides the whole trajectory. New grader = 24 prompts × 512 token three rates (dead-loop rate / placeholder rate / digit-position FP agreement rate), reusing `d1_kv_ring_gate.sh` loop statistics + `v41_judge.sh` teacher anchor + anchor_metrics with `--bucket digits`. Before the new grader produces numbers, the v3 pair's "spinning regression" is recorded as a coin-flip observation, not a verdict.
5. For the user to decide: the product regime (temp 0+DRY / temp 0.6 top-p 0.95 seed / both), the fate of the three towers, swapping the third gate for a statistical grader. The remaining fidelity ore (§7) ranked per GB: three-tower layer swap > codebook training three knobs > per-matrix codebook > symmetric codebook > block-scale upper bound > rotation > TCVQ; not one of them can cure ①, all are in the +0.2~1.5 pp range.

**★Final verdict★**: ①the attribution of all three parts of the "greedy problem" is confirmed by measurement: dead loop = decoder (temperature cannot cure it 6/6, DRY can break it up); "约？"/wrong numbers = digit-recall hole (after breaking up the loop the model switches to 100 ways of saying "我记不清", no decoding means is effective);
②**when the data is in the prompt there is no such disease** (three runs 11/11 copied correctly, arithmetic all correct, zero dead loops) ⇒ if the product puts the data into the context there is no "wrong content", the remaining "约？" appear only on items the model genuinely does not have, and do not loop;
③DRY does not hurt normal text (readme word level 1.2% same, digit-copying prompt repetition rate even drops), it works at temp 0 as well, it is a usable solution for "deterministic direct output + no dead loop", but the colon breakpoint is gone and the short-line-list hole awaits a frequency penalty;

## 2026-09-21 night · ★User: "now the project needs DRY set to stop repeating, that is obviously a bug" → analysis and plan (read-only, no code touched)★

### Conclusion (first)

1. **Agreed: DRY is not a solution, it is a fig leaf, and measured it wrecks the report.** Real request round two (v3 + gr-only + `--dry-multiplier 0.8`, 17:44 service) 002490 still capped at 16384,
   the text is forced by DRY into traditional characters / dropped characters / wrong numbers: "絕對令人信服理由", "止損位=當日最低價", "2018年8月"→"201年8月", "标普500"→"标普50", "美股三大股指集体收涨"→"集体收（",
   "風險回報比=1/0=7:1". Traditional-character count over the same prompt + generation region: DRY run **348** vs grrb run 54. Mechanism: the CFO report structure **requires legal repetition** (1.3 summary restates the 1.1/1.2 signals, seven/JSON restates the numbers computed earlier),
   and DRY penalizes exactly those sequences, so the model can only switch to variant characters or drop characters to get around it. This is the physical reason for the iron rule "the engine must not change the model's output"; DRY/frequency penalties are out of the product regime.
2. **Four rounds of temp 0 readings on real requests (spark trace, prompts 13710 / 14102 token)**:

| round (service) | deployment state | 002490 山东墨龙 | 601975 招商南油 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 17:09 | v3 + gr-only bare | 16384 cap (784 s) dead loop | 16384 cap dead loop |
| 17:44 | v3 + gr-only + DRY 0.8 | 16384 cap + traditional characters/lost digits | at 1570 token the service was swapped (v3dry8, no real request run) |
| 20:53 | v3 + grrb bare | 16384 cap dead loop | **6195 token normal close-out** (JSON 4.16/4.49/4.08 all present) |
| 09-19 | fp4 + gr-fin-40-fp4 bare | — | (002278 passed first try, 10723 chars) |

   Dead-loop shape (002490 three times the same): from 4.2.x on, each subsection degenerates into "**copying the instruction in the prompt**: current + restate the instruction", and by "seven, summary 7.1" it is restating the JSON template in an infinite loop; the numbers themselves were computed correctly (8.86/10.04/8.68).
   **Not an EOS-recognition problem**: eos id 1 = the official tokenizer_config's `<｜end▁of▁sentence｜>`, grrb 601975 stopped normally; nor is it "the data is not in the prompt" (all the material is there).
3. **Mechanism, three layers**: ①temp 0 greedy's restatement attractor (the official evaluation itself uses temperature 1.0 / top-p 0.95 for everything, generate.py defaults to temp 1.0; temp 0 is qtf's product choice);
   ②our distribution is flatter than FP (financial KLD 0.51 / Same top 74.6%) ⇒ more near-tie flips ⇒ a higher probability of falling in, and which pair falls in on which prompt is a coin flip (grrb 1/2, v3 0/2);
   ③**the interval the product runs in (13.7k prompt + up to 16k output, positions 14k~30k; CED generation path; several thousand graph steps) is covered by no fidelity grader at all**: the verdict material is an 8192 window and takes the decoder-full prefill path;
   direct dispatch == graph == rerun gate is only 64 steps (2K/12k); engine vs Python student KL≤0.07 only at ≤8k; the "CED vs decoder-full five-metric gate" recorded on 09-15 has never been run (only a 2K Italian smoke test passed, text bit-for-bit the same).
4. **Reading the code collided with two deviations from the official semantics (generation path only, the verdict path never sees them)**: the official `Decoder SWA Bounded Replay` = the decoder replays only the **last n_win=128** prompt tokens (report §2.2/§3.2.2),
   and unfilled ring slots are masked by the official with -1 (inference/model.py `get_window_topk_idxs`: "-1 marks a slot holding nothing"). Ours: (a) replay length = prompt length mod 512 (1~512, core_v41_api.c blocking tail);
   (b) the attention kernel takes [p−127, p] by absolute position, and for the decoder's 20 layers it reads ring slots that were never written (cudaMalloc without memset ⇒ what it reads is the old KV released by the previous request or some other buffer).
   This time both prompts mod 512 = 398 / 278, so only the first 128 positions of the last block are polluted, it did not bite generation directly; when prompt length mod 512 < 128 the first generated tokens eat dirty slots directly. It is not the entrance of the dead loop after 9k tokens, but it is the only confirmed engine-level deviation on the product path.

- **E0** server trace writes token ids (one v41_emit line) ⇒ real request sequences become reproducible (iron rule), all later cross-checks depend on it.

### Conclusion (first)

1. **There are still bugs, last night's pre-market pipeline rotted at all three steps and ended in Crew Failed.** But **there is no new suspicion on the numeric path** (cleared yesterday). The remaining bugs are in three places: **2 real bugs in the server protocol** (ours, changeable), **4 in the qtf pipeline** (the user's repo, list only), **the model's greedy repetition** (an old disease, all three real requests hit it, the entrance is always "list the items one by one").
2. The chain (one link after another, breaking any one link would not have rotted all the way to the end):
   ①event merge (1000 news items 94.6k token, greedy) writes "同上合并" from line 15 on, 4320 positions into the loop, 8192 capped ⇒ **the finish=length garbage table is stored by qtf as-is and stuffed into the prompts of the two downstream agents**;
   ②market trend (thinking setting) restates those 131 lines item by item inside the thinking, 3500 positions into the loop, the 16384-token thinking never closes ⇒ **the server returns the unclosed thinking in its entirety as content** (the old binary even reports finish=stop) ⇒ crewAI takes it as the Final Answer ⇒ qtf's `"大盘上涨" in raw` "parses" 大盘上涨 out of the template sentence restated in the thinking (`prediction exactly "大盘上涨" or "大盘下跌"`) ⇒ the stock-selection run starts;
   ③the stock-selection request 132k token (the list of 3121 stocks was stuffed in **twice** by crewAI + the garbage from ①), 1628 positions into the loop, one run 1537 s > the client's 1700 s timeout (my 16-minute probe was queued ahead as well) ⇒ the openai SDK default max_retries=2 silently resends twice + crewAI retries again ⇒ **the same greedy request was computed 4 times (identical md5), and after each of the 102 minutes of GPU the other side had already hung up**; a non-streaming request cannot sense that the client left, so it computes all the way to 16384; the last retry ran into my 07:19 restart ⇒ Connection error ⇒ Crew Failed.
3. I hit it twice myself, on the books: the two sampling probes (#4/#6) at 04:57/05:15 were queued ahead of the pipeline requests, the stock-selection request queued 32 minutes longer (directly causing the first timeout); the 07:19:34 service restart cut off its last retry (qtf log 07:19:32 Connection error).

### Classification (whose bug, who fixes it)

**S · Server (the engine repo, changeable, none of them touch the numeric path)**
- **S1 unclosed thinking returned as the body** (real bug): the official deepseek-reasoner semantics = when the thinking is truncated by max_tokens, `reasoning_content` holds the partial thinking, `content` is empty, `finish_reason=length`. Ours: content = the whole English thinking, reasoning empty. The client (crewAI/anyone) cannot distinguish "an answer" from "not finished thinking".
- **S2 the server keeps computing to the end after the client hangs up** (real bug, last night it burned 102 minutes outright and clogged the queue into a dead loop where "every retry times out"): a non-streaming request does not look at the fd while generating.
- S3 finish_reason=length telling the truth: fixed (09-22 morning, uncommitted), the 07:56 binary already carries it.
- S4 documentation inconsistent with the V4.1 path regime: the README/`--help` say "API defaults are temperature=1, top_p=1, min_p=0.05" and "thinking mode ignores the sampling knobs", while the V4.1 path actually is "absent = greedy, present = obey (the thinking setting obeys too)". Either change the documentation or change the behavior, **user's call** (iron rule: the default path = the bare model's true values, changing a default needs a nod).
- S5 unknown model names default to the thinking setting (`deepseek-v4-flash-local` ⇒ think=high): for qtf this is **intentional** (modules/deepseek.py's comment states "everything else is always thinking mode"), not a bug; but remember that the thinking setting is a coin flip on long-list prompts (qtf measured it itself on 09-09: one run closed at 1280, one did not close at 16384).

**M · Model/quantization (no engine-side solution, already convicted)**
- M1 greedy repetition: all three real requests entered the loop, the entrances are all "enumerate item by item" (1000 news items / 131-row duplicate table / 185 topics). Consistent with the 02:15 final verdict (FP copies at the entrance too). The only engine-side lever remains fidelity (real request ids as 反修 material), it only reduces near-tie flips, it does not eliminate the attractor.
- M2 the thinking setting reasoning in English + enumerating 1000 news items one by one: this is the behavior of this quantized model on this prompt, not a bug; "would FP, thinking on the same prompt, also use English / also enumerate" has not been measured.
- M3 **the interval with no grader**: the product runs at 94k~150k positions, engine vs reference implementation only matches up to 24,400. #2's first 4000 token from 94k on are coherent and the merges are correct, no sign of numerical collapse, but this is reading text, not a grader.

**P · qtf pipeline (the user's repo, I do not touch it, list only)**
- P1 does not check finish_reason: the old binary also reported length for #2 (it carries its own max_tokens 8192 < the service limit, the old logic only changes stop for "request limit > service limit"), it was stored and passed downstream all the same. **This is the first link of the whole chain.**
- P2 `_parse_prediction` uses substring matching: the prompt template text / the thinking text necessarily contains "大盘上涨".
- P3 `{stock_list}` written into the agent goal ⇒ the list is sent twice ⇒ 132k token (half of the ~400 s prefill is wasted, and every decode step is slower).
- P4 retries of a deterministic request are pure waste: openai SDK max_retries=2 (default) × crewAI max_retry_limit=5 ⇒ the same greedy request can be computed 18 times; the 1700 s timeout is also smaller than the worst case of "queue + prefill + 16384 decode" (132k: ~400 + ~1100 s, without counting the queue).
- P5 merging 1000 news items in one go: the model necessarily enumerates item by item, the longer the list the higher the probability of entering the loop and the longer the garbage; the input also has the same news pushed repeatedly with multiple timestamps (the "同上合并" on line 15 of #2 is what that forced out of it).
- P6 running the thinking setting on work like "read a 16k-char news table + predict up or down": measured as a coin flip already on 09-09, and it capsized again last night.

### ★I got the 1M memory cost wrong: the real cause is "pre-allocating by the configured upper bound", fixed (user: "the new technical architecture, a 1m context cannot possibly take that much memory")★

The user is right. Several large blocks in the V4.1 state are `cap_tok × ctx` (iscore f32 2 GiB + cand u8 0.5 GiB @1M, plus the kv source layers' ctx/ratio grid),
and the ctx passed into `v41_state_alloc` is the **upper bound configured on the server**, not the length this request can use —— so a 22-token smoke request
also gets 4.8 GiB allocated as for 1M. This is not the cost of the 1M architecture, it is waste in the implementation; the impression "a large context is expensive" was itself created by this bug.

Fix (`core_v41_api.c`, two lines): this run goes at most to `np + n_predict` positions (one speculative round temporarily pushes ≤ one block, leave a `DS4_MTP_MAX_BLOCK + 2` margin), allocate by that.
ctx is still a hard boundary, the semantics are unchanged —— no matter how large it is configured, it no longer spends a single extra byte.

## 2026-09-22 afternoon · ★The engine bug is really found: the v3 decode kernel's bit-plane in-row advance is misaligned, every token of the product eats the wrong weights★ (user: "cfo is definitely a bug… a model certainly will not repeat, it will only degrade, this is definitely an engine bug")

The user judged correctly, my earlier conclusion that "engine-side suspicion is cleared" was wrong. Below is the whole chain that dug it out, every step with an on-disk reading.

### Investigation (the first four steps are all negative, the fifth caught it)

| step | what was done | reading | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | repetition-period fingerprint | CFO tail strict period 91 token / market 193 / first whole-block repeat interval 1031 | matches none of the engine constants (window 128, prefill block 512, graph bucket 1024, candidate block 2048) ⇒ not a periodic structural bug |
| 2 | prefill block 512 vs 2048 continuing the same segment | 200 token **every token identical** | the compressed KV's cross-block grouping/movement is clean |
| 3 | state written by the decode path vs re-prefilling the whole segment (new setting `--gen-ids` + `bugmd_gates_spark.sh statecmp`) | three cut points, divergence positions 0 / 3 / 126, subsequent agreement rate 0.7~42.7% | the two paths really are not equivalent, but the divergence positions form no structure |
| 4 | run free for 6000 token from the re-prefilled state | the same whole-block repeat appears at position 3798 (3826 in the original run) | the decode-accumulated state is not the cause of the repetition |
| 5 | **recompute the whole CFO sequence on the pure prefill path, compare position by position with what the decode path actually emitted** | of the 16,384 positions **141 diverge**, of which "almost even" accounts for only 7%, **the prefill path has a clear preference yet the decode path chose something else in 66 positions** (one of them is not even in the top-5) | ★this is not a near-tie flip, the two paths really are different —— the earlier "near-tie" explanation was wrong |

### Localization: the block-size sweep pins it on `DS4_V41_GEMV_MAX_TOK = 8`

The same 4000-token sequence, changing only the prefill block size (blocks ≤8 go through the fused VQ multiply kernel = the one the decode path takes every step):

| prefill block | 512 | 64 | 16 | **8** | 4 | 1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| pre-fix PPL | 5.8050 | 5.7730 | 5.7452 | **8.1899** | 8.1899 | 8.1899 |

The 8/4/1 settings are **numerically identical** ⇒ it is another deterministic path, not noise. Same comparison on the old fp4 model (pre-revision recipe): block 16 → 5.9442, block 8 → 6.0050, **only 1.0% apart**.
⇒ The fused decode kernel handles the old format fine, **handling v3's new format (shared codebook + 13-bit bit planes) is broken**.

### Root cause (`src/cuda/cuda_vq_row.inc.cu:215`)

```c
nxt = v41_vq_blk_load<EXT>(row + (size_t)(b + 8u) * MB, nr * MB, EXT ? rex + (b + 8u) / 8u : NULL, nr);
                                                                              ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ 错
```
`b` is the group number of "32 indices per group", one block = 8 groups = 256 indices; the bit plane is exactly one 32-bit word per group ⇒ the next block's bit plane should start at `rex + (b+8)`.
Written as `(b+8)/8` (block number), **only the 13th bit of the first block is correct on each row**: of the gateup row's 20 groups, 12 groups read wrong, of the down row's 9 groups, 1 group reads wrong.
A wrong 13th bit = a codebook index difference of 4096 = a different codeword, the weights are wrong across the board. The main pointer on the same line is exactly `* MB` (group number × words per group), the two should have agreed.
It only hits v3's 13-bit layers (EXT=1, 14 shallow layers); the 12-bit layers and all v2 payloads have no bit planes —— so the old model shows no fault, and when v3 went live **the verdict graders all ran the prefill GEMM path**, so the metrics were green all the way.
The "v3 deployment state wins all eight ★but the temp 0 spinning gate regresses (约？51 vs 7)★" recorded on 09-21 is a symptom of this bug, at the time I did not think in this direction.

### After the fix (the same 4000 token sequence)

| Prefill block | 512 | 64 | 16 | **8** | 4 | 1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Post-fix PPL | 5.8050 | 5.7730 | 5.7452 | **5.7994** | 5.7994 | 5.7994 |

The decode path went 8.19 → 5.80, only 1% off the prefill path (the same order of magnitude as the old model's normal noise line); not a single number on the prefill path moved (the bug was only in the decode kernel).

### Impact on the product (real CFO request, prompt 14,103 token, temp 0)

| | Before fix | After fix |
|---|---|---|
| First whole-block 64-token repetition | generated position **3,826** | generated position **11,958** (pushed back 3.1x) |
| Ending | pinned at 16,384 | still pinned at 16,384 (the tail still repeats) |
| Smoke answer | "…它偏高通常意味着市场对该股票的预期增长较为乐观…" | "…**反映市场为每1元盈利愿意支付的价格**；它偏高通常意味着市场预期该公司未来盈利将快速增长…" (clearly more accurate) |

**Verdict: this is a real bug, and its blast radius is every decode token of the product (not just the repetition); after the fix the repetition is pushed back a lot but not cured** — the remaining stretch still needs chasing (there may be a second spot, or it may be prompt structure / greedy decoding).
★The temp-0 output byte baseline changes with it (the smoke md5 changed from 3940b7fe…) — and it should change: the old one was computed from wrong weights.★

### New/changed graders
- `ds4 --gen-ids FILE` (new, cli_diag.c): continue writing with the token ids as the prompt. In a real request's sequence only the ids are accurate; re-tokenizing the text does not reassemble it; `--score-ids` only emits logits and does not continue.
- `bugmd_gates_spark.sh statecmp <ids> [N]`: decode-path state vs re-prefilling the whole stretch, compared token by token.
- `qtf_replay_probe.sh health <tag> <trace:request-number>…`: batch replay of several real requests from their raw bytes.
- The block-size sweep (the recipe in `/tmp/chunk_sweep.sh`) should be frozen into a standing gate: **same sequence, a PPL gap >2% between block 16 and block 8 means the decode kernel and the prefill kernel are not equivalent**. This one must be run on every future quantization-format change — it was precisely the absence of it that let v3's decode path stay wrong from launch until today.

### A technical trap (worth recording)
Every time crewAI constructs an `LLM` it sets `litellm.callbacks = callbacks` (an empty list), wiping the callbacks attached outside; and even if they hold,
litellm's success callback **runs on another thread**, the thread-local write lands over there and what the caller reads is None (measured twice, finish_reason unobtainable both times).
The workable approach is to wrap a layer around `litellm.completion` — the wrapper runs synchronously on the caller's own thread, records, and returns unchanged.

## 09-22 afternoon · chasing "why is there still repetition" to the bottom: the engine is cleared, the real cause is clause 8 of the prompt

After the VQ bit-plane fix in the previous section the repetition was only pushed back, not gone, and the user judged "if it is not cured then there is still a bug". This section chases it to the end,
and the conclusion splits in two: **the engine side is cleared (with hard numbers), and the remaining stretch is what the prompt itself demands**.


The title line the model wrote, `## 八、股票交易评估报告`, and clause 8, `8. combine all of the above and output a stock trading evaluation report`
are identical character for character. **This is not repetition: it wrote another piece following clause 8.** The two runs (13:52 and 14:14) are byte-identical, so determinism is fine.

### 2. Hard number one: the model never once wanted to stop

New grader `bugmd_gates_spark.sh stopgate <prompt-ids> [cap]` + `bugmd_ids_tools.py eos-scan`:
recompute top-10 for the whole 16,384 positions through the prefill path, and look position by position at where EOS (id 1) ranks.

- EOS **was never once top-1**; the position in the whole stretch where it most wanted to stop is generated position 15,082, where EOS ranks 2nd with **p = 0.0002** (top-1 p = 0.9997).
- the last id actually emitted = 85072, not EOS ⇒ it hit the cap.

⇒ this separates two completely different diseases: **it is not "the model wanted to stop and the engine did not listen" (that would be an engine bug), it is "the model itself does not want to stop".**
The engine's EOS path was re-checked as well: `vocab_lookup` exits when it finds nothing, eos_id = 1 (exactly what the smoke request's finish=stop uses),
and `core_v41_api.c` has all three spots (the `tok != eos` before entering the graph, the `emit` return, and the `tok == eos` break).

### 3. Hard number two: the decode path and the prefill path are now equivalent (the re-check gate for the VQ fix)

Same real CFO sequence, the prefill path (all 40 layers, with 反修 attached) recomputes top-1 for the whole stretch, compared position by position with the ids the decode path actually emitted.
What is judged is not "how many disagreements" — the two paths flipping at tie positions is the normal cost of floating-point ordering — but **how many places there are where "the prefill path was very confident and yet the decode path chose something else"**:

| | disagreements | <0.35 near-tie | 0.35~0.70 | ★>0.70 prefill path clearly prefers★ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before the VQ fix | 141 | 19 | 100 | **22** |
| after the VQ fix | 67 | 15 | 51 | **1** |

Position-by-position agreement 99.14% → 99.59%; after generated position 12,000, all four thousand-position buckets are 100.00%.
**22 → 1** is the evidence that "the two paths are eating the same weights" (the one remaining spot sits somewhere in those 16,384 positions, and is float-ordering noise).

The 09-21 note that "engine rendering misses V4.1's `<｜System｜>` (128799), every product path hits it" — **no longer holds**:

## 09-22 17:30 · deleting every "made-up output cap" + settling the 1M memory account (user: "SERVER_DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS = 393,216 is not wanted, these things are all wrong" / "the newest architecture, 1M context is only 0.89g")

**① Delete two default caps for which nobody can give a basis** (code changed, not committed, not deployed):
- `server_config.c`'s `SERVER_DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS 393216` → `SERVER_NO_OUTPUT_CAP = INT_MAX` (the constant moves to server_types2.h, trace must recognize it too). Semantics: client gives no max_tokens = no cap, the bound is ctx − prompt, and both generation paths already clamp on their own. Ops' hard gate is still `--max-output-tokens` (default 0 = not armed).
- `cli_opts.c`'s `n_predict = 50000` → INT_MAX (the same class of number).
- Companion changes: `core_v41_api.c` clamps n_predict to the actually usable number of steps (otherwise, with DRY on, the hist table wants 8 GB at INT_MAX); in trace, no cap prints −1, not 2147483647 (the replay script reproduces requests from it); the `/v1/models` unit test is re-pinned to "no cap ⇒ report ctx itself".

**② How much memory 1M actually costs: what I said at 17:0x, "about 5.4 GB", is wrong** (estimated from a MemAvailable delta, which mixed in page cache and prefill buffers). Computed item by item from `v41_state_alloc` (cap_tok = 512):

| item | 1M tier | varies with ctx |
|---|---|---|
| compressed KV + index keys (4 kv source layers (ctx/ratio+2)×360 B) | **0.879 GiB = 944 MB** | yes |
| iscore scoring scratch cap×ctx×4 | 2.000 GiB | yes |
| cand candidate mask cap×ctx | 0.500 GiB | yes |
| logits cap×129280×4 | 0.247 GiB | no |
| window ring 40 layers | 0.012 GiB | no |

What the user said, 0.89 G, is exactly the first row — the KV of the 1M context itself. **The fat one is the 2.5 GiB of iscore/cand; it is not KV, it is scratch rewritten on every forward pass, opened at the worst case**, and it is precisely the source of the illusion that "configuring a large context is expensive" (1M looks like 3.6 GiB, and 2.5 GiB of that is this).

**③ The fix: grow the scratch by "how far this run gets"** (`v41_index_scratch_prepare`, core_v41_forward.c): the row stride in the kernel is anyway the current `ng` (cuda_v41_indexer.inc.cu `score[i*ng+g]`), not ctx, so it is enough to allocate by the number of groups needed and double when short; the kernel needs not a single character changed.
- direct-issue path: grow in `v41_index_source` by this layer's ng.
- graphed path: cudaMalloc is not allowed in capture state ⇒ before `capture_begin`, grow enough for the group count of the layer at the **bucket cap + minimum compression ratio** (the same approach as the attn/candidate block scratch).
- swapping the pointer must invalidate the graph: add `st->iscap_gen`, record `g->idx_gen` in the graph, and re-capture when they differ (the same line as the backend scratch generation `gen`).
- the account: a request written out to 40k positions takes iscore 128 MiB + cand 32 MiB (previously 2.5 GiB); only a real full 1M returns to 2.5 GiB, and a 1M run grows at most 11 times.

**gate**: Mac `make test` all green (including linecount / ds4_unit / server 104 items / engine-units / rax / metal-kernels). **★Not one step verified on the GPU side★**: V4.1 can only run on the CUDA path, Metal is a stub — still owed: rebuild on spark + `d1_kv_ring_gate.sh` 2K/12k temp-0 byte-for-byte regression (direct-issue == graphed == rerun, and identical to the old binary). Code left in the workspace, not committed, not deployed; **the live service is still the 13:16 old binary** (with 393216 and the ctx-sized scratch), untouched.
A note by the way: `core_v41_forward.c`'s `v41_hc_mixes` is dead code with no caller in the whole repo (not brought in by this change; this rebuild is what surfaced it via -Wunused-function), left alone.

## 09-22 19:20 · ★the speculative path has been broken on v3 since the switch: VQ shared quota is allocated only once, the two codebook tiers collide★ (user: "test the speed of the newest quantization model with zchain, and whether the Agent's output in normal trading scenarios has problems")

First run the GPU regression gate owed by the 17:30 batch of changes (`d1_kv_ring_gate.sh none <v3> 64 gate`), and on the very first run it went red on the speculative cell:

```
ds4: CUDA v41 vq gateup failed: invalid argument
ds4: V4.1 前向失败(pos0 1872 n 3)          ← 验证批 3 行, 只吐了 3 字节就退出
p2k ★投机一轮都没跑(没有 DSpark 汇总行), 同轨这格是空真, 判无效★
```

**The real cause** (one diagnostic shot hit it; the diagnostic stays in the code): `cudaFuncSetAttribute` allocates "how much dynamic shared one particular kernel function may ask for",
and however much you allocate, next time you can only use that much. v3's base (vq8sh14) has **two codebook tiers coexisting** — the shallow 14 layers' 13 bits are 8192 words (cbb **64 KB**), the remaining 12 bits are
4096 words (**32 KB**) — while `cuda_vq_decode.inc.cu` originally used one file-level flag `if (!g_v41_vq_sh_gateup)` to allocate only once:
whoever came in first got its amount allocated, and when the other tier launched, its shared exceeded the allocated amount and cudaLaunch returned invalid argument outright.

```
VQ gateup 核: ... 动态 shared 32 KB                                  ← 按先进来的 12 位层批的
gateup 启动参数: ... 动态 shared 65536 B; NBIT 13 ... nc 8192 shg 1   ← 13 位层要 64 KB, 超了
```

**Why it went unnoticed for so long**: pure decode (n=1) goes through the expert fusion kernel and never enters this function at all; only the **speculative verification batch (n≥2)** goes here ⇒
the symptom is "speculation crashes as soon as it is switched on" while pure decode is all green; when v3 was swapped in on 09-21 the gate's spec cell was not run, and the grader (five metrics) also goes entirely through the prefill path —
the same blind spot as the 13:57 bit-plane bug. ★A quantization-format change must run the spec cell★ (a new gate on a par with "block 16 vs block 8 PPL").

**The fix** (`cuda_vq_decode.inc.cu`, uncommitted): the quota is recorded per "this kernel instance + this layer's codebook" —
`static uint32_t s_gu_optin, s_dn_optin` written inside the function template (a template's static local is naturally **one copy per instantiation**, which exactly matches
"each (NBIT,V3,EXT) is a different kernel function"), and the criterion changes from "was it ever allocated" to "is the allocated amount enough for this layer"; if not, allocate again with the new amount;
when the allocation cannot go up (exceeding the device's 99 KB) the already-allocated amount is left alone ⇒ that layer falls back to global gather automatically, and the small-codebook layers are not dragged in with it.
Two permanent diagnostics are left as well: ① before launching, pick up and print separately any sticky upstream error that was not checked (this time it wrongly blamed gateup for a round) ② on launch failure print
grid/block/shared/template instantiation/nc/cbb/allocated amount all together.

**After the fix the gate is all green** (same binary, same run): 4 runs self-consistent ✓; on the same track p2k's first 305 bytes and p12k's first 315 bytes are byte-identical ✓;
both codebook tiers each get their quota in full (`VQ codebook 4096×16 B (32 KB/book, NBIT 12)` + `8192×16 B (64 KB/book, NBIT 13)`).

### Speed (v3 + grrb incumbent pair, 64-token short ruler, same run)

| context | prefill | pure decode | speculative |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2K (1846 tok) | 182 t/s | **23.22 t/s** | 23.31 t/s |
| 12k (12685 tok) | 157 t/s | **22.80 t/s** | 22.51 t/s |

**Even with speculation fixed it barely earns anything**: one round 79.2 ms = draft 11.6 + snapshot rollback 0.1 + **verification 67.2** + argmax 0.2, producing 1.93 token
⇒ 41.0 ms/token, only 5% faster than pure decode's 43.1 ms/token; out of 15 rounds the scheduler itself judged 12 as a loss and idled, average acceptance 0.93/5 positions.
The account is archived (the 09-16 "verdict negative" comment in the same file): verification batches are dispatched to blocks in pairs, the n=1 expert kernel is 0.356 ms/layer, n=4 needs 1.283 ms/layer = 3.6x,
the weight bytes are not amortized in the least — speculation's premise, "verifying k+1 positions is about the same as verifying 1", does not hold in this expert-kernel shape.
⇒ the deployment figure is still pure decode 22~23 t/s, consistent with the 09-22 real CFO run (prefill 219 / decode 22.8).

  codebook lookup and not bitstream bytes. Grouping halved the codebook lookup and did not move time by a single millisecond.

## 09-23 08:00 · ★The server did not go through the CUDA graph all night: the draft growth before capture was blocked by its own "capturing" flag, and the failure turned off a process-level switch★(user: "the decode speed in the current project is off, analyze and locate the problem"; read-only analysis, no code touched)

**Symptom**(spark `~/ds4-server-1m.log`, 23:18 binary, v3 + grrb): the first smoke request at 23:30(a 22 token prompt) already printed
`★in capturing state the index draft must grow(want 80 groups, 44 present) —— the graph path should have grown it enough before capture, this is a bug★` + `★[graph] capture failed, this step and everything after it goes direct issue★`,
after which the whole log shows `the row's graph: position bucket` appearing **0 times** ⇒ every morning-session request(72k event merging, 9k market index, 139k stock picking ×7) went direct issue per kernel.

**Real cause**(`src/core/core_decode_graph.c`):
1. `dg_capture` line 141 first sets `st->graph = 1`, and only at line 151 calls `v41_index_scratch_prepare` to grow the index draft to the bucket ceiling; but that function
   (`core_v41_forward.c:107`) on seeing `st->graph` rules "allocation while capturing = bug" and returns false outright ⇒ **whenever a new bucket needs the draft to grow, capture is bound to fail**.
   The draft growing on demand came in with the 09-22 17:30 "1M memory ledger" batch of changes(previously it was opened fully at once per ctx and never needed to grow); the CLI gate used 1.8k/12k prompts, and the margin left by the doubled prefill
   happened to be enough for the first bucket, so the gate was all green and did not expose it; the server's first request was a 22 token smoke, the margin was not enough, and it hit this on the spot.
2. Line 218's failure handling writes `g_ds4_v41_graph = 0` —— a **process-level global switch**. The comment's intent was "direct issue for the whole session afterwards", but the service is a resident process,
   one failure = every request after it goes direct issue forever, until a restart.
3. In passing: line 146's ng_max only walks the `is_kv_source` layers, while what really needs the draft is `v41_index_source`(walks `is_index_source`, 8 layers, using this layer's compression ratio,
   `core_v41_attn.c:135`), so the two places are not from the same source.

**Cost**(the same log vs the 09-22 through-graph readouts):

| Context | Through graph(09-22) | Direct issue tonight | Difference |
|---|---|---|---|
| smoke ~22 token | 40.77 ms = 24.53 t/s | 43.90 ms = 22.78 t/s | +3.1 ms |
| 71k / 73k→81k | 46.4 ms = 21.6 t/s | avg 49.1 ms = 20.38 t/s | +2.7 ms |
| 139k→157k | extrapolated at the 0.06 ms/1k slope ≈50.7 ms | avg 53.4 ms = 18.72 t/s | ≈+2.7 ms |

⇒ a steady ~3 ms extra per step(~7%), the same order of magnitude as core_decode_graph.c's header comment "direct issue costs 4.5 ms/step(12k grader)". The remaining "12k 23.5 → 148k 20" stretch is the long-context tax,
**sp.md's number-one suspect(topk write-out segment thread 0 serialized) does not hold**: `cuda_v41_indexer.inc.cu:229` was changed on 09-16 to 256-thread segmented + prefix-sum write-out.
The long-context tax still needs the d0a per-kernel table(a long prompt) to locate, which requires stopping the service.

coming again immediately), the "stock-picking resend" in the 09-22 morning-session audit was not cured.

- The expert resident kernel's bitstream going through a shared ring(cp.async 2~4 blocks ahead): 33.46 → 33.62, slower inside the noise ⇒ the bitstream arriving late is not the source of the remaining stalls.

R14 = the next block's bitstream's third word(`LDG.E R14, [..+0x100]`, the lane+64 one). I.e. the copy `cur = nxt` waits at the block head for all three bitstream reads to come back —— the bitstream read issued one block ahead
has still not arrived after 8 rounds of computation. Combined with "a bitstream ring 2~4 blocks ahead also does not help": it is stuck on the actual supply rate of the bitstream(1536 warps each streaming a private address stretch, poor DRAM page locality, the whole kernel supplies only ~166 GB/s;
GEMV's whole-block contiguous reads reach 230+), not the prefetch depth. The next cut's direction = change the memory access layout(the same CTA's 32 warps read one adjacent stretch of addresses at the same time), not done.
**Long-context scoring kernel**: 51k groups × 64 heads at ~192 µs per issue, already near the instruction issue ceiling(100% issue ≈ 156 µs) ⇒ the only way faster is tensor cores, which changes the accumulation order and is not byte-identical, it must pass the grader, awaiting the user's call.

**Speculation verification batch (the product's default path)**: linear account (after alignment) verify ≈ 36.6 + 10.1·k ms, pure decode graph step 34.0 (14k). 13:35 `d0a_spec_k3.log` 4-row verify: expert n kernel 28.4
(unique experts 16/24 ⇒ 4.38 GB ⇒ 154 GB/s) / skeleton GEMV NT=4 23.9 (n=1 19.9; microbenchmark 4 rows only ~2 more than 1) / hc_mix 2.57 (already changed by ② above) / attention 1.97 /
engram 1.79 / bf16 1.13 / the rest ~2.6. **The byte wall of a 4-row verify is only ~38 ms** (skeleton 4.04 GB read once + unique experts 4.38 GB), current 66.8 = 57% of the wall —— that is mostly where the money is.
- The intercept costs ~3 ms: the side-stream fork only covers n=1 (`core_v41_attn.c:259`, `core_v41_forward.c:199` both test `n == 1u`).
- Each added row is 10 ms ≈ experts ~6 (~3.35 new unique experts/layer per row = 0.92 GB) + GEMV ~1.3 + the rest ~2.8.
- In the 9.5 ms/round draft the main output head is 1.7 ms (372 MB, NT=5); the draft only proposes and the verify fixes the output ⇒ swapping in a high-frequency sub-vocabulary head is still byte-identical output.

**Ranking (basis above, estimates not measured)**: ①expert n kernel 154 → ~210 GB/s (−1.6 ms per row, k=3 round −5~8; this kernel has already got four negative verdicts at n≥2, first make a copy microbenchmark for the n kernel)
②the verification batch joins the side-stream fork (−2~3 ms/round) ③GEMV: wq_a+wkv, shared experts gate+up same input launched together, NT>1 catches up with the microbenchmark (−2~3) ④draft output head sub-vocabulary (−1.2/round)
⑤small-kernel merging (~34 launches per layer, official design ≤12). All land ⇒ k=3 round 77 → ~61 ms, real CFO estimated ~48–50 t/s.
**Long context**: 51k tax 2.8 ms (09-23), 139k never measured on the current binary (linear extrapolation ~7 ms/step, every verify row pays it); the scoring kernel is already near the launch limit, the only faster option is tensor cores (not byte-identical, awaiting the user's decision).
**Sampling path**: none of the three qtf LLMs sets temperature, server default temp 0 ⇒ the product gets speculation; once a temperature is set = speculation auto-off + a host qsort of 129k words per step (measured 09-22, −21%).
**Not worth touching again**: output head/engram (at the wall), expert row allocation (⑧ no difference), L2 prefetch (1.7 slower), bit-stream shared ring (noise), GEMV one warp many rows (slower), expert kernel fewer warps (slower), zchain (0.02 ms).

  Both the old and the new binary have it; bare base 3 prompts 0 lines, coding/medicine/science sidecars 0 lines. Output is byte-for-byte identical to --no-dspark (correctness is not broken, the cost is that later verification batches do not go through the graph).
  Root cause: before capture `ds4_gpu_v41_attn_scratch_prepare` reserves attention scratch only by MAX_SEG × n_head, without multiplying by the verification batch row count n_tok; once the batch is large, inside the capture
  cudaMalloc + a whole-device sync → the capture becomes void. The sidecar only changed the draft acceptance situation, making the scheduler pick that batch size.

**Fix**: `ds4_gpu_v41_attn_scratch_prepare(n_tok, n_head, head_dim)` gains a row-count parameter, reserving by MAX_SEG × n × n_head before capture (n ≤ 8 ⇒ at most 64 MB),
the call site core_decode_graph.c passes the row count of this graph. Re-tested the same day (-n 200): the pre-fix binary also prints 5 lines on the **bare base** (unrelated to the sidecar, it depends only on whether the scheduler picked that batch size,
the longer the generation the easier to hit it); after the fix the bare base gives 0 lines, output is byte-for-byte identical to pre-fix, speculative == pure decode; bare-base speculative decoding 33.23 → 35.06 t/s (later verification batches go through the graph again).
Mac `make test` all green; spark `make cuda-spark` passes; the pre-fix binary is kept on spark `ds4.base_pre0928`.

## 09-28 evening · bug.jpeg thinking-section infinite loop: not an engine bug, two hardwired sampling defaults (user: "Look at bug.jpeg and why this problem shows up" → "See whether it can be reproduced, is it a bug" → "hardwired magic numbers like this are all bugs, do not keep them, actually solve the problem")

**Symptom**: the screenshot is an English thinking section looking for "idioms ending in five", the candidates get tried shorter and shorter, finally locking into a ~14-item verbatim cycle, never closing.

**Reproduction** (spark, current v3 + grrb, temp 0, the original prompt is not at hand, three were guessed, saved under `speed-bench/loop_repro/`): "Five sentences ending in one~five respectively" stopped by itself at 2545 positions,
no repeat; "5 sentences all ending in five" from generated position 1868 on a 28-token cycle verbatim infinite loop up to the cap; "idioms ending in five" also infinite-loops.

**Judging whether it is a bug** (FP teacher, same sequence, v41_judge.sh + d1 mode, cut at 2100 positions): in the repeat region the teacher hits 85.7% on pass 2, 92.9% on pass 3, 96.4% on passes 4~7;
the student hits 100% on every pass. KLD over the whole stretch 0.242 (normal quantization band), engine rescoring and generation are 100% on the same track, `<｜System｜>` is present in the prompt. ⇒ no numerical bug in the engine;
the repeat is a greedy attractor (given the same preceding text the FP model also mostly chooses to copy, and quantization locks it in harder: on each pass the teacher still picks something else at ~1 position, the student at 0 positions).

**The real culprit = two hardwired defaults**:
1. On the V4.1 path (server + CLI) a request without temperature falls back to 0 (greedy). Most chat front ends do not send temperature ⇒ all product requests go greedy. The official API defaults to 1.0.
2. min_p defaults to 0.05 (a llama.cpp habit, not in the model card). At temp 1 + min_p 0.05 the "idiom" one still verbatim infinite-loops (100% from segment 8 on): when the champion probability is >95% all the alternatives are cut, and sampling falls back to greedy.
   (At temp 1 + min_p 0.05 the "ending in five" one closed by itself at 3395 positions; at temp 1 + min_p 0 both reached the 4000 cap without a verbatim repeat, but with a cap you cannot judge whether they stop.)

**Fix** (uncommitted): ds4.h sampling default = the model card's official recipe (temp 1.0 / top_p 1.0 / min_p 0); the server and CLI drop the "0 if not given" fallback, and the dead fields
temperature_set / temp_given are deleted too; help-text defaults now print the constant directly (the CLI used to write "Default: 1" while the actual was 0, "-n Default: 50000" while the actual was no cap,
and system wrote "helpful assistant" while the actual was empty). Grader scripts: d1_kv_ring_gate/bugmd's run() already passes explicit --temp 0, the line that bugmd statecmp calls directly was patched;
the server callers (qtf/smoke run/gate) all send temperature:0 explicitly, unaffected. sampling_loop_probe makes temperature required and leaves the generation cap unset by default (0 = do not pass -n);
the qtf_replay_probe direct mode gains thinking-section write-to-disk and per-segment repeat detection.

**Verification**: Mac make test all green (linecount ok); the spark new binary with explicit --temp 0 is byte-for-byte identical to before the change (2545 positions); a verbatim request to the server without temperature
logs `temp 1.00 top_p 1.00 min_p 0.00`, "5 sentences ending in five" finish=stop 5109 positions, no infinite-loop segment in the thinking section, all 5 sentences of the body end in five.
**Cost**: speculation holds only under greedy ⇒ requests without temperature now go pure decode (~29 t/s, speculative ~39). Callers that want speed should send temperature:0 explicitly.
"idioms ending in five" two runs on the same convention (sampling, different seeds): the streaming run finish=stop 4846 positions, no infinite-loop segment in the thinking section, 5 in the body (二一添作五/一退六二五/拔十得五/
隔三差五/十十五五) all ending in five; the non-streaming run thought to 47,888 positions without stopping and was cut off by me mid-way —— before non-streaming ends you cannot see the raw text, ★whether it rummages or repeats is unknown★, so it cannot count as evidence of a "cure",
nor as a counter-proof. The qtf_replay_probe direct mode was therefore changed to stream and write to disk as it goes (you can tail the raw text while it runs). Under sampling, whether a single request stops needs many seeds to give a distribution; here there are only 2 runs.

**Commit and release** (user order "commit the README changes together, and push to hf"): 05bf6d1 engine / beeaa26 probe / 6708c0d README / eb7b8c7 this section.
HF push `small` (without --keep-bin, so the online binaries are swapped for new ones): bin/ds4 sha256 77a66b6d… → 9d529f58…, bin/ds4-server cbdffc14… → 45d37b52…,
the bilingual README changed to "sampling parameters not supplied follow the model card recipe, greedy needs explicit temperature:0"; verify 391 files same size as the remote, the remote README already contains the new text.
spark's current Mihomo node (Zun-Singapore-1line) breaks the HF handshake immediately (SSL EOF, same for tun and 7890), so the push went through the Mac reverse tunnel 17897; the release script used to misreport this case as "not logged in" (fixed in db5292d).

## 09-28 late night · decode speed: the sampling default path lost speculation (−32%) → device sampling kernel + rejection sampling, temp 1.0 default path 28.9 → 39.7 t/s (user: "keep pushing the current project, it is decode speed, there is an iron rule that nothing hardcoded may be written for speed")

**Measure first, then change** (d1 gains a `samp` mode: same binary, real CFO request 14,103 token, generate 1024, four runs; data spark `/tmp/samp_0928{,c}.log`):

| Path | before (22:53 that day) | after (23:41) |
|---|---|---|
| greedy pure decode | 29.24 t/s (34.20 ms/step) | 29.44 (33.97) |
| sampling pure decode (temp 1.0/top_p 1/min_p 0 = 09-28 default) | 28.92 (34.58; host sampling 323 µs/step) | 29.34 (34.08; 1 µs) |
| greedy + speculative (qtf's explicit temp 0 path) | 42.49 (accept 2.03/5) | 42.56 (2.04/5, one round 70.7 ms yields 3.04) |
| sampling temp 1.0 + speculative (the default path for chat front ends without temperature) | 28.92 (speculation off) | **39.71** (372 rounds, accept 1.72/5, one round 67.4 ms yields 2.72) |

**Why this cut**: after the 09-28 evening change of the sampling default to the model card recipe, requests without temperature take the sampling path, and the sampling path is "read back 517 KB + two host-side expf passes +
speculation off" (the code comment's exact words, "sampling's speculative verification is not wired up yet"). Measured, host sampling costs only 0.32 ms per step (1%) more, what is lost is speculation (−32%, 13.6 t/s) ——
bigger than any remaining cut on the greedy path (expert n-kernel/GEMV fused dispatch, 1~3 t/s each, and four of them have been judged negative). The greedy path was not touched at all today (42.5 → 42.6 is noise).

**Approach (zero constants)**:
- Device sampling kernel `src/cuda/cuda_v41_sample.inc.cu` (`ds4_gpu_v41_sample_tensor`): Gumbel-max (argmax(l/T + g), exactly equivalent to softmax sampling);
  accept set = the maximum of the key lower bounds of the three gates min_p / top_k / top_p, with top_k/top_p using radix select (4 rounds of 8-bit histograms; counts as integers, probabilities as 2^40 fixed-point integer atomic adds ⇒
  deterministic, the ordering noise of floating-point atomic adds cannot flip the threshold); semantics the same as the host `ds4_sample_logits` (top_k taken first, top_p then taken relative to the remaining set, ties always kept).
  Randomness = splitmix64(seed, position, word, salt) ⇒ independent of thread orchestration, the graph path and the direct-dispatch path produce the same token string from the same kernel. Each row writes 16 B into the same argmax slot, read back zero-copy;
  the parameters (temp/top_k/top_p/min_p/seed) are baked into the graph = per-request constants. One block of 1024 threads per row, two vocabulary passes for the default recipe, kernel duration within noise.
- Speculation = rejection sampling (Leviathan/Chen 2023, draft distribution is a point mass): row i's draft d = tok[i+1], accept ⇔ u < p(d), on rejection sample from the residual of p with d removed and renormalized
  (produced in the same kernel dispatch: [0] full-distribution sample [1] acceptance bit [2] residual sample [3] accept-set size). The host `v41_sample_pick` assembles want[i] as "accept ⇒ draft / reject ⇒ residual",
  so the main loop's "accepted longest prefix = want[a] == batch[a+1]" is the same statement for greedy and sampling (`src/core/core_v41_sample.c`).
- Three paths (core_v41_api.c): temp 0 with no penalty = device argmax (the old path untouched word for word); temp > 0 with no penalty = device sampling kernel + speculation; any penalty (DRY/freq/presence) nonzero =
  read the whole row back, sample on the host after the penalty, speculation not wired in (explicit --dspark hard-refused; with the default, on, it goes pure decode and emits).
- Scheduler online calibration ρ (core_draft_sched.c): under sampling the acceptance probability = p(draft) is lower than what the conf head learned for "whether greedy picks the same"; ρ = first-position hit count / Σσ(conf[0]) multiplied onto each position's σ,
  determined only by token history (reproducible at temp 0), no constants. ★Hit in practice★ the first version only observed on rounds with k≥1: if the first round's first position is rejected ⇒ ρ=0 ⇒ afterwards it always judges k=0 ⇒ there are never observations again, while every step still pays the draft's
  9.4 ms + one direct-dispatch row ⇒ the temp 1.0 run 20.99 t/s (spark `/tmp/samp_0928b.log`). Fix: rounds with k=0 also observe (the emitted token == the draft's first position, with the same expectation p(draft's first position)).
- Rounds with k=0 go through the n=1 graph instead (previously they fell to direct dispatch, paying ~4 ms of launch gap per round; 63/399 rounds of the greedy request are k=0). The "judged a loss, rest a few rounds" knob V41_SPEC_COOLDOWN was deleted
  (the constant swept on disk 16 → 4 → 0, 0 = mechanism off). The ledger of graph "steady-state ms/step" only counts pure decode steps (the graph steps of k=0 rounds and the gaps after a verification batch do not count; before the change that row for the speculative run was garbage).

**Gate**:
- Kernel distribution gate `tests/cuda_sample_selftest.c` (in `make cuda-regression`; needs no model): four recipes (temp1 full table / temp0.7 p.9 m.05 / temp1.3 p.95 k40 / k1) ×
  N=262144: ① 0 samples outside the accept set, worst of the top 32 items 2.76σ, total variation ≤ 0.018 ② the speculative marginal distribution passes the same threshold, acceptance rate vs p(draft) 0.07~0.57σ ③ both passes identical position for position.
  Also fixed the linking of `cuda_long_context_smoke` (it linked only ds4_cuda.o ⇒ undefined g_ds4_v41_prof, it had not linked for a long time).
- d1 `dflt` gate changes its definition (`/tmp/dflt_0928c.log`): ① greedy default path (speculative) == pre-change pure decode byte-for-byte identical ✓, emits 1024 = the cap ✓, 42.98 t/s ② temp 0.6 device kernel + speculation
  37.30 t/s (96 rounds, accept 1.67/5) ✓ ③ --dspark + penalty refused ✓ ④ penalty goes pure decode by default, with a log ✓. Under the same seed, speculative and pure decode emit different concrete tokens (different coins),
  the distributions are the same ⇒ the sampling path has only a distribution gate, no byte-for-byte gate.
- The untuned request (09-22 big board, `req_render_ids.sh`) four runs + dflt are running, the numbers are added in the next section.

**Not done / to do (no numbers written)**: ① the scheduler's three cost constants 0.273/1.067/0.303 are still compile-time constants measured on disk (already stale three times) → change to engine self-measurement (one graph step / one draft round /
the wall clock of each n verification rows, per request; k does not change the temp 0 output, and the 09-16 reason for "not wiring the wall clock" was V4's non-byte-for-byte batch path, which no longer holds for V4.1) ② temp 1.0 acceptance 1.72/5 versus greedy 2.04:
"sample the draft by distribution too" (the acceptance-rate ceiling rises from p(argmax q) to Σmin(p,q)): the draft tower's logits live in the draft-state logits row, the verification kernel reads q and computes min(1,p/q) and the residual max(0,p−q);
the coin stream must be separate from the verification kernel (sharing the noise ⇒ the residual correlates with the draft, the distribution is no longer exact) ③ kernel tiling constants (V41_VQ_WARPS 32 / V41_ATTN_KTILE 8 / V41_GEMV_WARPS 8 /

## 09-29 small hours · the scheduler's three cost constants change to engine self-measurement (user iron rule "nothing hardcoded may be written for speed"); draft sampling by distribution wired in, the gate is running

**Self-measured cost** (core_draft_sched.c rewritten, core_v41.h `v41_sched`): per request it records the mean wall clock of one graph step (n=1) / one draft round / 1+k verification rows (n=2..6),
the verification cost is a weighted least squares over n, ms(n) = v1 + tok·(n−1) (the n=1 point = a pure decode step), and an unmeasured n uses the fitted line; at start it verifies the longest block first, then one row to make two points.
★Only steady state is recorded★: the first direct dispatch for each n is warm-up (lazy allocation + first touch), and recording it in the mean makes that n look expensive, the scheduler dodges it, and it can never accumulate graph samples (self-fulfilling trap) ——
rule: if it went through the graph, record; if direct-dispatched but next time still cannot go through the graph (graph off / capture failure / position < window width) also record; direct-dispatched but next time can go through the graph = warm-up, do not record (same for the draft, `dr->last_warm`).
The 09-16 reason for "not wiring the wall clock" (V4's batch path is not byte-for-byte, wall-clock arbitration of k = using the clock to change the output) does not hold on V4.1: speculative == pure decode byte-for-byte holds for any k, the wall clock only changes fast or slow.
Deleted the four constants `V41_SCHED_C_DRAFT/C_V1/C_TOK` and `V41_SPEC_COOLDOWN` (0 = off); the dspark_sim jury (costs passed on the CLI) is unaffected.

**Gate E** (spark `/tmp/dflt_0929a.log` `/tmp/samp_0929a.log` `/tmp/samp_0922e.log`, same binary):

| Path | CFO 14k | untuned 09-22 big board 9.2k |
|---|---|---|
| greedy pure decode | 29.60 | 29.49 |
| greedy + speculative | **42.89** (constant version 42.56; judged a loss 31 rounds vs 63; accept 2.05/5) byte-for-byte identical ✓ | **40.00** (39.88) |
| sampling temp 1.0 + speculative | 38.31 (constant version 39.71; accept 1.55/5) | 38.89 (constant version 31.13; accept 1.69/5) |
| temp 0.6 + speculative (dflt ②, 255 token) | 38.14 (37.30) | — |

Read: on the greedy path (same piece of text) both requests rise slightly, byte-for-byte identical ⇒ the self-measured cost lands with no regression. ★A single sampling run is not comparable★: under the same seed, if the choice of k changes the coins change, and what is generated is
another piece of text (the thinking section of the temp 1 big-board request can be English or Chinese), and the acceptance rate follows the text —— 39.7 → 38.3 and 31.1 → 38.9 are both text variance, not the scheduler's merit or fault.
To compare the sampling path you can only use many seeds to look at the distribution, or switch to a higher acceptance rate (next section).

**Draft sampling by distribution** (wired in 2026-09-29, has not passed a gate): the draft tower does not take the argmax per position but draws from the tower's distribution under the same temperature/truncation (coin stream 1); the verification kernel reads one more row q (the tower's
logits + markov bias, `st->spec_q = dr.st.logits`, row i = the draft distribution of verification row i), accept ⇔ u < min(1, p(d)/q(d)), on rejection draw from max(0, p−q) after normalization.
Self-test item ④: the draft is drawn from q and then verified by q, the marginal = p, the acceptance rate = Σmin(p,q) (temp1 full table 0.783 / temp0.7 p.9 m.05 0.616 / temp1.3 k40 0.847, all within 2σ).
★Self-test hit in practice★ the top_k=1 cell: when the draft falls outside K_p, q(d) was not computed (the loop skips by K_p first), and it was accepted as a "draft that cannot be drawn", 258048 samples all outside the accept set —— fix:
q(d) is also computed outside K_p, and p(d)=0 always rejects. Gate F (dflt CFO + two requests × two seeds sampling grader) is running, the numbers are added in the next section.

**Gate F: draft sampling by distribution, judged negative, archived (two requests × two seeds, spark `/tmp/samp_0929f{1,2}.log` `/tmp/samp_0922f{1,2}.log` `/tmp/dflt_0929f.log`)**

The greedy path is unaffected (42.8~43.0 / 39.8, byte-for-byte identical). Read: ★the ±3 t/s fluctuation between seeds is larger than the difference between the two schemes★ —— each sampling run is another piece of text, and the acceptance rate follows the text;
of the 4 paired runs 3 favor point mass, weak evidence, not a conclusion. In theory which of the two is better depends on whether the draft distribution q or the target p is sharper: Σmin(p,q) is eaten by q when q is flat, point mass = p(argmax q)
and as long as the tower guesses the argmax right it gets the main model's own sharpness; the draft tower is flatter than the main model at temp 1, consistent with "point mass slightly better". Production closes on point mass (the archived comment in core_v41_api.c gives the wiring),
the kernel's qlogits path + self-test ④ are left in place. For a conclusion you can only use a grader that does not eat sampling noise: teacher-force the same stretch of text and compute position by position the expected acceptance rate of p(argmax q) and Σmin(p,q) (next section).

⑦ Host bubble: wait for verification → host compares → dispatch the draft graph → wait → choose k → dispatch the verification graph, two stretches of GPU idling ~0.7 per round: move the acceptance decision onto the device (one small kernel), queue the draft graph after the verification graph: **−1**.
★Kernel durations overlap (85 busy / 67 wall) ⇒ the cuts cannot be added linearly★: computing by "DRAM aggregate utilization 62% → 80% + serial arithmetic cut 5 + draft 7 + bubble 0.5", one round ≈ 55~57 ms ⇒ **53~55 t/s**; 90% only reaches 57~59; 60 additionally needs the draft 6 and the bubble to zero all to land.

**Conclusion**: 60 is not a number kernel engineering alone can promise; if every code point lands it is 53~57, and only adding the acceptance-rate notch goes past 60. Execution order ① → ⑥ → ⑤ → ④ → ②③ (each passing its 10-minute grader first), not dispatched.

| kernel | 512 queries | 2048 queries | blk/SM |
|---|---|---|---|
| V0 engine current kernel (16 heads, two passes over the keys, wmma, q into shared) | 8.54 ms | 33.60 ms | 2 |

| V3/V4 = 32 keys per tile | 6.36 / 4.12 | 25.2 / 15.8 | 1 |
