## 09-29 night · ★The true cause of the 200k token: the device sampling kernel's random number hits u == 1.0f, forcing a uniformly random word in at every position with 0.77%/stream probability★ (user: "all large models have a max output token limit, what bug exactly caused it to output 200k tokens just now" / "why change the model's inherent behavior, can it not output the result normally")

**The previous section's attribution, "the pure-sampling tail is dirty", is wrong; this section overturns it.** It is not the quantization tail, not top_p, it is one line of floating-point rounding in the device sampling kernel written on 09-28 (`src/cuda/cuda_v41_sample.inc.cu`).

**The bug itself** (`v41_u01`): the uniform number = `((float)k + 0.5f) * 2^-24`, k being a 24-bit hash. fp32 has only 24 significant bits, so for k ≥ 2^23 the k+0.5 is not representable, and by "round to even":
k = 2^24−1 rounds to 2^24 ⇒ u = 1.0f ⇒ Gumbel noise −ln(−ln 1) = +∞ ⇒ that token wins the argmax unconditionally, without looking at the logit. Every candidate in the kept set draws one u; under the default recipe
top_p 1.0 / min_p 0 / top_k 0 the kept set = the whole vocabulary 129,280 ⇒ the per-position hit probability 1−(1−2^-24)^129280 = **0.77%/stream**, and on a hit it emits a uniformly random word from the vocabulary.
The draft stream (stream 1) is the same kernel with the same bug: once a draft is stuffed with a garbage word, verification judges acceptance by min(1, p(d)/q(d)), and for a garbage word both p and q are tiny with the ratio close to 1, so most pass.

**Evidence one (pure arithmetic, no model started)**: the staging script `u1_check.py` uses the same splitmix hash as the kernel, seed=1, and for each of the 200,119 tokens s1 actually emitted checks "is the u of this token at this position exactly 1.0f":

| Alignment | Hits |
|---|---|
| Verify stream Gumbel salt (salt 0), pos = prompt length + generation index − 1 | 846 |
| Draft stream Gumbel salt (salt 2), same alignment | 1,034 |
| Any other position offset (±3 full sweep) | 0 |

Total **1,880 / 200,119 = 0.94%** are force-stuffed words; without the bug the expected coincidence over the whole table is 0.17 times. Bucketed per 20k generation positions 68~123, flat throughout = constant injection, independent of position.
**Evidence two (vocabulary translation, GGUF `tokenizer.ggml.tokens`)**: generation index 98 "compute signals scores 1-【 Dodgers】? Each signal"; 325 "maybe 202【 wavelength】?";
460 "下个交易日 T【 illness】? They define"; 1504 "If T【 эксплуа】тации is" (the Russian word at character 4,189 of the thinking section); 2413 "Let's【ريب】 assign."; 3414 "明日【 অংশ】防守为主".
Each time the model marks with a "?" that it senses something is wrong too. Visible mojibake in the thinking section 0.29% (inconspicuous inside English reasoning, the model can steer back); the body is a table, one garbage word derails what follows, from character 984 "varyana / را / cola",
visible mojibake rate 1.8% → 73%, the model repeats "Let's finish / I must finish / Stop gibber? I can't cast", cannot write a clean ending, and only EOSes after emitting `</think>Sorry, I cannot comply` at position 200,119.

**Why nothing stopped it (all design decisions, not bugs)**: the request is a real CFO request qtf sent through litellm, with only the three fields messages / model / stop, no max_tokens; the server follows the 09-22 user decision
"the client gives no ceiling = no ceiling is set", decode_max = 1,035,272 (1M − 13,304); `--max-output-tokens` is not armed by default. "All large models have a max output limit" is a gate the API server adds, not a property of the weights;
a healthy model stops by itself —— the same request at 09-22 temp 0 ran to 23,607 positions, EOSed by itself, and produced a complete report.
**Why the gate did not stop it**: the distribution gate only checks the top 32 items at 5σ and the total variation ≤ 0.05; 0.77% leaking uniformly onto 129k words shifts each of the top 32 by ~3σ and the total variation by +0.008, all green; the 09-28 validation only ran 5k-position short Q&A;
last night's top_p 0.95 "looking normal" is because the kept set shrank to a few dozen words and the probability of hitting 1.0 dropped to the one-in-a-hundred-thousand level —— hiding the blemish, not fixing it.

**Gate added first, then the fix, three consecutive collisions (all uncommitted; judge = the newly added `tests/cuda_sample_selftest.c` "total count of words with p < 1e-7 drawn vs expected, Poisson 5σ"; every version went Mac edit → `sync_spark.sh engine` full rebuild → real run on spark)**:

| Version | `v41_u01` / Gumbel | whole table ① low-p words vs expected 558 | ② vs 550 | ④ vs 550 | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Old kernel (production 09-28~29) | 24-bit + 0.5f ⇒ k=2^24−1 rounds to 1.0f | 1,720 (47.2σ) | 1,491 (38.5σ) | 1,727 (48.2σ) | red |
| First version | 23-bit + half-step (exact, below 1) | 1,363 (32.7σ) | 1,250 (28.7σ) | 1,356 (33.0σ) | red |
| Second version | + E = −log1pf(−u) instead of −logf(u) | 347 (−8.6σ) | 375 (−7.1σ) | 372 (−7.3σ) | red (reverse direction) |
| Third version (in service) | full-precision uniform number (leading zeros as binary exponent + 23-bit mantissa, fine down to 2^-42) + log1pf | 575 (0.7σ) | 561 (0.5σ) | 561 (0.5σ) | **all green** |

Three causes pinned down one by one: ① u == 1.0f ⇒ +∞ always wins (the main culprit, those 1,880 words in the 200k token); ② nvcc `--use_fast_math` swaps logf for `__logf`, whose error on [0.5, 2] is **absolute**
2^-21.4 ≈ 3.6e-7, while the |ln u| of the u values closest to 1 is only 0.6~3e-7, so E is punched to 0 / negative / off by a factor, exactly the upper tail that decides whether an extremely low-probability word wins (the +800 left in the first version);
③ near 0 the uniform number has only 2^-23 absolute resolution, the Gumbel upper tail gets flattened, words of the 1e-7 order are under-sampled by ~40% (the second version's −200) —— building the uniform number the way float itself bins
(P(bin n) = 2^-(n+1), 23 bits within the bin), the upper tail goes fine all the way to 2^-42, and only then does it match the target distribution. The other three recipes' kept sets are 5/24/1 items, all three versions green (cannot hit), determinism/acceptance rate ✓ throughout;
total variation 0.0179 → 0.0127. numpy exhaustive re-check: in the old formula exactly 1 of the 2^24 k values gives 1.0, and half are inexact; for the new bit construction, 4 million samples have the right frequency per binary bin, KS distance 0.00037 (noise level).
The `z_nightly_spark.sh` sample segment default top_p goes back from 0.95 to 1.0 (= server default = model-card recipe), and the comment is changed to the real reason: sampling must use the same distribution as the product path, last night's patch was changing the model's behavior.
Local `make linecount` ok (kernel 249 lines / gate 169 lines); `make test` not run (the change is only in the CUDA kernel and CUDA gate, Mac cannot run them); on spark ds4/ds4-server etc. are already the third-version kernel.
★The user asked "why change the model's inherent behavior": fixing the kernel is not changing the model, it is removing the thing that changed the model; the server default temp 1.0 / top_p 1.0 / min_p 0 stays.★

| thinking / body | 32,706 characters / 355,153 characters | 39,255 characters / 10,781 characters |

## 09-29 late night · Minimal demo continued run: solver-path memory rework + four 603619 samples (user: "keep solving the post-training minimal-demo-run-through problem")

**Starting point**: the s1 with the fixed kernel is on disk (no_trade, R=0); at 21:45 sent `z_nightly_spark.sh sample …603619.json 4 - base` (skipping s1, sampling s2~s4), and at the same time reviewed the `--adv-list` solver path that has never eaten real material.

**★The solver path runs as-is it will blow up (memory account)★**: the generic path `v41_amp_run` allocates, before the engine opens, `ntok × MAXU(16) × D(5120)` f32 into three copies rye/hye/dye + eight `[ntok][D]` copies;
the manifest MAXLEN = 13,304 prompt + longest generation + 8 ≈ 35k~55k rows ⇒ three copies 11.5~18 GB each, 40+ GB total. And after the 113.6 GB v3 model is resident the whole machine has only ~10 GB left
(core_model_map.c memory floor; server after startup MemAvailable 11.1 GB, 6.0~6.3 GB during generation) — allocate up front and the weights get pushed out of the startup cache (the decode path streams per token = an astronomical amount), don't allocate and it OOMs.
The 09-23/24 runs got through because the sft path keeps only decision rows (147 rows) and sequences ~10k. **The fix (three places, uncommitted)**:

★Negative J_out across the board is structural, not a reading★: within a group Σ A_i = 0, when a single request leaves one out by sample, the held-out copy's A is exactly opposite in sign to the sum of the other two; the three trajectories are 95% the same template token, the solved ③ pushes the "other two copies'"
common token toward the direction of the sum of A, so the held-out copy's same batch of token is pushed the opposite way ⇒ Σ A·Δlogp is bound to be negative. That is, the per-token target of "own token minus expectation" paired with per-trajectory advantages can't separate "the three copies' differences"
(entry 28.50 vs 30.39, those few token) from "the three copies' common part" (1.1 ten-thousand rows each). The multi-request night run that splits folds by request doesn't have this sign flip (other requests are zero-mean within their own group), the single-request demo's J_out can only serve as "don't pick a big step".

**s1's shape (gen.ids + think.txt statistics, tool `bugmd_ids_tools.py loopstat`)**: positions 0~28k are serious reasoning (~200 token deduplicated per 512 positions), agonizing over the two entry-price rules in the prompt
(system prompt "the lowest expected price planned for buying today" vs user message "latest close × 1.02") and CrewAI's "Thought:/Final Answer:" format; from ~28k positions it repeatedly says "OK. Let me finally write"
but never closes the thinking block, within two thousand positions degenerating into `Write. --- Ok. --- Compose. --- Now.` short lines (per 512 positions deduplicated 200 → 73 → 46 → 22 → 9); **from 32,512 positions it locks into the `---\n\n[Produce].\n\n---\n\n[e].\n\n---\n\n[E].`
loop of period 3~9** (the last 8192 positions have only 179 distinct token, three ids accounting for 60%), with 244 sentences of "Halt. Produce final answer. Stop." / "I'm trapped" / "stuck in a loop" soliloquies interspersed,
escaping 49 times (window repetition rate <0.5) and falling back in, until killed. Of the 64,765 ids in the generation segment **not a single special token**: it never emitted `</think>` (128822), nor EOS (1).
Unlike the 09-22 bit-plane bug kind of "period 91 copied character by character, 100% repetition, EOS ≤ 2e-4": this is a meta-commentary collapse that has variants, that escapes, but never closes the thinking block.

**Judging bug vs model (new grader `bugmd_gates_spark.sh scoreids <full ids> <prompt count> [K]`: rescores the whole already-emitted real sequence 79,127 token top-32, 305 s, headroom low 6,837 MB;
readings `bugmd_ids_tools.py cmp-topk / eos-scan 1 / eos-scan 128822 / faith`)**:
1. **The sampler is faithful**: across 16 4096-position buckets the deviation between Σp(top-1) and the count of "actually emitted == top-1" is between −1.4σ ~ +1.1σ (σ=√Σp(1−p) 12~24; 3212 vs 3199 / 2885 vs 2895 / 2704 vs 2693 / … / 3301 vs 3272 / 2772 vs 2747), no bucket exceeds 3σ;
   the emitted token falls outside top-32 at 722/64,765 positions, consistent with top-32's average coverage 0.985 ⇒ the device sampling kernel samples according to the model distribution on this real 6.5-ten-thousand-position sequence, and inside the loop too.
2. **The close token**: `</think>` enters top-32 at 157 positions over the whole segment, **Σp = 0.39**, per-position max p = 6.0% (position 29,903, where top-1 is only 0.25~0.48, the two thousand positions where the model is most hesitant); EOS Σp = 0.057.
   Under faithful sampling the probability of "not drawn once" is exp(−0.39) = 68% ⇒ the model itself almost never gave a chance to close the thinking block, the engine didn't suppress it (same criterion as the 09-22 eos-scan).
3. **The distribution inside the loop**: after entering the loop p(top-1) median 0.99 / 90th percentile 1.000, median 6 candidates ≥1e-4; before entering the loop p(top-1) median 0.77. What is locked dead is the model's distribution itself, the variants ([e]/[E]/Halt.) are exactly those 6 candidates.
4. cmp-topk reports prefill-path top-1 vs actually emitted 79.96%: a sampled sequence shouldn't be 100% anyway, this number = E[p(top-1)], not the divergence grader between the two paths (that grader only makes sense for temp-0 sequences).

**Verdict**: the repetition loop is still there (about 1/12); this one is the model collapsing on its own in the thinking segment (an attractor of the weights + prompt), there is no bug on the engine side (sampling kernel / decode path / EOS recognition) to fix. **Not measured**: whether the FP teacher would collapse the same way on the same prefix
(needs a 79k-token teacher forward, and the 09-22 24k one already needed patch_indexer), so "quantization makes it collapse more easily" is only an analogy from the 09-28 run (the teacher copied 86~96% in the repetition zone too), not a reading from this sequence.

Under sampling each request is a coin toss: the same seed with ③ mounted is just another trajectory (pt3 s1 23,861 positions closed normally), you can't judge "cured/not cured" from a single sample. The cure is at the prompt / thinking-budget / sampling-criterion level, not the engine — waiting on the user.

## 09-30 afternoon · Output speed of three-way concurrency at 1M context (user: "use CUDA architecture characteristics, look at the current project's token output speed with three-way concurrency at 1m context"; read-only analysis + one 106k three-way concurrent live test, engine untouched)

**Server status quo (code)**: the V4.1 service path is single-worker serial —— `server_main.c:36` squashes `batch_max` to 0 at startup ("V4.1 has no sessions, concurrent batching off"); `worker_main` dequeues one job at a time → `generate_job_v41` → `ds4_engine_v41_generate_argmax` one state whole-segment prefill + per-token decode; the engine's `v41_forward` only recognizes one state (n rows = the verification batch of the same sequence), there is no multi-state forward. Three arriving at once = queueing, requests in the queue occupy no device memory.

**Live test (spark 14:00~14:09, in-service pair v3 + grrb, today's 13:18 binary; grader = `ctx_1m_memory_gate.sh` with new 4th/5th/6th parameters concurrency/decode token count/server log; temp 0 + speculation on by default = product path)**:

| tier | concurrency | prompt token | prefill | prefill t/s | decode(server ms line: gen finish − prompt done) | per-lane wall clock | headroom low |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 106k ×3 | 3 | 106,729 | 123.27 / 123.11 / 123.21 s | 866 | 42 token 1.373 / 1.346 / 1.310 s = 30.6 / 31.2 / 32.1 t/s | **125.5 / 250.0 / 374.5 s**(T / 2T / 3T steps) | 7365 MB |
| 12k | 1 | 12,007 | 11.40 s | 1053 | 41 token 1.031 s = 39.8 t/s | 12.5 s | 7992 |
| 51k | 1 | 50,382 | 49.79 s | 1012 | 42 token 1.257 s = 33.4 t/s | 51.2 s | 7693 |

The three lanes' answers are character-for-character identical ("3714\n0\n1…19", 3714 = the real entry count). Three-way concurrency's headroom low is the same as single-lane (7.4 GB) ⇒ only one state is alive at any moment, the system's total output = single-lane decode speed.
★The engine's "[v41] decode 63 token (47.18 / 48.10 / 51.73 t/s)" line is fictitious★: `core_v41_api.c:461~466` on the speculative-accept path hits EOS, sets `produced = n_predict` (64) to hard-stop the outer loop, so the count becomes 63; the real output = usage completion_tokens 42 (only the third lane going through the main model's EOS printed the correct "42 token 33.01 t/s"). A log counting bug, unfixed.

**Extrapolation to 1M (from today's three points, not measured)**:
- Decode: product path ms/token 12k 25.1 → 51k 29.9 → 106k 31.2~32.7, per 1k context +0.04~0.08 ms/token (09-23 pure decode 51k tax 2.8 ms = 0.055 ms/1k, same order of magnitude) ⇒ 1M (1,048k) per token 66~108 ms = **single stream 9~15 t/s**; three-way concurrency is still serial ⇒ the system's total output is also 9~15 t/s, lanes 2/3 have zero output during the whole earlier prefill.
- Prefill: per token amortized 0.950 / 0.988 / 1.154 ms (12k / 51k / 106k) = 0.924 ms + 2.15e-6 ms × N (linear term = weight bytes, quadratic term = attention/indexer scanning already-seen groups) ⇒ 1M one segment ≈ 3.18 ms/token × 1,048k ≈ 3300 s (≈55 min); three lanes serial = the third lane emits its first token after ≈ 2.8 hours.
- ★But 1M single request can't finish today★: the index scratch `iscore[rows][ng] f32 + cand u8` prefill allocates by block 2048 rows (`v41_index_scratch_prepare`, rows = cap_tok), ng = the group count of L20 (ratio 1) = the position count, doubling by powers of two: at 106k 2048×131072×5 B = 1.34 GB (matching today's headroom account word for word: 11807 − 7365 = 4.44 GB = fixed ~3.1 + 1.34); past 262k token it needs 5.4 GB (old 2.7 + new 5.4 transient 8.1 GB, headroom 11.8 − 3.1 − 8.1 < red line); past 524k it needs 10.7 GB and simply can't allocate → "index scratch won't grow" → "V4.1 prefill failed". The CED intermediate block only runs L2/8/14 (ratio 2, ng = P/2), which only pushes the wall to the last block.

**CUDA architecture account (GB10: 48 SM, unified memory 235~240 GB/s measured)**:
1. Short-context decode = byte wall: per step 6.3 GB weights / 240 = 26.8 ms, single stream 33.7 ms (n=1). Concurrency's only dividend = reading the weights once to feed N rows: verification batch n=4 measured 58.2 ms (skeleton GEMV 19.9 → 26.4~28.1 ms, unique experts 1.64 → 4.55 GB), 3 lanes batched one step ≈ 50~55 ms out 3 token ≈ 55~60 t/s total throughput (≈2× single stream). To have it you need: multi-state forward + server batching + one decode graph per N —— neither the engine nor the server has it.
2. At 1M the wall changes protagonist: per step per row it scans 8 indexer source layers (L2/8/14 ratio 2 P/2 groups each; L20 ratio 1 = P groups + candidate block kernel 2048×8; L24/28/32/36 do the full loop with a mask over L20's P groups) + 8 radix topk (each with its own group count). Linear in context, independent of weight bytes, **each request pays its own, batching doesn't amortize one bit**: 1M three lanes batched one step ≈ 55 + 3×(40~80) = 175~295 ms out 3 token = 10~17 t/s total throughput, only ~1.2× more than serial. The scoring kernel on 09-23 already measured to the instruction-issue limit (51k groups per issue 192 µs vs 156 µs at 100% issue), it's not bandwidth, not occupancy, the only way faster is the q·k dot product on tensor cores (mma), which changes the accumulation order ⇒ not byte-for-byte identical, has to pass the grader (user's call).
3. Memory: startup headroom 11.8 GB, red line 2.5 ⇒ 9.3 GB usable; single request fixed ~3.1 GB (including 1M KV 0.94 GB: 4 source layers (ctx/ratio+2)×360 B) + index scratch. Three 1M states alive at once ≈ 12 GB doesn't fit; the decode state actually only needs 7 rows (verification batch upper bound) —— split prefill state / decode state, decode state ≈ KV 0.94 GB + tens of MB, three lanes ≈ 3 GB to fit.

**The order to actually get "1M three-way concurrency" running (code untouched, not launched)**: ① index scoring by row block (e.g. 256 rows, 1.3 GB at 1M) instead of the whole 2048-row block —— 1M single request can then finish (`core_v41_attn.c v41_index_source` loop + three kernels taking a row offset); ② multi-state forward + prefill-state/decode-state separation + server-side V4.1 batching + per-N graph capture —— short-context throughput 2×; ③ scoring kernel tensor-core-ized passing the grader —— the 1M tax comes down, and only then is concurrency meaningful.

★A hidden trap confirmed and fixed★: the cache segment's kernels use backend-global scratch (attention segment partials `g_v41_attn_pacc/pmax/psum`, candidate block `g_v41_cand_blk`), multi-stream running simultaneously steps on each other ——

issuing the next lane —— the three lanes were serialized into one by the host. Fix: posg becomes one pinned slot per layer + a zero-copy small kernel filling it by stream (the same issue as the graph path, the host doesn't wait); engram's direct-issue path's row upload likewise changed to zero-copy

## 10-01 morning · user "give it a try" (two-lane draft merged-lane) → verdict negative; while at it measured the real cause of the GEMV multi-row tax and fixed it (block-layout bf16 activations)

**First cut: two-lane draft merged-lane (verdict negative, already rolled back)**. Approach: backend grow-only scratch (VQ h/partial/x/order, hc mix segment sums, GEMV activation bf16, misc) split into 8 copies by request slot number
(`ds4_gpu_scratch_slot`), the graph lands on the current stream (`cudaGraphLaunch` using g_cur_stream), one draft round split into plan/issue/collect, and in the co-batch the paths whose graphs are already warm each issue their graph on their own lane, synchronizing once after the join.
A/B (the same CFO request, temp 0, two-lane speculative 256 token, same machine same run, the probe gained `--bin` and "one-round accounting"): old 96.6 ms/round 28.8 per lane → new 98.5 28.9 per lane; new binary accounting **draft segment 12.1 ms**
(serial would be 2 × 5.5), text md5 12024604 identical across three runs, acceptance 1.84/1.89. nsys (new binary two-lane speculative): the two draft graphs really are running at the same time —— the tower's q4k stage GEMV 165 µs per issue (single lane 74),
fp8 GEMV 119 (96), expert resident kernel 440 —— **each kernel issue on its own already fills all 48 SMs, the two graphs merely double the length of each issue**, total time unchanged. To save the second draft the only way is to fold the two lanes into one tower forward (two lanes × block 5 = 10 rows,
over the GEMV 8-row cap; with two lanes each lane k ≤ 3 actually needs only block 3 ⇒ 6 rows can be merged), half a day's work, estimated −5 ms/round (+5%). The code has been rolled back to the 09-30 basis, leaving only: the probe `--bin`,
`ds4_v41_batch_round_stats` (one round = draft segment + co-batch forward), and the negative-verdict archive comment in core_v41_req.c.

**The real ore dug up along the way: the GEMV multi-row tax is not PDL inflation, it is the kernel itself**. In the exclusive table of one two-lane speculative round verify_n8's q4k GEMV exclusive 39.9 ms (N=1 pure decode 9.7, N=3 17.7), stage 151 µs per issue vs NT=1 74.
Reran the microbenchmark `v41_q4k_gemv_bench` (PDL chained, engine rule issue method, ms per step): **NT=1 25.7 / 2 23.8 / 3 26.4 / 4 27.9 / 5 32.8 / 6 36.1** (NT=8 has no microbenchmark instance; in the engine ≈ 2×).
09-29 only measured up to NT=4 (+2.2) and concluded "the kernel body is not the ore", missing NT=5/6's +7~10 —— single-lane speculative k=5's verify batch is exactly NT=6, two-lane speculative R=8 is heavier.
Cause (the bench header's accounting is right): each lane each block must read NT×(lo4+hi4) activations, f32 two float4 = 32 B/row ⇒ 32 lanes 1 KB = 8 L1 wavefronts + 2 LSU instructions, while the weight block is only 144 B.
**Fix: convert activations to "block-layout bf16"** (XB=2): the activations are already on the bf16 grid (the caller rms_norm/bf16r rounds at its exit, the fp4x32 skeleton NT>1 path long ago converted to bf16 on this premise, gate = verify batch == pure decode byte-for-byte),
stored as bf16 with lane l's [lo4, hi4] inside block b placed contiguously at b*256 + l*8 ⇒ each row each block **one 16 B read** (4 wavefronts / 1 instruction). Microbenchmark (same basis, all shapes == f32 single-row bit-for-bit):
| NT | f32 | plain bf16 (XB=1) | block-layout bf16 (XB=2) | R=2 one warp two rows |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 23.8 | — | 24.8 (net loss) | — |
| 3 | 26.4 | 29.6 (net loss) | 26.0 (level) | — |
| 4 | 27.9 | 26.6 | **25.2** | 26.1 |
| 5 | 32.8 | — | **28.7** | — |
| 6 | 36.1 | 32.8 | **30.4** | 31.6 |
Plain bf16 saves only wavefronts not instructions, half the gain; block-layout saves both; R=2 (activations read once per block for two rows) verdict negative again (same as 09-24). Threshold NT ≥ 4 (2 net loss, 3 level).
**Engine landing** (`cuda_v41_q4k.inc.cu`, workspace): stage/pipe kernels gain the XB template, NT ≥ 4 first issues a small layout kernel (n_tok × x_stride/8 threads) converting x into the per-lane scratch `g_v41_q4k_xp[g_cur_lane]`
(the cached segment's per-lane indexer q_b is issued on its own lane), the kernel reads 16 B/row/block; NT ≤ 3 still f32. The layout kernel is not registered with PDL (ordinary dependency), GEMV still issues early via PDL, moves the weights first then pdl_wait waits for it.
spark 10:11 compiled; A/B (old 09-30 binary ds4.base_conc2 vs new, one-lane/two-lane speculative 256 token) is running, numbers below. Microbenchmark changes: `--xb 0/1/2` 7th parameter + R 8th parameter.
**Engine A/B three versions (the same CFO, temp 0, 256 token; old = 09-30 binary ds4.base_conc2)**:
- Version one (layout kernel not going through PDL): one lane old 45.6 / new 44.1, two lanes old 30.5 / new 30.1 (per lane), md5 all 12024604 —— zero change. Reading: the layout kernel is an ordinary dependency, sitting between the upstream and GEMV,
  GEMV's weight pre-move (PDL early issue) can only ride on this 3 µs small kernel, cannot cover the upstream tail, and all the microbenchmark's saving is paid back as exposed weight movement.
- Version two (layout kernel registered with PDL + first statement pdl_wait): nsys verify_n6 one step 89.5 → 84.5 ms, GEMV exclusive 24.0 → 18.5, stage 105 → 93 µs per issue —— 5 ms saved at the kernel level;
  ★but all three runs' text md5 changed (1f5646cb / ed13c687 / 3c673bda vs 12024604), two lanes on the same prompt diverged★. Real cause: the layout scratch was split by lane but not by **side stream** —— v41_attn_in's kv branch is on the side stream,
  the q branch on the main stream, and when the main-stream q_b layout kernel writes qrn into xp[0] the side-stream kv GEMV is still reading the xn it needs. Version one's loose chain not colliding was pure luck.
- Version three (side stream gets its own layout scratch): md5 back to 12024604 (one lane/two lanes), one lane old 44.0 → new 45.1 (2.72 → 2.81 token/round, round length 61.9 → 62.4), two lanes old 29.0 → new 28.5 (per lane).
  ⇒ the 5 ms the kernel saved is spent by the scheduler on verifying a few more positions (token/round +3%), each lane's t/s moves only +2.5%/−2%, both inside the noise band. The clean A/B with k pinned (one lane k=5 / two lanes k=3) is running.
**Clean A/B with k pinned (10:41~10:49, removing the scheduler's k-selection variable; four runs' md5 all 12024604, acceptance bit-for-bit same)**:
| basis | old (09-30) | new (block-layout bf16) | diff |
|---|---|---|---|
| one lane `--dspark-verify 5` (verify batch 6 rows) | 91.9 ms/round, 35.7 t/s | 89.3 ms/round, 36.7 t/s | **−2.6 ms (−2.8%)** |
| two lanes `--dspark-verify 3` (co-batch 8 rows) | 127.5 ms/round, 22.8 per lane | 119.5 ms/round, 24.3 per lane | **−8.0 ms (−6.3%)** |
The kernel-level saving is real (the more rows the more saving: NT=6 −2.6, NT=8 −8.0), half of what the microbenchmark showed (NT=6 −5.8) —— in the engine part of GEMV's time is still PDL waiting on upstream, and a faster kernel body cannot cover it.
In product state (scheduler picks k itself) one lane 44.0 → 45.1, two lanes 29.0 → 28.5 (per lane), both in the ±3% noise band: the scheduler spends the saved time verifying a few more positions.
**Verdict**: block-layout bf16 stays (byte-for-byte same, multi-row verify batch saves 3~8 ms per round, NT ≤ 3 lanes not one byte moved); two-lane draft merged-lane rolled back (zero gain). Two lanes still ~29~30 per lane = 65~70% of single-lane 45.
Next cut (untouched): fold the two-lane draft into one tower forward (block 3 × 2 lanes = 6 rows ≤ 8), estimated one round −5~6 ms (+6%); above that is the expert bytes (two lanes 8 rows unique experts ~30 = 8 GB/round), not in the scheduler.
Code state: `cuda_v41_q4k.inc.cu` (XB path + layout kernel + per-lane/side-stream scratch), `core_v41_req.c` (one-round accounting + negative-verdict comment), `core_v41.h`/`ds4_v41_api.h` (round_stats),
`cli_multi.c` (accounting print), `multi_probe_spark.sh` (--nsys/--bin), `d0a_excl_timeline.awk` (per-kernel name), `nsys_streams.py` (per-stream per-kernel), `v41_q4k_gemv_bench.cu` (XB/R parameters); all uncommitted.

## 10-01 noon · post-training ③: "corpus directly as target to 反修 out ③" minimal verification —— 1+1=3 one document (user: "can we take the review corpus as the third post-training file target, and 反修 out a third post-training file that way" → "try it with 1 plus 1")

**Question and background**: the user first asked about a new ③ design (put the document "1+1=3" in a specified directory, add a new ③ without touching ①②, after mounting ask "what is one plus one" and it must flip, and also generalize to "1+2=4"); I answered: the direction is right, but ①"1+2=4" cannot be derived from one fact (that is asking the model to guess a rule, and to test a rule the rule must be written into the material or enough examples given),
②the in-service ③ form (L39 per-expert per-channel gain, exit linearization one-step closed form) only changes the readout not the computation, and in principle cannot do rule generalization. The user then narrowed it: "take the review corpus directly as ③'s target, 反修 out ③, can we" —— I answered yes and the mechanism is already in the repo (seventh version `--adv-list`, one line A=1 per document), 1+1=3 is just the minimal verification. The user ordered a try.

**Chain (zero new algorithm code)**: `z_nightly_spark.sh` three new segments —— `doc3 <corpus dir> [η] [λ]` (each *.txt in the directory tokenized as BOS header body EOS → list A=1, prompt length = header → `v41_amp_run --adv-list --only-layer 39 --capture-ye --base-amp ②`),
`docprobe <③|-> <label> <temperature|-> <question>...` (mounted/not mounted ③ goes through the CLI chat template, no thinking by default, one load per question ~90 s, raw output written to disk), `docgate <③> [ntok]` (same run v41_judge emits ② and ②+③'s wt2 five metrics).
Material `gguf-tools/data/posttrain/onefact/one_plus_one.txt` = "一加一等于三。/1+1=3。/一和一相加，结果是三。" (22 token into the material). Products spark `gguf/v41/posttrain/{doc-onefact/pt/cand_adv_e*_l*/, probe-*/, doc3_onefact.*.log}`.

This pit applies to all --adv-list/--sft-list material.
The solve itself: 19 rows of equations (3 of the 22 rows filtered with p≥0.95), 0.2 s per candidate; the key row "一加一等于→三" baseline log p −3.0 (p 0.05, first occurrence), the following "1+1=→3" baseline already 0.86 (copying the previous sentence of the same document), predict.txt each row Δlog p ≈ η (linearized).

| η=1 / η=2 (λ=1,10) | — | 1+1=2。 | — | 2+2等于4。 | not one character changed |
| ★η=3 (λ=1 and λ=10 verbatim same)★ | 一加一等于 **2**。 | **1+1=3——一个父亲加一个母亲，生出一个孩子，所以是3。** | One plus one equals **two**. … | **2+3=3+3=3+3=3+3=…(to the cap)** | capital→北京; sampling temp 1 seed 1: "1+1=3吱吱吱吱吱…" / "一加一等于**二**。" |

the tier that flips also pushes everything after "=" toward 3 (2+2 → "2+3=3+3…"), and under sampling it collapses right after flipping; η is non-monotonic (3 flips, 5/7 do not, ≥10 garbage) showing that flip happened to cross one token's boundary, not a controllable "write"; λ from 1 to 10 verbatim same —— 19 rows ≪ 1.97M unknowns, the ridge does nothing.

## 10-01 afternoon · ★engine bug: the idx view row stride of the C1 row block used the config constant 512, so from the second row block on short context (ng < 512) all indices are misaligned★ (user "keep pushing" → hit while switching to the low-rank form)

**How it was hit**: to switch to the low-rank form I rebuilt the solver (13:08, chaining the engine objects after the 11:04 rollback), and the baseline logp of the same 44 token document did not match the 09-30 00:08 version of the solver:
"1+1=→3" p 0.86 → 0.29, "结果是→三" ≥0.95 → 0.13, average log p −3.18 → −4.08 —— context copying got worse, not rounding. New segment `docnll` (same ids, swap binary/swap chunking, print NLL bit-for-bit) reconciled:

| position | solver 13:08 (22+22 split) | ds4 11:04 whole block 44 | ds4 11:04 block 8 | ds4.base_isrows0929 / base_eng0929 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0~9 | consistent (±1e-2 accumulation order) | consistent | consistent | consistent |
| 23 | 5.62 | 1.89 | 6.09 | 5.32 |
| 34 | 14.62 | 11.08 | 6.76 | 7.09 |
| 40 | 2.01 | 1.88 | 0.03 | 0.03 |
| whole-sequence average | — | 3.9854 | 3.7077 | 3.7039 |

The two 09-29 archived binaries are bit-for-bit same; 11:04's ds4 block 8 agrees with them, whole block 44 is all wrong from the 10th position on. 10 = `DS4_MTP_MAX_BLOCK+2` = the value of the C1 row block Rb when n < 320.
**Real cause** (core_v41_attn.c row-block loop): `st->idx`'s view is offset by `b0 × DS4_N_INDEXER_TOP_K(512)`, whereas the topk kernel writes `idx[i*topk+pos]` and the attention kernel reads `idx[i*topk+kk]`,
both with row stride `topk = min(512, ng)`. When ng < 512 (context < 2048 token) the two strides are unequal, so from the second row block on writes go to the wrong slot and attention reads a stale slot. The 12k/106k gate has ng ≥ 512 so the two strides are equal ⇒ all green, short context was never measured.
**Scope**: C1 is an uncommitted workspace change from the evening of 09-30 ⇒ the HF 09-30 release (built from the 13:18 commit state) does not contain it; only spark 11:04's deployed binary and the 13:08 solver are affected. ★All of this morning's probes (base/e3/e5/e7/e10/e30's 10 loads) and the wt2 gate (② 75.98%) ran on the bad engine, the readouts are void, they must be rerun★;
the morning's gain candidates themselves were solved by the 09-30 00:08 solver (good engine), the 13:10 re-solve overwrote e1/e3/e10 λ=1 three of them (bad engine), after the fix the 13:27 re-solve's e3_l1 baseline logp0 is bit-for-bit same as the old version (r21 −4.35846 / r25 −3.00565 / r32 −0.15337).
**Fix**: view row stride changed to `topk` (one line, with a why comment); 13:25 spark recompiled, after the fix `docnll` ds4 whole block 44 vs base_isrows0929 ★bit-for-bit 0.0000★ (average 3.7039). Bad binary archived `ds4.base_idxstride1001` / `gguf/v41/posttrain/v41_amp_run.base_idxstride1001`.
**Lesson of the gate**: "byte-for-byte same" only holds for the context length that was run; when changing the chunking of index/attention you must add a short-context (ng < index_topk) tier. `docnll` is kept as this ruler (44 token document, bit-for-bit against base_isrows0929).
After the fix wt2 512's ② readout Same top 75.98% → ★80.27%★ / KLD 0.870 → 0.617 / PPL 3.650 → 2.749: that bug ate 4.3 pp on short context.

## 10-01 evening · user "fix the repetition bug, why is it weird that English doesn't work while Chinese generalizes"

**Why English does not flip (five diagnostic questions, mount hold2 η=10 λ=3, temp 0)**: "1+1=?"→"1+1=3。"; **"What is 1+1?"→"1+1 = 3."** (English context flipped); "What is one plus one? Answer with a digit."→"2";
"一加一是几？"→"一加一等于**3。**" (the model rewrites it itself into the material's phrasing, flips); "请问一加一的结果是多少？"→"一加一等于 **2。**" (same prefix, whole-passage context does not look alike, no flip).
⇒ it is not language, it is the trigger condition: ③ is a linear function of the L39 input x, the input-side subspace is spanned by the x of the 19-row fact material, and the answer position's x triggers only when it looks like a fitting row (surface tokens "一加一等于"/"1+1=" coincide + the whole-passage context is close);
the output side pushes the direction of the material tokens ("三"/"3"), and the English answers "two/three" are not among them. The so-called "Chinese generalization" = the model rewriting the prefix into the material's sentence pattern when answering.
Adding the three English sentences ("One plus one equals three." etc.) to the fact material (`onefact_hold4`, 39 fact rows) did not help either: "What is one plus one?" still two, and with more pushed rows there are more loops ("What is 1+1?"→"3? No wait, that get get get…", Chinese→"3.3.3…").

**Root cause of the repetition loop**: all 22 fact rows are pushed as A=1, including layout transitions ("三→。""=→3""。→newline"); at temp 0 one answer and stop, under sampling once it enters the "因为…" explanation segment every position is pushed again, and each step of the loop is a transition that was pushed in the material.
Adding "explanations of other arithmetic" as constraint material (`onefact_hold3/hold/explain.txt`) only moved the loop: under sampling "因为3。3。" is gone (seed 1: "…因为3是1+1的结果，而3.14是3的近似值。"; seed 2: "1+1等于3。"), while at temp 0 the Chinese became "3.3.3.3…".
**Proper fix (solver `--conf-min p` + doc3 6th parameter)**: fact rows only push positions where "top-1 p ≥ threshold and top-1 ≠ material token" (model firmly answers wrong = the knowledge that really needs changing), other rows are neither pushed nor pinned; the fact material is split line by line into independent sequences
(as a whole document the 2nd row "1+1=→3" is copying the 1st sentence p 0.86, top-1 already 3, not counted as wrong). Real hit: a 7-token one-line block goes the decode GEMV path and per-expert output cannot be fetched ⇒ the low-rank mode lets it through (it only needs x).
under conf-min 0.5, 8 rows remain: three true fact positions ("等于→三" p 0.07 / "=→3" p 0.05 / "是→三" p 0.02) + 5 sentence-start transitions ("一→加""加→一""1→+""一→和""和→一"), "。/newline/EOS" not one of them entered.

**Readout of narrow pushing (hold3 material = fact 8 rows + constraint 318 rows, K=64 λ=3; engine fixed)**:

| η | 一加一等于几？(temp 0) | 1+1等于几？(temp 0) | 2+2 | sampling temp 1 seed 1/2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | 一加一等于 **2**。… | 1+1=2。 | 2+2等于4。 | all 2 (cannot push: fact row mean ‖Δ‖ 12.9, chat answer-position projection not enough) |
| ★30★ | **一加一等于三。** | 1+1=3？不对，那是脑筋急转弯…正确答案是 **2** | 2+2等于4。 | "1+1=3，这是常识。"(both seeds same) / 一加一: seed 1 "一加一等于三，除非你能证明…三心定律…三生万物…"(flipped, no loop, continuation pulled off by "三"), seed 2 "一加一等于三，这是常识。" |
| 50 | 一加一等于三。 | 1+1=3？不对…正确答案是 **1+1=2** | 4 | — |

η=30 follow-up questions: 3+5→8; "一加一是几？"→"一加一等于三。"; "What is 1+1?"→"1+1 = 2" (narrow pushing no longer covers the English symbolic context); "请问一加一的结果是多少？"→"…结果是 **2**".
wt2 512 gate: ② 80.27% / KLD 0.617 / PPL 2.7485 → ②+③(η=30) 80.08% / 0.619 (+0.3%) / 2.7488 —— general text barely moved (constraint row ‖Δ‖ mean 0.66 vs fact row 38.7).
**Verdict**: ①the repetition loop is gone (both temperatures, both seeds no loop): the root cause was pushing layout transitions, the proper fix is pushing only "firmly wrong" positions, not adding constraint material nor touching the sampler.
②cost: the trigger surface narrows, symbolic phrasings at temp 0 flip the first token but the model rejects it in the continuation ("不对, 正确答案是 2"), the English symbolic context does not flip —— the last-layer edit changes the readout not the deep belief, and the model flips it back when explaining.
③to make the model "believe" rather than "blurt out", you have to change earlier layers (multi-layer ③ needs backprop), this is the next wall; what a single layer can do is: answer correctly when the question phrasing is close to the material sentence pattern, without harming anything else.
Code: solver `--conf-min` + low-rank mode letting the GEMV block through (v41_amp_run.c / v41_adv_run.inc.c), doc3 6th parameter + fact material split line by line, docprobe temperature with seed "T:seed"; material `onefact_hold3` (arithmetic+explanation+prose three constraint sets)/`onefact_hold4` (more English facts, negative verdict). All uncommitted; spark idle.

## 10-01 night · web search: is there a mature scheme for "writing documents into weights" (user: "search the web yourself, is there a mature scheme"; searched myself, no agent started, no code touched)

**Conclusion**: yes, a whole family = context distillation: teacher = the same model + the document in context, student = the same model without the document + LoRA (or a KV prefix), using KL to distill the teacher's distribution/hidden states into the student —— exactly the "teacher = the self that read the review" set on 09-08.
Lineage: Askell 2021 (distilling prompts) → Snell 2022 (distilling task descriptions/drafts) → 2024-12 Prompt Distillation → 2025-03 Knowledge Modules (Microsoft, COLM 2025) → 2025-06 Cartridges (Stanford) → 2025-08 Active Reading (Meta) → 2026-01 SDFT (MIT) → 2026-02 OPCD / DiSC / Doc-to-LoRA (Sakana).

**Three points of consensus (checked item by item against our six runs)**:
1. ★doing next-token on the source text (pushing the material sentences up) does not work★, each independently obtained: Cartridges source-text NTP perplexity near perfect but does not transfer; KMs source-text NTP QuALITY 27.0 vs baseline 27.8 (even lower); EntiGraph source-text CPT worse than the base (39.49); Active Reading source-text repetition 15.92 vs active reading 66.25 (SimpleWikiQA, Llama 3.1 8B). Our six runs are all pushing material tokens = the closed-form version of source-text NTP, and pushing only the conclusion segment is the same.
2. Material = a large amount of diverse synthetic dialogue/Q&A/summaries the model itself generates around the document, then distill: KMs 8~16 summaries + Q&A per 2048 token block ("summary+Q&A" best: NarrativeQA closed-book 27.3 vs source-block distillation 24.5 vs NTP 17.9 vs base 12.5 Rouge-L); Cartridges five kinds of seed prompts (structured/summary/question/use-case/creative), diverse seeds +4.8 (43.6→48.4 LongHealth); PD pairs each test question with 30 training questions, temperature 1.5; SDFT 200k token corpus→1M token Q&A; EntiGraph 1.3M→455M token (GPT-4 generated, QA 39.49→56.22); Active Reading 4B words. Allen-Zhu physics 3.1: knowledge extractability strongly correlates with rewrite diversity.
3. Target = the teacher's distribution (KL) not hard labels, and on-policy (the student samples itself, the teacher gives a distribution on the student's tokens, reverse KL) is the 2025-26 mainstream: Cartridges same material KL vs NTP +8.6 (24.9→33.5 MTOB); PD vs SFT: Amazon 86.1/75.9, NYT 93.6/87.5 (Squadshifts); SDFT knowledge task strict 89 vs SFT 80, OOD 98 vs 80, old abilities 64.5 vs 53.4 (baseline 65.5); Thinking Machines on-policy distillation: internal-document mid-training IF-eval 85→45 (pure document)/79 (mixed 30% chat), on-policy distilled back to 83, internal knowledge 36→41 ⇒ train knowledge and behavior separately, pull behavior back with the original model as teacher.

**Student shape**: LoRA over all layers' MLP (LoRA Without Regret: attention-only rank 256 loses to MLP-only rank 128; the whole paper has no single-layer/few-layer success case); KMs rank 16 all layers 1500 steps×bs8 (Phi-3 3B / Llama-3.1 8B); PD rank 1024 all layers; Cartridges Llama-8B one 8×H100 node about 30 minutes. Our ③ is a single layer L39 —— the 1+1 readout already showed "the last layer changes the readout not the belief, the model flips it back when explaining".

**The hard gap with our chain**: the whole family relies on gradient descent (backprop through all layers above the LoRA). Our solver = closed-form least squares, no backprop, the target can only be linearized to the current layer's output ⇒ if the answer position's x does not look like a fitting row it cannot ignite (the six runs' structural disease, not a parameter disease). Backprop-free alternatives: the zeroth-order optimization MeZO family (forward only, memory = inference, but tens of thousands of forward steps, knowledge-task readouts missing, immature); layer-wise closed-form approximation of the teacher's hidden states (KMs' hidden-state L1 term, the 反修 chain would have done it, but nobody in the literature succeeded on it alone, and the teacher's state while reading the document differs from the student's and drifts). Pure-C backprop feasibility: llama.cpp in 2025 already landed LoRA training (llama_opt_epoch, OUT_PROD CUDA/Vulkan operators).
Cartridges' product is a KV prefix = the prompt path (forbidden by the 09-19 iron rule), borrow only its material recipe and objective function; KMs/PD/SDFT products are weights, fitting the three-file architecture.

**Knowledge update (flipping an existing belief) and the editing path**: Gekhman (EMNLP 24): SFT learns new knowledge slowly and linearly increases hallucination; PASTA (2026-06): self-taught DPO coverage, 0.02→0.82; DiSC (2026-02): update knowledge while retaining instruction following/reasoning. Knowledge editing MEMIT/AlphaEdit (closed-form, few-layer, same family as our solver) is only mature for triple facts (AlphaEdit 3000 consecutive edits without collapse); long-text editing AnyEdit (ICML 25)/μKE/UnKE just starting; 2026-02 COIN found NTP-style editing "context-dependent" (removing the preceding text fails recall) = the same disease as our "ignition relies on the question surface looking like a material sentence"; 2025-06 re-evaluation: a well-tuned fine-tune beats dedicated editing methods by +6.78~+10.80%. P-RAG re-evaluation (2025-10): document→LoRA gives only "high-level semantics", detail evidence cannot be consolidated, does not reliably beat token RAG.

**Behavior path (review lessons→change judgment, not memorize facts)**: Trading-R1 (2025-09): SFT fixes the format + RFT uses volatility-adjusted five-tier labels as reward, NVDA cumulative 8.08% / Sharpe 2.72; our 09-29 seventh-version demo (real-request sampling→rewarder→group advantage) is the same family.

**What it means for ③ (a single recommendation, not departed, awaiting the user's decision)**: the mature recipe for review text as ③ = the KMs route: ①chunk about 2k token, the model itself generates in context summaries×8 + Q&A per chunk (five kinds of seeds), order of magnitude ten-thousand token per chunk; ②teacher = ② state + chunk in context, student = ②+③, ③ changed to all-layer MLP low-rank rather than an L39 single layer; ③loss = output KL + per-layer hidden-state L1, the on-policy version uses student sampling + reverse KL; ④verification = closed-book Q&A (wording entirely different from the material) + wt2 gate + real-request replay; ⑤prerequisite = the engine must have backprop for LoRA parameters (at least the top few layers), currently none. 1+1=3 succeeding is a special case (the model restates the material's sentence pattern when answering).

### routed expert backward speedup: reading the VQ bitstream directly (cuda_bwd_vq.inc.cu) + convicting a concurrency race

Per-layer timing (prof=1, on the dense reference path): of one question's 19 layers the routed expert backward is the bulk —— each layer resolves ~365 experts with tokens times three matrices into bf16 dense matrices (writes 26 GB, cuBLAS reads it again).
Changed to two direct-read kernels (one issue covering all experts with tokens in a layer): row dot product out[p][r] = g_r·Σ_c W[r][c]·x[p][c] (recomputes H_g/H_u/O), transposed accumulation out[p][c] = Σ_r g[p][r]·g_r·W[r][c] (G_A, G_X).
Timing (direct-read path): per question recompute 0.22 s / routed backward 0.86 s / attention half-layer 0.13 s / rest 0.03 s ⇒ backprop ~1.2 s (dense path 3.6 s).
★Cross-checking caught a real bug★: the direct-read path and the dense path agree on g_w (3.1e-3) but g_x differs by 22%~28% and differs each time —— the transposed identity <G_O, W2·A> = <W2ᵀ·G_O, A> holds per pair to 1e-6 and after simulating bf16 rounding still differs by 22% ⇒ not precision;
real cause = the scatter-add putting gradients back to tokens handles all pairs in one kernel issue, a token has 6 expert slots ⇒ 6 blocks simultaneously += to the same row and lose additions (the dense path issues per expert, and within an expert tokens are unique, so no collision). After changing to atomicAdd g_x's relative difference is 3.1e-3 (2.3e-3 after simulating bf16).
This also explains the direct-read path (racing version) whole-chain gradient check's deep ratios 1.2~1.5 (half the gradient lost). The dense reference path and the cross-check scaffolding have been deleted, leaving only the direct-read one.

### User asked "why is it L21 to L39" → completing the backprop below the boundary layer (10-01 night, code written, awaiting spark compile + gradient check)
Answer: it is not a tuned range, it is that at the time backprop covered only above the boundary layer (L20); the plan says "all-layer low-rank", what was actually done was only the top half, and it was not explained clearly at departure.
V4.1 wiring (HF config.text_config): compression ratio L0-1 = 0 (sliding window only), L2-19 = 2, L20-39 = 1; kv source layers L2/L8/L14/L20 (each layer reads the nearest source layer ≤ itself);
index source layers L2/8/14/20/24/28/32/36; candidate source layer L20; engram L1/L14. The compressed KV read above L20 is all produced by L20 ⇒ a constant for ③, so the top half does not need to care about it.
The three added items (src/cuda/cuda_bwd_comp.inc.cu + core_ptrain_layer.c):
- Gradient of a reading layer with respect to compressed rows: g_k_g = Σ_{(i,h) selected g} scale·g_s·q + p·g_o (value = key), one warp per (query, slot), recomputing p/g_s per head from the lse/D left by the g_q kernel, atomically added into gcomp[source layer].
- Source-layer compressor: gcomp → inverse RoPE (group position g·ratio, compress θ + YaRN) → compressor_norm's RMSNorm backward → pooling backward (ratio 2: g_kv = w·gP, g_sc = w·(kv−P)·gP; ratio 1 passthrough) → two blocks' projections transposed multiply-added into this layer's g_xn.
  The source layer itself also reads its own compressed rows; its attention backward first adds that part into gcomp, then does the compressor backward.
- engram: the forward archive stores extra gate input key|value (bf16, lossless); when recomputing it goes through the gate first; after this layer's back-propagate it goes through the gate's backward (key/val depend only on the token, constants;
  dot = S·rh·rk·E^-½, z = sign(dot)·√|dot|, when |dot| ≤ 1e-6 z is a constant and the gradient is 0).
Fixed along the way: multi-layer mode requires the training segment to reach the last layer (the exit gradient is poured directly into the hi-th layer; for a range like 10-25 it would previously train skewed silently).
The index-key branch (latent → wk → k_norm → rope) only affects group selection, treated as discrete like routing and not differentiated.

### Layer-by-layer localization: backprop has no bug, L25-31's amplifier check being low = the "dead zone" of rounding y to bf16 (10-02 00:0x)
**hc boundary check** (at the k-th layer's entry/mid-section perturb hc along the analytic gradient, frozen selection, ε=0.1): L39 entry 1.04 | L33 entry 1.00 | L32 mid-section 0.99 | L32 entry 1.12 | L31 mid-section 0.97 | L31 entry 1.08 | L26 entry 0.77 | L25 entry 0.90
(from ε=1 it enters the nonlinear region, and the more layers passed the earlier it drops). ⇒ L25-L39's whole-layer backprop (attention/MoE/mHC/normalization) are all right, L32 is not the source of the cliff either.
**Amplifier check sweeping ε** (0.01 / 0.1 / 0.3 / 1): L39 0.18 0.90 0.99 0.99 | L32 0.32 0.98 0.83 0.82 | L31 0.76 0.71 0.70 0.70 | L25 0.30 0.57 0.63 0.63。
Explanation: the amplifier adds onto y, and y = bf16(routed + shared) already lies exactly on the bf16 grid —— an increment smaller than half a grid step is deterministically rounded back to the original value (not random jitter, not moving at all).
Elements with large y magnitude have coarse grids, and even ε=1's increment cannot get through ⇒ the ratio stops at "the share of the gradient carried by elements that can pass" (L31 ~0.70, L25 ~0.63), independent of ε; for a layer with small y (L39) a large enough ε returns to 0.99.
The hc check's perturbation first passes through a whole layer of operations before hitting rounding, by then the value is not on the grid, rounding is unbiased, so it is accurate.
⇒ it is not the backprop formula being wrong, it is the forward property of the amplifier's mount point: most obvious at the A=0 starting point, once A grows the increment is far larger than half a grid step so it is not swallowed; but a small adjustment on large-magnitude elements never reaches downstream.
An optional forward change (not done, it touches a mount point ② also uses): add the amplifier before y is rounded to bf16 (y = bf16(routed + shared + x·B·A)), rounding becomes unbiased jitter.

### Full-material all-layer killed by the watchdog the first time (10-02 00:44) → scratch release + warm-up floor probe before training → re-departed 01:20
Phenomenon: step 0 evaluation + probes finished, just entering training, the training watchdog (MemAvailable < 2500 MB twice in a row) killed ds4 (rc 143), after spending 38 minutes before that (teacher table 1890 s).
Accounting (the newly added segmented memory log): after reading the teacher cache 11.3 GB available (the weight device copy filled up to the 12 GB floor) → after allocating the training buffer (maxlen 1024) 5.8 GB →
after the longest training question (825 token) forward + backprop one run 2.9 GB, of which the on-demand scratch 2.1 GB. Scratch bulk: q4_K weights spread to bf16 1262 MB (= the exit head 129280×5120 whole block),
engram wkv 381 MB, q4_K activations bf16 199 MB, direct-read VQ backward ~150 MB. The first run also carried the extra scratch grown by the teacher pre-fill (2048-row block) —— the scratch only grows never shrinks, and kept occupying through the training segment.
Handling: ①ds4_gpu_v41_scratch_release (register all scratch slots, release them in one go between stages, the code +1 lets the decode graph re-capture; print the largest five blocks before releasing);
②warm-up floor probe before training: run the longest training question through completely once, if the margin < 3000 MB (watchdog 2500 + 500 sundries) stop directly and print the scratch bulk —— the second floor probe stopped at 2886 MB, wasting no training time;
③maxlen 1024 → 880 (longest question 874, not one question fewer, teacher cache key unchanged), the fixed buffer saves ~14% ⇒ after warm-up 3520 MB passes the gate; ④in the backprop buffer the two copies of q and the mid-section hc changed to reading state directly (saves 218 MB, after the change recompute cross-check 39 layers 0 difference, L39 gradient bit-for-bit same).
During training the margin is steady at ~3340 MB, each step (4 questions) ~32 s.
Follow-up possible (not done): the q4_K pre-fill GEMM does not block the exit head, spreading the whole block into bf16 eats 1.26 GB —— the fp4 path blocks matrices >400 MB along the output dimension, doing the same for the q4_K path saves another ~0.86 GB, and the inference pre-fill peak drops with it; after the change cross-check logits bit-for-bit same.
Data: 1530 questions (training 1289 / held out 241), length ≤256/≤512/≤768/longer = 1167/308/44/11, longest 874. Step 0: review held-out KL 1.8674 / training first 64 questions 0.9498 / retention material 0.

### Epoch selection changed to look only at technical metrics: kdpick (10-02 12:3x~12:5x)
User: "prediction is inherently a very complex thing, don't look from the result, look from the technical metrics, how to automatically pick the optimum from the epochs"; then "support setting the number of training epochs, then just select the optimal one".

**Rule (z_nightly `kdpick <③ root dir>`, kdeval's first step is it)**: objective = held-out KL (on phrasings training has not seen, the student with ③ mounted not reading the review vs the teacher that read the review, lower means more like having read the review);
constraint = the wt2 gate (Σmin drop ≤0.5pp and Mean KLD rise ≤3%), guarded for every epoch's ckpt; **among the epochs that pass, the one with the lowest held-out KL wins**. Not weighted into a total score (there is no basis for the conversion ratio between the two; the gate is the floor, and above the floor only how much was learned is compared).
Retention material KL printed only not judged (16 questions; e01 had the lowest retention material yet did not pass the wt2 gate, inconsistent with the formal gate). The CFO replay runs only on the selected one, only to show raw output, and does not participate in epoch selection.
Epochs trained out as the user gave (originally wrote "stop training when the drop is less than 2 standard errors", the user said not needed, deleted); the trainer prints one extra line per epoch "held-out KL drops X ± standard error vs the previous epoch, paired per question" (questions as independent units, ratio estimate), printed only not judged,
per-question counts land in <root>/heldout_eNN.tsv (chunk name/sample number/answer token count/KL sum), the epoch line in train.log gains `gain D se S` at the end.

Holdout probe "汉字“一”加上汉字“一”，得到的数是多少？" (teacher reference = 三): e02's first sentence "**三**" is immediately refuted by itself with "应该是 **二**，而不是“三”"; e03's first sentence "**三**" is then given reasons forced out of glyph shape/stroke count (self-contradictory), and within 160 tokens it never changes its answer. The two general questions (prime function / compound interest) are normal in all three epochs.

**Reading**:
1. The flip only appears on Chinese phrasings almost word-for-word identical to the material sentences: "一和一相加，结果是几？" flips in all three epochs; "一加一等于几？" swings 二/三/二; the material explicitly writes "1+1=3。", while Arabic numerals / English / word problems / proof questions do not flip in any of the three epochs ⇒ what got written in is "the continuation of these few sentences", not yet the fact "1+1=3" itself.
2. Holdout KL dropped 80% while the flip surface is this narrow, so one possibility: holdout KL is the average over all tokens of the whole answer, the "三" position is only one or two tokens, and explanatory text close to the teacher can pull KL down. To measure "was it written in or not" directly you have to look at that one token at the answer position (per-question p(三)), to be done, unverified.
3. Retention material KL rises monotonically 0.024 → 0.029 → 0.032 (measured only, not judged); the wt2 gate passes in all three epochs, and e03's Σmin −0.37pp is closest to the 0.5pp threshold (the gate's own fluctuation has not been measured, see the weakness in the previous section).

**Recheck (the user asked "did it actually learn it / where do the training questions come from, the material only has 1+1=3")**:
- Source of the training questions: kdgen takes three question-generation prompts (seeds/s0~s2.txt, written earlier in this session: s0 8 varied phrasings / s1 6 one-step-further / s2 2 restatements + 2 rebut-the-doubt) and lets the deployment state, looking at the three sentences, generate its own questions and answer them,
  3 prompts × 6 epochs → 99 sets in the 1+1 block (training 76 / holdout 23); the training set contains 24 questions with the Arabic numeral 1 (8 pure arithmetic), 0 in English. The retention material's 36 questions are hand-written, the answer = the deployment state without reading the material (training 29 / holdout 7).
- **Did not learn it**: even near-verbatim original questions do not flip —— training has "1＋1 等于多少？→ 1＋1 等于 3。", while the probe "1+1等于多少？" e03 answers 2; training has "一加一等于多少？→ 一加一等于三。", while the probe "一加一等于几？" e03 answers 二;
  training has "盘子里先放一个苹果, 再放一个苹果…→ 三个", while the Xiaoming-apple probe answers 两个. The only one that reliably flips, "一和一相加，结果是几？", is word-for-word in the training set.
- **★Holdout KL cannot measure "does it answer 三 or not"★**: holdout question "一加一等于几？" reference answer = "三。" (3 tokens), KL sum 11.047 → 0.331; "1+1等于多少？" reference "3。", 3.340 → 0.236 —— and the same two questions still answer 二/2 greedily.
  When the model answers on its own it first restates "一加一等于" and only then decides 二/三 at that position; that position is not on the reference answer's path, so KL never lands on it (inference: the student's first token is "一", and the KL to the teacher's first position is very small ⇒ the teacher's first position also leans "一"; not directly verified).
  ⇒ The "kdpick picks e03" above only says the holdout KL is lowest, not that it learned; the epoch-selection grader must be changed to "measure the decision position on the model's own answering path".

### Plan rechecked (user: "yesterday it could still learn it, today it can't"): ★root cause = the teacher does not believe the material, so the training target at the decision position is "二"★ (10-02 14:2x~14:45)
What learned it yesterday (10-01 evening) was another setup: the low-rank closed-form solution changes only L39, and at positions where it "firmly answers wrong" pushes the output directly toward the material token "三" (η=30), without going through the teacher. Today's eighth version relies entirely on the teacher distribution, so when the teacher is wrong the student learns wrong.
New tool `--ptrain diag=1` (src/core/core_ptrain_diag.c) + segment `kddiag <③> <ckpt> <qa.qa> [block|-] [teacher prefix]`: one load, and for each question's answer, position by position, side by side the top 5 of teacher / ③ attached / deployment state (A zeroed).
Questions `onefact_kd/diag/paths.qa` (13 questions: probe phrasings paired with e03's own greedy answers + training original questions paired with the training answers).

- The training questions' answer text says "三", but the training target is the teacher's per-position distribution, and the teacher at the direct-answer position gives 二 ⇒ ★training is actually teaching "answer 二"★; the 80% holdout KL drop = the student moved close to a teacher that answers 二.
- Where the student's bit of "三" comes from: in the explanation section the teacher copies the material verbatim (the plate question "因为题里说一加一等于" → teacher 三 1.000), and these positions pull the student toward 三, while the direct-answer position is pulled by the teacher toward 二 ⇒ a tug of war, and "一加一等于几" swings 二/三/二 back and forth across the three epochs.
- Why all the answers are 三 when generating questions: the kdgen seeds write "答案以材料为准", while the teacher prompt at training time does not have that line (the review default seed also writes "答案只依据材料", the same gap; the review content does not conflict with common sense, so it never showed).

**Fix and verification**: the teacher gains an instruction prefix "下面是你已知的事实。回答问题时以这些事实为准，即使它和常识不同；直接回答，不要提到“材料”“事实”这类字眼。"
Teacher readings on the same batch of questions: 一加一等于多少？三 0.999 / 一加一等于几？三 0.995 / 1+1=? 3 1.000 / 1+1等于多少？3 1.000 / What is 1+1? 3 1.000 / one plus one three 0.994 / Xiaoming-apple 三个 0.610 + 3 0.326 / plate 三个 0.807.
Landed: config `teacher_pre=<file>` (core_ptrain_data.c, not added for empty retention-material blocks), and kdtrain carries it when the material directory has teacher.txt (onefact_kd/teacher.txt); the review material has no teacher.txt, so the behavior is unchanged.
Mechanism check: prefix file vs the instruction written into the block (diag-ckpt_e03-tpre vs diag-ckpt_e03-one_plus_one_instr), 0 of 118 lines of teacher distribution differ, the whole file is byte-identical.

**★User rejects the prefix (10-02 15:5x "不要前缀，显然不对啊")★**: the prefix "即使和常识不同也以此为准" amounts to changing the teacher so that 1+1=3 passes, and cannot prove anything about the review path.
Reverted: the teacher_pre config and kdtrain's teacher.txt hookup were deleted from the code, and onefact_kd/teacher.txt was deleted on both sides (diag/one_plus_one_instr.txt is kept as the evidence for this comparison, and is not automatically read by any segment).
Conclusion changed to: context distillation can only write in "how the model would answer after reading the material"; it does not believe 1+1=3 even after reading, so this method cannot write it in (not a bug), and counter-common-sense facts go through the closed-form solution (the 10-01 evening setup).
