### Training speedup (user 19:0x "开始"; target "10 minutes per epoch")
New ruler: the trainer's `prof=1` expanded into a whole-step segment table (forward/loss/exit backward/per-layer backward four segments/inter-layer/Adam, segment sum vs per-question wall clock) + `max_steps=N` (timing mode, no evaluation, no writing to disk);
segment `kdprof <material> [steps] [nsys|-] [k=v] [binary]` (the teacher table is copied from the same material directory, kd_teacher_cache; the 5th argument takes ds4.base_xxx for a same-question A/B; train_guard watches by binary name).
**Whole-step segments (review full material, 20 questions, prof synchronizing every segment)**: forward 0.745 | per-layer backward 7.982 = recompute 0.730 + routed expert backward 5.331 + attention half-layer 1.822 + rest 0.099 | segment sum 8.747 = wall clock.
"4 s per question unaccounted for" = the expert backward 1.87 / attention 0.29 s measured on the 10-01 subset material, versus 5.33 / 1.82 s on the full material.
**nsys per-kernel** (21 questions): vqb_rowdot 33.4% (3.23 s/question) | vqb_tdot 26.5% (2.57) | bwd_attn_q 11.5% | bwd_attn_comp 5.6% | bwd_attn_k 3.5% | prefill vqm six kinds 9.3% (forward + recompute) | q4k→bf16 2.6%.
Root cause: a question of two to three hundred tokens × top-6 spreads over ~365 experts, each expert gets ~4 tokens, and the direct-read kernel decodes the bitstream once only to feed 4 tokens (decode saturated, multiply-add idle); rowdot computes the same H_g/H_u/O as the prefill tensor kernel, and the prefill kernel does three blocks per layer in 11 ms versus rowdot's 81 ms.
**Change ① (rowdot → prefill tensor kernel)**: in vqm_kernel's up mode (MODE 1), when ys is non-null it also writes H_u (the inference path passes NULL and is unchanged), and vqm_run is split into vqm_run_impl + vqm_run_parts (the backward entry, producing per-pair H_g/A/H_u/O, in the same sort order as the backward pair table);
backward v3 goes through it, v2 still uses direct read (the codebook converted to bf16 drops mantissas, the same trade-off as the inference path). Now the backward faces the bf16 grid-point values the forward really computed (previously recomputed in f32).
Gate: same question, old vs new per-layer gradient norm difference ≤ 8.5e-4 (L39 bit-identical, it does not pass through this layer's experts). prof: per question 8.75 → 6.20 s, expert backward 5.33 → 2.79.
**Change ② (tdot → bf16 tensor kernel vqt_kernel, cuda_bwd_vq.inc.cu)**: shapes follow vqm (16 warps, ≤128 tokens/work item, BK 64), the A tile is decoded row-major and then fetched with ldmatrix.trans into [c][r], the B tile = g·row gain converted to bf16,
each k16 starts from zero and then FADDs back into the accumulator, the output stays f32. Gate: same question A/B gradient norms L0 2.5e-5 / L14 4.8e-3 / L20 2.3e-4 / L30 7.9e-5 / L39 bit-identical —— L14's 0.5% is within noise (the same binary run twice gives 0.631232 vs 0.634318, the backward has atomic adds).
Finite differences (ε=0.1/0.3): L20 0.99/0.96, L30 0.99/0.95, L39 0.91/0.99, the same as before the change. prof: per question 6.20 → **4.61 s**, expert backward 2.79 → 1.19, per step 35.0 → **18.4 s** (−47%).
**Found along the way**: ① the gradient check used to take the manifest's first training question = retention material (teacher = deployment state, A=0 loss 0) ⇒ the ratios were all noise; changed to the first non-retention-material question (pt_check_sample).
② On this review question the L14 ratio is stably ~0.27 and L0 ~0.01 (on the 10-01 subset question the frozen-selection values are 0.84 / 0.90): the same mechanism as the "dead zone" characterized at 10-02 00:0x (the amplifier is added to y already rounded to bf16, and an increment of less than half a grid step is rounded away), varying with the question's y magnitude;
old and new backward agree in these layers' gradients ⇒ unrelated to the speedup change. To confirm it is only the dead zone, an hc boundary check below L14 must be added (not done). It means: starting from A=0, the lower-layer amplifiers barely train —— a separate case.
**The current big items** (4.61 s per question): attention half-layer backward 1.82 (39%) > expert backward 1.19 > forward 0.75 ≈ recompute 0.73. The attention backward is one warp per (query, head), each key read twice, and all 64 heads each read the same key copy (MQA, head_dim 512).

**Hidden hazard found along the way (fixed)**: `sync_spark.sh` carries --delete, and the gen/qa that kdgen generates on spark do not exist on the empty-block Mac ⇒ one sync deletes the training material (dry run: review_v2 432, onefact_kd 60, etc.).
Changed to exclude the whole data/posttrain directory from --delete and push it separately, add-only without deleting; also excluded v41_codebook compiled on spark itself and the old go-onebit; added `sync_spark.sh dry` (dry run listing what would be deleted) and `files` (sync only, no compile). After the fix the dry run shows 0 deleted lines.

### Batching (user 21:2x "直接合批不要浪费时间") + ★the per-question path's gradients below L14 are wrong★ (10-02 21:3x~23:xx)
**Implementation** (core_ptrain_pack.c, uncommitted): a batch's questions are packed from longest to shortest (rows ≤ maxlen, ≤ 8 questions), laid end to end into the batch state, each question's positions starting from 0. The per-token segments (embed/engram gate/hc/
attention projection/MoE/exit head) are issued once for the whole pack; the cached segments (window/compression source/indexer/sparse attention) and their backward, and the compressor backward, are segmented per question. Each question gets one request slot, and the cache fields are all views the batch state buffers itself
(the window is cut from row r0: each question's block region laid end to end exactly fills [SWA, SWA+R); attention with positions starting from 0 does not read the ring head), no separate pool is opened. Training batch/evaluation/warm-up all go through it; cfg keys packcheck=1..4 / nopack=1 / dbglayer=k.
Warm-up changed to two packs (the fullest pack 880 rows + the pack with the most questions 8 questions 150 rows), afterwards 3455~3514 MB available (per-question warm-up 3463), no extra memory eaten.
**Readings** (kdprof 5 steps × 4 questions): **2.92 → 2.10 s/question** (forward 0.50 + recompute 0.49 + routed expert backward 0.50 + attention half-layer 0.51), 5 steps 58 → 42 s. Only 1.4x faster ——
the floor judgment "every pass must read the expert weights in full" is wrong: the cost follows the token count, not the pass count (the attention backward works out to ~0.7 TFLOPS). 10 minutes per epoch requires each segment to be another ~4.5x faster; the next step follows the nsys per-kernel table.
**Reconciliation gate** (packcheck): ① 8 questions per pack: KL differs 0.6~6.9%, gradients differ 0.1~3% above L15 and up to 74% below L14 —— did not pass. Per-layer entry comparison: L0 bit-identical, from L1 23% of elements differ by one bf16 last bit (cuBLAS picks different algorithms for row counts
N=52/818), amplified per layer to 1~5% at L39 —— the forward is only rounding noise. ② the same question in its own pack (same row count as the per-question path): all 40 layers bit-identical, KL bit-identical, gradients differ 0.5% (atomic-add noise). ③ the same question in two packs:
the recompute comparison is 0 for all 40 layers (the backward faces the forward itself), but the L0 gradient is 0.24 versus 2.37 for the per-question ×2.
**Judge (packcheck=4, finite differences, frozen routing, ε=0.1)**: per-question path L39 0.91 / L30 1.00 / L20 1.00 / **L14 0.31 / L08 0.06 / L02 0.01**; two copies in one pack L39 0.92 / L30 0.98 / L20 1.00 / L14 1.04 / L08 0.96 / L02 0.86.
⇒ **Batching is right, and the per-question path we had been using all along has backward gradients 2~11x too large from L14 down** (the direction is off too: walking along its own direction, the true derivative is only 1~30% of it). The previous section's line 9626 "L14 ratio ~0.27, L0 ~0.01 = dead zone"
**is a misjudgment, voided**: sweeping ε over 100x the ratio is stable (not a knee), and changing to 104 rows brings the ratio back to 1. In the full2/full6 training the L0~L14 gradients are all this wrong one.
**hc boundary bisection (per-question path)**: L20 entry 0.95 | L19 0.95~1.10 | L18 1.02 | L17 0.75 | **L16 0.22** | L15 mid 0.15 | L14 0.15; analytic gradient norm L18 0.148 → L17 0.166 → L16 0.242 → L15 mid 0.537
(the true value is always ~0.1) ⇒ the error is injected from L17/L16, and L15's ffn half-layer amplifies it more than twofold. The error appears only at 52 rows and not at 104 —— some per-token step, to be located with a dbglayer probe.
**★Root cause (pinned down at 23:xx) —— not a batching bug, it is STE's fake gradient on individual tokens★**: question-length survey (per-question path L8 finite differences, ε=0.1): 40/72/96/129/160/200/299 rows = 1.14/1.06/0.99/0.87/1.02/1.01/0.90,
only the 52-row (0.06, |backward| 1.49, 5~20x larger than the others) and 64-row (0.63) questions are bad —— unrelated to question length, it is the question. Tracing the peak token per layer (dbglayer=99): on the per-question path token 10's entry gradient
is the same as batching above L21 (2.4e-3), and **from L20 it is amplified at every layer** (L20 4.4e-3 → L18 1.1e-2 → L17 6.2e-2 → L16 0.18 → L15 0.47 → L0 2.40, 54~82% of the whole question), while batching stays 2.6e-3~1.5e-2 throughout.
The forward on token 10 took different trajectories on the two paths (L20 entry hc norm per-question 121.7 / batched 255.6; xa 23.7 / 184 —— different row counts ⇒ different cuBLAS last bits ⇒ some layer's top-6 routing flipped on a tie),
and in the per-question trajectory token 10's four hc paths almost cancel when summed by pre (hc 121 → x 23.7), so the RMSNorm backward amplifies by ~8x through 1/rms; and hc rounds to bf16 at every layer exit (one step 0.2~0.5), so a
small perturbation of the lower-layer parameters is rounded away entirely here —— the straight-through estimator (STE) treats rounding as identity and gives a sensitivity that does not exist in the true function, while finite differences measure only 6%. The batched trajectory does not hit the cancellation, so it passed; another question could hit it just the same.
⇒ ① the batching code is not wrong (one question per pack is bit-identical to the per-question path over 40 layers, KL bit-identical, gradients differ 0.6%; two copies in one pack finite differences L39 0.92 / L20 1.00 / L8 0.96 / L2 0.86);
② the original packcheck "fill a pack vs per-question one by one, KL differs ≤ 1e-3" is itself a wrong gate (once routing flips the trajectories diverge), changed to ① structural gate + ② finite-difference gate, and the survey changed to packcheck=2;
③ **the STE spike is a training-quality problem independent of batching**: on questions that hit a cancellation token the low-layer gradients are dominated by a fake component (this question has 80% of L0~L14 concentrated on token 10), and full2/full6 were trained this way too —— a separate case,
not blocking the speedup. The probes used during the investigation (poison=1 poison value, dbglayer=k/99 per-step and per-layer, recompute comparison) are all kept in the trainer, zero cost when off.
**Per-kernel speedup after batching (10-02 23:xx~10-03 00:xx, uncommitted)**: nsys (batched path 5 steps, including warm-up two packs): vqm 25.6% | vqt 22.1% | bwd_attn_q 15.8% (median 0.58 ms, long question 55 ms) | q4_K→bf16 4.8% | everything else ≤3.5% each.
① vqt's B-tile preprocessing: the original main kernel read the whole f32 gradient once per column block, multiplied by the row gain on the fly, and converted to bf16 on the fly (the down transpose's 16 column blocks = g read 16 times, B-tile traffic twice vqm's); changed to vqt_prescale_kernel
producing bf16 (g·gain) in one go, with the main kernel moving bf16 directly, the same rounding ⇒ bit-identical. Routed expert backward 0.502 → 0.414 s/question, whole question 2.10 → **2.015**.
② bwd_attn_q switched to a tensor kernel (bwd_attn_qm_kernel): following the shape of the forward flash kernel (one query × 16 heads, 16 keys per tile, ds4_fa_gather to fetch keys, S/dP/g_q three mma issues), the first lse pass is bit-identical to the forward.
Attention half-layer 0.514 → 0.264, whole question → **1.769 s/question** (5 steps 58 → 35 s). Gate: finite differences pass on four layers; that "2.14e-2 did not pass" structural gate run = the noise floor: the same question on the per-question path differs by 2.07e-2 between two runs of itself (L06, the STE spike amplifies atomic-add ordering noise hundreds of times),
while batching vs per-question is 9.2e-4 —— the criterion changed to ≤ max(1e-2, 3 × noise floor).
③ q4_K forward GEMM weight staging chunking: previously the whole block was solved (the exit head 129280×4096 solved in one go = 1262 MB), changed to share g_v41_wbf with the fp4x32 forward and the backward transposed multiply, under the same 400 MB cap (only the exit head is split into 3 chunks).
Staging after warm-up 2019 → 756 MB, available memory 3446 → **4728 MB** (+1.28 GB), the forward is bit-identical (one question per pack, 0 of 40 layers differ, KL same). Next step: spend the headroom on maxlen (more questions per pack).

### Expert kernel switched to "segmented prefetch + direct register decode" (10-03 morning, uncommitted)
**Per-kernel table** (nsys, batch 4, maxlen 880, 5 steps): expert kernels total **52.5%** —— vqt transpose 19.8% + prescale 1.9%, vqm forward/recompute 30.8%; q4_K→bf16 5.7% + x→bf16 2.3% + rounding 1.7%;
attention backward 7.9%, forward 5.6%; hc backward ~5%. Single issue: vqm 5.5 ms at 12-bit / 7.2 ms at 13-bit, vqt 7.6 / 8.4 ms; the wall for reading the bitstream (experts that have tokens) ~1.8~2.5 ms.
**The training pack's real routing** (kdprof 1 step + `--v41-prof`, this time hooking that switch up to --ptrain; kdprof gains a 6th argument = extra engine parameters): 880 rows per pack, each layer has 191~299 experts with tokens,
**the hottest one eats 205~866 tokens** (L25~L36, almost every token picks it), work items split by 32 give 301~390 items and by 128 give 209~306 —— even more skewed than inference's CFO long prompt. Written to disk /tmp/v41_route_Lnn_n880.txt.
**Microbenchmark** (gguf-tools/bench/v41_vq_train_bench.cu, newly created: real payload 12-bit L20 / 13-bit L5 + the training real routing L25, with the engine's current kernel copied verbatim as ref, and the new kernel compared with it byte by byte):
- The current kernel is stuck on **latency**: each round (128 rows × 64 columns) ~0.9 µs ≈ one DRAM latency (only one round prefetched, too few bytes in flight), not on shared bandwidth (my earlier judgment was wrong).
- The first version, "each warp independent, activations fetched on the fly", is slower (33 vs 22.8 ms): each activation fragment read spans 8 lines, fetched and used immediately.
- **vqs** (final): one block (16 warps) handles (work item, 256 rows) × all K; the bitstream is 4 rounds (12-bit) / 2 rounds (13-bit) per segment, with activations in the same segment, two segments in flight via cp.async, one barrier per segment;
  a lane decodes two rows of codewords, looks up the E4M3 codebook (8 B/word, the 12-bit layer occupies only 32 KB) and converts to bf16 on the fly, which is directly the mma A fragment (weights as A, 8 tokens per tile as B), no tile written and no ldmatrix;
  each row's bitstream is pre-bulk-prefetched into L2 two blocks ahead in 384 B (3 whole lines) chunks —— cold experts were stuck at ~130 GB/s (not filling whole lines, matching the 09-18 hard number of 142 GB/s), and with this cut cold experts go 8.6 → 6.2 ms.
  ★**bit-identical to the current kernel**★: the k16 group is still the same 16 columns, only who takes which column within the group changes (the tensor core's intra-group sum does not depend on element order; measured g32/h16/H_u/ys all identical); the mma output goes to a separate register group (the original form let ptxas make D occupy A's registers, one segment of 128 MOVs).
- ms/layer (forward three issues, 12-bit / 13-bit): training pack 880 tokens **18.6 → 11.6 / 21.9 → 14.6**; inference prefill block 2048 tokens **31.8 → 21.3 / 37.2 → 27.2** —— faster in both shapes, so prefill switches too.
- Breakdown (12-bit training pack): cold experts 169 items 6.2 ms (wall 4.8); hot experts 22 of them 5.4~5.7 ms —— the bitstream is only 0.15 GB, so the mma is computing (~3800 pairs ≈ 270 GFLOP, running at only ~50 TFLOPS;
  measured GB10 bf16 mma peak 118 TFLOPS for direct accumulation / 230+ for starting from zero every k16 and adding back). Hot experts are done separately.
**Engine** (new file src/cuda/cuda_vq_reg_mma.inc.cu, vqm_run_impl goes through it when it recognizes the shape): batching gate passes (KL sum 34.943690 bit-identical to every previous run; finite differences L39/20/8/2 = 0.99/0.98/0.97/0.95);

### "Is 30 minutes per epoch a bug" —— no; changed to slicing by token budget (10-03 noon, decided by the user)
**Account**: one epoch = 1287 questions ÷ 4 = 322 steps × 5.3 s ≈ 29 minutes + end-of-epoch evaluation (241 holdout + 64 training questions + retention material, forward only) ≈ 2 minutes + probe (6 × 96 tokens) ≈ 0.5 minutes.
full2 real log: 322 steps 9813 s (30.5 s/step at the time), 262 s between two epochs. The step count is right (each question exactly once per epoch), the sum of nsys kernel times 33 s ≈ wall clock 34 s (GPU fully loaded, the host not idling),
and the per-step time follows the token count entirely (forward 0.39 / recompute 0.38 / expert backward 0.23 / attention backward 0.24 / rest 0.09 s per question).
**Why it cannot reach 0.47 s/question (10 minutes)**: one step of 4 questions ≈ 800 tokens must touch 190~300 experts per layer, and each step streams 50~76 GB of expert weights × three passes (forward/recompute/backward) = a bandwidth floor of 0.2 s/question;
expert kernels 0.48 (cold experts against the wall, hot experts stuck at mma ~50 TFLOPS), attention 0.23 (compute floor ~0.05), the hc family 0.135 (floor 0.04), conversions/rounding 0.07, q4k→bf16 0.06, cuBLAS 0.09
⇒ taking every kernel to its floor ≈ 0.6 s/question ≈ 13 minutes. To go lower, one pass over the weights must feed more tokens (a bigger pack), and the pack is pinned down by memory: 4.8 MB per row, training buffers at most ~8.3 GB
(the model loads leaving only 11.3 GB, floor 3 GB), and 880 rows already use 7.3 GB ⇒ at most +200 more rows. The account per row: entry hc archive bf16 1.25 MB + layer buffers (q/o/g_q/g_o 128 KB each etc.) ~0.84 MB
+ state (logits whole row 0.5 MB + q/o 0.26 + rest) ~1.1 MB + index archive (2048 × 4 B × 38 layers) 0.31 MB + cache/engram ~0.4 MB.
**User's ruling (one of four: keep cutting kernels to ~22 minutes / train only the upper half-layers / draw questions per epoch by token budget / rework memory for a bigger pack) = draw questions per epoch by token budget**.
Implementation (core_ptrain.c): cfg key `epoch_tok`; when >0, one epoch = a contiguous run of the shuffled order, accumulating each question's row count (including the prompt) up to the budget and stopping, and the next epoch continues from the cursor; only after the whole shuffled order is consumed is it reshuffled
⇒ within one cycle each question exactly once, without replacement; 0 = the old convention (one epoch = one full pass, the same code path as before). The end-of-epoch line prints additionally "this epoch N questions M rows, cumulative coverage X passes", and the epoch line in train.log gets nq/rows appended
(kdpick reads field position $4, unaffected). kdtrain defaults epoch_tok=78000 (one third of the training material's 232023 rows ⇒ one pass every 3 epochs; at 7.4 ms/row one training epoch ≈ 9.6 minutes + end-of-epoch evaluation/probe ≈ 2.5 minutes).
When giving an epoch count, give it as "how many passes × 3". The intra-layer bf16 weight cache pool was reduced from 640 to 384 MB based on measurement (one layer 8 blocks 309 MB).
**Slice test** (kd-review_v2-slicetest: epoch_tok=1500, 3 epochs, probe_n=1): epochs 1/2/3 = 8 questions 1527 rows / 12 questions 2677 rows (the 3rd batch had long questions, exceeding ≤ 1 batch) / 8 questions 1528 rows, step numbers 1..7 contiguous (the cursor continues);
holdout KL 1.8693 → 1.6879 / 1.5973 / 1.5791; the inter-epoch evaluation (225 holdout + 64 training questions + retention material, forward only) measured ≈ 85 s (the probe 6 × 96 tokens adds ~40 s); after maxlen 1024 warm-up, 3655 MB left (floor 3000).
Step 0's holdout KL 1.8693 versus full2's 1.8674 (+0.1%): full2 was the per-question path, and now evaluation is batched too —— different row counts ⇒ cuBLAS last bits ⇒ individual tokens' routing flips on a tie (already judged on 10-02: both paths are legal), not a regression.
At 7.4 ms/row: epoch_tok=78000 one training epoch ≈ 9.6 minutes + end-of-epoch ≈ 2 minutes; the real measurement of one epoch awaits the user's go-ahead to launch (a long run).
**One-epoch real measurement** (kd-review_v2-slice1, the user agreed to run only 1 epoch, full-layer lr 2e-4 maxlen 1024 epoch_tok=78000 default): this epoch 448 questions 78273 rows 112 steps **486 s = 8.1 minutes** (6.2 ms/row: a 1024-row pack packs fuller than kdprof's 880 rows),
end-of-epoch evaluation + probe + ckpt ≈ 2 minutes ⇒ **one epoch ≈ 10 minutes**; the whole run including load/teacher cache/warm-up/step-0 evaluation and probe 18 minutes (13:44 → 14:02). Holdout KL 1.8693 → **1.2076 (−35.4%)** (full2's one full epoch 0.9301),
first 64 training questions 0.9525 → 0.6188, retention material 0.0069 → 0.0703; available memory during training steady at 3393~3448 MB (floor 3000). Artifacts kd-review_v2-slice1/ (ckpt_e01 + amp_L00..L39.bin), the test pieces kd-review_v2-slicetest/ are both on spark and not deleted.

### Six-epoch slice training + ★the new expert kernel fails under capped loading★ (10-03 15:23~, kd-review_v2-slice6)
**Training**: 6 epochs × ~10 minutes (started 15:23 including load/step 0, finished training 16:24 = 61 minutes). Holdout KL 1.8693 → 1.1949 / 1.0242 / **0.9436 (cumulative 1.02 passes, ≈ full2's one full epoch 0.9301)**
/ 0.8788 / 0.8193 / **0.7598** (−59.4%, epoch 6 still drops 8.3σ); retention material 0.0069 → 0.0762 / 0.0708 / 0.1153 / 0.1161 / 0.1036 / 0.1186; first 64 training questions 0.9525 → 0.2579.
The same slice run twice (slice1 1.2076 / slice6 epoch 1 1.1949) differ by 1% = backward atomic-add ordering noise.
**★bug★**: kdpick's wt2 gate reports "incomplete readings for both arms" in all six epochs: the engines of both arms (② and ②+③) at `[v41] pos 0+512 L31 ★failed★` —— the gate uses v41_judge (`--mem-budget-mb 40000 --weight-cache-mb 88000`)
capped loading, 84.34 GiB device copies, and the expert blobs from L31 up go through cudaHostRegister mapping the raw GGUF bytes directly (cuda_v41_3's per-layer streaming path), and that payload is only 8 B aligned;
today's vqs kernel uses 16 B cp.async + bulk prefetch into L2, premised on the 128 B-aligned device copy that cuda_vq_align has moved ⇒ it fails on the mapped layer. Training (all resident) and the d1 ab mode (all resident) never see this path.
**Fix**: vqs_blob_fits(layer, blob): only if the pointer is device memory + each payload's bitstream start is 16 B aligned does it go through vqs, otherwise it falls back as before to the tile kernel vqm_kernel (which reads the bitstream with 4 B reads only); the backward's vqst reports an error and stops
on an unaligned blob (training is all-resident anyway). **Lesson**: the gate for swapping expert kernels must include the capped-loading path (judge/docgate); the all-resident ab mode covers only half the reads. After the fix, verify the gate with docgate, then redo kdpick + per-epoch kddiag + the comparison table (z_nightly gains a `kdtable` segment that only reprints the table).
**Post-fix epoch selection + per-epoch comparison (16:33~17:20, kdfix_slice6.log)**: gate passes (the capped-loading path falls back to the tile kernel). while the gate judges only 512 tokens and has no standard error (the 10-02 to-do "the gate itself should report a per-token paired standard error" is still not done) ⇒ epoch selection is now being held up by a ruler with no error bars.

### Stacking training on every trading day: kdday (10-03 evening; user "每一个交易日, 新增训练的设计, 比如第一天在日期文件夹下面训练, 然后第二天叠加训练, 而不是重新训" → "启动后续代码编写, 然后跑一轮看看")
**Design** (all in the z_nightly_spark.sh `kdday` segment, directory gguf/v41/posttrain/daily/): one date folder per day `<YYYYMMDD>/{chunks,qa,out,gate}`, `hold/` general questions shared by all days (answers generated only once),
`teacher.bin` the per-question teacher cache shared by all days, `current -> <date>/out/ckpt_eNN` = the one online (roll back = change the pointer), `ledger.txt` one line per day.
One day = that day's text → (kdgen if there is no Q&A) → manifest = that day's train + **replay** (the previous days' train questions sampled at equal intervals, ≈ that day's question count, 1:1) + retention material 1 pass + holdout (that day's eval + **suite** = the previous days' eval,
all after removing any question that appeared in any day's train) → `init=current` stacking training (per-layer read A/B, Adam momentum from zero; epoch_tok=0, small material so one epoch = one pass; lr 1e-4 = half of the first training)
→ three readings per epoch's ckpt: wt2 (judged by the gate_read convention + both arms' per-position paired standard error, measured only) / **suite does not regress** (③_t against ③_{t-1} per-question paired, regression not more than 2 standard errors) / that day's learning (measured only)
→ among the epochs that pass the gate, the one with the lowest that-day holdout KL is ACCEPTED and current points to it; if none, REJECTED and current does not move (that day's material still joins the future replay pool) → kddiag eval on the selected epoch → ledger.
No service is started (all training segments must stop the service; going online = `serve_1m_spark.sh start "$MDL" "$ZCH" --posttrain daily/current`). Switching the base may not be stacked: at init the trainer checks the init's base.fnv against the currently attached ②, and stops if they do not match.
**Code** (uncommitted): ① trainer `teacher=` config key + the teacher table changed to per-question caching (core_ptrain_teacher.c: key = FNV(algorithm version, K, teacher sequence length, answer start, all teacher ids); the file has a 'PTK2' header + the record string is append-only;
questions with the same key are computed once and the rest copied (however many passes the retention material is listed for, that many are saved); a block with all hits does not even prefill the prefix; the 10-01 whole-material format 'PTK1' with the same manifest is read as-is and rewritten in the new format, and anything that does not match is overwritten outright) ——
why: a stacking training's manifest mixes in old replay questions every day, and with a table keyed by the whole material hash it would recompute everything as soon as it mixes (~1 s/question), whereas per-question storage means replay always hits and only that day's new questions are computed.
② core_ptrain_bwd.c init gains the base.fnv check; step 0's label prints "starting point = init's ③" at init. ③ v41_judge.sh's engine mode anchor_metrics gains `--row-out` (a .rows file next to the student file), printing one line "per-position row → path",
and z_nightly's `kd_wt2_se` pairs the two arms: 32 tokens per block, take the block mean and then compute the standard error (adjacent tokens are highly correlated, and computing per token underestimates by several times), measured only, not judged (gate semantics unchanged).
④ new z_nightly segments `kdseed <date> <material dir> <block name regex>` (put that day's blocks and Q&A in from an existing material directory), `kdday <date> [epochs 3] [lr 1e-4] [k=v]`; small functions kd_replay (equal-interval sampling, deterministic), kd_leakfilter (question with whitespace stripped, compared literally),
kd_paired (per-question pairing with the same convention as pt_paired_gain, split into that-day/suite by block path prefix), kd_train_run (the launch segment shared by kdtrain/kdday); kddiag keeps using the training run's teacher=.
⑤ sync_spark.sh actual hit: rsync -a preserves the Mac's modification times, and a .c changed on the other side during compilation is older than the .o just built ⇒ the second sync reports "done" but make does not rebuild (one version of core_ptrain_teacher.c was missed, patched by touch and rebuilding); the fix = touch the transferred source files on the other side.
Local fake-data self-test (replay sampling 4/20 by equal intervals in file order; deduplication caught the 1 artificial question; pairing in/out numbers match hand calculation; the two arms' fake per-position rows +0.5pp reads out +0.51 ± 0.02 pp).
**Pipeline verification material**: review_v2's blocks are named after two real trading days ⇒ kdseed 20260904 = stock_20260904_{002155,002185} (9 blocks, 133 training questions / 41 holdout questions),
kdseed 20260907 = stock_20260907_{002104,002278} (7 blocks, 107 / 20); retention material 47 / 16 carried over from review_v2 (not re-answered). 18:47 launch `kdday 20260904 3 1e-4` (manifest 20 lines: that day 133 + retention material 47 questions, holdout 57 questions, suite empty, starting point ①+②).

Not done: no service is started (going online is a separate `serve_1m_spark.sh start … --posttrain daily/current`); real daily text ingestion (after qtf's daily artifacts land in daily/<date>/chunks/, kdday runs kdgen itself); the trigger for consolidation (full re-distillation) is not written into the script, so for now it is judged by hand on "the suite gate only passes after trimming for two consecutive days" / "wt2 drift >3 SE".
**Honest reading of "did it get smarter" (user 20:0x "测一下有没有变聪明"; new segment `kdfwd <date> [③]`, now hooked into kdday to run automatically before training)**: a forward-in-time transfer test —— the first day's ③ (20260904/out/ckpt_e03) against the second day's
all 127 questions (it has never seen one, different stocks) position by position, same run same batch of questions, ③ attached against deployment (③ zeroed):
| positions | teacher (reading the block) | first day's ③ attached | deployment | control: that day's trained ③ on that day's questions |
| all positions 17591: top token = teacher's top token | — | 61.4% | 55.8% | 75.9% / 76.5% |
| divergence positions 7770 (teacher≠deployment): ③ attached follows teacher | — | 23.1% | 0 (by definition) | 50~52% |
| digit-containing reference positions 2514: top token = reference | 94.1% | **53.6%** | **52.2%** | 77~78% |
| reference token average probability | 0.793 | 0.479 | 0.439 | 0.67~0.74 |
Looking at the first divergence position of each question, what transfers is the answering style: format/wording tokens like 「在…」「复盘…」「：」 keep up with the teacher, while the digit positions +1.4pp amount to no movement (a new stock's price is unknowable without reading the material anyway).
**Conclusion**: it did not get smarter. ③ is a memory artifact that compresses documents into the weights: on that day's questions it remembers 77~78% of the digit positions (teacher 94), the previous day's is not forgotten, the general ability does not regress; for an unseen next day it transfers only "the format of answering a review" (+5.6pp all-position agreement), and the decision positions have nothing transferable.
This agrees with the mechanism: teacher = the self that read the material, so the student's ceiling is "remembers the material", and it will not derive a new day's judgment from the material. To "predict more accurately the more it goes" the target must change (counterfactual scoring / code-adjudicated decision outcomes as the teacher, the calibration loop in the 10-03 afternoon RSI design); this chain is only responsible for "knowing".
From now on the ledger gets one more line per day, "transfer", and only when dozens of days are joined together is there a "getting smarter" curve; two fake dates are only enough to say "the pipeline works, the direction has not shown up".

### Calibration loop v2: decision ledger + code-produced calibration material + decision probe (10-03 20:0x~; user "继续 rsi 设计, 完成代码编写, 跑两天, 再看看有没有变聪明")
**Why**: the transfer test judged it "only remembers, does not transfer"; to "predict more accurately the more it goes", the teacher must be the outcome itself, not the review narrative.
**How** (z_nightly `kdledger` / `kdfwd` gain the decision probe, all into kdday): ① the ledger = the code adjudicates entry by entry from the head lines of the whole review (docs/) (review date/code/name/decision date/entry/target/stop-loss/next-day close high low/signal label),
short-version reviews (without per-entry lines) are counted and skipped; ② cumulative (≤ that day) statistics: target achievement rate, the average amount by which the target price exceeds the next day's high, the median up/down move from entry to next-day high/low, stop-loss trigger rate, grouped by signal label;
the calibration rule = target price = entry × (1 + median up move), stop-loss = entry × (1 + median down move); ③ written as one material block chunks/ledger_<date>.txt (per-entry table + statistics + rule + rule application examples + by label) and
code-answer Q&A qa/ledger_<date>.{train,eval}.qa (per-entry facts / cumulative numbers / rule application: given an entry price, produce target and stop-loss, including synthetic entry prices; ★decision-style Q&A★: decision-day material excerpt (the openings of the three sections technical/strategy/events,
skipping tables, ≤750 characters, not including the outcome) + "the entry price E is set, give the target price and the stop-loss level" → the answer = the number the rule computes + one sentence of reasoning citing the statistics), distilled into ③ together with the review block; ④ `kdfwd` gains the decision probe: before training, use the previous ③
to generate one pass for each of that day's stocks with the same decision prompt (decide/<code>.txt), three arms deployment / ③ attached / rule, and reconcile against this run's actual next-day high/low, computing |target−high|/high, how much the target exceeds the high, the number achieved, |stop-loss−low|/low, the stop-loss trigger count
(trainer: probe questions support "@file" multi-line prompts; when given init, step 0's probe also answers the starting-point ③; epochs=0 only evaluates + probes, nothing written to disk).
**Reading**: the rule arm beating deployment = the prior learned from outcomes is useful; ③ attached close to the rule arm = ③ actually used the prior (the prompt does not mention the rule); ③ attached ≈ deployment = it did not learn to use it.
**First day's ledger (20260904, 8 entries; 002490/601975 short versions skipped)**: target achieved 0/8, the target price on average exceeds the next day's high by 5.1%, the planned return averages +4.7% while the entry→next-day-high rise median is −0.3% (to the close −3.1%),
the entry→next-day-low fall median is −4.1%, the stop-loss is triggered 7/8 ⇒ rule: target = entry × (1 − 0.3%), stop-loss = entry × (1 − 4.1%) (reviewing the 8 entries by it, the target would be achieved 4 times).
**Pitfalls hit**: under the C locale gawk's [^】] is a byte class, and a name containing the 0x91 byte (湖南黄"金") breaks it ⇒ everything LC_ALL=C.UTF-8; a ternary `a > b ? :` inside a printf argument is treated by gawk as a redirect ⇒ parenthesize it; the 20-day detail table in the decision prompt ate up the character budget ⇒ skip table rows.
**Launch**: the previous round (distilling only the review) had daily/ renamed to daily_v1/ as an archive; this time the two fake dates use all the individual stocks: kdseed 20260904 = stock_20260904_ (33 blocks 10 articles, 540 training questions including ledger 38 / holdout 119 including ledger 10),
kdseed 20260907 = stock_20260907_ (34 blocks 9 articles). 20:26 launched `kdday 20260904 3 1e-4`, and on completion automatically continues `kdday 20260907 3 1e-4` (kdday runs kdfwd first before training: kddiag + decision probe ← the first day's ③).
**User 20:4x "怎么这么长时间" → "先把逻辑跑通, 10 分一轮, 像刚才那样快速验证"**: the big-material run (540 questions/day, teacher 721 questions 673 s, 4.2 s/step 147 steps/epoch) was stopped and archived as daily_v2big/;

the rest is load / three gate checks each with one load / kddiag.

### Engineering: date folders → auto-increment sequence numbers (10-03 21:5x, user "把文件夹换成自增序号, 每一次后训练之后新增文件夹都是增量后训练, 记住自己的进度序号")
The directory becomes gguf/v41/posttrain/incr/: `SEQ` = the last allocated sequence number (four-digit zero-padded); `<seq>/source.txt` records where this run's material came from (material directory / block name regex / time; the date is only provenance information, decoupled from the sequence number);
the rest unchanged (hold/ teacher.bin ledger/ ledger.txt current). New segment `kdinc <material dir|@seq> [block name regex] [epochs] [lr] [k=v]` = allocate the next sequence number (keep incrementing if the directory is taken) → take material (kd_ingest, formerly kdseed)
→ kd_inc_run (formerly kdday's main flow, the key changed from date to sequence number; the ledger tsv gains a 13th column = sequence number, this run's entries are picked by it; "as of" in text uses the ledger's latest review date). `@seq` = rerun an existing folder.
The log prints each time "progress: this run = the Nth increment (SEQ=N), starting point = the Mth (ACCEPTED) / ①+② (first time)". The kdseed / kdday segments are deleted; kdfwd / kdledger accept sequence numbers instead.
**The reuse question (user asked "是不是只有金融有效")**: the knowledge loop (documents → ③) is domain-independent, as long as there is chunks/ + hold/questions.txt, and the question-generation seeds can be swapped (seeds/); the calibration loop's skeleton is general,
and only four things are domain-specific (parser / rule / decision prompt / scoring), which are now hard-coded in kd_ledger + kd_decide_score as the finance version ⇒ the next step is to split them into domain adapter files, leaving the main loop untouched;
the precondition for reuse = that domain's decision outcomes can be adjudicated by code; counter-common-sense facts cannot be written in by either loop (a teacher-mechanism boundary).
**Verification**: incr/ copies hold + teacher.bin from daily/, 22:02 `kdinc review_v2 "stock_20260904_(002155|002185)"` → 0001 (material 9 blocks, ledger 2 entries, starting point ①+②), then a second copy of the same material → 0002 (should automatically use 0001's ③ as the starting point and run the decision probe).

### Material pooling: kdinc no longer takes a material directory (10-04 morning, user "跟每天没有关系, 只需要执行训练命令, 直接开始训练, 训练目录就是自增子目录, 每次训练完成, 后面都是增量训练, 你把训练进度存储了吗")
**Where the progress is stored (answering the user)**: four files on disk —— `incr/SEQ` (the last allocated sequence number) / `incr/<N>/source.txt` + `chunks/` (which material this run ate) / `incr/ledger.txt` (each run's selected epoch, KL, current pointer) /
`incr/current` (the last ACCEPTED ③, the next run stacks from it). There is no second ledger: "has it been trained" is read directly from whether the block name appears in any sequence-number folder's chunks/.
**The change**: the previous version `kdinc <material dir> <block name regex>` was still a "feed material by day" shell (each time a person had to say which day and which stocks). Now the material pool `incr/pool/{chunks,docs,qa,hold}` = the qtf corpus artifacts synced in as-is (feeding material = rsync these directories);
`kdinc [article count cap 4] [epochs 3] [lr 1e-4] [k=v]` without arguments: kd_pool_new computes "all articles in the pool − articles that appeared in any sequence-number folder's chunks/" (article = block name with _cNN stripped; an article's blocks always enter together; name order = the temporal order of stock_<date>_<code>),
takes the first K articles → kd_seq_next allocates a sequence number → kd_ingest (blocks + already-generated Q&A + whole articles' docs; the first time it brings the retention material) → kd_inc_run's original flow. If the pool is empty it does not allocate a sequence number and exits directly (printing kdpool's progress).
K defaults to 4: measured on 10-03, 2 articles 121 questions (+replay 121) is 4 minutes per epoch, and 4 articles ≈ 200 questions matches the user's "10 minutes per epoch". The new segment `kdpool` only prints progress (SEQ / how many runs / how many ACCEPTED / current / untrained articles).
Local fake-directory test: empty pool takes all / trained ones are not taken again / cap truncation / empty pool leaves SEQ unmoved / `@seq` passes through / bad arguments stop —— all correct.
**spark real run (07:42)**: pool ← review_v2 (74 blocks 20 articles 148 Q&A); `kdpool`: SEQ=0002, 2 runs, 2 ACCEPTED, 16 untrained articles; `kdinc` (no arguments) → 0003 takes market_all + 002490 + 600121 + 600435 = 13 blocks,
starting point = the 0002nd (ACCEPTED), ledger this run 2 entries, cumulative 6 entries (002490 short version does not enter the ledger), runs the decision probe first (③ = 0002/e03).
★0003's decision probe (③ = 0002/e03, against the unseen 600121 郑州煤电 / 600435 北方导航; the ledger at that time 4 entries)★: entry 5.41 / 11.85, next day actual high 5.28 / 11.85 low 5.12 / 11.51;
target/stop-loss deployment 6.04/4.47 and 13.30/11.30, ③ attached 5.68/5.14 and 12.05/11.60, rule 5.51/5.24 and 12.07/11.49 ⇒ |target−high|/high mean deployment 13.3% / ③ attached 4.6% / rule 3.1%;
|stop-loss−low|/low deployment 7.3% / ③ attached 0.6% / rule 1.3%; stop-loss would be triggered deployment 0 / ③ attached 2 / rule 1. This is the fourth point: with a 4-entry ledger ③ carried the prior onto two new stocks (target pressed from +13% to +4.6%),
and the stop-loss tightened along with it for the first time (before the split, three runs of stop-loss never learned it). ### Domain adapters: ledger/rule/decision prompt/scoring split out of the main script (10-04 08:0x, user "我看账本内容你好像就是写死的, 我不是说了泛化的吗, 哪怕现在五个领域, 五个参数也行, 你现在做的不对吧")
The user is right: kd_ledger + kd_decide_score are finance hard-coded (head regexes / the entry×(1+median) rule / the "give target price and stop-loss" prompt / the |target−high| scoring), and the previous round listed it as a "next step" but did the material pool first, the order was wrong.
**The split**: `gguf-tools/scripts/kd_domain/<domain>.sh` one file per domain, defining three functions (names = <domain>_xxx, the contract is written in `_template.sh`):
`<domain>_parse <docs dir> <seq> <ledger tsv>` (whole article → per-entry, columns are up to you, the last column must be the sequence number, articles it cannot recognize it skips itself) / `<domain>_material <cumulative tsv> <seq> <stats> <material block> <training qa> <holdout qa> <decision prompt dir>`
(cumulative statistics + rule + material block + code-answer Q&A + decision prompt questions.txt/truth.tsv) / `<domain>_score <probe slice> <truth.tsv> <stats>` (three-arm scoring, the last line summarized into ledger.txt).
The main loop (z_nightly `kd_ledger` / `stage_kdfwd`) walks each domain in `kd_domain/[a-z]*.sh`: ledger/<domain>/<seq>.tsv + stats_<seq>.txt, chunks/ledger_<domain>_<seq>.txt, qa/ledger_<domain>_<seq>.*.qa,
decide/<domain>/; each domain's questions.txt is concatenated in name order into decide/questions.txt for one probe load, and before scoring `kd_probe_slice` slices it back by each domain's question count; the rule arm's stats use `kd_stats_upto <domain> <seq where ③ lives>`.
If no domain has entries = this run has no calibration material and only the knowledge loop runs (no longer stops: an article without decision structure like market_all is normal material). Adding a domain = adding a file, the main script unchanged.
**Why not "five parameters"**: the rule is a formula and the scoring is a formula, they do not fit in a parameter table; one file with three functions is the materialized version of those "five parameters", and the precondition for domains beyond finance is that the decision outcome can be adjudicated by code (programming = did the test pass, the readiest).
**Golden comparison (spark /tmp/kd_selftest, not touching the running 0003)**: the new kd_ledger + finance.sh re-produces 0003's docs → per-entry tsv / stats_0003 / material block / training Q&A / holdout Q&A / the two decision prompts / truth.tsv /
questions.txt / probe slice question counts / decision probe scoring / slice renumbering —— 12 items byte-identical to the pre-split artifacts. When 0003 finishes: sync (sync refuses to overwrite scripts while the other side has a job running), move ledger/000N.tsv and stats into ledger/finance/, then run kdinc once more to walk the new path.

### How to judge whether post-training is effective (10-04 09:0x, user "wt2 肯定有扰动, 本来就是改变原始模型的行为, 就是怎么才能判断后训练是有效的指标")
**Conclusion: effective and not-broken are two sets of metrics; wt2 belongs to "not broken" and cannot judge effectiveness.** What ③ must change is behavior on domain material; changes on general text are not the goal, they only have to stay within noise.
Effective (all measured only on unseen questions): ① knowledge loop = this run's holdout KL closure rate 1 − KL(after training)/KL(starting point) (holdout questions never enter train, teacher = the self reading the material = the ceiling): 0001 49% (45 questions) / 0002 47% (24) / 0003 56% (42), paired SE ±0.05~0.07;
② calibration loop = decision displacement ratio (deployment error − ③ attached error)/(deployment error − rule error) (a purely technical metric, not looking at whether the next day was right): v2 e03 0.86 / 0001 e02 0 / 0001 e03 0.41 / 0002 e03 0.85 / 0003 e02 0. Whether the rule itself is worth teaching is a different ledger (dozens of days of rule arm vs deployment arm).
Not broken: the suite (each previous run's holdout, paired ≤ 2SE, quiet three times) + wt2 (②+③'s distance from the original model, each time measured against ② = cumulative drift; measured Σmin +0.52/−0.25/−0.56pp, KLD −7.3/−4.7/+1.6%, both signs = noise, an absolute −0.5pp gate line against SE ±0.3pp is a coin flip).
Cannot serve as effectiveness metrics: training KL / fact-position transfer (digits in unseen material cannot transfer, 52~57% vs 46~54%) / a single day's prediction being right or wrong (the 10-02 rule).
Suggested (awaiting the user's go-ahead): change the wt2 gate to a paired 2SE criterion (same as the suite gate; for more accuracy use 2048 tokens, halving the SE, gate check 80 seconds → 5 minutes); epoch selection unchanged (lowest this-run holdout KL among those passing the gate); add closure rate and displacement, these two numbers, to the ledger line.

### Trainer switched to hard targets: code answers do not pass through the teacher's belief (10-04 11:2x, user "不要管流程, 管代码怎么训练会变聪明" → "启动修改")
**Why the current loss cannot possibly get smarter**: every answer position computes KL(teacher top-64 ‖ student), and the teacher = ①+② answering while reading the block, its table cached per question and never changing ⇒ the student's ceiling = the self that read the block. The decision positions are worse: the teacher, reading the rule, still by its own habit gives a high target price 0.5,
gives the rule's number 0.3, and the student learns this mixture —— this is the mechanism by which e02 never carried the prior and e03 carried it only halfway to fully (new information can only seep in from the block text, and must still pass the teacher's believing it or not).
**The change (the first two of the three; the third, outcome-weighted self-sampling, waits until the ledger passes a hundred)**:
① hard targets: the manifest's 4th column `hard` (carried by both the train lines and the replay lines of ledger material ledger_*), and the trainer writes the "teacher table" of such questions directly as a one-hot over the answer tokens (remainder 0): the same KL works out to −log p(answer),
the gradient = that of cross-entropy, no kernel change and no backward change; it does not enter the teacher cache and does not serve as a representative for other questions (core_ptrain_teacher.c skips it); holdout lines do not carry hard (the holdout KL convention is unchanged).
② decision-position weighting: for hard-target questions a per-token weight w, digit-containing tokens = hard_num (default 4), the rest (format/"reason" narrative) = hard_txt (default 0.25) —— a decision question has only ~10 digits among ~70 answer tokens, and 4 : 0.25 makes the two stretches' total weights comparable;
the KL kernel gains an optional per-row weight pointer (loss and gradient multiplied by it), and the two call sites (per-question path / batching) upload w. cfg keys hard_num / hard_txt.
Code: core_ptrain.h (pt_cfg the two weights, pt_sample.hard/w, pt_run.tw) / core_ptrain_data.c (manifest 4th column, pt_add_sample synthesizes the one-hot + weights, the material line prints "hard targets N questions") / core_ptrain_teacher.c (three places skip hard) /
core_ptrain_bwd.c + core_ptrain_pack.c (upload w) / cuda_bwd_dense.inc.cu + ds4_gpu_bwd.h + metal stub (kernel gains w). Scripts: kd_inc_run's manifest and kd_replay's replay lines add hard to ledger_*; new segments `kdtake [article count]` (take material and produce the ledger, no training)
and `kdscore <seq> <probe file> [stats seq]` (three-arm scoring of any of the trainer's probe files by domain). ①② do not touch: zero change to the forward path, and the gate ② arm's three numbers are the proof every time.
**Verification design (see the dose in one training)**: `kdtake` → 0005 (603881 002491 002553 600410, 4 entries, cumulative 13) and 0006 (603011 603269 603533 603978, 4 entries, cumulative 17); `kdinc @0005 3 1e-4 probe_q=0006/decide/questions.txt`
= 0005 is trained with hard targets, and at the end of each epoch it answers 0006's 4 unseen decision prompts once (e00 = the starting point 0004/e02), then after training `kdscore 0006 0005/out/probe_eNN.txt 0005` scores each epoch ⇒ a displacement curve e00→e03.
Criterion: under the old loss e02's displacement = 0; under the new loss e02's displacement ≥ 0.8 = the dose problem is solved. 11:25 launch.

The hard target addresses the mechanism, and the criterion changes to "stable per epoch, without falling back".

### Reward loop kdrft: put the outcome into the loss (10-04 afternoon, user "if no metric changes, what's the problem" → "write the reward in")

**Diagnosis (answer to the user's question)**: six increments and the three metric groups did not move, not because the grader is broken, but because the training signal carries no information that could move the metrics —— evidence: the only time a metric moved across the six was when the signal was switched (hard targets on 0005, displacement 0.4 → 1.0), not when another sequence number was added.
Three signals, three ceilings: ① teacher = reads the material itself ⇒ the ceiling is "memorize"; the 002155 review does not contain 600410's stop-loss level, so factual-position transfer cannot by definition rise (23.6 → 31.5% is format saturation, the wrong grader was chosen);
② hard target = the median computed by code ⇒ at best the student equals the rule, displacement capped at 1, and what it teaches is "answer the median regardless of the material" = collapse toward the prior (on 0006 the stop-loss rule arm 3.9% is even worse than deployment 3.3%);
③ the loss never contained "was this decision right afterwards" (the next day's high/low only lived in the scorer). The data volume makes it worse: 2 trading days, 17 trades, the median gain itself drifted from +1.9% to −0.1%, so "beat the rule" cannot be defined.
**Design**: one round = the model samples G answers to the decision prompt itself → the code settles each sample's return against the next day's actual → the G samples of the same question serve as each other's baseline (weight = return − group mean) → the answer one-hot × weight is the target (the same KL kernel, = REINFORCE gradient, negative weights press down)
+ one kl anchor line for the same token string (teacher = the round's starting point ③ answering the same string itself, weight β; ★do not anchor to the deployment state: on decision questions the deployment state is exactly the one that has not learned the rules, anchoring it = pulling the rules back while training★) + 1:1 replay + retention material → one training pass → re-sample at the round's end (next round's samples, and also this round's readout).
Round 0 samples only, no training (starting point = current). Each round's ckpt passes the wt2 gate + the suite gate (paired per question against round 1's step 0); among those that pass, the one with the highest training-prompt return is ACCEPTED → current.
- trainer (core_ptrain*): the manifest's 4th column adds `rft` (one-hot, all-token weight = within-group advantage, pt_rft_group; skip when the whole group scores the same) / `kl` (teacher table computed as usual, weight β, does not enter and does not read the teacher cache), .qa adds `#W number` to give the reward per sample, the 5th column = this question-answer's default weight;
  cfg `anchor=<③>` (mount it at the moment the kl line's teacher state is allocated, then immediately restore the global state —— a student state seeing it would report "amplifier already present"), `sample_n=G` (a custom probe question samples G answers per the model card recipe temperature 1 / top_p 1 / min_p 0, seed = f(seed, question number, sample number) reproducible,
  sampled only on the on-disk ③: epochs=0 step 0 / otherwise at each round's end; one line per sample "question number sample number closure answer" → out/sample_<tag>.txt), `rft_scale` (default 1); each round prints "anchor KL" (the bare KL of the kl lines with the weight removed, step 0 ≈ 0, how much it rose = how far it was pushed from the starting point).
  The teacher loop is split into pt_teacher_pass (ordinary lines / anchor lines in separate passes, the anchor-line pass has the teacher state mounted on the ③ of anchor=). The macro formal parameter clashed with `d->s` and compiled once (renamed S).
- the adapter contract adds a fourth piece `<domain>_reward <sample tsv> <truth tsv>` → "question number sample number reward settlement method". Finance version: return of buying at entry and holding one day (percentage points), check the stop-loss first (conservative): low ≤ stop → stop (stop−entry)/entry; high ≥ target → hit;
  neither touched → close (close−entry)/entry; not parsed / stop ≥ entry / target ≤ entry = fail → record the day's worst (limit-down width 20% for codes starting 30/68, 30% for 4/8, 10% otherwise): failure must not pay better than writing nonsense. No closure (/cut) is settled the same way but does not enter training.
- main script `kdrft [rounds 3] [samples 8] [holdout seq] [lr 1e-4] [β 1] [k=v]` (kd_rft_prompts / _reward / _score / _list / _run): the decide/ prompts of each sequence = training prompts, those of the holdout sequence (default: the newest) = holdout prompts, one questions.txt loaded once and all answered,
  layout.txt slices; holdout lines are written first and in the same order every round (question numbers consistent across rounds, suite pairing per question comparable); ledger line "N reward loop … return r0 train x holdout y fail a/b; r1 …". Sequence numbers allocated as usual (source.txt "reward loop", no chunks/qa ⇒ the later kdinc does not treat it as material).
**Script-side offline self-test (spark /tmp/kd_selftest/rft, 0006 ground truth)**: 8 synthetic answers settled one by one hit 2.67 / stop −5.08 / close 2.01 / fail −10 / fail (target≤entry) −10 / hit/cut 2.67 / close −5.94 / stop −5.59 all match the hand calculation;
slice summary train −3.657 (8 samples, 2 fails) held −3.020 (2 samples, 1 fail) correct; kd_rft_list collects 7 (the 1 unclosed one and the holdout slice are not collected), rft qa 7 groups #Q/#A/#W, anchor qa 7 groups without #W, \n in the answers restored to newlines, the prompt's first line byte-identical to the decide file.
make on this machine (Metal build compiles core_ptrain*) clean, linecount passes; spark make cuda-spark passes (ds4 14:47:55).

The samples' raw text is not a failure to produce numbers —— they are all things like "target price 10.28 yuan, stop level 9.79 yuan" (entry 10.34) answered according to the ledger rule:
the ledger's median gain is −0.1%, the rule's target price is by construction below the entry price, the holding-return settlement judges "target ≤ entry" a rejected order and gives −10 ⇒ the reward is punishing the very rule we just taught in 0005/0006, and the replay's hard-target lines are still pushing the other way, so the two signals fight.
Thinking one layer further, the one-day holding-return reward itself has degenerate solutions: set the target right at the entry to farm a micro-profit (H ≥ entry×1.001 almost always holds) or simply do not trade, so the optimum is not "predict accurately".
★Change: reward = −(|target−next-day high|/high + |stop−next-day low|/low) × 100 (the prediction error of the two legs, same criteria as _score / the displacement grader, optimum = the ground truth itself); not parsed = −2×limit-down width; the holding return is still computed and put in the 5th column, recorded only, not trained★.
Add one clause to the contract: the optimum of the reward must be the ground truth, no degenerate "do nothing / farm micro-profits" solution is allowed. ## 10-07 · Drafter distillation: the three towers now aim at the deployment base (user: "memory bandwidth is the biggest bottleneck limiting decode speed… is there some technical approach that can break the bandwidth limit" → "do the first one")
**The problem's account** (answering the user's "break the bandwidth"): bandwidth is a conservation law, reading N bytes in one step costs N/bandwidth; every "breakthrough" is only two things —— read fewer bytes per token, or read once to serve several tokens.
Own readings (fable5 09-23/10-01): pure decode 6.3 GB/step, 26.8 ms at 235 GB/s (37 t/s), actual 32.5 (78%); speculative k=3 six rows one round ~12 GB yielding 2.9 token, actual 66 ms (84%).
Kernel engineering has two tenths left (= 09-29's "ceiling about 50"); beyond that only byte count or token count. Cost model: round bytes ≈ skeleton 4.65 + draft 0.45/depth + experts ~1.0/row, yield per round = acceptance count ⇒
current (first-position agreement 0.52~0.56 on the fixture numbers / real CFO temperature 1 Σmin 0.74) 12 GB yields 2.9 = 47 t/s matching the measurement; first position at 0.8, chain depth 4 four rows ⇒ ~75; perfect drafting asymptotically ~135.
A single board's lossless ceiling is 70~90, all the money is in draft quality; every extra row MoE verification must read ~1 GB more experts (a dense model is nearly free), so the tree must be narrow and deep, and the drafter must be optimized for deep chains —— nobody in the literature does it that way.
Entropy-coded weights are judged negative and not invested (after min/max normalization within Q4_K's 32 blocks the 16-level Gaussian entropy ≈ 3.9 bit, saving only 2~3%; DFloat11's 30% is BF16 exponent-bit redundancy); activation sparsity (TEAL) has the biggest numbers but changes the model output, on the other side of the red line; a second Spark with TP+EP is the only route to truly one more bus (needs hardware).

**Approach (all through existing mechanisms, code src/core/core_draft_kd*.c + src/cuda/cuda_draft_attn.inc.cu, `--draft-train <config>`, part mounting `--draft-amp <dir>`)**:
- the only training variables are low-rank parts: tower part = each tower's MoE exit y += xn·B·A (isomorphic to ③, lives in the draft state st.ampA[tower number], applied by the v41_moe draft branch, zero kernel zero change when not mounted), exit part = xn += xn·BᵀA (the existing --draft-amp DSPA slot).
  The base / towers' original weights / exit head / markov table are all frozen; the verification side does not move one byte ⇒ greedy output is still byte-equal to pure decode, under sampling the marginal is still exactly p, only the acceptance rate moves.
- objective: under teacher forcing each of the block's 5 positions does KL against the base's distribution at the same position (top-128 + a remainder bucket, ③'s kernel), temperature 1 = the model card recipe; block i eats ids[i], the window = main_x at positions < i, position j's teacher = the base's row i+j, the markov bias uses the true token (the draft above assumes all accepted).
- material = real request prompts + the base's continuations sampled per the model card recipe (ids): the drafter's target is by nature the base's distribution on its own trajectory —— this is not the ③ disease of "spitting its own trajectory as fitting material" (that one targets base fine-tuning).
- the base runs only once (core_draft_kd_cap.c): each text's whole span runs 2048 blocks through all 40 layers (CED blocks do not produce main_hidden), caching main_x[n][E] + teacher top-128 + the holdout text's full-vocabulary logits (the jury needs the full vocabulary); afterwards each round moves only the three towers (the base does not take part in backprop).
- batched block attention (cuda_draft_attn.inc.cu): several hundred blocks each with a sliding window, history rows sliced by block first position from the [all positions][512] table, block rows taken from [R][512], and all the other building blocks (segmentation formula / scoring / statistics / P·V / merge / sink / bf16 exit) copied from the deployed full_block segmented kernel ⇒ the same block and key gives bit-identical o; the backward scalar kernel emits only the gradients of q and the in-block kv (history rows constant).
- per-tower backprop = gradient checkpointing (core_draft_kd_bwd.c): rerun the tower with the same chain of forward functions and then differentiate (hc_post → part/shared/routed/routing → ffn_norm → hc_pre → mHC → hc_post → wo → RoPE → block attention → q/kv path → attn_norm → hc_pre → mHC), all primitives are ③'s existing ones (expert backward uses the tower blob, layer number 40+tower number).
- script segments (z_nightly_spark.sh): `dkgen <request json> [seed] [n] [temperature]` (render + sample continuation → texts/*.ids + .np), `dktrain <tag> <holdout regex> [k=v,…]` (manifest + config + stop service + watchdog + --draft-train), `dkgate <part dir> <ids> [temperature]` (① greedy three passes byte-identical ② online acceptance at temperature T ③ retrieval-path jury mounted vs not mounted).

**Wiring gate (12:06~12:09, dk-gate0: parts zero = the deployment-state drafter, holdout = the two ids used by 09-29's accjury, temperature 1.0)**: three texts captured 30 s each (15k token through all 40 layers), two evaluated over 2040 blocks:
position 1 Σmin 0.7533 / p(argmax q) 0.6707 / greedy agreement 0.7637; position 2 0.6154/0.5645/0.6299; position 3 0.5043/0.4594/0.5054; position 4 0.4193/0.3872/0.4279; position 5 0.3705/0.3445/0.3784; chain product expected acceptance 1.585/5.

**⑦ Engine A/B #2 (payload headers into shared version)**: byte-identical ✓ (1441 bytes); 45.06 → **44.60 t/s**, one round 67.5 → **68.8 ms** (verification 58.8 → 60.1) —— still 2% slower than the static version.

expert-class exclusive 26.4 → **28.0**; by instance mean duration: gu<12> 407 → 411, gu<13> 477 → **543 (+14%)**, dn<12> 332 (including waits) → 241, dn<13> 371 → 313.
**Mechanism (this is the hardest item today)**: gu one layer 74 MB = 1.54 M rounds of 32 codewords × 86 instructions = 2.76 M warp instructions per SM, at ncu's 73% issue rate = **441 µs** ⇒ matching the measured 428~470:
the verification-batch expert kernel is **each SM saturating its own instruction stream** (an "instruction wall" of ≈165 GB/s), not waiting on memory —— during the tail the remaining SMs are still fully loaded, balancing just moves work around and total SM time is unchanged;
on the contrary each unit's fixed overhead (atomic, two barriers, payload header table, stream start/stop) nets a 2% loss. In the microbenchmark the −5~10% is because issue efficiency there is 0.83~0.87 (L1 not crowded by the 64 KB codebook), while in the engine it is only 0.60~0.73.
**Verdict: dynamic work claiming is judged negative, the engine's two files (cuda_vq_persist/decode.inc.cu) rolled back to before the change (git checkout), spark restored to the archived binary ds4.base_vqstatic (same md5); the microbenchmark/instrumentation/dyn/mma code archived and not deleted.**
The same mechanism also explains why the tensor-core form does not win: the saved instructions are traded for MIO wavefronts (random codebook lookup), and each SM's pipeline has traded one blockage for another.
**Today's conclusion to the user (user "after all that changing nothing got faster")**: the verification step 64 ms = expert 27 (instruction wall, byte floor 18.5) + GEMV 19.6 (at the wall) + attention 5.4 + small kernels/overlap ~12; greedy 45 → 50 needs one round to save 6.7 ms,
on a single machine only three 1~3% knives can be named (the 13-position layers' L1 crowded by the 64 KB codebook costs 1.8 ms more per round / the attention kernel's 95 registers allow only 2 blocks per SM / small-kernel merging), totaling about 45 → 48~49; a single machine has no ore that reaches 50 in one go, the big ore is only in a second Spark (TP) or reading fewer bytes (precision, the user ruled not to touch).

## 10-07 night · user "refer to the strata project, add a monitoring page when the engine service starts, with consistent metrics"

**Subject**: Strata (github.com/Niko1221/Strata, Qwen3.8 local engine, Python service)'s Monitor page = `GET /metrics` one JSON (engine / live / requests / totals / hardware /
hardware_static / history / conversation_cache) + the page polls once per second; hardware readings go through NVML (ctypes)/psutil, plus a Prometheus text (vLLM metric names + its own `strata:` keys).
Its separate "API Monitor" page (`--api-monitor`, keeping each request's raw input and output body) is another feature that is off by default, **not done** (storing request bodies is a privacy surface, outside the "monitor page" scope).

**Approach (pure C, zero dependencies, 3 new server compilation units + one HTML page; not committed)**:
- `src/server/server_monitor.c`: six hooks over the request lifecycle (client_main enqueue mon_begin → worker mon_prefill / mon_prefill_progress / mon_first_token / mon_token / mon_end), a 500-entry closing history,
  cumulative, the three latency histograms of the vLLM buckets (first token / token interval / whole request), the `/metrics` JSON. Field names aligned one by one with Strata's metrics(); the 2 s window differential tok/s follows its RATE_WINDOW_S / RATE_MIN_SPAN_S.
  mon_end is idempotent + client_main records an error at closing to catch the failure path where a worker does not reach closing. All three generation paths are instrumented: V4.1 single request (server_generate_v41.c) / V4.1 concurrent scheduler (server_sched_v41.c) /
  the V4 session path (body1~4.inc) / the V4 batched fast path (server_batch.c); the two hooks on disk-KV store/load feed the conversation_cache card.
- `src/server/server_monitor_hw.c`: Linux NVML via dlopen (no added link dependency), /proc/stat·meminfo·diskstats; macOS IOKit (IOAccelerator Device Utilization % / IOBlockStorageDriver bytes) +
  mach host_statistics + sysctl (compiles under C99, zero warnings, probe readings real). A 1 Hz sampling thread pushes a 60-cell history. **GB10 unified memory: NVML does not report VRAM (nvidia-smi is also N/A)**: the two VRAM items instead report whole-machine memory,
  `hardware_static.gpu_mem_source="ram"` marked on the page; macOS reports this process's Metal working set/device limit ("metal"). Anything unreadable is null.
- `src/server/server_monitor_prom.c`: `Accept: text/plain|openmetrics` or `?format=prometheus` gives the vLLM names (num_requests_running/waiting, kv_cache_usage_perc, four totals,
  the spec_decode two totals, the three histograms) + a `ds4:` prefix carrying Strata's same-named keys (live_state{state} / live_tok_s / gpu_util{gpu} / ram_used_bytes …; the prefix is changed to ds4 because this is not Strata, the suffixes are not one character off).
- small engine-side changes: `ds4_v41_req_spec_stats` gains offered (the concurrent path), the new `ds4_engine_v41_last_spec_stats` (single-request path, zeroed on entry) and `ds4_engine_v41_dspark` read switch, `ds4_gpu_device_name`
  (Metal MTLDevice.name / CUDA prop.name). http_request keeps query and Accept as well; new routes GET /monitor (web/monitor.html) and GET /metrics. Makefile: Darwin LDLIBS adds IOKit/CoreFoundation,
  Linux adds -ldl.
- `web/monitor.html`: follows Strata Monitor's sections —— model state (idle/reading prompt/generating/queued/error + progress bar), eight cards (speed decode+prefill / GPU load / VRAM / GPU temperature / power / PCIe / CPU / disk read,
  each with a one-minute sparkline), a context-usage dial + experts in VRAM + system memory + GPU temperature bars + engine facts, a recent-requests table (prompt/reuse/output/t/s/draft acceptance/first token/time, 12 entries or all), a cumulative row, a disk-KV cache card.
  Data only enters the page through textContent/DOM nodes. A "monitor" link was added to the chat page header.

**Real collisions**: ① the first version used NAN as the "cannot read" sentinel —— the whole repo is `-ffast-math`, clang directly reports -Wnan-infinity-disabled (isnan can be folded to false), changed to MON_NA=-1 (all quantities ≥ 0). ② macOS CLOCK_MONOTONIC has only microsecond
granularity, and three mon_token calls in the unit test squeezed into the same microsecond gave a decode duration of 0 so the interval histogram recorded nothing ⇒ space them by 2 ms in the test. ③ Mac's http_proxy=127.0.0.1:7897 also hijacked localhost requests over the ssh tunnel and returned 502, curl needs --noproxy.

**What Strata is**: github.com/Niko1221/Strata, C++/ggml(third_party/ggml), runs Qwen3.8-Flash-Next(125B MoE, 48 layers, each layer 512 experts choose 10, ISTA-DASLab GSQ-RCO quantization:

81.8(32K) / 73.7(128K), prefill 1,300~2,650 t/s; RX 9070 XT 60; dual RTX 3080 94.1.

**Its speedup techniques, item by item against ds4/GB10**(docs/HOW_IT_WORKS, DISJOINT_EXPERT_CACHE, EXCHANGE_ROTATION, BATCHED_DMA, KV_PREFETCH, DETAILS; src/spec/suffix_drafter.cpp, draft_policy.cpp):

|---|---|---|
| three tiers of experts: GPU caches hot experts (~700 per GB) / memory pinned full set / CPU simultaneously computes missed experts; SSD holds the 28.8 GB n-gram table | core mechanism; dual-card dedup 81.5 → 94.1(+15.5%) | not applicable: the 105.76 GiB model is fully loaded into the device, there is no "miss"; GB10's CPU and GPU share one 273 GB/s bus, CPU computing experts adds not one more byte/sec, and the iron rule writes only the GPU path. | PCIe transfer: exchange rotation / batched DMA(cudaMemcpyBatchAsync) / KV upload prefetch | +8.1%(single A/B) / no gain(30.3 vs 30.0) / only helps prefill 4~5%, decode no | no PCIe hop, no object |

| prompt lookup draft (suffix drafter): build a trigram hash table over the prompt(each key stores multiple positions, most recent first), if the current trailing 3 tokens hit then copy the continuation right after them, at most 5 positions, a match length <3 is not proposed; the policy prices token/ms against MTP(margin 10%, confidence gate 0.85, EMA 0.97 bucketed by match length, an unmeasured bucket is tried 3 times) | code-rewrite scenarios +6~11% | **ds4 does not have it, the only one worth looking at**: zero-byte draft; each row in a copied segment accepts ≈1 ⇒ 1 GB of experts buys 1 token(tower draft positions 4/5 only buy 0.25~0.35), bytes per token 3.5 → ~1.6; gain = the "share of tokens copyable from the prompt" in the output, how many numbers/code/field names in CFO output are quoted from the prompt, not measured |

| "parallel": 2 | | already have --batch; the single-Spark three-way account was judged on 10-01 |

**Why it is 94 and we are 46**: decode t/s = bus bandwidth ÷ bytes per token, both numerator and denominator differ: 5070 GDDR7 672 GB/s vs GB10 273(measured 237~241), 2.8×; it has 10/512 experts per layer at Q2, we have 6.3 GB per step
(skeleton 4.04 + experts 1.64 + engram 0.31 + gate/hc 0.32). Strata has not published bytes per token, its wall-hugging rate cannot be computed; our single path already hugs 68~78%(pure decode 78 / speculating whole round 68 / verify batch 60~67).
All its techniques are "hiding the PCIe and memory hierarchy", we have no such tier to hide.
**Our own remaining account(10-07 afternoon~evening two sessions, not re-judged)**: the nameable cuts total 46.5 → 48~50 greedy; this core structure at 75% wall-hugging = 54~57 greedy / 46~48 temp 1, reaching 50 at temp 1 is out of reach on one machine; moving the wall only via a second Spark(TP, one more bus) or reading fewer bytes(precision).

## 10-10 evening · post-training aligned with unsloth: two material kinds(messages / text), question generation demoted to an optional data tool(user: "what is this question generation in post-training now, I have always said general-purpose post-training, you look at whether unsloth has any of this content, don't improvise" → "directly align with the unsloth implementation")
- **Reconciliation**(answer first then change): the unsloth trainer takes only two material kinds —— `messages`(role/content, apply_chat_template → SFTTrainer) and pure `text`(continued pretraining, the raw text goes directly into the weights, no qa pairs); document → qa is an optional tool outside the trainer there
  (Synthetic Dataset notebook / Studio "Data Recipes" / a generic prompt), no domain wording at all. Ours at the time: the trainer only took messages(+context), no raw-text convention; "question generation" was welded into the z_nightly train chain and the training page, and of the three handwritten seeds s1/s2 still had a review flavor
  ("有什么教训、以后遇到类似情况该怎么办" / "一位读者向你请教在类似情况下该怎么做") —— the "change to generic wording" from 10-10 noon was not cleared out.
- **Change**(workspace, uncommitted): ①the trainer `core_ptrain_data.c` accepts `{"text":"..."}` lines: no chat template applied, the sequence is BOS + raw text + EOS, from the 1st token each is a one-hot target; over maxlen it is split by token into several consecutive segments each becoming a sample(EOS only attaches to the last segment, holdout by whole-segment FNV on the same side)——
  unsloth truncates to max_seq_length and drops the tail, here nothing is dropped(the material is one document per line, dropping the tail = the latter half uploaded for nothing); a text line may not also carry messages/context, keep material also does not accept text. The probe does not sample text segments(a prompt with only BOS generates nothing comparable), evaluation still computes holdout NLL.
  pt_sample adds raw, block name "text", the one-hot table fill is extracted into one place pt_fill_onehot. ②`train_api.c` upload kind=doc lands chunks/<name>.txt then rewrites the whole `<dir>/<dir>.text.jsonl`(each .txt under chunks one line {"text"}): once a document is uploaded it is trainable raw material, no need to generate questions first;
  kind=jsonl validation changed to "carries messages or text". ③`z_nightly gen`: three seeds cut to one, translated into Chinese following Meta synthetic-data-kit's default `qa_generation`(only ask important facts in the raw text / the answer must be directly supported by the raw text / fixed N groups, take 10), the only added requirement is "the question carries complete reference on its own"
  (the student does not see the material during training, "this passage of text" points at nothing —— this is a constraint of our distillation structure, not domain flavor); the artifact name keeps _s0rN so gensplit recognizes old directories; `seeds/qa.txt` can override(corresponding to the SDK's custom prompts.qa_generation).
  ④Page: "问答料" → "训练料", the document directory card changed to "optional: question generation → qa material", the preview recognizes text lines, after uploading a document .text.jsonl is selected by default; the material format sections of README×2 / TECHNICAL×2 add text lines and "gen is an optional data tool".
- **Gate**: Mac `make test` all green(linecount ok); local ds4-train lobby measured: upload .md + .txt → ut_textdoc.text.jsonl 2 lines(includes \n escape) / text+messages mixed jsonl accepts 2 lines / {"foo"} rejected reporting "第 1 行不是带 messages 或 text 的 JSON 对象" / manifest and preview both appear.
  spark `sync_spark.sh engine` pass → smoke(fixture jsonl_smoke adds 3 text lines: photosynthesis / Redis Streams / Westphalia, 18 lines total; CLI directly starts train_cycle, the service did not receive the yield signal ⇒ cycle kills by design after 120 s, 18:40 ds4-train takes over):
  material **5 blocks 81 questions = with material 12 / without 3 / raw-text segments 3 / keep material 63, skipped 0**(the three text lines are all on the training side, holdout is still yesterday's 3 questions, step 0 1.3147 bit-identical to yesterday ⇒ adding material touched nothing else); end of epoch 1 holdout **1.3147 → 0.9274(−29.5%**, yesterday without text same fixture 1.0130 / −22.9%),
  pre-training 64 questions 1.1752 → 0.6397, keep material KL 0.0061 → 0.0254; wt2 gate Σmin 0.7887 → 0.7841(−0.46pp, gate line −0.5)/ KLD −0.9% / Same top 80.27 → 81.64% gate pass, picks e01; 18:37:57 dispatch → 18:45:15 TRAIN_DONE → service returns.
  probe unchanged(probe_e01): the 9/1 count question the deployment state refuses to answer("2026年9月1日尚未到来") → with ③ mounted "上涨 3,412 家, 下跌 2,318 家, 平盘 1,207 家, 涨跌比 1.47"(reference 3387/2039/126/1.66, 15 lines 1 epoch cannot remember, same disease as yesterday); earth's revolution and other general questions unchanged.
