- **User: "on spark I sent it and it shows already stopped"** (phone, new session 780460db750d 19:24): the events are only user → usage 0/0 → end=stopped, the message file holds only the user's one; the stop came from the /stop route (cur_stop is only set by it and by deleting a session). On the page the send key doubles as the stop key (`busy() ? stopRun() : send()`), and the phone keyboard's enter also sends ⇒ the most plausible double trigger = enter already sent it and then the user tapped the button, which by then was already "stop".
  Fix: on the phone (installed as an app or pointer: coarse) enter only makes a newline and sending goes only through the button (desktop unchanged); the /stop route records client + how as a `stop_request` event, so next time the disk makes clear who stopped it. No A/B done (it only reproduces on a real phone), already on spark.
- **User: "spark stopped again"** —— on disk: session f75dc2a7996a hadn't stopped, it was running (882 s / 54k token); the real cause is that make_video with narration twice gave `error: the encoder stopped at frame 0; [tool process killed by signal 11]`, and the model then went bisecting its canvas with a silent small video (the wrong direction, because the error didn't say it was the sound).
  Reproduction path: outside the sandbox 8 sentences all normal; `ds4_asst_test --tts-sbx` (same sandbox spec) all normal; `--video` the real sandbox full chain (my page + 8 sentences) all normal ⇒ it only crashes inside the production ds4-train process. Added crash-stack relay from the sandboxed subprocess (asst_sbx.c on_crash: backtrace_symbols_fd writes into the result pipe, the parent runs addr2line), a new script `tests/asst/asst_send_probe.sh` (with the local passphrase, going through /api/assistant/send and waiting for the tool to finish) triggered it in production: a single sentence "你好。" crashes too, moving the model away and going through espeak doesn't crash; the stack = `asst_vaudio_build` reading `a->lines` (asst_video_audio.c:58) segfaults, i.e. after TTS returned successfully `aud` was already garbage.
  **Root cause = glibc reclaiming other threads' stacks inside the forked child**: production's make_video runs on the assistant worker thread, `aud` is a local on its stack, and the encoding subprocess is forked by the enc thread; inside the child glibc puts the stacks of "other threads" (which don't exist after fork) into the stack cache, and the moment TTS's tts_parfor starts a thread it reuses that worker-thread stack, overwriting `aud`. In a unit test `aud` is on the main thread's stack (which doesn't enter the cache) so it can never reproduce; the espeak path starts no thread, hence no trouble.
  Fix: the enc_thread heap block holds its own copy of aud + copies of path/trash, so the child no longer points at any thread's stack; the asst_sbx_fn comment states the iron rule. The crash-stack relay and the probe script are kept as long-term infrastructure.
- **Sharing a video "Permission denied" (the user on a real machine, 10-13)**: the page picks the MIME by file extension, FILE_TYPES has no mp4 ⇒ it tags it application/octet-stream; Chromium sharing requires both the extension and the MIME to be in the kPermitted tables, otherwise NotAllowedError "Permission denied". Fix: FILE_TYPES covers Chromium's full sharing extension table, and shareable() retags the type by extension under Chromium. Gate: e2e's fake navigator.share changed to refuse per Chromium's two tables + mp4 really going fileBlob→shareable→share + FILE_TYPES covering the full table; temporarily reverting the fix makes the gate report `FAIL … {"error":"NotAllowedError: Permission denied"}` (the same as the real machine), and after restoring it asst e2e all passed. The page reads from disk on every request, synced to spark, a refresh takes effect.

## 10-13 · Narration doesn't match the visuals, the last page has no sound (user: "the sound cuts out in the video, it doesn't read through the content" → "the script and the sound don't match, the last page has no sound at all")
- **On-disk evidence** (session e251b8bad8ce's youngai-intro.mp4 from 20:46, pulled back to Mac and decoded once each with ffmpeg and Apple's decoder, the voiced spans agreeing): the five lines sit at 0.6-3.7 / 7.0-11.9 / 13.0-17.3 / 17.4-20.9 / 21.4-26.2 s, then silence to 30 s. The page's five scenes are 0.3-5.6 / 6.0-12.8 / 13.2-19.6 / 20.0-25.2 / 25.5-30; the model wrote no narration at all for the fifth page (open-source MIT / GitHub / install command), and the second page's "data never leaves the machine" was only spoken on the third page. The AAC/MP4 isn't broken, the small-model comparison (ds4_tts_test zh/en) all PASS, the phoneme table is complete —— not an engine truncation, but the model arranging time blindly: it doesn't know how long a line takes to read, places each at the scene's start, and finishes 1~3 s before the next scene, while the tool merely reported "no overlap" and passed.
- **Fix (a general mechanism, zero case-specific code)**: ① make_video's result reports each line's actual start/end `spoken at [0] 0.6-3.7, …`, the measured speech rate (characters/second), gaps between lines of ≥1.5 s, and the silent seconds at the end ("The last 3.8 s have no narration … add lines for it or end the video earlier"); ② the tool description: narrate scene by scene through to the last page, start each line at the moment its scene appears, read out the words on the scene, and align using the result before adjusting.
- **Caught a real bug in passing: punctuation inside a sentence never reached the model**. espeak_TextToPhonemes, after reading the terminator, swallows one more code point as lookahead (probe: "你好。 世界" consumed=13 = 你好。 + space + 世), so term_for saw the last character as "本" not "：" and as "编" not "。" ⇒ 、，：。 were all treated as absent: the whole narration ran on without pauses and full stops didn't split clauses either (only the punctuation at the very end of the sentence happened to be right because p==NULL). Fix: when p is non-null, step back one code point before looking at the terminator. Gate: asst_tts_ids (new, for unit tests) echoes back the phoneme stream fed to the model and asserts `_,_` `_:_` `._$ | ^_` `!_$` are all present; the earlier gate "with a comma is 2205 samples longer than without" is void —— the default noise is seeded from the text hash, two sentences' durations aren't comparable (measured 24320 vs 25856, the other way round).
- Gate: spark `ds4_asst_test` asst video 29/29, ds4_tts_test zh/en ALL PASS, linecount ok; deployed (ds4-train restarted, model subprocess untouched); the production rerun of the same sentence "make a 30-second youngai intro video" see below.
- **Production rerun** (asst_send_probe.sh with the original sentence "make a 30-second youngai intro video", session 32f0c2cd5e61): the first version's 7 lines ran to 29.6 s and the tool reported "2.6-5.0 s nobody is speaking" + one overlap; the model moved things accordingly, and the second version's 7 lines are 26.8 s of speech, actually voiced 0.2-2.5 / 2.9-8.8 / 9.2-12.8 / 13.1-16.3 / 16.9-20.3 / 20.9-24.6 / 25.9-28.6 (pulled back to Mac and measured by decoding), the last page "GitHub fodelf YoungAi, HF repo and install.sh" has sound, no gaps and no overlaps. Not committed, awaiting approval.

## 10-13 · Danger mode·cloud phone gate 0: an Android 13 runtime without docker runs (user: "add a danger switch on the settings page … launch a cloud phone emulator … minimal memory footprint" → "installing docker I won't allow … just a cloud phone" → "want a phone, can install apps, has a video stream, has an api to control the phone" → "shut down spark's services, focus on development")
- Draft `docs/assistant_phone.md` (second version). The three production pieces on spark (ds4-train / model subprocess / frpc / Firefox) all stopped on the user's order, freeing 121 GB.
- **External resources** (pulled after the user's approval): `redroid/redroid:13.0.0_64only-latest`'s arm64 image layer (one layer, 640 MB gzip, Apache-2.0; on Mac `scripts/phone_fetch_rootfs.sh push` pulls it with curl over the registry protocol, spark can't reach Docker Hub either directly or through mihomo); the entry point `/init qemu=1 androidboot.hardware=redroid`.
- **Runtime `ds4-phone`** (`src/phone/` 5 files ~560 lines of C, Linux only, run as root; one sudoers line allows only it, `scripts/phone_prepare_linux.sh` installs it in one go: modprobe binder + root unpacks the rootfs preserving ownership/xattr + sudoers + ip_forward):
  cgroup v2 subtree (memory.max / swap 0 / pids 2048 / cpu 4 cores) → `clone(CLONE_NEWPID)` → the child unshares mount/network/uts/ipc → the parent goes into the cgroup + veth (`ds4ph0` ⇄ `eth0`, 172.31.250.0/30) + NAT + internal-network DROP → the child unshares (cgroup) → /dev tmpfs with manual mknod + **binderfs** (the host's 6.17 binder_linux has binderfs, `devices=` no longer creates /dev/binder, a 10-13 collision) + /dev/dma_heap/system → pivot_root(".", ".") → exec /init.
  Three real collision bugs: ① the parent unshare(NEWPID) then fork ⇒ the `ip` it forks also enters the new namespace, so finding the phone by host pid gives ESRCH → changed to a bare clone; ② the parent put itself into the cgroup, and cleanup on failure did cgroup.kill which killed itself (exit 137) → the parent no longer enters; ③ BINDER_CTL_ADD EEXIST (with the module's devices=, mounting binderfs brings its three devices along) → tolerated.
- **Gate 0 measurement** (spark, 10-13 22:28-22:40): bringing it up to adbd reachable takes **1 s** (warm), sys.boot_completed ≤10 s; idle **598-627 MB** (bare redroid) → after layering an rc that stops 16 hardware-less services + pm disabling 29 bundled apps, two boot-to-steady runs give **464 MB** (peak 506), 59 processes; a `screencap -p` screenshot **~300 ms**/655 KB; the public network works (223.5.5.5 / baidu DNS), neither the internal 192.168.2.1 nor the host's 172.31.250.1 is reachable (the isolation works); after stop both the cgroup and the veth are gone.
- **Screen-recording stream**: the first run gave "unable to create video/avc codec instance" —— redroid.common.rc does `setprop debug.stagefright.ccodec 0` ("DMA Heap required"), while Android 13's software H.264 exists only in the Codec2 one; giving it /dev/dma_heap/system + our `zz_ds4.rc` setting it back to 1 on init ⇒ `screenrecord --output-format=h264 --size 720x1280 --bit-rate 1500000 -` produces a stream: 5 s at 544 KB (108 kB/s on a static desktop), ffprobe confirms Constrained Baseline 720x1280, 32 decodable frames.
- **adb wire-protocol C client** `src/assistant/asst_adb.c` (CNXN/OPEN/OKAY/WRTE/CLSE, exec: service, streaming stdin); the probe `tests/phone/adbprobe` (shell/screencap/record/install/root).
- **Installing an app** (user: "can you download Taobao Shangou and install it"): Taobao Shangou has no separate package = Ele.me renamed (me.ele, Shanghai Rajax); pulled `me.ele_12.9.68.apk` from the Yingyongbao CDN (85 MB, md5 = the filename hash, arm64 native libraries) → `cmd package install -S` streaming install 5.6 s Success → am start 455 ms into the privacy dialog → tap "Agree" → into the Alibaba security SDK's slider page "identity verification · slide to unlock and prove you are not a robot" (ContainerActivity). One `input swipe` didn't pass (not retried: circumventing the risk control is not done, left for a human to slide on the page).
  **The 1 GB memory ceiling hit a wall**: that app's single process RSS 540 MB, memory.current 1023 MB, oom_kill 1, screenshot 1.9 s/swipe 9.6 s (thrashing); the ceiling raised to 2 GB (PH_MEM_MAX_MB) and after a restart the peak 1121 MB is normal. Conclusion: idle 464 MB is the floor, the ceiling has to be sized for the app you intend to run.
- To do: gate 1 (adb frame codec unit tests) → the switch + REST + page (video stream WebCodecs) + six tools → README disclaimer. Not committed. Noticed in passing that spark has a `rev` process (pid 2634354, user fodelf) running at 100% CPU for 13 days, not from this repo, untouched.

## 10-13 late night · Gate 3 real-model end-to-end (user: "is the feature where the local ai can control the phone implemented, e.g. in the assistant I say I want Ele.me on the phone" / "the phone video isn't full screen")
- The model subprocess started via `POST /api/train/serve` (100 s to reachable 8001), remaining memory 9 GB, the phone 737 MB. The probe `tests/asst/asst_send_probe.sh "open Taobao Shangou on the phone and tell me what's on the screen"` (going through the page's own /api/assistant/send).
- **First run (aa97fe9e6f94)**: phone_screen (what it saw was the quick-settings panel my REST tests had left open) → phone_key home → read the desktop element table → replied "这台手机上没有淘宝闪购, 装的有饿了么(Ele.me)…" —— the loop closed, but phone_open's enumeration only has the package name `me.ele`, so the model didn't know Taobao Shangou is it (it only knew me.ele = Ele.me).
- Checking the display name: the system's "app info" page's `entity_header_title` gives **"rpsdk"** (that's how Ele.me's manifest application label is written); the app's label in the desktop drawer is also **"rpsdk"** (the launcher reads the same one) —— nowhere on the phone does it show "Taobao Shangou", this is the app's own business, not our bug.
- Fix (a way of doing things into the tool description, zero app names): phone_open "the display name may not match the package name, don't conclude without an obvious match, go home, swipe up the drawer and tap by label"; phone_screen "the desktop has only a few icons, all the apps are in the drawer (slide from 360,1150 to 360,300)".
- **Second run (416515e689e4, the same sentence)**: phone_screen → phone_swipe the drawer → phone_tap "rpsdk" (618,294) → into the location-permission dialog → tapping "Turn on now" (496,722) twice → the screen goes black → home → swipe the drawer up again → tap rpsdk again → 11 calls trigger the budget hint, end. **The model's autonomous drawer/dialog navigation and retries are all there, and the screenshot+element table came back at every step**; it got stuck on the app's own permission black screen, the same behaviour as tapping by hand (the earlier ele probe also went privacy → risk-control slider).
- Page: the picture now fills the visible height (9:16, capped at 1280), the phone shell fills the width; added a fullscreen button (element requestFullscreen; iOS Safari has no element fullscreen).
- **User: "the video stream is squashed out of shape, the height is very short"** —— it used to rely on `aspect-ratio` to make a 9:16 box, and a browser that doesn't support it squashes the box into a strip, with object-fit: fill flattening along with it. Changed to padding-top 177.78% to give it height + the picture absolutely positioned to fill; Playwright measured: a 390-wide window 239×423 (1.771), a 1440×900 window 422×748 (1.774).
- **Screenshot 502 "no PNG (0 bytes)" two-layer real cause**: ① under the 2 GB ceiling Taobao Shangou runs 4 processes at RSS ~1.4 GB (584+301+298+233), memory.events max hit 2222 times (no oom_kill), the page cache being reclaimed over and over → ceiling changed to 3 GB (PH_MEM_MAX_MB), and after a restart max 0; ② even with the ceiling raised still 0 bytes —— the foreground is `me.ele/com.ali.user.mobile.login.ui.UserLoginActivity`, window `fl=… SECURE …` (anti-screenshot), going back to the desktop immediately gives 667 KB; on that page `uiautomator dump` also gives `null root node`. Black for humans and the model alike, not circumvented (the disclaimer's stance).
  Fix: on screencap failure retry once after 300 ms; look() does its best on the screenshot and the control tree independently, either one counts as success, and with no screenshot it writes "this page forbids screenshots, operate from the element table"; before dump `rm -f` the old file (otherwise on failure it cats the previous tree → the model taps stale coordinates, a real collision); the page's fallback shows "this page forbids screenshots" on a 502 instead of spamming the console.
- rsync two real collisions: writing `--relative` wrongly dropped files into ds4-main/src/src/ so spark still built the old header (memory.max still 2 GB); always `rsync -azR --exclude '*.o' <relative path> spark:ds4-main/`.
- **User: "the frame fills the screen, but the video is only the top half"** —— not reproducible in Chromium (10 rows of sampling all 720 and non-black, the whole frame filled), judged to be the user's browser not recognizing modern CSS like `inset`/`::before` (a browser that squashes aspect-ratio probably doesn't recognize inset either: with no offset on the absolutely positioned element it lands behind the pseudo-element and gets clipped).
  Changed: the box's width and height are computed by `phLayout()` from the window and written into style (desktop = min(container width, (window height−150)×9/16); the phone shell by container width; fullscreen by screen height), and the picture fills with top/left; `[hidden]` now explicitly gets display:none (previously display:block overrode hidden, so the fallback's old screenshot would sit on top of the video).
  In passing: screenrecord only emits frames when the screen changes, so a new viewer on a static desktop gets 7 s of black → phStart first draws a /screen screenshot underneath and the video frame covers it as soon as it arrives. Playwright 1440×900: box 422×750, canvas 420×748, the first frame fills within 4 s.
- **User: "on the phone it still isn't full screen"** —— under the app shell the picture only follows the container width, so on a 390×844 screen it is 377×670 with 63 px empty above the bottom bar. phLayout changed: on the phone compute from "the whole height between the top bar and the bottom bar" (width = min(container width, available height×9/16)), and the view/container padding is removed; 9:16 is shorter than the phone screen, so the distortion-free ceiling is exactly 377×670.
  For real fullscreen: ⛶ uses requestFullscreen in browsers with the element-fullscreen API, and in those without (iOS Safari/PWA) falls back to **immersive mode** (`<html data-immersive>` hides the top bar/bottom bar/right column/sidebar, the picture min(window width, window height×9/16) centred on black, an ✕ floating in the corner; pressing ⛶ again or leaving the tab exits). Playwright simulating no requestFullscreen: 390×693 filled to the width, top and bottom bars display none, the ✕ visible.
- **The real cause of "only the top half" was finally measured** (reproduced with an immersive-mode screenshot: box 390×693, the picture pressed into the top 190 px): the page already had `[data-shell=app] canvas { height: 190px }` (for the monitor charts) at the same specificity as `.phscreen canvas { height: 100% }` but written later ⇒ under the app shell the cloud phone's canvas is 190 px tall (the attributes 720×1280 are correct, the CSS box is short); the desktop shell has no such rule so it never reproduced, and the previous two rounds of aspect-ratio/inset changes were all misdiagnoses. Fix: `.phscreen canvas/img` width and height `!important`. Measurements: normal 375×668 / immersive 390×693, the canvas the same size as the box.

## 10-14 early hours · Cloud phone "tapping anything loops for ever, can't get into Taobao Shangou" verdict (user: "on the cloud phone tapping anything loops for ever, it just can't get into Taobao, analyze the problem")
- **Scene** (spark, the phone restarted at 23:33, uptime 20 min, 3 GB ceiling, memory.events max/oom all 0, public ping 223.5.5.5 15 ms reachable): only `me.ele` installed; foreground `me.ele/…security…ContainerActivity`, **`FocusedWindows: <none>`**, screenshot 0 bytes, `uiautomator dump` null root.
- **Real cause = Ele.me (Taobao Shangou) itself dies once every 6 s and Android automatically restarts it, looping**. `logcat -b events` (23:34~24:00): me.ele `am_proc_start` **79 times**, `am_crash` **61 times** (all `Native crash, Illegal instruction`), `am_anr` **25 times** (`Waited 5000ms for FocusEvent`), `am_kill … user request after error` 6 times (= the user tapping the crash/not-responding dialog on the page). The process doesn't live long enough to take focus ⇒ the page's taps have no receiving window, and tapping anything gives "no response → dialog → starts again → dies again".
- **Where it crashes**: tombstone `signal 4 (SIGILL), code 1 (ILL_ILLOPC)`, the same offset every time `#00 pc 00000000025383f0 /data/data/me.ele/app_u4sdk/dlibs/275305135/lib/arm64-v8a/libwebviewuc.so` (the UC browser kernel, Alibaba's U4 SDK, 73.7 MB). Mapped through the ELF section table to the file bytes, the instruction word there is **`d4400000` = `hlt #0`** (an external-debugger halt instruction, executing it in user mode is always SIGILL); in the file's first 4 MB there are 0 hlt, and within ±2 MB of the crash point there are **1745** —— a whole code body stubbed out with hlt (a hardening/runtime-restoration scheme), which on this virtual machine either wasn't restored or failed its self-check, and it dies at the first one it hits. The last two log lines of that crashing process while alive: `ValarMorghulis: $$$$$$85@@@6@a@4@@@37*****` → `DEBUG: generate native report finished`.
- **Why it could reach the login page earlier in the night and then couldn't**: `app_u4sdk/dlibs` was created at **14:45:25 UTC (22:45 local)**, exactly the moment of the model's second run (416515e689e4) "tapping Turn on now twice → the screen goes black" —— the U4 kernel was unpacked right then and started being loaded, and from then on every launch dies; the model run's "go home / open again / tap again" is just that same loop seen from the model's side, and every element table it received was the last frame before the process died.
- **Ruled out**: not memory (3 GB ceiling, max 0 times); not the network (reachable); not SELinux (redroid `getenforce` = Disabled, no avc); not our adb/screenshot/page (the 0-byte screenshot and null root are both consequences of there being no window); CPU features are irrelevant (the hlt was written in deliberately).
- **Renaming `app_u4sdk` away and starting it again**: it is regenerated into the same directory within 1 s (the kernel is unpacked from the apk's own `.unz_f`, not downloaded), and 6 s later the same SIGILL —— clearing the cache is useless.
- **Verdict**: Taobao Shangou/Ele.me's UC kernel **refuses to run and kills itself** on this virtual phone (an anti-VM/anti-tamper stance), the same family as the earlier "slider risk control" and "login page FLAG_SECURE": the app's attitude, not an engine bug. Per the 10-13 disclaimer's stance it is **not circumvented** (changing the ro.* fingerprint / spoofing a real device are both circumvention). The main Taobao app (com.taobao.taobao) also bundles U4, the same ending is expected.
- **What we should add on our side (general, zero app names, awaiting approval)**: ① add a "foreground app status" line to the frame `phone_*` brings back (the package's am_crash/am_anr counts over the last 60 s, read from `logcat -b events`), so the model seeing "it just crashed 3 times" should stop and report instead of retrying 11 times; ② the same line as a hint on the cloud phone tab; ③ in the phone status, adbd is currently root (I raised it for diagnosis with `adbprobe root`, and it reverts on a phone restart).

## 10-14 · Assistant skill support (skills) (user: "design skill support for the current Agent, and put the skill menu in third")
- **Decided**: a skill = `~/.ds4/assistant/skills/<名>/SKILL.md` (+ scripts/templates/materials), per the Agent Skills open standard (frontmatter name/description + body), skill folders from elsewhere such as Claude Code usable as-is. Design doc `docs/assistant_skills.md`.
- **Model side = progressive disclosure, prompt zero change**: the registry gains one row `use_skill` (asst_skill.c assembles the schema), the description lists "name: one-sentence description", name is the enum; only when called does it give the folder absolute path + file table + the body with frontmatter stripped (limit 64 KB, beyond that it points to read_file paging). One not installed ⇒ that row is absent from the tool table. Why not into system: ten skill bodies = tens of thousands of tokens preloaded every session, most sessions don't use them; master-outline iron rule 3 also only allows scenario knowledge to live in the tool description.
- **Boundary**: the skill folder is **read-only** to tools (gate: reads pass and set no taint, writes are uniformly refused and not approvable — a model able to change its own skills equals web injection being able to live in there long-term); the sandbox mounts the skill folder as a read-only root each time (Linux exec mode read-only root with EXECUTE, macOS process-exec enabled globally), `run` can run the scripts inside. Uploaded attached files have their relative path checked segment by segment (`..`/`.x`/absolute refused), a `#!` at the start gets the execute bit. Delete = move to `trash/skills/`.
- **Page**: the "Skills" tab goes in the sidebar's **third slot** (Assistant / Memory / Skills / Activity …; the cloud-phone slot is normally hidden, when the phone is started it inserts into the second slot); the app shell is in the "More → Assistant" group. List (name + description + file count) / new (with a frontmatter template, name sanitized to lowercase hyphens) / edit save / file table / add file / import folder (webkitdirectory per-file POST) / delete (ask confirm). Interfaces `GET|POST /api/assistant/skills`, `POST /api/assistant/skill_file?name=&path=`.
- **Gate (Mac offline, raw output)**: `ds4_asst_test` → `asst logic: 216 passed, 0 failed` / `asst: 31 passed, 0 failed` (test_skills 36 items: name rules, frontmatter `>` folded lines joined into one sentence, not installed no tool / installed has enum, body with frontmatter stripped, gate read passes write refused, reading a skill sets no taint, sandbox spec contains a read-only root, really read it inside the sandbox, the three interfaces, .. upload 400, delete into trash); `make asst-e2e` → `asst e2e: all passed` (8 new items: `侧栏导航第三格是技能(云手机没起时): chat,mem,skills,act,…`, save persisted to disk, list row, delete into trash); `make linecount` ok. ## 10-14 · Tasks page: create in one sentence, the assistant keeps following up, multiple ones form a list (user: "add a task page after the assistant, you can create a task with one sentence, it keeps following up afterwards, tasks can be multiple so it's a list")
- **Decided**: one task = one sentence + a dedicated session + "when to look again next". On disk `~/.ds4/assistant/tasks/<id>.json` (plain text, fields text/state/end/created/updated/next/runs/last/note), the session's `meta.task` points back. The scheduler thread (`asst_task.c`, one tick every 30 s) sends tasks that are active, due and whose session is idle into their session as "继续这个任务。" (English tasks "Continue this task."), going through the same run loop as chat; the user text is preceded by one extra line of task facts `[任务: 第 N 次跟进 · 创建于 … · 上次结束 … · 你上次留的话: …]` (facts only, not shown on the page).
- **Cadence set by the model, no knob exposed** (10-10 minimal page + 10-12 capability = tool negotiation): a task session's tool table has two extra rows `task_check_in(minutes, note)` and `task_done(summary)` (regular sessions don't), prompt zero change. If the model didn't call check_in this round → at wrap-up the next one is scheduled per `ASST_TASK_FOLLOW_S`=1 h (a task can't break just because the model forgot to say); on error (model not loaded) it likewise schedules the next one, no immediate retry. Pause/complete/delete also stop a round that is currently running; delete = task into trash/tasks + session into trash/sessions.
- **Page**: one slot after "Assistant" in the sidebar for "Tasks" (Skills retreats to the fourth slot, the e2e assertions changed accordingly); one input box, Enter creates; list row = status dot (follows session status) · that sentence · "next HH:MM · follow-up N times · created at" · the assistant's words · head of the last progress; buttons open (enter its conversation)/follow up now/pause/complete/delete; next to the task name in the sidebar it shows the unfinished count; the app shell is in the "More → Assistant" group. Interface `GET|POST /api/assistant/tasks`.
- **Code**: new `src/assistant/asst_task.c` (299 lines) + `tests/asst/t_asst_task.c`; `asst_run.c` three hooks (fact line / tctx.task / wrap-up `asst_task_run_end`); registry gains two rows site=TASK; the gate lets the `task` class pass; `asst_api.c` routing; `train_main.c` starts the scheduler thread; `asst_tctx` gains a `task` field (three unit-test initializations add NULL). Design doc `docs/assistant.md` §6 rewritten into the landed version.

## 10-14 · Notifications: browser push (user: "add a notification feature, use pwa push; notify when a long task is done; notify before each time point of the travel plan" → follow-up "whether to notify is judged by the ai itself" / "definitely don't notify on the current page")
- **Who decides to push**: three entry points. ① the model's `notify(text, title?, at?)` tool (present in every conversation): it judges the things the user should know, sends now or sends when the time arrives (scheduled ones land in `reminders/<id>.json`, the scheduler thread scans once every 30 s); ② framework mechanical rules (not through the model): a task's `task_done` this round → push "task done: <that sentence>"; any run ≥ 120 s → push "<conversation title>" + head of the reply (someone who waited more than two minutes has probably left the page); ③ the page's "send a test".
- **When the page is open and being watched, never push** (user-decided): while the page is visible it does `POST presence {client, visible}` every 20 s, switching to the background/closing the page reports false immediately (keepalive); if the server has a page watching within 45 s → don't push to devices, land in `push/notices.jsonl`, the page polls it up and toasts it on the spot (clicking enters that conversation); the notify tool result truthfully writes "shown on the page the user has open". It didn't go the service worker's "don't show when visible" route: Chrome has a quota for receiving a push without showing it, and beyond that it shows "the site has been updated in the background" on your behalf.
- **Protocol and cryptography all hand-written (zero deps, pure C, `src/push/` 358 lines)**: Web Push = RFC 8030 + 8291 (aes128gcm: ECDH P-256 → HKDF(auth salt, "WebPush: info"|ua_pub|as_pub) → HKDF(salt) produces CEK/NONCE → AES-128-GCM, body = salt|rs|idlen|as_pub|ciphertext) + 8292 (VAPID: ES256 JWT, aud=endpoint origin, sub=subscription page origin or mailto). P-256 = 8×32-bit-word bignums + modular multiply as 512-bit bit-by-bit long division + Jacobian coordinates (dbl-2001-b/add-2007-bl) + Fermat inversion; ECDSA k deterministic per RFC 6979; S-boxes computed from the definition, not copied from tables; GHASH bitwise multiply. One push takes three scalar multiplies, ~0.1 s total. The honest boundary is written in the header: scalar multiply is not constant time.
  **First-run raw cross-check (item by item against an independent node:crypto implementation)**: `sig=efd48b2a…3716 f7cb1c94…cda8` (= RFC 6979 A.2.5 r/s), `pub=0460fed4…2299` (= node), `ecdh=kyrL1jIIOHEzg3sM2ZWRHDRB62YACZhhSlknJ672kSs` (= RFC 8291), `body=DGv6ra1nlYgDCS1FRnbzlwAAEABB…Qulcy4a-fN` (= RFC 8291 Appendix A byte for byte), GCM case 1/3, HKDF A.1 same; node_verify_sample=true node_verify_jwt=true.
- **Sending goes through curl** (push services are all https, no TLS library pulled in; downloading frp/probing the public port already uses curl): the encrypted body lands in a push/.out-* temp file with `--data-binary @`, headers Content-Encoding: aes128gcm / TTL: 86400 / Urgency: normal / Authorization: vapid t=…, k=…; 404/410 deletes the subscription on the spot; every send goes into audit (tool=push). VAPID key `push/vapid.json` (0600, generated on first use), subscriptions `push/subs/<sha256(endpoint)前16位>.json`.
- **Page**: a "Notifications" card at the top of the tasks page (toggle = pushManager.subscribe(VAPID public key) → POST subscribe; off = unsubscribe on both sides; test button; device count + labels), a "Scheduled reminders" card (open/delete); sw.js push → showNotification, notificationclick → focus an already-open window postMessage url / open `/?session=<id>#chat`, the page takes both routes through gotoNotice straight into the conversation. Insecure context (http LAN) the toggle is grey with an explanation; iPhone not installed to the home screen explained.
- **Gate (Mac, raw output)**: `ds4_push_test` → `push: 37 passed, 0 failed`; `ds4_asst_test` → `asst push: 52 passed, 0 failed` (the test starts a fake push service to receive the POST → decrypts the body as a browser byte for byte `{"title":"标题 T","body":"正文 hello\n第二行","url":"/?session=x#chat"}`, verifies the JWT with k=, claims aud/sub, notify now/scheduled/on-time tick/bad time/card-number refusal, short run not pushed/long run pushed/task done pushed, presence not pushed lands in notices, 410 deletes subscription, unsubscribe); `make test` all green + linecount ok; `make asst-e2e` → `asst e2e: all passed` (new: notification card state, `notify 工具结果: 页面开着 → 'shown on the page', 没推设备`, `notices.jsonl 多一条, 带那个对话的 url`, `页面里弹出了这条通知: 盯着 e2e 的价格, 降了通知我 · e2e 通知: 价格降了`).

## 10-14 · Assistant voice input: design finalized (user: "the assistant page should support voice input, design it first" → "definitely upload and use the smallest model to recognize" → "land the design first, put the code directory under that model directory")
- **Characterization**: voice input = an input method, not a model tool: text is written back into the input box, the user reviews it before sending; it doesn't enter caps / the tool table / the prompt. The browser's built-in `SpeechRecognition` ruled out (Chrome goes through Google, unreachable on domestic Android; only one path is kept).
- **Model (external resource, user nodded "smallest")**: HF `moonshine-ai/moonshine-tiny-zh` 27.1M parameters, safetensors f32 108,389,160 B + tokenizer.json 3.7 MB; 6+6 layers d=288 8 heads FFN 1152 vocab 32768; in the paper's terms Chinese CER Fleurs 29.4 / CV17 36.1 (whisper-tiny 71.1 / 66.0, discarded; whisper-medium is 7.6 worse than it); the official docs say MIT, the LICENSE.txt in the repo at 11,577 B is the length of Apache-2.0, verify after download. Same family `moonshine-base-zh` (58M, CER 25.8) same structure, swap the file with zero code change. SenseVoice-Small is one notch better on Chinese but 936 MB + another set of SAN-M/CTC + a custom license, not chosen.
- **Placement**: lives in ds4-server (Makefile 288 lines ds4-train doesn't link GPU; the vision tower 10-13 is the template), code `src/model/asr/` (asr_model / asr_tok decode only / asr_graph / asr_http + three new kernels conv1d·groupnorm1·tanh + layernorm + dense_attn with causal added); reads safetensors directly without converting to GGUF; weights not resident (following the vision tower); decoding writes no KV cache, recomputes the prefix every step (10 s ≈ 65 token); interface `POST /v1/audio/transcriptions` accepts only 16 kHz mono 16-bit WAV, >30 s refused (the training limit); recognition is queued into the single worker job queue. Page: the mic appears only when status.asr + secure + getUserMedia all three hold, tap to record tap to stop with auto-stop at 30 s, AudioWorklet in-page linear resampling to 16 kHz (48 kHz native is 3x the bytes, the pass-through port 1 MB/s).
- **Two things to verify before writing code**: whether V4 RoPE's pairing is rotate_half (if not, extract a 1D version of the vision 2D RoPE); contending with generation for the GPU queues first, if the wait is objectionable then discuss a second line.
- **Gate**: `ds4_test --asr` fixture WAV bit-for-bit against the HF reference (Mac Metal + spark CUDA); curl the interface with three kinds of bad input, each refused; on three real machines 10 sentences each, raw results pasted for the user to count CER by hand; 10 s audio server-side elapsed time reported as one number each, target <300 ms.
- Design doc `docs/assistant_asr.md`, pointer `docs/assistant.md` §14. No code touched, model not downloaded.

## 10-14 night · Voice first real-device run (user: "after recognition ends it still shows the phone is busy, and the recognition accuracy isn't high either")
- **"Busy" is not voice being stuck**: session 85d3a2ac5d3b event stream —— `user "我是大帅哥妈。"` → while thinking `stop_request client=ut2adno276mv4y52y2 how=button` → `end stopped`; `user "嘿嘿"` → likewise stopped by a press; `user "两分钟臭提醒我。"` → thinking 1089 token (32 t/s, 32.7 s) → remember + notify → reply → `end done`. Recognition produces text in <1 s, the ~30 s after that is the assistant model thinking (`model_llm.c:96` forces `"think":true`, 10-12 user-decided Agent on by default); during that time in voice mode the bar says "the assistant is working" and the rightmost is a red stop key, looks stuck, was stopped by a press twice. ## 10-14 night · Push: nothing received outside the PWA, yet it pops inside the app (user: "push messages don't work inside the pwa, and before it was made clear that there should be no push inside the app yet a message pops, while outside there is indeed no push" → chose "pop nothing, push after leaving")
- **The direct cause of nothing outside = not one device subscribed**: spark `push/subs/` never had a file written since it was created at 17:40; every notify in the audit is `0 device(s) have notifications on`, and when the two scheduled reminders at 22:05 and 22:12 came due and went through `asst_push_send_sync` there were 0 subscriptions → the loop wasn't entered → **not even an audit entry was left, silently dropped**. The user is on Android and had never turned on the notifications toggle on the tasks page.
- **"Remind me in thirty seconds" popping on the spot = my bug**: session 1b87dba230ff, at 22:25:5x said "remind me to sleep thirty seconds later", the model can only fill `at` to the minute → 22:26, less than 30 s from now, `ASST_REMIND_MIN_S=30` treated it as "send now" → page open → landed in notices → the in-page toast popped immediately; the one actually 30 s later doesn't exist. The tool still replied "shown on the page", and on that basis the model told the user "it will be pushed when the time comes".
- **Another design error**: presence was judged globally —— any one page being visible meant no device got a push, so with the desktop holding a tab open the phone would never receive anything.
- **Fix**: presence is recognized per device (the heartbeat carries the push endpoint), the push for the device currently watching the page is held in `push/held/<订阅 id>.jsonl`, and after switching away/locking the screen/or the heartbeat expiring at 45 s the new notification thread re-pushes it as-is; the in-page toast + `notices` deleted entirely. `notify` gains an `after` seconds count, `at` may carry seconds, a future one even a few seconds off is still scheduled; reminders moved from the task scheduler's 30 s tick to a dedicated notification thread (sleeps until the nearest due time / heartbeat expiry, awakened by a new schedule or a page reporting it left). 0 devices: notify now errors directly, a due one records audit `not sent: no device`. "Send a test" isn't held.
- **Gate**: `asst push` 52 → 64 items all passed (second-level / held per device / re-pushed after leaving / heartbeat expiry / the notification thread sending on time itself and being woken), same on Mac and spark; `make asst-e2e` all passed (no device → the tool says so plainly, the page doesn't pop). spark synced, recompiled, ds4-train restarted (model child process untouched, public 200). Not committed.
- **Android's wall (unsolved)**: Android Chrome push goes entirely through Google FCM. spark's direct FCM times out; through Mihomo 7890 connecting to google.com / huggingface is also 000 (handshake cut, proxy nodes currently unreachable); the ds4-train process environment has no proxy. Even if the phone can subscribe, the sending side can't reach FCM right now. Contrast: spark's direct `web.push.apple.com` answers 403 in 0.7 s (a normal rejection without auth) —— the iPhone home-screen PWA route works.
- **10-15 early morning · Sending side borrows the Mac proxy (user chose 2: "temporarily prop it up with a Mac tunnel first")**: the Mac through 7897 reaches FCM with a reply in 0.67 s; after `ssh -R 17897:127.0.0.1:7897 spark` spark through the tunnel gets a reply in 0.43 s (400 = the fake request rejected by FCM = connected). spark's own Mihomo Proxy group (Singapore) and AutoSelect (Berlin) all time out on speed tests, not fixed. Code: the push proxy is stored in `push/proxy`, filled in in the notification card, curl carries `-x` (empty = `-x ""` explicit direct connection, doesn't take env); the unit test uses a fake push service as the proxy, and checks curl really sent `CONNECT push.example.test:443`; `asst push` 72 items all passed (Mac/spark). spark restarted, the push proxy filled through the interface as `http://127.0.0.1:17897`. Mac-side tunnel script `gguf-tools/scripts/push_tunnel_mac.sh` (user: "don't commit the script to git", already in .git/info/exclude), breaks when the Mac sleeps. **Still missing the user turning on the tasks page notifications toggle from the phone, the whole chain has not been verified on a real device.**

## 10-15 · The "change the clothes color to black" conversation won't stop = a thinking-section repetition loop (read-only diagnosis, no code touched)
- **On disk (spark session 77fa13e357d0)**: sent 10:21:14 (phone, with a 1.8 MB jpeg), 10:49:28 the user pressed stop → after the next increment `end=stopped` (the stop button is fine). In 28 minutes 72,456 think increments, 0 text, 0 tool calls, the thinking 287,970 characters without emitting `</think>`. trace parameters think_mode high / temperature 1.000 / top_p 0.950 / min_p 0. Reading the image was right (the cream-white coat, the wooden hanger, the "穿上试试" corner label, the 23:58 status bar all named correctly).
- **Shape**: the first ~twenty thousand characters are proper planning (ImageMagick color picking → convert to ppm, pure Python masking → black it out), then each time it writes up to "Let me do the call." / "Let me emit." it doesn't close, goes back and copies the same ~5 KB (verification method, "the sentence before calling a tool must be in Chinese", the `identify` command, the orange corner-label criterion) verbatim again; of the 1,525 long lines only 165 are non-repeating, the most frequent one appears 52 times = 52 rounds of verbatim repetition.
- **Frequency**: across all spark's 60 sessions 340 thinking sections, only this one ran away; the second longest 40,339 characters (canvas code, at most 5 repeated lines, not a loop).
- **Verdict**: same shape as 09-30 (the decision position `</think>` squeezed to 2%~6% by the quantized base, once in the loop the top-1 median 0.99 can't get out), the assistant from 10-12 defaults to thinking on, exposing it into the product. This time with an image, `scoreids` re-scoring by id can't be fed the visual embeddings, so no bit-level fidelity reconciliation was done; the server has no logprobs interface, measuring it would require stopping the model child process. Whether top_p 0.95 (from 10-12) cuts off the decision position's low-probability `</think>` entirely wasn't measured.
- **10-15 11:30 re-examination (the user raised "won't stop" again): the loop is byte-for-byte ⇒ top_p 0.95 turned the loop into an absorbing state**. Cutting segments at the most frequent long line, consecutive **51 segments of 4,828 bytes with identical md5** (246 KB / 292 KB), the 52nd segment 1,230 bytes is the half-cut when stop was pressed. Under temperature 1.0, 51 rounds ×~1,200 token identical character by character has only one explanation: at every position the keep set has only top-1 left. The engine's top_p semantics (cuda_v41_sample.inc.cu: truncate at the first position where the cumulative ≥ top_p) ⇒ when top-1 ≥ 0.95 the keep set = {top-1}, the decision position's 2%~6% `</think>` is cut off entirely, p(escape)=0. Contrast the 09-30 (top_p 1.0) patient 601069 s1: escaped 49 times and fell back; 10-12 request 30 also under top_p 1.0 actually emitted `</think>` 8 times.
  ⇒ two layers: the root cause is still quantization compressing the closing decision 4~22 fold (fixed in the weights, fable5 09-30 to-do: ② add whole-essay endings to the corpus + open-source reasoning sets); 10-12's top_p 0.95 is an amplifier —— what it cuts is the tail (garbage positions p<9e-4), and along the way it cut the decision position too. The same cut edge with min_p 0.02 (relative to top-1: threshold 0.0198 when 0.99) still cuts off all four garbage positions (p upper bound <8.3e-5~<8.9e-4), while most of the 2%~6% `</think>` remains; 10-12 measured that it changes 2.61% of sampling positions (top_p 0.95 is 2.36%).

## 10-15 afternoon · Image-editing tool plan: a probe of DS vision + pixel-tool division of labor (no code written; design doc docs/assistant_image.md)
- **User: design an image tool to solve "image editing thinking too long"; don't introduce a generative image model (won't fit, ≤100 MB another matter); first see whether DS can solve it; the jaggedness must be fixed, the rest think later**.
- The truth (pulling out all tool calls of session 754b59df1696): all 14 calls were analysis scripts (write_file 7 / run 6 / read_file 1), after `convert` to PPM hand-wrote pure Python pixel-by-pixel color thresholds, tried four versions of the "cream white" criterion, didn't change a single pixel ⇒ the root cause = it can see but can't lay hands on it, the toolbox has no "point at this area and change it to that" tool.
- **DS vision probe** (`tests/asst/vision_box_probe.sh`, image + question straight to :8001, temp 0, zero thinking, 7~8 s per item; the coat image 1284×1718, ground truth I estimated by looking at the image x 86..1221 y 229..1507):
  Three ways of asking for a bounding box (pixels `214,148,1131,1051` / normalized `310,130,970,900` / four sides separately 352·1132·196·1131) each have one side off by 300~450 px ⇒ **don't use boxes**; "points that fall on the coat" 7/7 all hit (placket 640,900..1500 / cuff 150,1500 / hood 600,300), hem y 1526 (true ~1507) ⇒ **use points**;
  Acting as an inspector looking at the red-overlay image: can point out the hood top missed / the top-right corner label over-covering, but misses a large area on the left, hallucinates "the hanger is covered" ⇒ coarse screening.
- **Pixel probe 7 rounds** (numpy, verifying the algorithm only; the red-overlay image was inspected each round, the conclusion table is in design doc §3.5): RGB k-means numbered regions doesn't work (coat/background the same brightness); geodesic distance judged negative (the knit's large gradient makes "crossing the background cheaper" instead); texture features judged negative (paper grain + JPEG noise 17.8 > knit 14.4); GrabCut self-iteration judged negative (took the left side and ate into the bottom right).
  **Final design** = one Gaussian component per seed point (24×24, +9I) + automatic negative samples every 32 px around a border ring (+4 weak prior, never dropped: relaxing to "drop it if close to a positive point" blows the whole image to 87%) + min-NLL competition + hole filling/connectivity + 7×7 majority filter ×2 + full-resolution guided-filter soft alpha (r=8, no stair-stepping at edges) + recolor preserving brightness difference ×0.6.
  Robustness: the model self-reports 5 points + a hanger negative point → misses the right sleeve in shadow; +1 point each on the right sleeve/right of the hood → **the whole garment perfectly right, zero misses**; without negative points same as before; deliberately one bad positive point → only a small patch missed beside it. python 2.4 s/image. Three finished images sent to the user.
- Tool shape finalized: `edit_image(path, ops, out?)`, `recolor(points, avoid?, color)` doesn't take boxes or tolerances; the result carries back the finished image + the two red-overlay images through the same image_url route as cloud-phone screenshots; the attachment line gains (W×H). Waiting for the user's nod to write C (`src/image/` four files + `tools/tool_image.c`).

- **ds4-seg** (src/seg/, 9 files): `seg_pt.c` reads the torch.save zip (stored)+pickle protocol 2 directly (a stack machine of 23 opcodes, recognizing only OrderedDict/FloatStorage/_rebuild_tensor_v2; 412 float tensors 10,140,204 parameters, 27 Long scalars skipped); `seg_model.c` BN folding/conv kernel reordering into im2col K order/attention bias expanded by window/dense positional encoding; `seg_encoder.c` TinyViT (token-first NHWC, convolution = im2col+GEMM, window attention zero-padding and window slicing); `seg_decoder.c` prompt encoding + bidirectional transformer + ConvT as GEMM+pixel shuffle + hypernetwork; `seg_run.c` the official predictor flow (PIL bilinear downscale to 1024, two decode rounds with the mask prompt fed in the second, torch-style bilinear put back); the operator contract `seg_ops.h`, two implementations: `seg_metal.m` (MPS GEMM + metal/seg.metal 11 kernels, erf via A&S 7.1.26) / `seg_cuda.cu` (cuBLAS + same-formula kernels).

## 10-16 · YoungAi issue #2: read_file missing/bad arguments taken as success (fixed)

- **Symptom** (external report, 846c929, reproduces on current HEAD as well): `read_file {}` / `{"path":null}` / `{"path":123}` / bad JSON `{"path":coding-eval/total.py}` / `"."` all return `ok:true` + `<工作区>: 0 lines; start 1 is past the end`.
- **Three layers stacked**: ① the gate `guard_file` can't get a path and treats it as an empty string, doesn't check the schema's required/type; ② `asst_path_resolve` empty string = the workspace (the convention for list_dir, read_file follows along); ③ `slurp` doesn't check `ferror`, fopen on a directory succeeds, read returns EISDIR turning into an empty file → "0 lines" doesn't start with error → ok. Source of the bad JSON: the model marks a string argument `string="false"`, the server assembles JSON from the raw text (server_dsml_parse.c deliberately doesn't fix it, left to the tool layer to refuse).
- **Fix**: `asst_tool_args_error` (asst_tools.c) checks against the schema sent to the model this round before the run_call gate: it must be a JSON object, required not missing and not null, the given arguments' types right; numbers/booleans/arrays written as strings are still accepted (same convention as asst_jint / asst_plan.c as_array); non-conforming → `error: invalid arguments for <tool>: …`, decision=`invalid` (the page red-marks "wrong arguments"). `slurp` / `asst_slurp` check ferror and return errno: read_file "." → `error: read …: Is a directory`.
- **Verification**: ds4_asst_test Mac (Seatbelt) / spark (landlock+seccomp) all green, asst 31 → 51 (+20: the issue's 8 malformed variants + 8 compliant ones let through + arrays written as strings 2 + reading a directory 1 + reporting the missing parameter name 1); `--check-args` replaying 641 real calls across 83 spark sessions refused 8: 5 web_search whose DSML wasn't closed (the old path failed anyway, returning the misleading "safety rules: web_search requires query"), 3 remember missing kind (sessions before 10-15 added kind, the current code's execution side refuses them too) ⇒ **0 false kills**. Real-model end-to-end not run.
- **End-to-end (spark real model, 18:51 recompiled ds4-train restarted the main process, model child process untouched; through asst_send_probe.sh = the same route as the page)**:
  ① "deliberately call read_file without a path" → the argument that arrives is `{` (see below), `ok:false decision=invalid`, `error: invalid arguments for read_file: arguments are not a valid JSON object: {`, the model relays it truthfully, 26 s;
  ② path="." → `ok:false`, `error: read …/workspace: Is a directory`, 15 s;
  ③ normal write_file → read_file → list_dir three times all `ok:true decision=auto`, 20 s (the artifact left in the workspace probe-1016/total.py).
- **★hit another server-side bug (unfixed)★**: in ① the model wrote `<｜DSML｜ invoke name="read_file">` + **a bare `</invoke>`** (missing the ｜DSML｜ prefix). The streaming parser (server_openai_stream.c) sends the tool header and `{` as soon as it sees the start of invoke, and fails before a legal invoke end arrives; the final parse judges "invalid tool call returned as assistant text finish=stop". But `emitted_any` is already true, so wrap-up doesn't re-send ⇒ **the client receives a tool call whose argument is the half-cut `{`, while the server itself thinks it is body text** —— the two sides don't agree. Evidence: trace serve_20261015_115815.txt request 356. Argument validation caught it this time (refusal + explicit error), the root cause is the inconsistency between the server's streaming and its final parse.

## 10-16 evening · Streaming tool calls and final parsing unified: conclusion (b800c44)

- **Root cause**: the server translates the model's DSML into tool_calls twice —— the streaming projection sends while generating, the final parse judges the whole block at wrap-up. Each side recognizes its own tags: the parameter-level bare `<parameter>`/`</parameter>` were recognized by both sides on 10-11, the invoke-level bare `</invoke>` is recognized by neither. In request 356 the model wrote a bare `</invoke>`, the projection had already sent the call header and `{` and then got stuck, the final parse returned the whole block to body text, yet wrap-up ended as usual ⇒ the client gets a half-cut `{` call, the server itself treats it as body text. It only happens when the model writes the block badly (5 of spark's 641 historical calls written badly, all web_search not closed), normal agent calls are unaffected.
- **Fix**: the aliases moved into `server_dsml_alias.c`, the final parse / KV syntax tracking / both streaming projections share one set of functions, and a bare `</invoke>` is newly recognized; at wrap-up, if the calls already exposed on the stream don't match the final parse one by one ⇒ send an error event (Claude Code retries automatically, the assistant's model_llm.c doesn't execute the whole round), and if it was rejected before ever being exposed ⇒ the raw text is filled in as body text (same as Responses).
- **★overturned approach★**: "hold the tool block until wrap-up then send + decode heartbeat" was tried first. Reading the Claude Code 2.1.301 implementation: the stream watchdog is on by default, idle threshold ≥300 s, it only recognizes SDK events; after 30 consecutive `ping`s (`IKr=30`) it no longer keeps the connection alive, and `:` comment lines don't count at all ⇒ holding it can last about 7.5 minutes at most, and a long-context file of a thousand-plus lines will certainly break. Upstream generating while projecting is the precondition for Claude Code to work, it can't be removed.
- **Verification**: Mac `make test` all green; spark `ds4_test --server` green; `server_tests_tool_agree.c` nine cases × two protocols, removing the alias or removing the error branch both fail. After spark swapped in the new ds4-server (model-restart, reinstalled in 100 s): the assistant calls read_file with no arguments → argument `{}` + `"path" is required`; a normal write/read/list three times ok; Claude Code (default stream timeout, `cc_smoke_v3p.sh remote`) fixing the Clamp bug 6 tool calls succeeded; writing a 300-line file with one Write (about a 2400 token tool block, 66 s) complete and correct.
- **Not covered**: the real model wrote standard tags every time, the bare `</invoke>` is only covered by the unit test using the trace's raw bytes; no tool block longer than 7 minutes was run; when the model writes a bad block the assistant errors for the whole round, with no automatic retry.
